## 其他赞誉：

<!--en-->
*Additional Praise for*

《财务报表分析》第四版：“这是一次对财务报表的深刻而富有洞见的探索，书中阐述了如何利用财务报表来获取信息、如何被用以误导他人，以及如何借此分析企业的财务健康状况。”——哈佛商学院荣休院长杰伊·O·莱特
“任何在证券市场投入资金或建议他人这样做的人，都应把《财务报表分析》列为必读书目。”——Neuberger Berman共同基金及Idealab公司总监杰克·L·里夫金
“弗里德森和阿尔瓦雷斯为理解、解读以及批判性评估企业发布的财务报告提供了宝贵的实用指南。鉴于近期企业频现报告问题，他们关于利润——“盈利质量”的论述尤为有见地。我强烈推荐此书给所有希望透过数字来预测未来利润与股价的人。”——纽约大学伦纳德·N·斯特恩商学院执行MBA项目副院长保罗·布朗
“愿本书能助力提升财务透明度、报告标准以及对所有利益相关者的责任感。”——加州大学荣休财务主管、KCM投资顾问公司合伙人帕特里夏·A·斯莫尔
“本书是一部精心打磨的佳作，全面涵盖了财务报表分析内容。其论述详尽、观点审慎且极具实用性。”——Loomis, Sayles & Company, LP副董事长丹尼尔·J·富斯

<!--en-->
*Financial Statement Analysis, Fourth Edition*
"This is an illuminating and insightful tour of financial statements, how they can be used to inform, how they can be used to mislead, and how they can be used to analyze the financial health of a company."
—Jay O. Light, Dean Emeritus, Harvard Business School
"*Financial Statement Analysis* should be required reading for anyone who puts a dime to work in the securities markets or recommends that others do the same."
—Jack L. Rivkin, Director, Neuberger Berman Mutual Funds and Idealab
"Fridson and Alvarez provide a valuable practical guide for understanding, interpreting, and critically assessing financial reports put out by firms. Their discussion of profits—'quality of earnings'—is particularly insightful given the recent spate of reporting problems encountered by firms. I highly recommend their book to anyone interested in getting behind the numbers as a means of predicting future profits and stock prices."
—Paul Brown, Associate Dean, Executive MBA Programs, Leonard N. Stern School of Business, New York University
"Let this book assist in financial awareness and transparency and higher standards of reporting, and accountability to all stakeholders."
—Patricia A. Small, Treasurer Emeritus, University of California; Partner, KCM Investment Advisors
"This book is a polished gem covering the analysis of financial statements. It is thorough, skeptical, and extremely practical in its review."
—Daniel J. Fuss, Vice Chairman, Loomis, Sayles & Company, LP

# 第四版前言

<!--en-->
*Preface to Fourth Edition*

《财务报表分析》第四版与前几版一样，旨在帮助读者应对当代商业中的实际挑战。本书再次旨在让已经掌握基础会计技能的读者了解：将教科书中的知识应用于信贷发放和证券投资等现实场景时所面临的复杂情况。正如快速变化的环境促使第二版和第三版进行了大量修订与补充一样，21世纪头十年里，财务报表使用者也面临着新的问题与挑战。

<!--en-->
This fourth edition of *Financial Statement Analysis*, like its predecessors, seeks to equip its readers for the practical challenges of contemporary business. Once again, the intention is to acquaint readers who have already acquired basic accounting skills with the complications that arise in applying textbook-derived knowledge to the real world of extending credit and investing in securities. Just as a swiftly changing environment necessitated extensive revisions and additions in the second and third editions, new concerns and challenges for users of financial statements have emerged during the first decade of the twenty-first century.

第三版所反映的一个根本性变化是：企业高管薪酬计划从以报告盈利为重点转向提升股东价值。理论上，这种新方式能够协调管理层与股东的利益，但这一概念也有其阴暗面。面临越来越大的压力以提升公司股价的首席执行官们，再也无法通过那些在股市中显而易见的财务报告手段来虚增盈利、从而增加奖金。相反，他们不得不采用更加隐蔽的方法，哄骗投资者相信所报告的盈利增长是真实的。

<!--en-->
A fundamental change reflected in the third edition was the shift of corporations' executive compensation plans from a focus on reported earnings toward enhancing shareholder value. In theory, this new approach aligned the interests of management and shareholders, but the concept had a dark side. Chief executive officers who were under growing pressure to boost their corporations' share prices could no longer increase their bonuses by goosling reported earnings through financial reporting tricks that were transparent to the stock market. Instead, they had to devise more opaque methods that gulled investors into believing that the reported earnings gains were real.

为了适应新环境，企业管理者在歪曲业绩方面变得更加激进。他们不再满足于夸大数字，而是直接使用衍生工具和特殊目的实体来伪造盈利；这些工具根本不会出现在财务报表中，且与商品和服务的生产与销售几乎无关。这一险恶趋势最终演变成了安然、世界通信等公司引发的巨大会计丑闻，不仅动摇了人们对财务报告体系的信任，也损害了证券市场的信心。

<!--en-->
To adapt to the new environment, corporate managers became far more aggressive in misrepresenting their performance. They moved beyond exaggeration to outright fabrication of earnings through the use of derivatives and special purpose vehicles that never showed up in financial statements and had little to do with the production and sale of goods and services. This insidious trend culminated in colossal accounting scandals involving companies such as Enron and WorldCom, which shook confidence not only in financial reporting but also in the securities markets.

针对财务欺诈引发的愤怒，政府于2002年颁布了《萨班斯-奥克斯利法案》。根据该法案，公司的首席执行官和首席财务官必须对财务报表的真实性负责。这意味着他们比以往更容易因虚假陈述而面临起诉和定罪的风险。《萨班斯-奥克斯利法案》确实对不实报告起到了威慑作用，但正如本新版中的案例研究所显示的那样，财务报表使用者仍无法高枕无忧。xi xii 前言

<!--en-->
Government responded to the outrage over financial frauds by enacting the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002. Under its provisions, a company's chief executive officer and chief financial officer were required to attest to the integrity of the financial statements. They were thereby exposed to greater risk than formerly of prosecution and conviction for misrepresentation. Sarbanes-Oxley did create a deterrent to untruthful reporting, but as case studies in this new edition demonstrate, users of financial statements still cannot breathe easy.
xi xii
PREFACE

为帮助读者避免被具有欺骗性的财务报表所误导，我们继续敦促他们将会计原理的理解与企业金融视角相结合。

<!--en-->
To help readers avoid being misled by deceptive financial statements, we continue to urge them to combine an understanding of accounting principles with a corporate finance perspective.

我们在《财务报表分析》一书中贯穿了这种学科整合，并涉及经济学与企业管理领域的内容。此外，我们鼓励分析师考虑财务报告所处的制度环境。组织层面的压力会导致实际分析与优雅的理论产生偏差，无论是在财务报表分析过程中还是在审计师对会计原则的解释上均是如此。财务报表的编制者也对会计原则的制定施加着强大影响，有时连有权势的政治人物也会为其撑腰。

<!--en-->
We facilitate such integration of disciplines throughout *Financial Statement Analysis*, making excursions into economics and business management as well. In addition, we encourage analysts to consider the institutional context in which financial reporting occurs. Organizational pressures result in divergences from elegant theories, both in the conduct of financial statement analysis and in auditors' interpretations of accounting principles. The issuers of financial statements also exert a strong influence over the creation of the accounting principles, with powerful politicians sometimes carrying their water.

与第三版一样，我们重点介绍了在财务报表审查中的成功案例。只要能找到必要的文档，我们就会展示：不仅如何通过运用基础分析技术预见企业危机，还展示分析师们如何在问题被广泛知晓之前就察觉到它。希望这些例子能激励读者开展真正有目标导向的分析，而不是仅仅机械地计算标准的财务比率。此外，这些案例研究应能说服他们：一旦发现问题，就要坚持己见，即便管理层会给出那些老套的辩解之词。

<!--en-->
As in the third edition, we highlight success stories in the critical examination of financial statements. Wherever we can find the necessary documentation, we show not only how a corporate debacle could have been foreseen through application of basis analytical techniques but also how practicing analysts actually did detect the problem before it became widely recognized. Readers will be encouraged by these examples, we hope, to undertake genuine, goal-oriented analysis, instead of simply going through the motions of calculating standard financial ratios. Moreover, the case studies should persuade them to stick to their guns when they spot trouble, despite management's predictable litany.

（“我们的财务报表符合公认会计原则，且已由全球顶尖的审计事务所认证。我们绝不会允许一群贪婪的卖空者毁掉我们优秀员工创造的价值。”）通常来说，管理层的抗议越激烈，公司状况就越恶化；原本关于激进会计处理的指责，最终会演变成财务造假曝光。

<!--en-->
("Our financial statements are consistent with generally accepted accounting principles. They have been certified by one of the world's premier auditing firms. We will not allow a band of greedy short sellers to destroy the value created by our outstanding employees.") Typically, as the vehemence of management's protests increases, conditions deteriorate, and accusations of aggressive accounting give way to revelations of fraudulent financial reporting.

新增的一章（第11章）题为“欺诈能否被察觉？”，旨在起到警示作用。有些公司仍能通过标准技术（如比率分析）无法察觉的方式掩盖不实信息。它们要么让审计师蒙在鼓里，要么成功收买审计师，从而消除了财务报表使用者的一道重要防线。通过阅读本章中的案例研究，读者可以看到那些会引起经验丰富的金融侦探（如卖空者）怀疑的企业行为。我们还重点介绍了近期的研究：这些研究将财务错报与企业管理者在投资者和分析师电话会议中使用的词汇和表述联系起来。

<!--en-->
A new chapter (Chapter 11) titled "Is Fraud Detectable?" serves as a cautionary note. Some companies continue to succeed in burying misrepresentations in ways that cannot be detected by standard techniques such as ratio analysis. They manage to keep their auditors in the dark or succeed in corrupting them, removing a key line of defense for users of financial statements. By reading the case studies presented in this chapter, readers can observe corporate behavior that puts companies under suspicion by seasoned financial detectives such as short sellers. We also highlight recent research linking financial misreporting to words and phrases used by corporate managers in conference calls with investors and analysts.

关于《财务报表分析》这本书的阅读顺序，读者无需拘泥于我们设定的章节排列。

<!--en-->
As for the plan of *Financial Statement Analysis*, readers should not feel compelled to tackle its chapters in the order we have assigned to them.

为了帮助那些想从书中某处开始阅读的读者，我们提供了交叉引用和术语表。术语表中定义的词汇在文中会以粗体显示。尽管跳着读对许多读者而言是最有效的方式，但章节编排背后仍遵循着逻辑顺序。前言 xiii 在第一部分“字里行间的秘密”中，我们指出财务报表并非对公司财务业绩的客观写照，并解释了原因。该部分探讨了发行公司及其管理者的复杂动机，也研究了分析师所处组织环境所产生的扭曲效应。

<!--en-->
To aid those who want to jump in somewhere in the middle of the book, we provide cross-referencing and a glossary. Words that are defined in the glossary are shown in bold-faced type in the text. Although skipping aroundwill be the most efficient approach for many readers, a logical flow does underlie the sequencing of the material.
Preface xiii
In Part One, “Reading between the Lines,” we show that financial statements do not simply represent unbiased portraits of corporations’ financial performance and explain why. The section explores the complex motivations of issuing firms and their managers. We also study the distortions produced by the organizational context in which the analyst operates.

第二部分“基本财务报表”深入剖析了资产负债表、利润表和现金流量表中披露的信息。仔细审视后就会发现，“价值”和“收入”等术语远比抽象理解时显得更加模糊。就连通常被认为能带来清晰解读的现金流，也容易成为操纵投资者和债权人认知的工具。

<!--en-->
Part Two, “The Basic Financial Statements,” takes a hard look at the information disclosed in the balance sheet, income statement, and statement of cash flows. Under close scrutiny, terms such as *value* and *income* begin to look muddier than they appear when considered in the abstract. Even cash flow, a concept commonly thought to convey redemptive clarification, is vulnerable to stratagems designed to manipulate the perceptions of investors and creditors.

第三部分“深入剖析利润”聚焦于资本主义体系的命脉。

<!--en-->
In Part Three, “A Closer Look at Profits,” we zero in on the lifeblood of the capitalist system.

我们对利润的细致分析揭示了盈利数据被夸大甚至伪造的多种手段。读到此处，读者应已充分具备进行严谨、结构化财务报表分析所需的健康怀疑精神。

<!--en-->
Our scrutiny of profits highlights the manifold ways in which earnings are exaggerated or even fabricated. By this point in the book, the reader should be amply imbued with the healthy skepticism necessary for a sound, structured approach to financial statement analysis.

第四部分“预测与证券分析”的主题是应用。无论是信贷评估还是股票估值，前瞻性分析都比那些诱人却终究无法令人满意的回顾性分析更为重要。书中包含了提高预测准确性的技巧，并对现实中的预测案例进行了剖析。无论那些标准财务比率和估值模型多么广为接受，我们都会以批判的眼光加以审视。

<!--en-->
Application is the theme of Part Four, “Forecasts and Security Analysis.” For both credit and equity evaluation, forward-looking analysis is emphasized over seductive but ultimately unsatisfying retrospection. Tips for maximizing the accuracy of forecasts are included, and real-life projections are dissected. We cast a critical eye on standard financial ratios and valuation models, however widely accepted they may be.

金融市场虽在不断演变，但某些现象总会以新面目反复出现。企业总能想出新办法来扭曲外界对其业绩的认知。通过分析这些方法，分析师有望预见到未来可能出现的老调新弹。马丁·弗里德森 费尔南多·阿尔瓦雷斯

<!--en-->
Financial markets continue to evolve, but certain phenomena appear again and again in new guises. In this vein, companies never lose their resourcefulness in finding new ways to skew perceptions of their performance. By studying their methods closely, analysts can potentially anticipate the variations on old themes that will materialize in years to come.
MARTIN FRIDSON
FERNANDO ALVAREZ

第1章

<!--en-->
CHAPTER 1

## 财务报告的对抗性本质

<!--en-->
*The Adversarial Nature of Financial Reporting*

财务报表分析是多种职业中不可或缺的技能，包括投资管理、公司财务、商业贷款以及信贷发放。对于从事这些工作的人，或是需要依据财务数据做出个人投资决策的人来说，有两种截然不同的分析方法。

<!--en-->
Financial statement analysis is an essential skill in a variety of occupations, including investment management, corporate finance, commercial lending, and the extension of credit. For individuals engaged in such activities, or who analyze financial data in connection with their personal investment decisions, there are two distinct approaches to the task.

第一种方法是遵循既定流程，按照精确且僵化的定义填入标准的财务比率。满足财务分析领域许多职位的正式要求，或许只需如此简单的操作即可。然而，纯粹机械式地操作并不会带来太大的专业挑战；即便按部就班地完成所有标准分析步骤，也不一定能得出有用甚至无害的结果。不过，有些人可能会认为这些只是微不足道的缺点。

<!--en-->
The first is to follow a prescribed routine, filling in boxes with standard financial ratios, calculated according to precise and inflexible definitions. It may take little more effort or mental exertion than this to satisfy the formal requirements of many positions in the field of financial analysis. Operating in a purely mechanical manner, though, will not provide much of a professional challenge. Neither will a rote completion of all of the proper standard analytical steps ensure a useful, or even a nonharmful, result. Some individuals, however, will view such problems as only minor drawbacks.

本书面向的是选择第二种且更有价值的方法的分析师——他们不懈地追求对所分析实体准确的财务画像。坚韧不拔至关重要，因为财务报表往往掩盖的信息比揭示的还要多。

<!--en-->
This book is aimed at the analyst who will adopt the second and more rewarding alternative, the relentless pursuit of accurate financial profiles of the entities being analyzed. Tenacity is essential because financial statements often conceal more than they reveal.

对于采取这种主动方法的分析师而言，制作一份关于公司的标准电子表格只是手段而非目的。如果一份不合时宜的股票购买建议仅仅是因为软件中列出了长长的数字行作为支撑，投资者从中获得的满足感微乎其微。真正有价值的分析要在回答完所有常规问题之后才开始。事实上，优秀的分析师会通过提出清单之外的问题来创造额外价值。

<!--en-->
To the analyst who embraces this proactive approach, producing a standard spreadsheet on a company is a means rather than an end. Investors derive but little satisfaction from the knowledge that an untimely stock purchase recommendation was supported by the longest row of figures available in the software package. Genuinely valuable analysis begins *after* all the usual questions have been answered. Indeed, a superior analyst adds value by raising questions that are not even on the checklist.

有些读者可能不会立刻认同有必要超越那种将所有公司置于统一、客观尺度上的分析框架。当合理的评估依赖于标准财务比率之外的因素时，他们或许会对完全抛弃这一框架的想法感到抵触。**可比性**毕竟是**公认会计原则（GAAP）**的基石。因此，似乎可以推断：依照GAAP编制的财务报表必然能给出公平且有用的相对价值指示。透过现象看本质

<!--en-->
Some readers may not immediately concede the necessity of going beyond an analytical structure that puts all companies on a uniform, objective scale. They may recoil at the notion of discarding the structure altogether when a sound assessment depends on factors other than comparisons ofstandard financial ratios. **Comparability**, after all, is a cornerstone of **generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP)**. It might therefore seem to follow that financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP necessarily produce fair and useful indications of relative value.
READING BETWEEN THE LINES

此外，发布财务报表的公司似乎也有天然的动力来促进便捷、千篇一律的分析。

<!--en-->
The corporations that issue financial statements, moreover, would appear to have a natural interest in facilitating convenient, cookie-cutter analysis.

这些公司投入大量资金来传播有关其财务业绩的信息。它们聘请投资者关系经理，通过中期财务报告和新闻稿与现有及潜在股东沟通，并派遣高层管理人员定期与证券分析师会面。既然公司如此渴望让投资者了解其财务成果，它们理应也希望分析师能够轻松监测其进展。由此看来，它们应该会以透明、直接的方式报告结果……至少表面上是这样。

<!--en-->
These companies spend heavily to disseminate information about their financial performance. They employ investor-relations managers, they communicate with existing and potential shareholders via interim financial reports and press releases, and they dispatch senior management to periodic meetings with securities analysts. Given that companies are so eager to make their financial results known to investors, they should also want it to be easy for analysts to monitor their progress. It follows that they can be expected to report their results in a transparent and straightforward fashion . . . or so it would seem.

## 财务报告的目的

<!--en-->
*THE PURPOSE OF FINANCIAL REPORTING*

那些相信GAAP数字具有内在可靠性且认为企业管理者出于善意的分析师，其实误解了财务报告的本质。不过，这种概念性错误并非源于智力不足，而是反映了会计教科书中所秉持的那种理想化却脱离实际的财务报告目的观。就连霍华德·希利特（参见本章后面关于MicroStrategy的讨论）——一位对现行财务报告实践持尖锐批评态度的人，也对此持有一种高尚但脱离现实的观点：

<!--en-->
Analysts who believe in the inherent reliability of GAAP numbers and the good faith of corporate managers misunderstand the essential nature of financial reporting. Their conceptual error connotes no lack of intelligence, however. Rather, it mirrors the standard accounting textbook's idealistic but irrelevant notion of the purpose of financial reporting. Even Howard Schilit (see the MicroStrategy discussion, later in this chapter), an acerbic critic of financial reporting as it is actually practiced, presents a high-minded view of the matter:

*财务报告的首要目标是发布能够准确衡量公司盈利能力和财务状况的财务报表。¹* 但这种表述并未指明“谁”的首要目标是实现准确计量。希利特的话听起来很符合本章第一段所列的财务报表使用者的心声，但真正编制财务报表的并非他们。相反，报表编制者是营利性公司，通常以股份有限公司的形式存在。² 公司的存在是为了股东的利益，其目标并非向公众披露自身的财务状况，而是最大化股东的财富。

<!--en-->
*The primary goal in financial reporting is the dissemination of financial statements that accurately measure the profitability and financial condition of a company.¹*
Missing from this formulation is an indication of *whose* primary goal is accurate measurement. Schilit's words are music to the ears of the financial statements users listed in this chapter's first paragraph, but they are not the ones doing the financial reporting. Rather, the issuers are for-profit companies, generally organized as corporations.²
A corporation exists for the benefit of its shareholders. Its objective is not to educate the public about its financial condition, but to maximize its shareholders' wealth.

如果管理层能够通过“发布准确衡量公司盈利能力和财务状况的财务报表”来实现这一目标，那么原则上管理层应当这么做。但充其量，以透明、直接的方式报告财务结果也只是达到目的的一种手段而已。

<!--en-->
If it so happens that management can advance that objective through "dissemination of financial statements that accurately measure the profitability and financial condition of the company," then inprinciple, management should do so. At most, however, reporting financial results in a transparent and straightforward fashion is a means unto an end.

财务报告的对立本质 5

<!--en-->
The Adversarial Nature of Financial Reporting
5

管理层可能会认为，最大化股东财富的更直接方法是降低公司的*资本成本*。简而言之，公司借贷所需的利率越低，或者向新投资者出售股票的价格越高，股东的财富就越多。从这个角度看，最好的财务报表并非最能全面、公正反映公司状况的报表，而是能带来最高信用评级（见第13章）和市盈率**倍数**（见第14章）的报表。如果最高的评级和倍数源自对盈利能力和财务状况的*不准确计量*，那么基于其对股东的受托责任，管理层就有义务公布这类报表，而非会计教科书中推崇的那种理想化报表。

<!--en-->
Management may determine that a more direct method of maximizing shareholder wealth is to reduce the corporation's *cost of capital*. Simply stated, the lower the interest rate at which a corporation can borrow or the higher the price at which it can sell stock to new investors, the greater the wealth of its shareholders. From this standpoint, the best kind of financial statement is not one that represents the corporation's condition most fully and most fairly, but rather one that produces the highest possible credit rating (see Chapter 13) and price-earnings **multiple** (see Chapter 14). If the highest ratings and multiples result from statements that measure profitability and financial condition *inaccurately*, the logic of fiduciary duty to shareholders obliges management to publish that sort, rather than the type held up as a model in accounting textbooks.

最理想的结果是公司获得的资本成本低于其实际应支付的水平。这一看似荒谬的观点可以用以下从财务报表编制者角度提出的准则来概括：

<!--en-->
The best possible outcome is a cost of capital lower than the corporation deserves on its merits. This admittedly perverse argument can be summarized in the following maxim, presented from the perspective of issuers of financial statements:

*财务报告的目的是获取廉价资本。*细心的读者会立刻提出两点异议：首先，他们会说，通过呈现过于乐观的财务数据来获取低于公允水平的资本属于欺诈行为；其次，有些读者会认为，误导财务报表使用者并非可持续的长期策略。依赖被高估的历史利润来预测公司未来收益的股市投资者，最终会发现实际结果达不到预期。此后，他们会因财务报表中的向上偏差而调低对未来收益的预测，其结果就是股票估值不会高于真实报告所能达到的水平。由于意识到这种做法会适得其反，公司自然会停止夸大其财务业绩。按照这种逻辑，财务报表使用者可以完全信任这些数字，因为追求自身利益的公司会诚实地报告结果。

<!--en-->
*The purpose of financial reporting is to obtain cheap capital.*
Attentive readers will raise two immediate objections. First, they will say, it is fraudulent to obtain capital at less than a fair rate by presenting an unrealistically bright financial picture. Second, some readers will argue that misleading the users of financial statements is not a sustainable strategy over the long run. Stock market investors who rely on overstated historical profits to project a corporation's future earnings will find that results fail to meet their expectations. Thereafter, they will adjust for the upward bias in the financial statements by projecting lower earnings than the historical results would otherwise justify. The outcome will be a stock valuation no higher than accurate reporting would have produced. Recognizing that the practice would be self-defeating, corporations will logically refrain from overstating their financial performance. By this reasoning, the users of financial statements can take the numbers at face value, because corporations that act in their self-interest will report their results honestly.

但这些论点面临一个令人尴尬的事实：财务报表并不总能如实反映编制者的业绩。财务报表使用者往往看到的并非易于理解且准确的数据，而是虽符合GAAP规定却会给人造成盈利误导的数字。更糟糕的是，违反会计准则的情况频繁出现。就连分析师的第二道防线——独立审计师对报表符合GAAP要求的确认——也无法保证数据的可靠性。字里行间的真相

<!--en-->
The inconvenient fact that confounds these arguments is that financial statements do *not* invariably reflect their issuers' performance faithfully. In lieu of easily understandable and accurate data, users of financial statements often find numbers that conform to GAAP yet convey a misleading impression of profits. Worse yet, outright violations of the accounting rules come to light with distressing frequency. Not even the analyst's second line of defense, an affirmation by independent auditors that the statements have been prepared in accordance with GAAP, assures that the numbers are reliable.
READING BETWEEN THE LINES

近年来的几个例子表明，过度信任财务报表的使用者可能会受到多么严重的误导。

<!--en-->
A few examples from recent years indicate how severely an overly trusting user of financial statements can be misled.

## Interpublic屡次尝试……再尝试

<!--en-->
*Interpublic Tries Again...and Again*

宏盟集团于2002年8月13日宣布，该公司错误地将6850万美元的费用计入账目，因此将重新编制自1997年以来的财务报表。这家广告公司运营商称，重新编报的原因与麦肯·埃里克森全球广告部门各欧洲办事处之间的交易有关。有消息称，当不同办事处合作开展国际项目时，实际上会多次重复确认同一笔收入。在宣布重新编报的前一周，由于公司推迟发布季度财报以便审计委员会审查账目，其股价下跌了近25%。

<!--en-->
Interpublic Group of Companies announced on August 13, 2002, that it had improperly accounted for $68.5 million of expenses and would restate its financial results all the way back to 1997. The operator of advertising agencies said the restatement was related to transactions between European offices of the McCann-Erickson Worldwide Advertising unit. Sources indicated that when different offices collaborated on international projects, they effectively booked the same revenue more than once. In the week before the restatement announcement, when the company delayed the filing of its quarterly results to give its audit committee time to review the accounting, its stock sank by nearly 25 percent.

或许并非巧合的是，宏盟集团的巨额账目调整恰逢美国**证券交易委员会（SEC）**新认证要求的生效之日。根据新规，如果首席执行官和首席财务官签署虚假财务报表，可能会面临罚款或监禁。对于那些一直在财务报告中玩“数字游戏”的公司而言，这正是纠正错误的绝佳时机。

<!--en-->
Perhaps not coincidentally, Interpublic's massive revision coincided with the effective date of new **Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)** certification requirements. Under the new rules, a company's chief executive officer and chief financial officer could be subject to fines or prison sentences if they certified false financial statements. It was an opportune time for any company that had been playing games with its financial reporting to get straight.

2002年8月的重新编报并未彻底解决宏盟集团的问题。

<!--en-->
The August 2002 restatement did not clear things up once and for all at Interpublic.

10月，该公司将计划重新编报的金额几乎翻倍至1.2亿美元；到了11月，这一数字可能还会更高。此时，宏盟集团的股价较年初已下跌55%，标准普尔公司将其信用评级从BBB+下调至BBB，几位高管也被解雇。

<!--en-->
In October, the company nearly doubled the amount of the planned restatement to $120 million, and in November, it emerged that the number might go even higher. By that time, Interpublic's stock was down 55 percent from the start of the year, Standard & Poor's had downgraded its credit rating from BBB+ to BBB, and several top executives had been dismissed.

与许多后来需要修正财报的其他公司一样，宏盟集团也面临着盈利压力。广告支出大幅减少，导致该行业出现数十年来最糟糕的表现。此外，公司在整合大量收购业务方面也遇到困难。董事长约翰·J·杜纳急于转移外界注意力，他表示：“指责过去毫无意义，我关注的是现在和未来。”³ 不幸的是，未来带来了更多会计问题。杜纳发表声明几天后，公司便将预计重新编报金额上调至1.813亿美元，几乎是最初估计数的三倍。一周后，SEC又要求提供与导致重新编报的错误相关的信息。事实证明，账目错报并不限于麦肯·埃里克森欧洲办事处的收入重复计算问题。

<!--en-->
Like many other companies that have issued financial statements that subsequently needed revision, Interpublic was under earnings pressure. Advertising spending had fallen drastically, producing the worst industry results in decades. Additionally, the company was having difficulty assimilating a huge number of acquisitions. Chairman John J. Dooner was understandably eager to shift the focus from all that. "The finger-pointing is about the past," he said. "I'm focusing on the present and future."³
Unfortunately, the future brought more accounting problems. A few days after Dooner's statement, the company upped its estimated restatement to $181.3 million, nearly triple the original figure. Another blow arrived a week later as the SEC requested information related to the errors that gave rise to the restatement. It also turned out that the misreporting was not limited to double-counting of revenue by McCann-Erickson's European offices.

其他问题还包括对尚未实现的保险理赔款的估算、应收账款及在制品的冲销，以及宏盟集团其他子公司可追溯至1996年的负债少计问题。杜纳评论道：“我们经历的这一番重新编报终于完成了。”⁴ 他还表示，他决心确保此类会计问题引发的混乱绝不再发生。

<!--en-->
Other items included an estimate of not-yet-realized insurance proceeds,write-offs of accounts receivable and work in progress, and understated liabilities at other Interpublic subsidiaries dating back as far as 1996. Dooner commented, “The restatement that we have been living through is finally filed.”⁴ He also stated that he was resolved that the turmoil created by the accounting problems would never happen again.

财务报告的对立性 7

<!--en-->
The Adversarial Nature of Financial Reporting
7

时间快进到2005年9月。自会计问题首次浮现以来的第三位首席执行官、杜纳的继任者迈克尔·I·罗斯宣称，他的首要任务是彻底解决宏盟集团的财务报告问题。公司首次承认，单纯的疏忽未必能解释所有的账目错误。宏盟集团还指出，投资者不应再依赖此前对重新编报金额的估计，这些估计还涉及对公司数百次收购案的记录程序。这其实还是轻描淡写——宏盟集团最终宣布，2000年至2004年9月30日期间的重新编报金额将达到5.5亿美元，是此前估计数的三倍。

<!--en-->
Fast-forward to September 2005. Dooner's successor and the third CEO since the accounting problems first surfaced, Michael I. Roth, declared that his top priority was to put Interpublic's financial reporting problems behind it. For the first time, the company acknowledged that honest mistakes might not have accounted for all of the erroneous accounting. Furthermore, said Interpublic, investors should not rely on previous estimates of the restatements, which also involved procedures for tracking the company's hundreds of agency acquisitions. That proved to be something of an understatement. Interpublic ultimately announced a restatement of $550 million, three times the previous estimate, for the period 2000 through September 30, 2004.

2008年5月，该公司支付1200万美元以和解SEC的指控：公司将内部往来款项记为应收账款而非费用，从而虚报财务结果。

<!--en-->
In May 2008, the company paid $12 million to settle the SEC's accusation that it fraudulently misstated its results by booking intercompany charges as receivables instead of expenses.

## MicroStrategy改变主意

<!--en-->
*MicroStrategy Changes Its Mind*

2000年3月20日，MicroStrategy宣布将1999年的营收从原先报告的2.053亿美元调整为约1.5亿美元。该公司股价随即暴跌140美元，跌至每股86.75美元，导致首席执行官迈克尔·塞勒的账面财富缩水超过60亿美元。公司解释称，此次调整与软件公司大型复杂项目的收入确认有关。⁵ MicroStrategy及其审计师最初声称，公司之所以必须重新编报财报，是因为响应了SEC于1999年12月发布的关于软件收入确认规则的建议。在SEC对这一解释提出异议后，公司承认其最初的会计处理不符合美国注册会计师协会早在1997年发布的会计准则。

<!--en-->
On March 20, 2000, MicroStrategy announced that it would restate its 1999 revenue, originally reported as $205.3 million, to around $150 million. The company's shares promptly plummeted by $140 to $86.75 a share, slashing Chief Executive Officer Michael Saylor's paper wealth by over $6 billion. The company explained that the revision had to do with recognizing revenue on the software company's large, complex projects.⁵ MicroStrategy and its auditors initially suggested that the company had been obliged to restate its results in response to a recent (December 1999) SEC advisory on rules for booking software revenues. After the SEC objected to that explanation, the company conceded that its original accounting was inconsistent with accounting principles published way back in 1997 by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

在MicroStrategy抛出这一重磅消息之前，该公司的审计师一直对公司的收入确认政策予以认可。尽管六个月前会计专家霍华德·希利特以及记者大卫·雷蒙德已在2月21日发行的《福布斯ASAP》杂志上对MicroStrategy的财务状况提出质疑。⁶据报道，直到读了雷蒙德的文章后，审计机构总部的一名会计师才联系负责此次审计的地方办事处，最终导致该公司撤销对1998年和1999年财务报表的先前认证。⁷ 言外之意值得玩味。

<!--en-->
Until MicroStrategy dropped its bombshell, the company's auditors had put their seal of approval on the company's revenue recognition policies. That was despite questions raised about MicroStrategy's financials by accounting expert Howard Schilit six months earlier and by reporter David Raymond in an issue of *Forbes ASAP* distributed on February 21.⁶ It was reportedly only after reading Raymond's article that an accountant in the auditor's national office contacted the local office that had handled the audit, ultimately causing the firm to retract its previous certification of the 1998 and 1999 financials.⁷

## Lernout & Hauspie公司避而不谈真相

<!--en-->
*No Straight Talk from Lernout & Hauspie*

2000年11月16日，Lernout & Hauspie语音产品公司（L&H）的审计师撤回了对该公司1998年和1999年财务报表的无保留意见。此前，这家比利时的语音识别和翻译软件生产商已于11月9日宣布：内部调查发现了会计错误和违规行为，因此需要对这两年及2000年上半年的财务数据进行重述。两周后，该公司申请破产。

<!--en-->
On November 16, 2000, the auditor for Lernout & Hauspie Speech Products (L&H) withdrew its clean opinion of the company's 1998 and 1999 financials. The action followed a November 9 announcement by the Belgian producer of speech-recognition and translation software that an internal investigation had uncovered accounting errors and irregularities that would require restatement of results for those two years and the first half of 2000. Two weeks later, the company filed for bankruptcy.

在2000年11月16日之前，尽管投资者依赖审计师的意见，认为Lernout & Hauspie的财务报表符合公认会计原则，但已有多起事件令这种看法受到质疑。1999年7月，卖空者大卫·罗克批评了L&H与布鲁塞尔翻译集团（BTG）之间的交易。在两年的时间里，BTG向L&H支付了3500万美元用于开发翻译软件；随后L&H收购了BTG及其翻译产品。其实际效果是：L&H并未将这3500万美元记为研发开支，反而将其确认为营业收入。⁸ 2000年8月，一些被L&H列为客户的韩国公司称自己实际上并未与该企业发生业务往来。同年9月，美国证券交易委员会和欧洲的EASDAQ股市开始调查L&H的会计做法。⁹在此过程中，Lernout & Hauspie的股价从2000年3月的72.50美元高位跌至7美元，并于11月被暂停交易。回顾起来，盲目依赖基于审计意见且假定管理层希望帮助分析师了解真实情况的财务报表，确实是一项错误的决策。

<!--en-->
Prior to November 16, 2000, while investors were relying on the auditor's opinion that Lernout & Hauspie's financial statements were consistent with generally accepted accounting principles, several events cast doubt on that opinion. In July 1999, short seller David Rocker criticized transactions such as L&H's arrangement with Brussels Translation Group (BTG). Over a two-year period, BTG paid L&H $35 million to develop translation software. Then L&H bought BTG and the translation product along with it. The net effect was that instead of booking a $35 million research and development expense, L&H recognized $35 million of revenue.⁸ In August 2000, certain Korean companies that L&H claimed as customers said that they in fact did no business with the corporation. In September, the Securities and Exchange Commission and Europe's EASDAQ stock market began to investigate L&H's accounting practices.⁹ Along the way, Lernout & Hauspie's stock fell from a high of $72.50 in March 2000 to $7 before being suspended from trading in November. In retrospect, uncritical reliance on the company's financials, based on the auditor's opinion and a presumption that management wanted to help analysts get the true picture, was a bad policy.

## 推理中的漏洞

<!--en-->
*THE FLAWS IN THE REASONING*

正如前述偏离公认会计原则的情况所示，无论是对反欺诈法规的畏惧还是出于自身利益考虑，都未必能阻止企业操纵账目。认为这两种力量能确保会计诚实的逻辑建立在隐含的假设之上；而这些假设在审视财务报告所处的组织环境时均站不住脚。

<!--en-->
As the preceding deviations from GAAP demonstrate, neither fear of antifraud statutes nor enlightened self-interest invariably deters corporations from cooking the books. The reasoning by which these two forces ensure honest accounting rests on hidden assumptions. None of the assumptions can stand up to an examination of the organizational context in which financial reporting occurs.

首先，企业在违反公认会计原则之前就能将数字扭曲到相当程度，更不用说面临欺诈指控了。当重大的财务报告违规事件曝光时——如同大多数白领犯罪一样——真正的丑闻在于那些并未被明确禁止的行为。实际上，公认会计原则允许大量至少在短期内明显不准确的计量方式。

<!--en-->
To begin with, corporations can push the numbers fairly far out of joint before they run afoul of GAAP, much less open themselves to prosecution for fraud. When major financial reporting violations come to light, as in most other kinds of white-collar crime, the real scandal involves what is *not* forbidden. In practice, generally accepted accounting principles countenance a lot of measurement that is decidedly inaccurate, at least over the short run.

财务报告的对抗性本质 9

<!--en-->
The Adversarial Nature of Financial Reporting
9

例如，企业常常毫不掩饰地平滑其盈利数据。也就是说，它们制造出利润逐年稳定增长的假象。企业在审计师的默许下采取这种行为，是因为看似平稳的增长能给股票市场投资者带来更高的市盈率。

<!--en-->
For example, corporations routinely and unabashedly smooth their earnings. That is, they create the illusion that their profits rise at a consistent rate from year to year. Corporations engage in this behavior, with the blessing of their auditors, because the appearance of smooth growth receives a higher price-earnings multiple from stock market investors than the jagged reality underlying the numbers.

假设在某个季度的最后几周，盈利有望达不到预设的年度增幅目标，企业便会通过给予客户特别折扣来提前收取下个季度的订单，从而“借用”下个季度的销售额（及相应利润）。*高于趋势线的增长*对试图平滑盈利的企业而言同样是个问题：利润的突然跃升随后又回归普通的增长水平，会造成波动，而波动被视为必须不惜一切代价避免的“恶果”。管理层的解决办法是在当期增加开支，比如安排培训计划和工厂维护——尽管这些工作本可在后续季度进行，但确实有必要。

<!--en-->
Suppose that, in the last few weeks of a quarter, earnings threaten to fall short of the programmed year-over-year increase. The corporation simply borrows sales (and associated profits) from the next quarter by offering customers special discounts to place orders earlier than they had planned. *Higher-than-trendline* growth, too, is a problem for the earnings-smoother. A sudden jump in profits, followed by a return to a more ordinary rate of growth, produces volatility, which is regarded as an evil to be avoided at all costs. Management's solution is to run up expenses in the current period by scheduling training programs and plant maintenance that, while necessary, would ordinarily be undertaken in a later quarter.

这些并非只有那些不靠谱的公司才会采用的手段。蓝筹股企业也公开承认，鉴于华尔街对意外情况的厌恶，他们别无选择，只能平滑其盈利数据。通用电气的高管们表示，当某个业务部门有可能无法完成年度盈利目标时，在报告期尾声进行收购便成了惯例。该公司金融服务业务的一位高管称，他和他的同事们会在此时四处寻找收购对象，并说：“哎呀，别人那里有现成的收入吗？”

<!--en-->
These are not tactics employed exclusively by fly-by-night companies. Blue chip corporations openly acknowledge that they have little choice but to smooth their earnings, given Wall Street's allergy to surprises. Officials of General Electric have indicated that when a division is in danger of failing to meet its annual earnings goal, it is accepted procedure to make an acquisition in the waning days of the reporting period. According to an executive in the company's financial services business, he and his colleagues hunt for acquisitions at such times, saying, "Gee, does somebody else have some income?

“我们还能达成其他交易吗？”¹⁰ 这家新收购的子公司整个季度的利润可以并入通用电气的账目中，从而有助于确保投资者所看重的稳定增长。

<!--en-->
Is there some other deal we can make?"¹⁰ The freshly acquired unit's profits for the full quarter can be incorporated into GE's, helping to ensure the steady growth so prized by investors.

为什么审计师不禁止这类花招呢？它们似乎与财务报告的表面目的——即准确反映企业的盈利情况——并不相符。原因在于，健全的会计理论原则只是制定财务报告准则时所参考的诸多因素之一。

<!--en-->
Why do auditors not forbid such gimmicks? They hardly seem consistent with the ostensible purpose of financial reporting, namely, the accurate portrayal of a corporation's earnings. The explanation is that sound principles of accounting theory represent only one ingredient in the stew from which financial reporting standards emerge.

除了会计专业人士外，财务报表的编制者和使用者也在**财务会计准则委员会（FASB）**中拥有代表权。该委员会是在证券交易委员会授权下运作的规则制定机构。当FASB发现某个领域需要制定新准则时，其专业团队通常会在几个月内界定相关的理论问题。不过，新准则的颁布可能需要数年时间，因为财务报表的编制企业所追求的目标显然要更加务实、具体。

<!--en-->
Along with accounting professionals, the issuers and users of financial statements also have representation on the **Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB)**, the rule-making body that operates under authority delegated by the Securities and Exchange Commission. When FASB identifies an area in need of a new standard, its professional staff typically defines the theoretical issues in a matter of a few months. Issuance of the new standard may take several years, however, as the corporate issuers of financial statements pursue their objectives on a decidedly less abstract plane.

时不时地，诸如高管股票期权和并购等备受争议的问题，会引发FASB与企业界之间相当激烈的对抗。

<!--en-->
From time to time, highly charged issues, such as executive stock options and mergers, lead to fairly testy confrontations between FASB and thecorporate world.

从这些争执中产生的妥协方案无法令理论上的纯粹主义者满意。另一方面，通过协商制定的规则能够避免企业盟友在国会发起的全面攻击。一旦议员们被激怒，他们可能会大幅削弱FASB的职权。在极端情况下，他们甚至可能会用一个新规则制定机构来取代FASB，以便企业能更轻易地将其操控于股掌之间。 言外之意

<!--en-->
The compromises that emerge from these dustups fail to satisfy theoretical purists. On the other hand, rule making by negotiation heads off all-out assaults by the corporations' allies in Congress. If the lawmakers were ever to get sufficiently riled up, they might drastically curtail FASB's authority. Under extreme circumstances, they might even replace FASB with a new rule-making body that the corporations could more easily bend to their will.
READING BETWEEN THE LINES

还有一个原因导致开明的自身利益并不总能促使企业做出坦诚的财务报告。领导着反对FASB斗争的企业高管们有着自己的目的。就像购买本企业股票的投资者一样，管理者也试图最大化自身的财富。如果创造真实的经济利润有助于实现这一目标，那么首席执行官（CEO）努力去做便是理性的选择。不过在某些情况下，CEO可以通过利用财务报告上的花招来钻薪酬制度的空子，从而获得更大的个人收益。

<!--en-->
There is another reason that enlightened self-interest does not invariably drive corporations toward candid financial reporting. The corporate executives who lead the battles against FASB have their own agenda. Just like the investors who buy their corporations' stock, managers seek to maximize their wealth. If producing bona fide economic profits advances that objective, it is rational for a chief executive officer (CEO) to try to do so. In some cases, though, the CEO can achieve greater personal gain by taking advantage of the compensation system through financial reporting gimmicks.

例如，假设首席执行官的年终奖金取决于每股收益的增长情况。同时再假设，出于财务报告的需要，该公司的**折旧**计划将固定资产的平均使用年限设定为八年。

<!--en-->
Suppose, for example, the CEO's year-end bonus is based on growth in earnings per share. Assume also that for financial reporting purposes, the corporation's **depreciation** schedules assume an average life of eight years for fixed assets.

通过随意将该年限修改为九年（并获得审计师的认可），公司便能降低其年度折旧费用。这纯粹是一项会计上的变更；实际更换因使用而磨损的设备所需的成本并不会减少。公司的折旧费用税收抵扣额也不会增加，相应地，现金流¹¹（参见第4章）也不会改变。投资者意识到真实的利润（参见第5章）并未增加，因此公司股价不会因这项新会计政策而发生变化。真正有所增加的是首席执行官的奖金——这一奖金是根据人为抬高后的每股收益来计算的。

<!--en-->
By arbitrarily amending that assumption to nine years (and obtaining the auditors' consent to the change), the corporation can lower its annual depreciation expense. This is strictly an accounting change; the actual cost of replacing equipment worn down through use does not decline. Neither does the corporation's tax deduction for depreciation expense rise nor, as a consequence, does cash flow¹¹ (see Chapter 4). Investors recognize that bona fide profits (see Chapter 5) have not increased, so the corporation's stock price does not change in response to the new accounting policy. What *does* increase is the CEO's bonus, as a function of the artificially contrived boost in earnings per share.

这个例子解释了为何企业会改变其会计做法，从而导致投资者更难以追踪其经营状况；尽管从股东的长远利益来看，简明透明的财务报告才是最佳选择。根本问题在于，企业高管有时会将自身利益置于股东福祉之上。他们通过虚增利润来抬高自己的奖金，而股东却要为反映**报告盈利质量恶化**的市盈率下降承担代价。¹² 对企业而言，合乎逻辑的解决方案似乎是使管理层与股东的利益保持一致。

<!--en-->
This example explains why a corporation may alter its accounting practices, making it harder for investors to track its performance, even though the shareholders' enlightened self-interest favors straightforward, transparent financial reporting. The underlying problem is that corporate executives sometimes put their own interests ahead of their shareholders' welfare. They beef up their bonuses by overstating profits, while shareholders bear the cost of reductions in price-earnings ratios to reflect deterioration in the quality of **reported earnings**.¹²
The logical solution for corporations, it would seem, is to align the interests of management and shareholders.

董事会不应再根据每股收益来计算高管奖金，而应根据股价上涨所带来的股东财富增值来奖励高层管理人员。这种安排能防止首席执行官通过那些无法真正增加利润、因而也无法推高股价的手段来虚报盈利。

<!--en-->
Instead of calculating executive bonuses on the basis of earnings per share, the board should reward senior management for increasing shareholders' wealth by causing the stock price to rise. Such an arrangement gives the CEO no incentive to inflate reportedearnings through gimmicks that transparently produce no increase in bona fide profits and therefore no rise in the share price.

财务报告的对立性 11

<!--en-->
The Adversarial Nature of Financial Reporting
11

按照逻辑推断，随着企业越来越多地将高管薪酬与股价升值挂钩，财务报告理应更接近于准确反映企业绩效的理想状态。然而现实中却看不到这种趋势。事实上，Interpublic、MicroStrategy和Lernout & Hauspie的例子表明，企业在财务报告方面变得越来越富有创造力且更加激进。

<!--en-->
Following the logic through, financial reporting ought to have moved closer to the ideal of accurate representation of corporate performance as companies have increasingly linked executive compensation to stock price appreciation. In reality, though, no such trend is discernible. If anything, the preceding examples of Interpublic, MicroStrategy, and Lernout & Hauspie suggest that corporations have become more creative and more aggressive over time in their financial reporting.

事实证明，协调管理层与股东利益的做法也有其阴暗面。企业高管再也无法通过投资者容易察觉的财务造假手段来增加奖金；他们必须想出更为隐蔽的手法来欺骗市场并人为抬高股价。

<!--en-->
Aligning management and shareholder interests, it turns out, has a dark side. Corporate executives can no longer increase their bonuses through financial reporting tricks that are readily detectable by investors. Instead, they must devise better-hidden gambits that fool the market and artificially elevate the stock price.

财务报表分析师必须比以往更加努力地识别企业的种种伎俩。

<!--en-->
Financial statement analysts must work harder than ever to spot corporations' subterfuges.

## 微薄的利润与巨额冲销

<!--en-->
*SMALL PROFITS AND BIG BATHS*

当然，财务报表分析师并非孤军奋战。美国证券交易委员会和财务会计准则委员会禁止企业为了抬高股价而过度美化利润。不过，这些监管机构并未明确界定“过度”的界限。企业对是否披露可能损害其市场估值的负面信息持不同看法；对某些企业而言，披露标准似乎是：只要没人询问某特定事件，不主动提供相关信息就不算撒谎。

<!--en-->
Certainly, financial statement analysts do not have to fight the battle singlehandedly. The Securities and Exchange Commission and the Financial Accounting Standards Board prohibit corporations from going too far in pretifying their profits to pump up their share prices. These regulators refrain from indicating exactly how far is too far, however. Inevitably, corporations hold diverse opinions on matters such as the extent to which they must divulge bad news that might harm their stock market valuations. For some, the standard of disclosure appears to be that if nobody happens to ask about a specific event, then declining to volunteer the information does not constitute a lie.

并非所有情况都如此悲观，但这种悲观现象确实相当普遍。由哈佛经济学家理查德·泽克豪泽领导的研究团队收集的证据显示，缺乏完全坦诚的现象十分普遍。¹³研究人员重点关注那些季度盈利仅略高于或略低于上年同期水平的企业。

<!--en-->
The picture is not quite that bleak in every case, but the bleakness extends pretty far. A research team led by Harvard economist Richard Zeckhauser has compiled evidence that lack of perfect candor is widespread.¹³ The researchers focus on instances in which a corporation reports quarterly earnings that are only slightly higher or slightly lower than its earnings in the corresponding quarter of the preceding year.

假设企业财务报告遵循会计师所设定的理想目标——即准确反映经营绩效。

<!--en-->
Suppose that corporate financial reporting followed the accountants' idealized objective of depicting performance accurately.

根据概率法则，企业季度报告中盈利略高于上年同期的情况应与盈利略低于上年同期的情况数量相近。然而泽克豪泽及其同事发现，企业出现小幅盈利增长的情况远比小幅盈利下降的情况要多得多。这强烈暗示：当企业面临盈利略低于上年的风险时，它们会找到足够的可操纵项目来勉强得出略为改善的业绩结果。言外之意不言而喻。

<!--en-->
By the laws of probability, corporations' quarterly reports would include about as many cases of earnings that barely exceed year-earlier results as cases of earnings that fall just shy of year-earlier profits. Instead, Zeckhauser and colleagues find that corporations post small increases far more frequently than they post small declines. The strong implication is that when companies are indanger of showing slightly negative earnings comparisons, they locate enough discretionary items to squeeze out marginally improved results.
READING BETWEEN THE LINES

另一方面，如果企业季度盈利的下滑幅度过大，以至于无法通过可操纵项目来弥补，那么企业便有动机通过最大化报告的亏损来进行“巨额冲销”。其逻辑是：投资者对30%的盈利降幅并不会比20%的降幅更为担忧。因此，管理层可能会选择将某些未来费用提前计入本季度，从而确保下一期报表中显示出盈利。此时也是确认诸如过时生产设施以及过去收购中产生的商誉等资产长期价值损失的合适时机。

<!--en-->
On the other hand, suppose a corporation suffers a quarterly profit decline too large to erase through discretionary items. Such circumstances create an incentive to take a big bath by maximizing the reported setback. The reasoning is that investors will not be much more disturbed by a 30 percent drop in earnings than by a 20 percent drop. Therefore, management may find it expedient to **accelerate** certain future expenses into the current quarter, thereby ensuring positive reported earnings in the following period. It may also be a convenient time to recognize long-run losses in the value of assets such as outmoded production facilities and **goodwill** created in unsuccessful acquisitions of the past.

实际上，企业对这类资产的冲销金额可能会超出准确反映原则所要求的范围。而超额冲销的逆转则成为在后续期间稳定报告盈利的人为手段。

<!--en-->
In fact, the corporation may take a larger write-off on those assets than the principle of accurate representation would dictate. Reversals of the excess write-offs offer an artificial means of stabilizing reported earnings in subsequent periods.

泽克豪泽及其同事通过研究表明，利润大幅下滑的情况比大幅增长更为常见，从而证实了“大洗澡”假说。这意味着管理者并非被动地记录自身能力与不可控商业因素共同作用的结果，而是利用会计准则中的弹性空间来干预利润计算。研究人员的总体印象是：企业把财务报告视为抬高股价的工具，而非传播客观信息的手段。¹⁴ 如果企业的这些伎俩能逃过投资者和债权人的察觉，所能获得的回报将是巨大的。例如，对于10亿美元的借款而言，利率每降低0.5个百分点，每年就能节省500万美元（税前）的成本。若该企业适用34%的税率，且股价为其盈利的15倍，那么通过隐瞒风险的财务报表所能换来的股票累计价值将高达4950万美元。

<!--en-->
Zeckhauser and his associates corroborate the big bath hypothesis by showing that large earnings declines are more common than large increases. By implication, managers do not passively record the combined results of their own skill and business factors beyond their control, but intervene in the calculation of earnings by exploiting the latitude in accounting rules. The researchers' overall impression is that corporations regard financial reporting as a technique for propping up stock prices, rather than a means of disseminating objective information.¹⁴
If corporations' gambits escape detection by investors and lenders, the rewards can be vast. For example, an interest-cost savings of half a percentage point on $1 billion of borrowings equates to $5 million (pretax) per year. If the corporation is in a 34 percent tax bracket and its stock trades at 15 times earnings, the payoff for risk-concealing financial statements is $49.5 million in the cumulative value of its shares.

除了泽克豪泽研究的“大洗澡”手法外，常见的用于谋取财富增值机会的方法还包括：

<!--en-->
Among the popular methods for pursuing such opportunities for wealth enhancement, aside from the big bath technique studied by Zeckhauser, are:

- 最大化增长预期。
- 淡化不确定性因素。

<!--en-->
- Maximizing growth expectations.
- Downplaying contingencies.

### 最大化增长预期

<!--en-->
*MAXIMIZING GROWTH EXPECTATIONS*

假设某家企业目前年度净利润为2000万美元。再假设五年后其增长势头有所放缓时，该企业的估值将达到盈利的15倍。同时假定未来五年内该公司不发放股息，且成长型股票的投资者目前要求的回报率为25%（未计资本利得税）。

<!--en-->
Imagine a corporation that is currently reporting annual net earnings of $20 million. Assume that five years from now, when its growth has leveled off somewhat, the corporation will be valued at 15 times earnings. Further assume that the company will pay no dividends over the next five years andthat investors in growth stocks currently seek returns of 25 percent (before considering capital gains taxes).

财务报告的对抗性本质 13

<!--en-->
The Adversarial Nature of Financial Reporting
13

基于上述假设以及一个额外数值，分析师便可算出该企业流通股的总价值。最后一个必需的输入参数是预期的盈利增长率。假设该企业的盈利年增长率一直保持在30%，且未来五年仍有望维持这一水平。五年后，盈利额（取整）将达到7400万美元。以此乘以15倍的倍数，便得出第五年末的企业估值为11.14亿美元。追求25%回报率的投资人今天将支付3.65亿美元来获取这一未来价值。

<!--en-->
Based on these assumptions, plus one additional number, the analyst can place an aggregate value on the corporation's outstanding shares. The final required input is the expected growth rate of earnings. Suppose the corporation's earnings have been growing at a 30 percent annual rate and appear likely to continue increasing at the same rate over the next five years. At the end of that period, earnings (rounded) will be $74 million annually. Applying a multiple of 15 times to that figure produces a valuation at the end of the fifth year of $1.114 billion. Investors seeking a 25 percent rate of return will pay $365 million today for that future value.

对于拥有20%流通股的创始人或首席执行官而言，这些数字无疑令人欣喜。

<!--en-->
These figures are likely to be pleasing to a founder or chief executive officer who owns, for the sake of illustration, 20 percent of the outstanding shares.

这位成功的企业家在账面上的身价达到了7300万美元，而几年前他可能还是一文不名。与此同时，这位新晋的百万富翁也成了市场预期的俘虏。

<!--en-->
The successful entrepreneur is worth $73 million on paper, quite possibly up from zero just a few years ago. At the same time, the newly minted multimillionaire is a captive of the market's expectations.

假设出于某种原因，投资者认定该企业盈利增长潜力从每年30%降至25%。尽管这一数字仍远高于美国企业的平均水平，但在原有假设不变的情况下，该企业股票的价值仍将从3.65亿美元跌至3亿美元。

<!--en-->
Suppose investors conclude for some reason that the corporation's potential for increasing its earnings has declined from 30 to 25 percent per annum. That is still well above average for corporate America. Nevertheless, the value of the corporation's shares will decline from $365 million to $300 million, keeping previous assumptions intact.

一夜之间，这位长期奋斗的创始人会发现其个人持股价值骤减1300万美元。金融分析师或许不会为他感到惋惜——毕竟他账面上的身价仍有6000万美元。但倘若换作是他们，又有多少人能心平气和地接受1300万美元的损失呢？大多数人至少会试图利用公认会计原则（GAAP）所允许的一切手段，来避免遭受同等程度的财务损失。

<!--en-->
Overnight, the long-struggling founder will see the value of his personal stake plummet by $13 million. Financial analysts may shed few tears for him. After all, he is still worth $60 million on paper. If they were in his shoes, however, how many would accept a $13 million loss with perfect equanimity? Most would be sorely tempted, at the least, to avoid incurring a financial reverse of comparable magnitude via every means available to them under GAAP.

这种人之常情正是所有者兼管理者在面对增长预期下滑时通常表现出的反应。许多人——或许大多数——并无意欺骗。只是企业家天生就是自信的乐观主义者。

<!--en-->
That all-too-human response is the one typically exhibited by owner-managers confronted with falling growth expectations. Many, perhaps most, have no intention to deceive. It is simply that the entrepreneur is by nature a self-assured optimist.

此外，这位成功的企业家此前已证明了自己的乐观是有道理的。他历经重重困难，将公司从零做到2000万美元的盈利规模，因此他相信自己能够解决出现的任何短期问题。他坚信自己能让企业重回30%的增长轨道，也许他确实如此。有一点是肯定的：如果他不是那种相信自己能再次创造奇迹的人，他绝不可能建立起一家价值3亿美元的公司。

<!--en-->
A successful entrepreneur, moreover, has had this optimism vindicated. Having taken his company from nothing to $20 million of earnings against overwhelming odds, he believes he can lick whatever short-term problems have arisen. He is confident that he can get the business back onto a 30 percent growth curve, and perhaps he is right. One thing is certain: If he were not the sort who believed he could beat the odds one more time, he would never have built a company worth $300 million.

金融分析师需要更客观地评估事实。他们必须认识到，企业的这种困境并非独一无二，恰恰相反，它十分普遍。几乎无一例外，高层管理者都会试图消除人们对其增长放缓的印象，因为这种认知所带来的代价实在太高。字里行间的玄机

<!--en-->
Financial analysts need to assess the facts more objectively. They must recognize that the corporation's predicament is not unique, but on the contrary, quite common. Almost invariably, senior managers try to dispel the impression of decelerating growth, since that perception can be so costly
READING BETWEEN THE LINES

***图表 1.1** 增长放缓的必然性* *注：* 通过缩小企业实际增长与管理层预测增长之间的差距来提升投资者的预期，对企业而言是一项潜在有价值但难度极大的任务。

<!--en-->
***EXHIBIT 1.1** The Inevitability of Deceleration*
*Note:* Shifting investors' perceptions upward through the Corporate Credibility Gap between actual and management-projected growth is a potentially valuable but inherently difficult undertaking for a company.

宽松的财务报告做法或许能略微减轻这一任务的难度。有鉴于此，分析师在解读财务报表时应持怀疑态度。然而，简单的数学规律往往会让那些将高增长率无限期外推的企业沦为“伪预言家”。此外，一旦增长开始趋于平缓（参见图表 1.1），要将其恢复到历史水平就需要克服诸多强大的限制因素。

<!--en-->
Liberal financial reporting practices can make the task somewhat easier. In this light, analysts should read financial statements with a skeptical eye.
to them. Simple mathematics, however, tends to make false prophets of corporations that extrapolate high growth rates indefinitely into the future. Moreover, once growth begins to level off (see Exhibit 1.1), restoring it to the historical rate requires overcoming several powerful limitations.

### 持续增长的限制

<!--en-->
*Limits to Continued Growth*

**市场饱和**：一款热门的新消费品在一段时间内可能以惊人的速度销售。但最终，所有有需求的消费者都会拥有一件（或两件，或是他们认为足够的某个有限数量）。此时，潜在销量将仅限于替换性销售以及人口增长所带来的新增购买者数量。

<!--en-->
**Saturation** Sales of a hot new consumer product can grow at astronomical rates for a time. Eventually, however, everybody who cares to will own one (or two, or some other finite number that the consumer believes is enough). At that point, potential sales will be limited to replacement sales plus growth in population, that is, the increase in the number of potential purchasers.

**竞争对手的进入**：很少有企业的产品或服务无法被复制，或被足以满足相同需求但又因不属于专利和商标保护范围而可规避法律限制的仿制品所侵蚀。

<!--en-->
**Entry of Competition** Rare is the company with a product or service that cannot either be copied or encroached on by a knockoff sufficiently similarto tap the same demand, yet different enough to fall outside the bounds of patent and trademark protection.

财务报告的对抗性特征：**基数效应**：一家第一年售出1000万件产品的企业，第二年只需再多卖400万件就能实现40%的增长。然而，如果按此速度继续增长，到第10年该企业需额外售出5900万件产品才能达到40%的增长率。

<!--en-->
The Adversarial Nature of Financial Reporting
**Increasing Base** A corporation that sells 10 million units in Year 1 can register a 40 percent increase by selling just 4 million additional units in Year 2. If growth continues at the same rate, however, the corporation will have to generate 59 million new unit sales to achieve a 40 percent gain in Year 10.

从绝对数值上看，销量确实可以无限增加。但增长率若远超**国内生产总值**的年增长率，则几乎不可能长期维持下去。

<!--en-->
In absolute terms, it is arithmetically possible for volume to increase indefinitely. On the other hand, a growth rate far in excess of the **gross domestic product's** annual increase is nearly impossible to sustain over any extended period.

根据定义，增速高于GDP的产品每年所占的GDP份额会越来越大。随着数值不断增大，要改变消费者的消费模式以维持该产品的持续高速增长就愈发困难。

<!--en-->
By definition, a product that experiences higher-than-GDP growth captures a larger percentage of GDP each year. As the numbers get larger, it becomes increasingly difficult to switch consumers' spending patterns to accommodate continued high growth of a particular product.

**市场份额限制**：一段时间内，企业可以通过抢占竞争对手的市场份额来突破自身及整个经济的增长极限。即便这种增长源于市场份额的提升而非产品总体需求的增加，企业最终也会遇到恒定增长率下的增长天花板。例如，假设某生产商目前占据10%的市场份额，年增长率为25%，而该产品的总需求年增长率仅为5%。到第14年，为维持这一增速，该企业需占据115%的市场份额。（早在面临这种数学上的不可能之前，反垄断机构很可能就会限制其增长。）

<!--en-->
**Market Share Constraints** For a time, a corporation may overcome the limits of growth in its market and the economy as a whole by expanding its sales at the expense of competitors. Even when growth is achieved by market share gains rather than by expanding the overall demand for a product, however, the firm must eventually bump up against a ceiling on further growth at a constant rate. For example, suppose a producer with a 10 percent share of market is currently growing at 25 percent a year while total demand for the product is expanding at only 5 percent annually. By Year 14, this supergrowth company will require a 115 percent market share to maintain its rate of increase. (Long before confronting this mathematical impossibility, the corporation's growth will probably be curtailed by the antitrust authorities.)

基本经济学原理和复利表表明，所有增长故事终将结束，这一残酷现实最终必然会在股价中体现出来。

<!--en-->
Basic economics and compound-interest tables, then, assure the analyst that all growth stories come to an end, a cruel fate that must eventually be reflected in stock prices.

然而，财务报告常常讲述截然不同的故事。尽管这有悖常理，但考虑到其中的利害关系，这样的说法几乎不可避免。财务报表使用者应了解企业最常使用的“杰克与魔豆”式说辞——即盈利确实能像传说中那样直冲云霄。

<!--en-->
Financial reports, however, frequently tell a different tale. It defies common sense yet almost has to be told, given the stakes. Users of financial statements should acquaint themselves with the most frequently heard corporate versions of “Jack and the Beanstalk,” in which earnings—in contradiction to a popular saw—do grow to the sky.

### 关于增长放缓的常见借口

<!--en-->
*Commonly Heard Rationalizations for Declining Growth*

**“我们的同比数据存在偏差”**：由于投资者对增长放缓极为敏感，面临盈利减速的企业通常会采用某些惯用说辞，试图说服投资者：真正的、潜在的利润趋势仍按历史速率上升（参见图表 1.2）。异常天气状况可能被用来解释偏离趋势线的反常低盈利现象；或者企业会声称发货延迟（绝非取消，只是延迟）是由于临时性生产问题所致，而讽刺的是，这些问题恰恰由企业自身的爆发式增长引起。

<!--en-->
**“Our Year-over-Year Comparisons Were Distorted”** Recognizing the sensitivity of investors to any slowdown in growth, companies faced with earnings deceleration commonly resort to certain standard arguments to persuade investors that the true, underlying profit trend is still rising at its
READING BETWEEN THE LINES

<!--en-->
