***图表 1.2** “我们的同比数据存在偏差”* *注：* 最新的盈利数据是异常值，还是增长放缓的开端？除非时间推移，否则无人能确定答案，但企业很可能会竭力宣扬前者。

<!--en-->
***EXHIBIT 1.2** “Our Year-over-Year Comparisons Were Distorted”*
*Note:* Is the latest earnings figure an outlier or does it signal the start of a slowdown in growth? Nobody will know for certain until more time has elapsed, but the company will probably propound the former hypothesis as forcefully as it can.
historical rate (see Exhibit 1.2). Freak weather conditions may be blamed for supposedly anomalous, below-trendline earnings. Alternatively, the company may allege that shipments were delayed (never canceled, merely delayed) because of temporary production problems caused, ironically, by the company’s explosive growth.

（看似对股价不利的因素，实际上却是个利好。订单涌入的速度超过了公司的供货能力——这确实算得上是一种“甜蜜的烦恼”。）像千年虫问题¹⁵这类广为人知的宏观经济事件，往往被过分指责为盈利下滑的罪魁祸首。无论这些解释听起来多么可信，分析师们都应记住：在过去许多案例中，那些看似短暂的异常现象，其实正是盈利放缓的前兆。**“新产品将让增长重回正轨”** 有时，企业声称其显然已**成熟**的产品线能恢复以往的增长势头，这种说法便站不住脚。此时，管理层若能拿出一两种新产品来展示，倒也不失为良策。即便这些产品仍在研发中，那些迫切希望相信企业的投资者仍会坚信盈利会继续以历史水平增长。（这种期望或许源于他们以远高于当前市价的成本融资买入股票。）不过，精明的分析师会持观望态度，毕竟新产品的失败率相当高。

<!--en-->
(What appeared to be a negative for the stock price, in other words, was actually a positive. Orders were coming in faster than the company could fill them—a high-class problem indeed.) Widely publicized macroeconomic events such as the Y2K problem¹⁵ receive more than their fair share of blame for earnings shortfalls. However plausible these explanations may sound, analysts should remember that in many past instances, short-term supposed aberrations have turned out to be advance signals of earnings slowdowns.
**“New Products Will Get Growth Back on Track”** Sometimes, a corporation’s claim that its obviously **mature** product lines will resume their former growth path becomes untenable. In such instances, it is a good idea formanagement to have a new product or two to show off. Even if the products are still in development, some investors who strongly wish to believe in the corporation will remain steadfast in their faith that earnings will continue growing at the historical rate. (Such hopes probably rise as a function of owning stock on margin at a cost well above the current market.) A hard-headed analyst, though, will wait to be convinced, bearing in mind that new products have a high failure rate.

财务报告的对抗性本质 17

<!--en-->
The Adversarial Nature of Financial Reporting
17

**“我们正在从成熟市场向其他领域多元化发展”** 如果一家追求增长的企业所处行业整体步入放缓期，它或许别无选择，只能将盈利重新投入到增长更快的业务中。对增长的渴望以及实现周期性平衡的需求，正是企业采取多元化战略的主要动机。

<!--en-->
**"We're Diversifying Away from Mature Markets"** If a growth-minded company's entire industry has reached a point of slowdown, it may have little choice but to redeploy its earnings into faster-growing businesses. Hunger for growth, along with the quest for cyclical balance, is a prime motivation for the corporate strategy of diversification.

多元化战略在20世纪60年代的企业集团浪潮中达到鼎盛。在此之前，关于通过收购各类高增长行业中的公司来实现高盈利增长的实际可行性，相关证据还相对较少。后来许多企业发现，它们的多元化策略在纸上谈兵时效果尚可，实践中却不尽如人意。其中一个问题是：它们不得不为那些同样受其他企业集团青睐的成长型公司支付极高的市盈率倍数。除非在新企业架构下盈利增长能大幅提速，否则收购方的投资回报注定平庸。对于那些对所收购业务并无专业知识的管理者而言，这一制约尤为明显。

<!--en-->
Diversification reached its zenith of popularity during the conglomerate movement of the 1960s. Up until that time, relatively little evidence had accumulated regarding the actual feasibility of achieving high earnings growth through acquisitions of companies in a wide variety of growth industries. Many corporations subsequently found that their diversification strategies worked better on paper than in practice. One problem was that they had to pay extremely high price-earnings multiples for growth companies that other conglomerates also coveted. Unless earnings growth accelerated dramatically under the new corporate ownership, the acquirer's return on investment was fated to be mediocre. This constraint was particularly problematic for managers who had no particular expertise in the businesses they were acquiring.

更糟糕的是，有些企业为收购某个热门行业中的二流企业而支付了巨额溢价。遗憾的是，可供收购的行业领军企业数量本来就很有限。

<!--en-->
Still worse was the predicament of a corporation that paid a big premium for an also-ran in a hot industry. Regrettably, the number of industry leaders available for acquisition was by definition limited.

到了20世纪80年代，股市已经给出了定论：业务多元化的公司其市盈率会面临“企业集团折价”。一个实际问题是，证券分析师很难跟踪那些横跨多个行业的公司。这些企业集团并未如承诺的那样实现“1+1>2”的效果，反而导致其整体估值低于各子公司单独上市时的总和。

<!--en-->
By the 1980s, the stock market had rendered its verdict. The price-earnings multiples of widely diversified corporations carried a conglomerate discount. One practical problem was the difficulty security analysts encountered in trying to keep tabs on companies straddling many different industries. Instead of making 2 plus 2 equal 5, as they had promised, the conglomerates' managers presided over corporate empires that traded at cheaper prices than their constituent companies would have sold for in aggregate had they been listed separately.

尽管有此类前车之鉴，人们仍不时试图重振多元化战略，以期在未来无限期维持高盈利增长。其中一种变体是：管理层大肆吹嘘将一个部门的服务交叉销售给另一部门客户的可能性。但令人费解的是，为何要支付高额收购价将两家企业合并，反而比让一家独立公司付费使用另一家的邮寄名单更划算呢？

<!--en-->
Despite this experience, there are periodic attempts to revive the notion of diversification as a means of maintaining high earnings growth indefinitely into the future. In one variant, management makes lofty claims about the potential for cross-selling one division's services to the customers of another. It is not clear, though, why paying premium acquisition prices to assemble the two businesses under the same corporate roof should prove more profitable than having one independent company pay a fee to usethe other's mailing list.

经验丰富的分析师不禁怀疑：这类企业战略究竟有多少依赖于真正的**协同效应**，又有多少只是借助并购会计手段的漏洞罢了（参见第10章）。字里行间的玄机

<!--en-->
Battle-hardened analysts wonder whether such corporate strategies rely as much on the vagaries of mergers-and-acquisitions accounting (see Chapter 10) as they do on bona fide **synergy**.
READING BETWEEN THE LINES

总而言之，财务报表使用者应对所谓“通过多元化实现增长复苏”的说法持审慎态度。这往往不过是“永远高于平均水平增长”神话的另一种版本而已。多行业经营的企业同样会受到限制盈利增长的数学规律制约。

<!--en-->
All in all, users of financial statements should adopt a show-me attitude toward a story of renewed growth through diversification. It is often nothing more than a variant of the myth of above-average growth forever. Multi-industry corporations bump up against the same arithmetic that limits earnings growth for focused companies.

### 轻描淡写地对待或有负债

<!--en-->
*DOWNPLAYING CONTINGENCIES*

第二种迎合发行方利益的披露方式，便是轻描淡写地处理那些极其重要的或有负债。由于**集体诉讼**的出现，即便是市值数十亿美元的企业，其全部净资产也可能因环境危害或产品责任相关的诉讼而面临风险。不难理解，财务报表的发布者自然希望证券分析师能将注意力转移 elsewhere。

<!--en-->
A second way to mold disclosure to suit the issuer's interests is by downplaying extremely significant contingent liabilities. Thanks to the advent of **class action** suits, the entire net worth of even a multibillion-dollar corporation may be at risk in litigation involving environmental hazards or product liability. Understandably, an issuer of financial statements would prefer that securities analysts focus their attention elsewhere.

过去，分析师往往倾向于忽视那些看似会将大型企业逼入破产境地的指控。他们注意到，大规模诉讼最终往往只以原索赔额的一小部分达成和解。此外，诉讼结果常常取决于案件进入审判阶段后才浮现的事实（而如果诉讼在庭外和解，则根本不会进入审判程序）。考虑到陪审团易受情感诉求影响的特点，昔日的证券分析师很难将法律风险纳入主要基于**微观经济**和**宏观经济**变量的盈利预测中。充其量，那种可能吞噬企业全部股权的突发事件，只会成为确定公司盈利估值倍数时的一个定性因素。

<!--en-->
At one time, analysts tended to shunt aside claims that ostensibly threatened major corporations with bankruptcy. They observed that massive lawsuits were often settled for small fractions of the original claims. Furthermore, the outcome of a lawsuit often hinged on facts that emerged only when the case finally came to trial (which by definition never happened if the suit was settled out of court). Considering also the susceptibility of juries to emotional appeals, securities analysts of bygone days found it extremely difficult to incorporate legal risks into earnings forecasts that relied primarily on **microeconomic** and **macroeconomic** variables. At most, a contingency that had the potential of wiping out a corporation's equity became a qualitative factor in determining the multiple assigned to a company's earnings.

曼维尔公司1982年的破产标志着分析师看待法律突发事件的方式发生了转折。值得称赞的是，建筑产品行业的专家在该公司申请破产前很久，就一直在详细询问其面临的石棉相关人身伤害诉讼风险。然而，许多投资者似乎仍将该公司于1982年8月26日根据《破产法》**第11章**提出的申请视为突如其来的灾难。曼维尔公司的股价在申请次日便暴跌了35%。

<!--en-->
Manville Corporation's 1982 bankruptcy marked a watershed in the way analysts have viewed legal contingencies. To their credit, specialists in the building products sector had been asking detailed questions about Manville's exposure to asbestos-related personal injury suits for a long time before the company filed. Many investors nevertheless seemed to regard the corporation's August 26, 1982, filing under **Chapter 11** of the Bankruptcy Code as a sudden calamity. Manville's stock plunged by 35 percent on the day following its filing.

这种意外性部分源于信息披露问题。该公司在破产前向美国证券交易委员会提交的最后一份季度报告曾暗示，解决石棉相关索赔的总成本约为3.5亿美元，这一数字还不到曼维尔公司8.3亿美元股东权益的一半。相比之下，8月26日曼维尔公司估计潜在的赔偿金额不少于20亿美元。

<!--en-->
In part, the surprise element was a function of disclosure. The corporation's last quarterly report to the Securities and Exchange Commission prior to its bankruptcy had implied a total cost of settling asbestos-related claims of about $350 million. That was less than half of Manville's $830 millionof shareholders' equity. On August 26, by contrast, Manville estimated the potential damages at no less than $2 billion.

财务报告的对抗性本质 19

<!--en-->
The Adversarial Nature of Financial Reporting
19

对于财务报表分析师而言，曼维尔事件证明了此前被认为不可能发生的情景确实具有现实可能性：一家财务状况原本良好的公司，仅仅因为法律诉讼而陷入破产，这已成为令人噩梦般的现实。

<!--en-->
For analysts of financial statements, the Manville episode demonstrated the plausibility of a scenario previously thought inconceivable. A bankruptcy at an otherwise financially sound company, brought on solely by legal claims, had become a nightmarish reality.

更令人震惊的是，这一问题已潜伏多年。曼维尔公司的破产源于数十年前因接触该公司产品而患上的疾病所引发的索赔。随后几年里接连出现的破产申请进一步凸显了石棉责任的长期性。其中较为突出的案例包括沃尔特工业公司（1989年）、国家石膏公司（1990年）、USG公司（1993年及2001年）、欧文斯·康宁公司（2000年）以及阿姆斯特朗世界工业公司（2000年），每起案件的涉及资产都超过十亿美元。

<!--en-->
Intensifying the shock was that the problem had lain dormant for many years. Manville's bankruptcy resulted from claims for diseases contracted decades earlier through contact with the company's products. The long-tailed nature of asbestos liabilities was underscored by a series of bankruptcy filings over succeeding years. Prominent examples, each involving a billion dollars or more of assets, included Walter Industries (1989), National Gypsum (1990), USG Corporation (1993 and again in 2001), Owens Corning (2000), and Armstrong World Industries (2000).

与石棉暴露、硅胶乳房植入物以及各种环境危害相关的破产事件（详见第13章）提高了分析师对法律风险的认识。即便如此，分析师有时仍会只见树木不见森林，过分关注那些面临类似巨额或有负债的公司的财务比率细节。他们仍可能被公司对巨额索赔请求的平淡回应所蒙蔽。

<!--en-->
Bankruptcies connected with asbestos exposure, silicone gel breast implants, and assorted environmental hazards (see Chapter 13) have heightened analysts' awareness of legal risks. Even so, analysts still miss the forest for the trees in some instances, concentrating on the minutiae of financial ratios of corporations facing similarly large contingent liabilities. They can still be lulled by companies' matter-of-fact responses to questions about the gigantic claims asserted against them.

从发行方的角度来看，不难想象为何投资者关系专员对重大法律突发事件的描述，往往会比经济现实要温和得多。

<!--en-->
Thinking about it from the issuer's standpoint, one can imagine several reasons that the investor-relations officer's account of a major legal contingency is likely to be considerably less dire than the economic reality.

首先，公司管理层显然有动机淡化那些威胁其股票和期权价值的风险。此外，作为极具争议性诉讼的当事方，高管们自身存在利益冲突。他们很难在为公司辩护的同时，又向投资者承认原告的主张有理有据且很可能胜诉。（事实上，任何此类公开承认都可能损害公司的诉讼前景。因此，坦诚披露或许并不可行。）最后，如果管理层在潜意识层面否认公司被判决破产的真实可能性，也并不算反常行为。对于管理者而言，承认自己的公司可能因看似无法控制的原因而倒闭，在心理上必定极为困难。尽管该公司有着优异的盈利增长记录和稳健的资产负债表，但申请破产或许仍是唯一的选择。

<!--en-->
To begin with, the corporation's managers have a clear interest in downplaying risks that threaten the value of their stock and options. Furthermore, as parties to a highly contentious lawsuit, the executives find themselves in a conflict. It would be difficult for them to testify persuasively in their company's defense while simultaneously acknowledging to investors that the plaintiffs' claims have merit and might, in fact, prevail. (Indeed, any such public admission could compromise the corporation's case. Candid disclosure may therefore not be a viable option.) Finally, it would hardly represent aberrant behavior if, on a subconscious level, management were to deny the real possibility of a company-wrecking judgment. It must be psychologically very difficult for managers to acknowledge that their company may go bust for reasons seemingly outside their control. Filing for bankruptcy may prove to be the only course available to the corporation, notwithstanding an excellent record of earnings growth and a conservative balance sheet.

出于上述种种原因，当潜在的毁灭性或有负债超过了分析师精心计算的财务比率所反映的程度时，他们必须格外依赖自己的独立判断。

<!--en-->
For all these reasons, analysts must take particular care to rely on their independent judgment when a potentially devastating contingent liability looms larger than their conscientiously calculated financial ratios.

这并非是对管理层诚信和坦率的评判。察言观色，洞悉言外之意。

<!--en-->
It is not a matter of sitting in judgment on management's honor and forthrightness.
READING BETWEEN THE LINES

如果企业高管对问题的严重性仍持否认态度，他们并非故意通过呈现过于乐观的图景来误导分析师。此外，即便他们冷静面对事实，也可能无法提供可靠的评估。很可能他们从未在面临类似问题的公司工作过，因此几乎没有依据来估计最坏情况发生的可能性。曾目睹其他企业陷入类似困境的分析师对此会有更深刻的认识，也更具客观性。分析师不应完全依赖公司对大规模集体诉讼的定期更新，还应与原告方代表交谈。尽管他们的观点绝非客观中立，但能揭示管理层所谓“索赔请求绝不会在法庭上成立”这一说法中的逻辑漏洞。

<!--en-->
If corporate executives remain in denial about the magnitude of the problem, they are not deliberately misleading analysts by presenting an overly optimistic picture. Moreover, the managers may not provide a reliable assessment even if they soberly face the facts. In all likelihood, they have never worked for a company with a comparable problem. They consequently have little basis for estimating the likelihood that the worst-case scenario will be fulfilled. Analysts who have seen other corporations in similar predicaments have more perspective on the matter, as well as greater objectivity. Instead of relying entirely on the company's periodic updates on a huge class action suit, analysts should also speak to representatives of the plaintiffs' side. Their views, while by no means unbiased, will expose logical weaknesses in management's assertions that the liability claims will never stand up in court.

### 保持怀疑态度的重要性

<!--en-->
*THE IMPORTANCE OF BEING SKEPTICAL*

至此，读者或许已经明白为何本章标题为“财务报告的对立性”。财务报表的编制者往往被描绘成不光彩的形象——他们总是选择能够支撑股价的会计处理方式，而非慷慨地协助分析师准确了解公司的财务状况。分析师已被警告不要沾染那种推动伟大企业的乐观情绪，而应保持近乎不信任的怀疑态度。有些读者可能会觉得，如果这份工作意味着不断唱反调、提出令人难堪的问题，还要成为那些渴望在投资者、客户和供应商中赢得好感的公司的眼中钉，那自己并不适合做财务分析师。

<!--en-->
By now, the reader presumably understands why this chapter is titled “The Adversarial Nature of Financial Reporting.” The issuer of financial statements has been portrayed in an unflattering light, invariably choosing the accounting option that will tend to prop up its stock price, rather than generously assisting the analyst in deriving an accurate picture of its financial condition. Analysts have been warned not to partake of the optimism that drives all great business enterprises, but instead to maintain an attitude of skepticism bordering on distrust. Some readers may feel they are not cut out to be financial analysts if the job consists of constant nay-saying, of posing embarrassing questions, and of being a perennial thorn in the side of companies that want to win friends among investors, customers, and suppliers.

虽然一味采取敌对态度确实是一种令人不悦的生活方式，但本书对财务报表编制者所建议的态度并不包含这种敌意。相反，分析师应像在业余篮球赛中暂时将对手视为敌人一样，将编制者视为对手。在球场上，竞争可能十分激烈，但这反而增添了乐趣。

<!--en-->
Although pursuing relentless antagonism can indeed be an unpleasant way to go through life, the stance that this book recommends toward issuers of financial statements implies no such acrimony. Rather, analysts should view the issuers as adversaries in the same manner that they temporarily demonize their opponents in a friendly pickup basketball game. On the court, the competition can be intense, which only adds to the fun.

赛后，大家还可以一起出去吃披萨、喝啤酒。简而言之，财务分析师和投资者关系专员可以像诉讼律师那样，以超然的态度对待工作——他们运用各种合法手段激烈争辩，纯粹是为了赢得案件，而非因为对方的主张本身具有内在合理性。

<!--en-->
Afterward, everyone can have a fine time going out together for pizza and beer. In short, financial analysts and investor-relations officers can view their work with the detachment of litigators who engage in every legal form of shin-kicking out of sheer desire to win the case, not because the litigants' claims necessarily have intrinsic merit.

财务类撰稿人常常以高度道德化的口吻描述财务报告与分析中的讨价还价过程。通常，作者会揭露数字呈现中的诡计，并指责公司的贪婪与欺诈行为。将财务报表的编制视为善恶之间的史诗级斗争，或许适合激进的记者，但财务分析师无需充当道德警察也能做好本职工作。

<!--en-->
Too often, financial writers describe the give-and-take of financial reporting and analysis in a highly moralistic tone. Typically, the authorexposes a tricky presentation of the numbers and reproaches the company for greed and chicanery. Viewing the production of financial statements as an epic struggle between good and evil may suit a crusading journalist, but financial analysts need not join the ethics police to do their job well.

财务报告的对立性 21

<!--en-->
The Adversarial Nature of Financial Reporting
21

另一种选择是学会理解财务报告中的博弈技巧，甚至在一定程度上欣赏那些不断想出新招数来误导投资者的编制者的聪明才智。公然的欺诈行为固然不可容忍，但那些在不违法的前提下歪曲经济现实的做法，确实需要非凡的创造力。

<!--en-->
An alternative is to learn to understand the gamesmanship of financial reporting, perhaps even to appreciate on some level the cleverness of issuers who constantly devise new stratagems for leading investors off the track. Outright fraud cannot be countenanced, but disclosure that shades economic realities without violating the law requires truly impressive ingenuity.

将财务报表编制者与使用者之间的互动视为一场游戏，而非道德剧，分析师就能更容易从对立面审视整个过程。正如棋手会预判对手的下一步棋，分析师也应思考：若自己身处编制者之位，会采用何种策略。

<!--en-->
By regarding the interaction between issuers and users of financial statements as a game, rather than a morality play, analysts will find it easier to view the action from the opposite side. Just as a chess master anticipates an opponent's future moves, analysts should consider which gambits they themselves would use if they were in the issuer's seat.

“哦，不！”此时一些读者可能会这样想，“作者先是说我不能简单地把数字填入标准化表格，现在又让我进行角色扮演，去猜测报表发布前会隐藏哪些伎俩。我原以为这本书是为了让我的工作更轻松，而不是更复杂。”

<!--en-->
"Oh no!" some readers must be thinking at this point. "First the authors tell me that I must not simply plug numbers into a standardized spreadsheet. Now I have to engage in role-playing exercises to guess what tricks will be embedded in the statements before they even come out. I thought this book was supposed to make my job easier, not more complicated."

实际上，本书的目标是让读者成为更优秀的分析师。如果能通过提供捷径来实现这一目标，作者定会毫不犹豫地这么做。财务报告发生在特定的制度环境中，这要求尽职的分析师必须超越常规的财务比率计算。如果没有本书所倡导的那种额外警惕性，财务报表的使用者就会陷入一个为复杂问题提供过于简单答案的体系之中；该体系会压制那些不愿轻信报表数据的个体，并不明智地给予编制者过多的信任。

<!--en-->
In reality, this book's goal is to make the reader a better analyst. If that goal could be achieved by providing shortcuts, the authors would not hesitate to do so. Financial reporting occurs in an institutional context that obliges conscientious analysts to go many steps beyond conventional calculation of financial ratios. Without the extra vigilance advocated in these pages, the user of financial statements will become mired in a system that provides excessively simple answers to complex questions, squelches individuals who insolently refuse to accept reported financial data at face value, and inadvisably gives issuers the benefit of the doubt.

这些系统性偏差是股票销售中固有的现象。在投资者群体中，有许多规模庞大且经验丰富的金融机构，它们会运用最先进的分析技术来挑选证券纳入投资组合。此外，股票买家中还包括一些未受过财务报表分析训练的个人，他们很难评估年度及季度盈利报告。这两类投资者都是行业融资的重要来源，从长期来看，他们都能从市场经济中资本所产生的回报中获益。然而，针对这两类投资者的股票推销方式却截然不同。

<!--en-->
These systematic biases are inherent in selling stocks. Within the universe of investors are many large, sophisticated financial institutions that utilize the best available techniques of analysis to select securities for their portfolios. Also among the buyers of stocks are individuals who, not being trained in financial statement analysis, are poorly equipped to evaluate annual and quarterly earnings reports. Both types of investors are important sources of financing for industry, and both benefit over the long term from the returns that accrue to capital in a market economy. The two groups cannot be sold stocks in the same way, however.

对个人投资者而言，最能吸引他们的往往是“故事”。有时，这类故事会涉及具有无限销售潜力的新产品；另一种故事则将推荐购买的股票描述为对当前经济趋势的押注，比如利率下降或国防开支增加。还有一些故事属于谣言范畴，尤其是那些与潜在企业并购相关的传言。大多数此类故事的共同特点是：承诺惊人的收益、表面上看似合理的逻辑，以及缺乏定量数据的支撑。

<!--en-->
What generally sells best to individual investors is a story. Sometimes the story involves a new product with seemingly unlimited sales potential. Another kind of story portrays the recommended stock as a play on some current economic trend, such as declining interest rates or a step-up in defense spending. Some stories lie in the realm of rumor, particularly thosethat relate to possible corporate takeovers. The chief characteristics of most stories are the promise of spectacular gains, superficially sound logic, and a paucity of quantitative verification.

字里行间的含义

<!--en-->
READING BETWEEN THE LINES

当分析师基于对公司财务报表的详尽研究而提出的股票购买建议，被转化为通俗易懂、定性的表述以便非专业人士理解时，并不会造成太大危害。不过，很多时候这类“故事”其实源自股票经纪人，甚至来自发行公司的高层。在这种情况下，故事传播的热情往往更多取决于其叙事吸引力，而非支撑性分析的可靠性。

<!--en-->
No great harm is done when an analyst's stock purchase recommendation, backed up by a thorough study of the issuer's financial statements, is translated into soft, qualitative terms for laypersons' benefit. Not infrequently, though, a story originates among stockbrokers or even in the executive offices of the issuer itself. In such an instance, the zeal with which the story is disseminated may depend more on its narrative appeal than on the solidity of the supporting analysis.

个人投资者对“故事”的偏好削弱了进行严谨财务分析的动力，但机构投资者所创造的环境也并非理想。尽管最优秀的投资机构会开展严谨且富有创意的研究，但许多其他机构仍采用本章前文所批评的那种机械式做法。它们将财务报表分析简化为简单的每股收益预测，并据此得出市盈率倍数。实际上，那些不够尽责的投资经理认为，只要一只股票在这一单一指标上表现良好，便属于有吸引力的投资对象。遗憾的是，华尔街的许多研究报告正是迎合了这些机构的狭隘视角，为了及时更新大量公司的盈利预估，而牺牲了分析的全面性。

<!--en-->
Individual investors' fondness for stories undercuts the impetus for serious financial analysis, but the environment created by institutional investors is not ideal, either. Although the best investment organizations conduct rigorous and imaginative research, many others operate in the mechanical fashion derided earlier in this chapter. They reduce financial statement analysis to the bare bones of forecasting earnings per share, from which they derive a price-earnings multiple. In effect, the less conscientious investment managers assume that as long as a stock stacks up well by this single measure, it represents an attractive investment. Much Wall Street research, regrettably, caters to these institutions' tunnel vision, sacrificing analytical comprehensiveness to the operational objective of maintaining up-to-the-minute earnings estimates on vast numbers of companies.

此外，严肃的财务报表分析师面临风格受限的情况并不只出现在投资公司中。制造商和批发商的信贷部门同样存在特有的制度性障碍。

<!--en-->
Investment firms, moreover, are not the only workplaces in which serious analysts of financial statements may find their style crimped. The credit departments of manufacturers and wholesalers have their own set of institutional hazards.

首先，来看看“信贷审批流程”这一术语本身。顾名思义，供应商的倾向是批准而非拒绝信贷。在一定程度上，这无可厚非。如图表1.3所示，中性临界点A意味着一半申请人获批、另一半被拒，这一信贷标准实际上过高了。采用这种标准的公司会错失许多几乎不会拖欠款项的潜在客户。即便是允许更多业务开展却又不产生信贷损失的临界点B，也并非最优选择。旨在最大化利润的信贷经理们会以临界点C为目标——在这一水平上，虽然会出现应收账款损失，但新增客户带来的利润足以抵消这部分损失。

<!--en-->
Consider, to begin with, the very term *credit approval process*. As the name implies, the vendor's bias is toward extending rather than refusing credit. Up to a point, this is as it should be. In Exhibit 1.3, neutral Cutoff Point A, where half of all applicants are approved and half are refused,represents an unnecessarily high credit standard. Any company employing it would turn away many potential customers who posed almost no threat of delinquency. Even Cutoff Point B, which allows more business to be written but produces no credit losses, is less than optimal. Credit managers who seek to maximize profits aim for Cutoff Point C. It represents a level of credit extension at which losses on receivables occur but are slightly more than offset by the profits derived from incremental customers.

***EXHIBIT 1.3** The Bias toward Favorable Credit Evaluations*
The Adversarial Nature of Financial Reporting
23

为了达到这一最优结果，信贷分析师必须批准一定数量的最终可能无法还款的账户。

<!--en-->
To achieve this optimal result, a credit analyst must approve a certain number of accounts that will eventually fail to pay.

实际上，分析师被迫犯下本可通过严格遵循对申请人财务报表分析所得结论而避免的错误。公司通过避免相反类型的错误（即拒绝那些不会拖欠款项的潜在客户）来弥补这类错误带来的成本。

<!--en-->
In effect, the analyst is required to make mistakes that could be avoided by rigorously obeying the conclusions derived from the study of applicants' financial statements. The company makes up the cost of such mistakes by avoiding mistakes of the opposite type (rejecting potential customers who will not fail to pay).

只要目标是真正最大化利润，用一种错误来换取另一种错误完全是理性的，也符合合理的分析逻辑。然而，公司总是存在以牺牲利润为代价来追求销售额最大化的风险。也就是说，信贷经理可能会进一步扭曲系统，将临界点推至图表1.3中的D点。如果销售人员的薪酬与佣金挂钩，且他们的报酬并未与客户回款情况紧密关联，这种问题就必然会出现。面对此类激励机制，理性的反应便是向信贷分析师施压，让他们批准那些财务报表明显应被拒绝的申请人。

<!--en-->
Trading off one type of error for another is thoroughly rational and consistent with sound analysis, so long as the objective is truly to maximize profits. There is always a danger, however, that the company will instead maximize sales at the expense of profits. That is, the credit manager may bias the system even further, to Cutoff Point D in Exhibit 1.3. Such a problem is bound to arise if the company's salespeople are paid on commission and their compensation is not tightly linked to the collection experience of their customers. The rational response to that sort of incentive system is to pressure credit analysts to approve applicants whose financial statements cry out for rejection.

在商业贷款领域，同样存在想要确认收入与做出合理信贷决策之间的张力。在银行或金融公司中，财务报表分析师可能会面临来自长期合作客户的特殊请求，这些客户声称自己正面临暂时的经营困难。

<!--en-->
A similar tension between the desire to book revenues and the need to make sound credit decisions exists in commercial lending. At a bank or a finance company, an analyst of financial statements may be confronted by special pleading on behalf of a loyal, long-established client that is under allegedly temporary strain.

或者，信贷官员可能会辩称，尽管申请人的财务比率不达标，仍应批准其贷款申请，理由是该公司虽处于初创阶段但具有成长为重要客户的潜力。在贷款需求低迷时期，要求对既定信贷政策破例处理的请求在数量和迫切程度上都可能增加。

<!--en-->
Alternatively, the lending officer may argue that a loan request ought to be approved, despite substandard financial ratios, on the grounds that the applicant is a young, struggling company with potential to grow into a major client. Requests for exceptions to established credit policies are likely to increase in both number and fervor during periods of slack demand for loans.

在考虑那些请求宽限的情况时，信贷分析师当然应把财务报表无法反映的相关定性因素纳入考量。同时，分析师必须牢记：定性信贷因素分为有利和不利两类。此外，务必记住一个冷冰冰的事实：暂时陷入困境或处于初创阶段的企业违约的可能性高于平均水平。

<!--en-->
When considering pleas of mitigating circumstances, the credit analyst should certainly take into account pertinent qualitative factors that the financial statements fail to capture. At the same time, the analyst must bear in mind that qualitative credit considerations come in two flavors, favorable and unfavorable. It is also imperative to remember that the cold, hard statistics show that companies in the temporarily impaired and start-up categories have a higher-than-average propensity to **default** on their debt.

每家申请贷款的高风险企业都能提出看似合理的理由，试图推翻既定的财务比率标准。但从整体来看，这类借款人中很大一部分最终会违约，这证明他们那些看似站得住脚的定性论据往往站不住脚。1989年至1991年间发生的大规模高收益债券违约潮便印证了这一残酷现实；这些债券正是凭借发行方资产负债表上未体现的所谓“有价值资产”而被推销出去的。

<!--en-->
Every high-risk company seeking a loan can make a plausible soft case for overriding the financial ratios. In aggregate, though, a large percentageof such borrowers will fail, proving that many of their seemingly valid qualitative arguments were specious. This unsentimental truth was driven home by a massive 1989–1991 wave of defaults on high-yield bonds that had been marketed on the strength of supposedly valuable assets not reflected on the issuers’ balance sheets.

债券投资者曾被告知，管理层的宏伟梦想和野心足以保证企业的偿付能力。2001年发生的另一波大规模违约涉及处于起步阶段的电信企业，当时几乎没有任何可用于计算财务比率的数据。给这些初创企业放贷的理由，竟是所谓新技术能带来无限的服务需求。READING BETWEEN THE LINES

<!--en-->
Bond investors had been told that the bold dreams and ambitions of management would suffice to keep the companies solvent. Another large default wave in 2001 involved early-stage telecommunications ventures for which there was scarcely any financial data from which to calculate ratios. The rationale advanced for lending to these nascent companies was the supposedly limitless demand for services made possible by miraculous new technology.
READING BETWEEN THE LINES

诚然，即便满足既定定量标准的企业也会发生违约现象。区别在于：分析师可以将财务比率与历史记录进行对比，从而判断其作为破产预测指标的可靠性（参见第13章）。但对于资本薄弱的企业在申请贷款时所引用的那些高度主观、难以量化的定性因素，却无法进行类似的检验。因此，分析师依赖数字而非企业提出的模糊理由时，判断才会更可靠。

<!--en-->
To be sure, defaults also occur among companies that satisfy established quantitative standards. The difference is that analysts can test financial ratios against a historical record to determine their reliability as predictors of bankruptcy (see Chapter 13). No comparable testing is feasible for the highly idiosyncratic, qualitative factors that weakly capitalized companies cite when applying for loans. Analysts are therefore on more solid ground when they rely primarily on the numbers than when they try to discriminate among companies’ soft arguments.

## 结论

<!--en-->
*CONCLUSION*

本章的主要目的之一是补充许多财务报表分析讨论中所缺失的关键要素。除了会计规则、现金流以及标准比率的定义外，分析师还必须考虑企业管理者的动机以及其所处组织的运作机制。忽视这些因素会导致对发行人向报表使用者传达信息的真实意图产生错误假设。

<!--en-->
A primary objective of this chapter has been to supply an essential ingredient that is missing from many discussions of financial statement analysis. Aside from accounting rules, cash flows, and definitions of standard ratios, analysts must consider the motivations of corporate managers, as well as the dynamics of the organizations in which they work. Neglecting these factors will lead to false assumptions about the underlying intent of issuers’ communications with users of financial statements.

此外，如果分析师不了解自身组织的运作方式，就可能对自己工作的质量做出错误判断。如果通过详尽财务分析得出的结论被认为是错误的，那么重要的是要弄清这一判断源于分析本身的缺陷，还是高层决定无视分析师的建议。高级管理人员有时会为了动用闲置资金或增加贷款量而置财务报表分析于不顾。此时，组织会通过说服自己“财务报表解读原则已经根本改变”来为这种行为辩解。分析师无需采取辞职抗议的极端做法，但只要能避免陷入这种普遍的错觉，便会受益无穷。

<!--en-->
Moreover, analysts may make incorrect inferences about the quality of their own work if they fail to understand the workings of their own organizations. If a conclusion derived from thorough financial analysis is deemed wrong, it is important to know whether that judgment reflects a flawed analysis or a higher-level decision to override analysts’ recommendations. Senior managers sometimes subordinate financial statement analysis to a determination that idle funds must be put to work or that loan volume must be increased. At such times, organizations rationalize their behavior by persuading themselves that the principles of interpreting financial statements have fundamentally changed. Analysts need not go to the extreme of resigning in protest, but they will benefit if they can avoid getting caught up in the prevailing delusion.

财务报告的对立性 25

<!--en-->
The Adversarial Nature of Financial Reporting
25

诚然，在财务报表分析文献中，组织行为并未完全被忽视。通常，学术研究将发行方描述为追求利润最大化的企业，只要合法且认为能提升股权市场估值，它们就倾向于夸大盈利。这一模型已落后于当前金融学其他分支中对企业的普遍认知。¹⁶如今，企业不再被视为始终致力于实现股价最大化这一明确目标的单一整体，而是更现实地被看作是由动机各异的个体组成的集合体。

<!--en-->
To be sure, organizational behavior has not been entirely overlooked up until now in the literature of financial statement analysis. Typically, academic studies depict issuers as profit-maximizing firms, inclined to overstate their earnings if they can do so legally and if they believe it will boost their equity market valuation. This model lags behind the portrait of the firm now prevalent in other branches of finance.¹⁶ Instead of a monolithic organization that consistently pursues the clear-cut objective of share price maximization, the corporation is now viewed more realistically as an aggregation of individuals with diverse motivations.

运用这一更为复杂的模型，分析师便能解开有关企业报告的棘手难题。从长远来看，夸大盈利似乎是一种适得其反的策略，因为这种行为最终会反过来困扰企业自身。例如，假设一家企业对资产的折旧年限长于物理损耗及制造技术变革所决定的合理期限。当需要更换现有设备时，该企业将面临两种糟糕的选择。

<!--en-->
Using this more sophisticated model, an analyst can unravel an otherwise vexing riddle concerning corporate reporting. Overstating earnings would appear to be a self-defeating strategy in the long term, since it has a tendency to catch up with the perpetrator. Suppose, for example, a corporation depreciates assets over a longer period than can be justified by physical wear and tear and the rate of technological change in manufacturing methods. When the time comes to replace the existing equipment, the corporation will face two unattractive options.

第一种选择是冲销那些已过时、在二手市场上价值微乎其微的设备上剩余的未折旧余额，从而削弱报告中的盈利水平。另一种选择则是推迟购置更先进的设备，进而导致竞争力下降并减少未来盈利。倘若该企业当初没有夸大盈利，岂不是会更好？这种夸大行为很可能已经损害了其在投资者心中的信誉。

<!--en-->
The first is to penalize reported earnings by writing off the remaining undepreciated balance on equipment that is obsolete and hence of little value in the resale market. Alternatively, the company can delay the necessary purchase of more up-to-date equipment, thereby losing ground competitively and reducing future earnings. Would the corporation not have been better off if it had refrained from overstating its earnings in the first place, an act that probably cost it some measure of credibility among investors?

如果分析师从管理层的角度来考量此事，这个难题的解决办法便浮现出来。企业必须通过少提折旧来“偿还”所虚增的盈利，而这一清算之日可能超出了高层管理者的规划视野。一位打算五年后退休、且在此期间薪酬与报告盈利增长挂钩的首席执行官，或许会毫无顾忌地为了眼前利益而牺牲未来运营能力。换句话说，企业所有者的长期利益可能与他们的代理人——受薪经理人的短期利益并不一致。

<!--en-->
If the analyst considers the matter from the standpoint of management, a possible solution to the riddle emerges. The day of reckoning, when the firm must pay back the reported earnings borrowed via underdepreciation, may be beyond the planning horizon of senior management. A chief executive officer who intends to retire in five years, and who will be compensated in the interim according to a formula based on reported earnings growth, may have no qualms about exaggerating current results at the expense of future years' operations. The long-term interests of the firm's owners, in other words, may not be consistent with the short-term interests of their agents, the salaried managers.

显然，不能指望分析师能洞悉所有人的心思或揣摩管理层的真实动机。不过，仅仅意识到存在会计入门教材中所预设目标之外的其他目的，便已有所裨益。即便仅此而已，意识到管理层可能另有图谋这一点，也会促使读者在公司披露信息有悖常理时相信自己的直觉。在某些情况下，管理层可能会认为，减轻分析师对其明显糟糕决策批评的最佳办法就是顽固地坚持该决策、拒绝改变方向。尽管首席执行官或许能面不改色地蒙混过关，但这一失误终究还是失误。记住管理者可能另有图谋的分析师将占据先机；他们会合理怀疑管理层是否真的在做出旨在为股东创造长期利益的艰难抉择，而这些抉择往往是公司外部人员无法想象的。字里行间的玄机

<!--en-->
Plainly, analysts cannot be expected to read minds or to divine the true motives of management in every case. There is a benefit, however, in simply being cognizant of objectives other than the ones presupposed by introductory accounting texts. If nothing else, the awareness that management may have something up its sleeve will encourage readers to trust their instincts when some aspect of a company's disclosure simply does not ring true. In a given instance, management may judge that its best chance of minimizing analysts' criticism of an obviously disastrous corporate decision lies instubbornly defending the decision and refusing to change course. Even though the chief executive officer may be able to pull it off with a straight face, however, the blunder remains a blunder. Analysts who remember that managers may be pursuing their own agendas will be ahead of the game. They will be properly skeptical that management is genuinely making tough choices designed to yield long-run benefits to shareholders, but which individuals outside the corporation cannot envision.
READING BETWEEN THE LINES

秉持“举证责任在于披露信息者”的态度，分析师现在已准备好着手分析基本财务报表。

<!--en-->
Armed with the attitude that the burden of proof lies with those making the disclosures, the analyst is now prepared to tackle the basic financial statements.

揭示财务报表中所隐藏及所披露信息的方法，构成了接下来三章的核心内容。从基础层面一直到运用最后两章介绍的技术做出投资决策，始终保持一种对立的视角都是大有裨益的。

<!--en-->
Methods for uncovering the information they conceal, as well as that which they reveal, constitute the heart of the next three chapters. From that elementary level right on up to making investment decisions with the techniques presented in the final two chapters, it will pay to maintain an adversarial stance at all times.

## 资产负债表

<!--en-->
*The Balance Sheet*

资产负债表是一项了不起的发明，但它存在两个根本性缺陷。首先，虽然从理论上讲，汇总企业所拥有资产的价值很有用，但在实践中这些价值往往难以确定。其次，许多事物都具有价值，至少在外行人看来可以被视为资产；然而并非所有资产都能被赋予具体数值并记录在资产负债表上。例如，服务行业的经营者常说：“我们的资产每晚都会乘电梯离开。”所有人都承认公司人力资本——即员工的技能和创造力——的价值，但至今无人能找到一种足够精确的估值方法将其反映在资产负债表上。会计师们并未走向另一个极端，将无形资产全部排除在资产负债表之外，但允许记录与禁止记录之间的界限不可避免地带有随意性。¹ 20世纪90年代末，随着智力资本在许多大公司的估值中占比日益增大，关于资产会计处理的理论争议也愈发激烈。由五大会计师事务所之一的安达信开展的一项研究显示：1978年至1999年间，美国上市公司的**账面价值**占其股市价值的比例从95%下降至71%。² 投资者越来越愿意为那些传统会计准则（GAAP）所涵盖的资产以外的东西支付对价，包括建筑物、机器设备、存货、应收账款以及有限范围内的资本化支出。

<!--en-->
The balance sheet is a remarkable invention, yet it has two fundamental shortcomings. First, while it is in theory quite useful to have a summary of the values of all the assets owned by an enterprise, these values frequently prove elusive in practice. Second, many kinds of things have value and could be construed, at least by the layperson, as assets. Not all of them can be assigned a specific value and recorded on a balance sheet, however. For example, proprietors of service businesses are fond of saying, “Our assets go down the elevator every night.” Everybody acknowledges the value of a company’s human capital—the skills and creativity of its employees—but no one has devised a means of valuing it precisely enough to reflect it on the balance sheet. Accountants do not go to the opposite extreme of banishing all intangible assets from the balance sheet, but the dividing line between the permitted and the prohibited is inevitably an arbitrary one.¹
During the late 1990s, doctrinal disputes over accounting for assets intensified as intellectual capital came to represent growing proportions of many major corporations’ perceived value. A study conducted on behalf of Big Five accounting firm Arthur Andersen showed that between 1978 and 1999, **book value** fell from 95 percent to 71 percent of the stock market value of public companies in the United States.² Increasingly, investors were willing to pay for things other than the traditional assets that generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) had grown up around, including buildings, machinery, inventories, receivables, and a limited range of capitalized expenditures.

极端情况下，那些实物资产微乎其微的互联网初创公司竟能获得巨大的**市值**。它们的估值源于那些承诺在未来创造巨额利润的商业模式。通过大量广告营销来积累用户群是一笔昂贵的开支，但投资者相信，终有一天庞大的忠实用户群会转化为丰厚的收入流。基本财务报表

<!--en-->
At the extreme, start-up Internet companies with negligible physical assets attained gigantic **market capitalizations**. Their valuations derived from business models purporting to promise vast profits far in the future. Building up subscriber bases through heavy consumer advertising was an expensive proposition, but one day, investors believed, a large, loyal following would translate into rich revenue streams.
THE BASIC FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

2000年的科技股崩盘期间，许多网络公司的股市价值骤然蒸发，但信息密集型的新经济与传统资产观念之间的不匹配现象依然存在。著名的会计理论家们指出，源于重工业主导时代的财务报告做法严重低估了研发支出所创造的价值，而GAAP却不愿将此类支出予以资本化。他们进一步指出，传统会计通常只有在资产被出售时才允许其价值上升。“在当今经济中，许多价值的创造与消亡已不再以交易为基础，因此传统会计系统根本无法捕捉到其中的大部分活动，”纽约大学的巴鲁克·列夫如此说道。

<!--en-->
Much of the dot-coms' stock market value disappeared during the tech wreck of 2000, but the perceived mismatch between the information-intensive New Economy and traditional notions of assets persisted. Prominent accounting theorists argued that financial reporting practices rooted in an era more dominated by heavy manufacturing grossly understated the value created by research and development outlays, which GAAP was resistant to capitalizing. They observed further that traditional accounting generally permitted assets to rise in value only if they were sold. “Transactions are no longer the basis for much of the value created and destroyed in today's economy, and therefore traditional accounting systems are at a loss to capture much of what goes on,” argued Baruch Lev of New York University.

他举例说，某种药物通过关键临床试验或某款计算机软件成功完成测试后，其价值便会上升。“由于没有金钱往来，所以不存在会计事项，”列夫指出。³

<!--en-->
As examples, he cited the rise in value resulting from a drug passing a key clinical test and from a computer software program being successfully beta-tested. “There's no accounting event because no money changes hands,” Lev noted.³

## 价值问题

<!--en-->
*THE VALUE PROBLEM*

会计师所面临的估值难题，历史上也一直困扰着哲学家、经济学家、税务评估员和司法人员。几个世纪以来，道德哲学家们一直在探讨商人应收取的公平价格问题。早期的经济学家试图通过计算产品中所包含的劳动单位来推导其内在价值。对于不动产的评估则发展出了几种不同的方法，包括租金资本化法、参照类似物业的销售价格来推断价值，以及估算该物业在用于最佳用途时的价值。当法院需要评估破产公司的资产时也会采用类似的理论，不过不同类别债权人之间的激烈谈判在最终裁定中起着至关重要的作用。

<!--en-->
The problems of value that accountants wrestle with have also historically plagued philosophers, economists, tax assessors, and the judiciary. Moral philosophers over the centuries grappled with the notion of a fair price for merchants to charge. Early economists attempted to derive a product's intrinsic value by calculating the units of labor embodied in it. Several distinct approaches have evolved for assessing real property. These include **capitalization** of rentals, inferring a value based on sales of comparable properties, and estimating the value a property would have if put to its highest and best use. Similar theories are involved when the courts seek to value the assets of bankrupt companies, although vigorous negotiations among the different classes of creditors play an essential role in the final determination.

会计行业以值得称赞的清晰视野，早已通过确立**历史成本**作为非金融资产估值的基础，从而理清了各种相互竞争的理论纷争。获取或建造某项资产的成本具有客观且可验证的优势；作为价值基准，它也与会计师传统的谨慎性原则相契合。

<!--en-->
With commendable clarity of vision, the accounting profession long ago cut through the thicket of competing theories by establishing **historical cost** as the basis for valuing nonfinancial assets. The cost of acquiring or constructing an asset has the great advantage of being an objective and verifiable figure. As a benchmark for value, it is, therefore, compatible with accountants' traditional principle of conservatism.

无论其优点如何，历史成本制度也存在一些显而易见的缺点，即便是初学会计的人也能察觉。如前所述，以交易为基础进行估值意味着：除非某项资产曾参与交易，否则它无法反映在资产负债表上。由这一惯例引发的最为人熟知的难题便涉及商誉。A公司除了有形资产外，还拥有备受推崇的品牌名称以及与商家多年建立的紧密关系等无形价值。然而，由于这些无形价值从未出现在交易中，因此并未反映在A公司的资产负债表上。不过，当B公司以高于账面价值的价格收购A公司时，这些无形资产便突然被确认了。对财务报表使用者而言，A公司的资产现在得到了更全面的反映。但从负面来看，A公司的资产负债表现在显示其价值高于C公司——尽管C公司拥有同等的有形和无形资产，却从未被收购过。《资产负债表》31

<!--en-->
Whatever its strengths, however, the historical cost system also has disadvantages that are apparent even to the beginning student of accounting. As already noted, basing valuation on transactions means that no asset can be reflected on the balance sheet unless it has been involved in a transaction. The most familiar difficulty that results from this convention involves goodwill. Company A has value above and beyond its tangible assets, inthe form of well-regarded brand names and close relationships with merchants built up over many years. None of this intangible value appears on Company A's balance sheet, however, for it has never figured in a transaction. When Company B acquires Company A at a premium to book value, though, the intangibles are suddenly recognized. To the benefit of users of financial statements, Company A's assets are now more fully reflected. On the negative side, Company A's balance sheet now says it is more valuable than Company C, which has equivalent tangible and intangible assets but has never been acquired.
The Balance Sheet
31

一个人在追求真正价值的过程中可能会遇到诸多困难。例如，考虑一台价值50,000美元的专用机械设备。

<!--en-->
The difficulties a person may encounter in the quest for true value are numerous. Consider, for example, a piece of specialized machinery, acquired for $50,000.

在设备投入使用的当天，甚至在围绕折旧率的争议出现之前，其价值就已经取决于主观判断了。购买该设备的公司如果认为其价值低于50,000美元，想必不会支付这笔费用。然而，担保贷款机构很可能会采取更为保守的观点。一方面，由于每年生产的同类机器数量极少（如果该设备是定制的，甚至可能根本没有同类产品），贷款机构将来很难通过可比资产来评估抵押品的价值。此外，如果贷款机构最终不得不进行强制拍卖，可能找不到愿意以50,000美元价格购买该机器的买家，因为其专业性决定了它只对少数制造商有用。再者，所有可能的买家可能都位于数百英里之外，因此清算时机器的价值还会因运输和重新安装成本而进一步缩水。

<!--en-->
On the day the equipment is put into service, even before any controversies surrounding depreciation rates arise, value is already a matter of opinion. The company that made the purchase would presumably not have paid $50,000 if it perceived the machine to be worth a lesser amount. A secured lender, however, is likely to take a more conservative view. For one thing, the lender will find it difficult in the future to monitor the value of the collateral through comparables, since only a few similar machines (perhaps none, if the piece is customized) are produced each year. Furthermore, if the lender is ultimately forced to foreclose, there may be no ready purchaser of the machinery for $50,000, since its specialized nature makes it useful to only a small number of manufacturers. All of the potential purchasers, moreover, may be located hundreds of miles away, so that the machinery's value in a liquidation would be further reduced by the costs of transporting and reinstalling it.

在评估独一无二的非标工业设备时所遇到的问题，似乎在处理原油储备等活跃交易的商品时便不复存在。然而，即便是这类资产，也难以进行精确且易于达成共识的估值。

<!--en-->
The problems encountered in evaluating one-of-a-kind industrial equipment might appear to be eliminated when dealing with actively traded commodities such as crude oil reserves. Even this type of asset, however, resists precise, easily agreed-on valuation.

由于石油公司经常买卖地下油气储量，当前的交易价格很容易获取。然而，这些交易是基于对特定地质构造中最终产量的估算，因为无法直接测量石油储量。即便石油工程师采用最先进的技术，他们的估算仍严重依赖主观判断和推理。此外，井口的产油速度有时会按照最佳科学方法预测的速率开始生产，但很快便衰竭，最终产量仅为预估储量的一小部分。鉴于这种程度的不确定性，记录石油储量的真实价值对会计师而言并非现实目标。财务报表的使用者最多只能指望得到有根据的猜测，而诚实的人（更不用说那些有既得利益的奸商）之间也存在很大的分歧空间。《基本财务报表》

<!--en-->
Since oil companies frequently buy and sell reserves in the ground, current transaction prices are readily available. These transactions, however, are based on estimates of eventual production from unique geologic formations, for there are no means of directly measuring oil reserves. Even when petroleum engineers employ the most advanced technology, their estimates rely heavily on judgment and inference. It is not unheard of, moreover, for a well to begin to produce at the rate predicted by the best scientific methods, only to peter out a short time later, ultimately yielding just a fraction of its estimated reserves. With this degree of uncertainty, recording the true value of oil reserves is not a realistic objective for accountants. Users of financial statements can, at best, hope for informed guesses, and there is considerable room for honest people (not to mention rogues with vested interests) to disagree.
THE BASIC FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

## 估值中的可比性问题

<!--en-->
*COMPARABILITY PROBLEMS IN THE VALUATION*

金融资产

<!--en-->
OF FINANCIAL ASSETS

由于评估实物资产存在诸多困难，历史成本凭借其客观性成为了一种颇具吸引力的、尽管并不完美的解决方案。不过，某些金融资产并不会受到这些困难的影响。它们在纽约证券交易所等组织良好的市场上每日活跃交易。对于这类资产而言，依据财务报告期末的市场报价来估值，而非采用历史成本，既能保证客观性，又能确保准确性。

<!--en-->
The numerous difficulties of evaluating physical assets make historical cost an appealing, if imperfect, solution by virtue of its objectivity. Some financial assets are unaffected by those difficulties, however. They trade daily and actively in well-organized markets such as the New York Stock Exchange. It is feasible to value such assets on the basis of market quotations at the end of the financial reporting period, rather than according to historical cost, and achieve both objectivity and accuracy.

然而，分析师必须牢记：许多公司资产负债表上所列巨额金融资产的价值，无法根据流动性强、交易活跃的市场中持续报出的价格来核实。在**公允价值会计**准则下，此类资产的价值是指其在自愿交易的双方之间当前能够买卖的价格，不包括清算销售情形。如果该资产不存在活跃市场，公司可以依据类似资产的报价来确定其账面价值，前提是这些类似资产确实在活跃交易。在这种情况下，公司必须做出假设，以反映活跃交易资产与非活跃交易资产之间的差异会对市场产生的相应影响。

<!--en-->
Analysts must keep in mind, however, that the values assigned to huge amounts of financial assets on many companies' balance sheets are *not* verifiable on the basis of continuously quoted prices determined in deep, liquid markets. Under **Fair Value Accounting**, an asset of this sort is valued at the amount at which it currently could be bought or sold in a transaction between willing parties, not including a liquidation sale. If no active market for the asset exists, a company can determine its balance sheet value on the basis of quoted prices for similar assets that do trade actively. In this case, the company must make assumptions about how the market would adjust for the fact that the actively traded and non-actively-traded assets are not identical.

如果没有可比较的资产，公司可以依据自身对市场参与者在评估或竞标该资产时会采用的假设的推断来进行估值。财务报表使用者可以合理预期：部分公司对这些假设的设定会较为宽松，从而可能高估非活跃交易资产的价值。对这种自由裁量权的滥用正是安然公司欺诈案的一个因素（参见第11章）。

<!--en-->
If no comparables exist, a company can use its own assumptions about the assumptions market participants would use to offer or bid for the asset it is valuing. Users of financial statements can reasonably expect that some companies' assumptions about assumptions will be on the liberal side, potentially inflating the value of non-actively-traded assets. Abuse of this discretion was one element of the Enron fraud (see Chapter 11.)

得益于近几十年的市场创新，一大类主观估值的金融资产由非交易所交易的**衍生品**构成。（这类资产的统称反映了其估值源自其他资产的价值，如大宗商品或证券指数。）在金融市场危机期间，此类工具的买卖价格会出现剧烈波动。企业自然希望决定其股价的投资者不会看到或考虑到这类价值损失；企业通常将这些损失描述为暂时性的（但未必准确）。对于金融机构而言，更大的担忧在于监管机构可能会基于市场引发的、确实属于暂时性的衍生品账面价值下降，判定该机构已资不抵债。

<!--en-->
Thanks to market innovations of recent decades, a large category of subjectively valued financial assets consists of non-exchange-traded **derivatives**. (The collective term for these assets reflects that their valuations derive from the values of other assets, such as commodities or indexes of securities.) In a financial market crisis, the price at which such instruments can be bought or sold is subject to violent swings. Companies understandably would prefer that the investors who determine their stock prices not see or consider such losses in value, which the companies invariably (but not always correctly) characterize as temporary. For a financial institution, an even bigger worry is that its regulator will declare the institution insolvent, based on a market-induced and genuinely temporary decline in the balance sheet value of its derivatives.

鉴于这些不利因素，财务报表编制者一直抵制全面推行公允价值会计。根据《财务会计准则公告》（SFAS）第115号所体现的折中方案，金融工具的估值取决于编制财务报表的公司对其的用途定位。如果公司打算持有债务证券直至到期，则按摊余成本扣除减值后的金额记录其价值。（摊余成本是指在剩余到期期内对面值溢价进行的摊销或对面值折价进行的摊销；减值则是指因明确迹象表明债务人无法履行偿债义务而产生的价值损失。）如果公司打算近期出售债务或权益证券以赚取交易利润，则按公允价值记录该工具，并将未实现损益计入损益表。第三种选择是公司将债务或权益证券归类为既非持有至到期也非交易性证券，而是归入“可供出售”这一模糊类别。在这种情况下，该工具按公允价值记录，但未实现损益不计入损益表，而是列入其他综合收益——即股东权益中的一个独立组成部分。

<!--en-->
Seeing these disadvantages to themselves, issuers of financial statements have resisted the imposition of full-blown fair value accounting. Underthe compromise embodied in Statement of Financial Accounting Standards (SFAS) 115, financial instruments are valued according to their intended use by the company issuing the financial statements. If the company intends to hold a debt security to maturity, it records the value at amortized cost less impairment, if any. (The amortization is the write-down of a premium over face value or write-up of discount from face value, over the remaining period to maturity. Impairment is a loss of value arising from a clear indication that the obligor will be unable to satisfy the terms of the obligation.) If the company intends to sell a debt or equity security in the near term, hoping to make a trading profit, it records the instrument at fair value and includes unrealized gains and losses in earnings. A third option is for the company to classify a debt or equity security as neither held-to-maturity or a trading security, but instead in the noncommittal category of available for sale. In that case, the instrument is recorded at fair value, but unrealized gains and losses are excluded from earnings and instead reported in other comprehensive income, a separate component of shareholders' equity.

资产负债表 33

<!--en-->
The Balance Sheet
33

关键在于：同一资产在一家公司资产负债表上的估值，可能与另一家公司资产负债表上的估值存在显著差异，而这些差异源于各公司对其用途意图的不同表述。

<!--en-->
The essential point is that an asset may be valued on one company's balance sheet at a substantially different value than an identical asset is valued on another company's balance sheet, all based on the different companies' representations of their intentions.

甚至有可能在同一张资产负债表上，一项资产被记录为两种不同的价值。例如，2008年股票价值暴跌时，杠杆收购合伙企业的管理者在计提资产减值时的严格程度各不相同。许多交易涉及多家私募股权公司。大学捐赠基金或养老金计划发起人可能是某家由两家或以上私募股权基金持有的私营公司的有限合伙人，而这些基金对该公司的估值并不一致。因此，在该机构的资产负债表上，相同股份的价值基础实际上是不同的估值结果。

<!--en-->
It is even possible for an asset to be carried at two different values on a single balance sheet. For instance, when equity values plummeted in 2008, managers of leveraged buyout partnerships varied in the severity with which they wrote down their holdings. Many deals were shared by multiple private equity firms. A university endowment fund or pension plan sponsor might be a limited partner in a privately owned company held by two or more private equity funds that placed different values on the company. Underlying the value for those funds on the institution's balance sheet would be nonequivalent valuations of identical shares.

即便没有私募股权公司等外部方的参与，不一致的估值也可能损害企业资产负债表的完整性。对2008年9月雷曼兄弟破产的调查发现，这家投资银行内每个交易台都有自己的一套资产定价方法。

<!--en-->
Inconsistent valuations can also undermine the integrity of an enterprise's balance sheet without involvement of outside parties such as private equity firms. An inquest into the September 2008 bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers found that each trading desk within the investment bank had its own methodology for pricing assets.

即便是同一资产类别内部，定价方法也存在差异；而本应负责强制实施估值标准化的产品控制小组，人员配备却不足以完成此项任务。顺便提一下，雷曼兄弟采用的一些方法至少可以说是值得怀疑的。例如，该投行在2008年第二季度对某类资产的定价依据是摩根士丹利当年第一季度发布的一份研究报告。⁴ 基本财务报表

<!--en-->
Methodologies differed even within a single asset class, and the Product Control Group, which was supposed to enforce standardization in valuation, was understaffed for the task. Incidentally, some of the methodologies employed at Lehman Brothers were dubious, to say the least. For example, the investment bank based its second-quarter 2008 prices for one group of assets on a Morgan Stanley research note published in the first quarter of that year.⁴
THE BASIC FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

## 价值的瞬间蒸发

<!--en-->
*INSTANTANEOUS WIPEOUT OF VALUE*

由于许多资产的价值具有高度主观性，资产负债表极易出现突然且随意的修订。举一个极端的例子：2001年7月27日，电信网络组件制造商JDS Uniphase将其商誉价值减少了448亿美元。这是当时企业史上规模最大的资产减记。

<!--en-->
Because the value of many assets is so subjective, balance sheets are prone to sudden, arbitrary revisions. To cite one dramatic example, on July 27, 2001, JDS Uniphase, a manufacturer of components for telecommunications networks, reduced the value of its goodwill by $44.8 billion. It was the largest write-off in corporate history up to that time.

这种经济价值的急剧下降并非一蹴而就。几个月前，JDS Uniphase就曾警告投资者：由于公司在20世纪90年代末电信热潮中收购的企业前景黯淡，公司将面临巨额资产减记。⁵然而，如果投资者完全依赖JDS的资产负债表，他们就会把这种价值损失视为突发事件。

<!--en-->
This drastic decline in economic value did not occur in one day. Several months earlier, JDS Uniphase had warned investors to expect a big write-off arising from declining prospects at businesses that the company had acquired during the telecommunications euphoria of the late 1990s.⁵ If investors had relied entirely on JDS's balance sheet, however, they would have perceived the loss of value as a sudden event.

就在JDS Uniphase采取这一行动前不久，北电网络曾进行了123亿美元的商誉减记，随后互联网软件和光纤领域的几家大型企业也纷纷效仿。不过，账面价值瞬间蒸发的现象并非高科技公司所独有。2000年第四季度，宣伟公司确认了3.52亿美元的减值费用（税后金额为2.936亿美元）。此次减记主要源于这家涂料及相关产品制造商通过一系列收购所形成的商誉减少。

<!--en-->
Shortly before JDS Uniphase's action, Nortel Networks took a $12.3 billion goodwill write-off, and several major companies in such areas as Internet software and optical fiber quickly followed suit. High-tech companies had no monopoly on instantaneous evaporation of book value, however. In the fourth quarter of 2000, Sherwin-Williams recognized an impairment charge of $352 million ($293.6 million after taxes). Most of the write-off represented a reduction of goodwill that the manufacturer of paint and related products had created through a string of acquisitions.

即便在遭受如此巨大的冲击后，商誉仍占宣伟公司资产的18.8%，并占股东权益的47.9%。

<!--en-->
Even after the huge hit, goodwill represented 18.8 percent of Sherwin-Williams's assets and accounted for 47.9 percent of shareholders' equity.

简而言之，传统经济企业和新经济企业都容易突然出现账面资产价值的流失。因此，财务报表使用者不应想当然地认为资产负债表上的数字必然对应资产的当前经济价值。更合理的预期是这些数字是根据公认会计原则（GAAP）计算得出的。关键在于理解这些会计惯例与现实之间的关联。

<!--en-->
Both Old Economy and New Economy companies, in short, are vulnerable to a sudden loss of stated asset value. Therefore, users of financial statements should not assume that balance sheet figures invariably correspond to the current economic worth of the assets they represent. A more reasonable expectation is that the numbers have been calculated in accordance with GAAP. The trick is to understand the relationship between these accounting conventions and reality.

如果这看起来是一项艰巨的任务，读者或许可以从评级机构的成功中获得鼓舞（参见第13章）：它们能够从繁杂的财务报告中提炼出经济实质。2001年的数十亿美元商誉减记并未如人们所料引发大规模的评级下调。与以往许多公司资产减记的情况类似，穆迪和标准普尔并未将会计价值的变化等同于对贷款人保护程度的降低。诚然，如果一家公司减记了价值十亿美元的商誉，其资产与负债比率确实会下降。

<!--en-->
If this seems a daunting task, the reader may take encouragement from the success of the bond-rating agencies (see Chapter 13) in sifting through the financial reporting folderol to get to the economic substance. The multibillion-dollar goodwill write-offs in 2001 did not, as one might have expected, set off a massive wave of rating downgrades. As in many previous instances of companies writing down assets, Moody's and Standard & Poor's did not equate changes in accounting values with reduced protection for lenders. To be sure, if a company wrote off a billion dollars' worth of goodwill, its ratio of assets to liabilities declined.

不过，其有形资产与负债的比率却并未改变。评级机构同时监控这两种比率，但通常更重视忽略商誉等无形资产的那一种。资产负债表

<!--en-->
Its ratio of *tangible* assets to liabilities did not change, however. The rating agencies monitored both ratios but had customarily attached greater significance to the version that ignored intangible assets such as goodwill.
The Balance Sheet

## 商誉到底有多“好”？

<!--en-->
*HOW GOOD IS GOODWILL?*

在20世纪90年代末的新经济热潮中，穆迪和标准普尔对无形资产的价值持怀疑态度，这与当时主流观点背道而驰。当时更流行的看法是：根据公认会计原则编制的资产负债表严重低估了计算机软件及电子商务等动态行业中企业的价值。按照这种说法，企业的盈利能力源自创新的理念和更优的经营方式，而非传统会计所依据的实体资产。新范式的倡导者宣称，为了适应经济结构的变革，会计准则制定者必须允许将各种传统上被费用化的项目资本化为资产负债表上的资产。在此背景下，那些质疑商誉价值的分析师显得相当保守——毕竟商誉长期以来一直被视为符合公认会计原则的正当项目。

<!--en-->
By maintaining a skeptical attitude to the value of intangible assets throughout the New Economy excitement of the late nineties, Moody's and Standard & Poor's were bucking the trend. The more stylish view was that balance sheets constructed according to GAAP seriously understated the value of corporations in dynamic industries such as computer software and e-commerce. Their earning power, so the story went, derived from inspired ideas and improved methods of doing business, not from the bricks and mortar for which conventional accounting was designed. To adapt to the economy's changing profile, proclaimed the heralds of the new paradigm, the accounting rule makers had to allow all sorts of items traditionally expensed to be capitalized onto the asset side of the balance sheet. Against that backdrop, analysts who questioned the value represented by goodwill, an item long deemed legitimate under GAAP, look conservative indeed.

实际上，Uniphase令人震惊的减记事件之前出现的股市狂热，恰恰典型地说明了评级机构对商誉持怀疑态度的原因。通过股票互换式收购，20世纪90年代末股价的飙升被转化为资产负债表价值的增加；尽管通常认为公司股价波动并不会改变其账面净值。

<!--en-->
In reality, the stock market euphoria that preceded Uniphase's mind-boggling write-off illustrated in classic fashion the reasons for rating agency skepticism toward goodwill. Through stock-for-stock acquisitions, the sharp rise in equity prices during the late 1990s was transformed into increased balance sheet values, despite the usual assumption that fluctuations in a company's stock price do not alter its stated net worth.

这堪称一种堪比第3章所述“股票销售所得转化为营业收入”的神奇金融炼金术。

<!--en-->
It was a form of financial alchemy as remarkable as the transmutation of proceeds from stock sales into revenues described in Chapter 3.

股价上涨与商誉增加之间的联系可通过图表2.1中的虚构案例来说明。在情景一中，联合合并公司（“Amalgamator”）和联合整合公司（“Consolidator”）的股票交易价格均为每股账面价值的1.0倍。Amalgamator的股东权益为2亿美元，Consolidator为6000万美元，这与两家公司的市值相等。Amalgamator用其库存股票以8000万美元的价格收购Consolidator。这一收购价格较当时的市场价格高出33又1/3%。

<!--en-->
The link between rising stock prices and escalating goodwill is illustrated by the fictitious example in Exhibit 2.1. In Scenario I, the shares of Associated Amalgamator Corporation ("Amalgamator") and United Consolidator Inc. ("Consolidator") are both trading at multiples of 1.0 times book value per share. Shareholders' equity is $200 million at Amalgamator and $60 million at Consolidator, equivalent to the companies' respective market capitalizations. Amalgamator uses stock held in its treasury to acquire Consolidator for $80 million. The purchase price represents a premium of 33 1/3 percent above the prevailing market price.

现在让我们来考察一个关键的信贷质量指标。在收购之前，Amalgamator的总资产与总负债比率（参见第13章）为1.25倍，而Consolidator的相应数值为1.18倍。此次换股收购并未引入任何新的有形资产（如现金、存货或厂房），交易也没有消除任何现有负债。因此从逻辑上讲，Consolidator的1.18倍比率应该会拉低Amalgamator的1.25倍比率，从而使合并后的公司比率介于两者之间。

<!--en-->
Let us now examine a key indicator of credit quality. Prior to the acquisition, Amalgamator's ratio of total assets to total liabilities (see Chapter 13) is 1.25 times, while the comparable figure for Consolidator is 1.18 times. The stock-for-stock acquisition introduces no new hard assets (e.g., cash, inventories, or factories). Neither does the transaction eliminate any existing liabilities. Logically, then, Consolidator's 1.18 times ratio should drag down Amalgamator's 1.25 times ratio, resulting in a figure somewhere in between for the combined companies.

然而实际上，交易后的总资产与总负债比率仍为1.25倍。通过向Consolidator的有形资产价值支付溢价，《基本财务报表》*附表2.1：模拟资产负债表，20XX年12月31日（省略了千美元单位）*

<!--en-->
In fact, though, the total-assets-to-total-liabilities ratio after the deal is 1.25 times. By paying a premium to Consolidator's tangible asset value,
