<!--en-->
*Ignores possible impact of earnings per share dilution.

合并方创造了2000万美元的商誉。这项无形资产仅占合并后公司总资产的1.4%，但足以使合并方在收购债务质量较差的公司时，不会在该指标上出现恶化。

<!--en-->
Amalgamator creates $20 million of goodwill. This intangible asset represents just 1.4 percent of the combined companies' total assets, but that suffices to enable Amalgamator to acquire a company with a weaker debt-quality ratio without showing any deterioration on that measure.

如果这一结果看似荒谬，不妨看看情景二。起初，股市的强劲反弹推动两家公司的股价升至账面价值的150%。然而，合并方的资产对负债比率仍为1.25倍，被合并方则为1.18倍。保守的债券投资者感到欣慰的是，资产仍按历史成本扣除折旧后在账面上反映，不受股市狂热情绪的影响——这种情绪随时可能毫无征兆地消退。与情景一类似，合并方以高于市价33又1/3%的价格收购被合并方；不过这一溢价是基于更高的市值计算的。因此，收购价格从8000万美元升至1.2亿美元。此次收购并未产生2000万美元的商誉，而是形成了6000万美元的无形资产。

<!--en-->
If this outcome seems perverse, consider Scenario II. As the scene opens, an explosive stock market rally has driven up both companies' shares to 150 percent of book value. The ratio of total assets to total liabilities, however, remains at 1.25 times for Amalgamator and 1.18 times for Consolidator. Conservative bond buyers take comfort from the fact that the assets remain on the books at historical cost less depreciation, unaffected by euphoria on the stock exchange that may dissipate at any time without notice.
The Balance Sheet
As in Scenario I, Amalgamator pays a premium of 33 1/3 percent above the prevailing market price to acquire Consolidator. The premium is calculated on a higher market capitalization, however. Consequently, the purchase price rises from $80 million to $120 million. Instead of creating $20 million of goodwill, the acquisition gives rise to a $60 million intangible asset.

当保守的债券投资者计算合并后公司的总资产对负债比率时，他们有了惊人的发现：一家资产对负债比率为1.25倍的公司与另一家比率为1.18倍的公司合并后，竟产生了1.28倍的比率。此外，稍作数字推算便会发现：如果合并方以更高价格收购被合并方，这一比率还会更高。显然，改善企业信用质量的最简单方法就是以极高的价格进行换股收购。

<!--en-->
When the conservative bond investors calculate the combined companies' ratio of total assets to total liabilities, they make a startling discovery. Somehow, putting together a company boasting a 1.25 times ratio with another sporting a 1.18 times ratio has produced an entity with a ratio of 1.28 times. Moreover, a minute of experimentation with the numbers will show that the ratio would be higher still if Amalgamator had bought Consolidator at a higher price. Seemingly, the simplest way for a company to improve its credit quality is to make stock-for-stock acquisitions at grossly excessive prices.

当然，这一荒谬的结论其实是一种谬误。实际上，在情景二中可用于偿还债权人债权的应收账款、存货及机器设备并不比情景一中更多。鉴于被合并方的总资产对负债比率低于合并方，合并后的比率理应低于合并方单独时的水平。常识也告诉我们：如果合并方为收购被合并方支付了过高价格，其信用质量并不会因此真正改善。

<!--en-->
Naturally, this absurd conclusion embodies a fallacy. In reality, the receivables, inventories, and machinery available to be sold to satisfy creditors' claims are no greater in Scenario II than in Scenario I. Given that the total-assets-to-total-liabilities ratio is lower at Consolidator than at Amalgamator, the combined companies' ratio logically must be lower than at Amalgamator. Common sense further states that Amalgamator cannot truly have better credit quality if it overpays for Consolidator than if it acquires the company at a fair price.

事实上，解决这一逻辑难题的方法很简单。

<!--en-->
As it happens, there is a simple way out of the logical conundrum.

我们在计算资产对负债比率时排除商誉因素。如图表所示，无论情景一还是情景二，合并方在收购被合并方后的*有形*资产对总负债比率均为1.23倍。这一结果最能反映经济现实。为确保得出这一符合常识的结论，信贷分析师应效仿评级机构的做法：分别计算包含商誉及其他无形资产和不含这些因素的资产负债表比率，并更重视后者。

<!--en-->
Let us exclude goodwill in calculating the ratio of assets to liabilities. As shown in the exhibit, Amalgamator's ratio of *tangible* assets to total liabilities following its acquisition of Consolidator is 1.23 times in both Scenario I and Scenario II. This is the outcome that best reflects economic reality. To ensure that they reach this commonsense conclusion, credit analysts must follow the rating agencies' practice of calculating balance sheet ratios both with and without goodwill and other intangible assets, giving greater emphasis to the latter version.

仅基于有形资产计算比率，并不等同于认为无形资产没有价值。如果合并方明天就将被合并方出售，它很可能收回全部或大部分记为商誉的6000万美元。不过这种交易可能性极低；更现实的情形是几年后股价从当前高位回落时再出售。在这种情况下，6000万美元很可能无法完全收回。

<!--en-->
Calculating ratios on a tangibles-only basis is not equivalent to saying that the intangibles have no value. Amalgamator is likely to recoup all or most of the $60 million accounted for as goodwill if it turns around and sells Consolidator tomorrow. Such a transaction is hardly likely, however. A sale several years hence, after stock prices have fallen from today's lofty levels, is a more plausible scenario. Under such conditions, the full $60 million probably will not be recoverable.

即便不考虑股价暴跌的可能性，在基于资产负债表的信用质量分析中剔除或大幅淡化商誉的价值也是极为合理的。

<!--en-->
Even leaving aside the possibility of a plunge in stock prices, it makes eminent sense to eliminate or sharply downplay the value of goodwill in a balance-sheet-based analysis of credit quality.

与存货或应收账款不同，商誉并非能够轻易出售或**贴现**以换取现金的资产。企业也无法像处置厂房和设备那样，对其商誉进行**售后回租**。简而言之，商誉并非管理层可以转换为现金或用以筹集资金以摆脱财务困境的可分离资产。因此，商誉在资产保护分析中的相关性值得怀疑。

<!--en-->
Unlike inventories or accountsreceivable, goodwill is not an asset that can be readily sold or **factored** to raise cash. Neither can a company enter into a **sale-leaseback** of its goodwill, as it can with its plant and equipment. In short, goodwill is not a separable asset that management can either convert into cash or use to raise cash to extricate itself from a financial tight spot. Therefore, the relevance of goodwill to an analysis of asset protection is questionable.

基本财务报表

<!--en-->
THE BASIC FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

总体而言，评级机构在20世纪90年代似乎展现了明智的判断力，抵制住了新经济的诱惑。尽管当时人们对各种无形资产的热情高涨，但它们仍继续以仅包含有形资产的版本来计算关键的资产负债表比率。因此，当企业突然削减其无形资产时，穆迪和标准普尔对它们的评价并未发生改变。

<!--en-->
On the whole, the rating agencies appear to have shown sound judgment during the 1990s by resisting the New Economy's siren song. While enthusiasm mounted for all sorts of intangible assets, they continued to gear their analysis to tangible-assets-only versions of key balance sheet ratios. By and large, therefore, companies did not alter the way they were perceived by Moody's and Standard & Poor's when they suddenly took an ax to their intangible assets.

更普遍地说，资产减记并不会导致评级下降。当然，偶尔减记公告会与先前未披露的价值减值同时出现，这种减值通常源于经营问题。

<!--en-->
More generally, asset write-offs do not cause ratings to fall. Occasionally, to be sure, the announcement of a write-off coincides with the disclosure of a previously unrevealed impairment of value, ordinarily arising from operating problems.

此类情况可能会引发评级下调。此外，减记有时恰逢企业决定关闭某些业务。相关的遣散费（支付给被解雇员工的款项）可能构成一笔数额庞大的现金支出，从而削弱企业的财务状况。最后，减记还可能导致企业违反债务契约（参见第12章）。紧张的贷款人可能会利用这种**技术性违约**来取消企业的信贷额度，进而引发**流动性**危机。不过，单凭调整资产负债表以反映经济现实这一行为，并不等同于信用保护措施的减少。

<!--en-->
That sort of development may trigger a downgrade. In addition, a write-off sometimes coincides with a decision to close down certain operations. The associated severance costs (payments to terminated employees) may represent a substantial cash outlay that does weaken the company's financial position. Finally, a write-off can put a company in violation of a debt covenant (see Chapter 12). Nervous lenders may exploit the **technical default** by canceling the company's credit lines, precipitating a **liquidity** crisis. In and of itself, however, adjusting the balance sheet to economic reality does not represent a reduction in credit protection measures.

## 以传统方式导致的价值缩水

<!--en-->
*LOSING VALUE THE OLD-FASHIONED WAY*

像JDS Uniphase这样的科技公司进行的商誉减记会在财经新闻中掀起波澜，但这绝非资产负债表资产价值突然大幅缩水的唯一原因。在“旧经济”中，无数制造商在低技术工业产品上获得的利润微薄，因此这些企业很容易面临长期盈利能力的侵蚀。常见的陷阱包括激烈的价格竞争，以及由于短期现金流压力而未能充分投资于厂房和设备的现代化。随着固定资产回报率下降，造纸、化工和钢铁等工业产品的生产商最终不得不面对其账面资产价值的永久性减值。

<!--en-->
Goodwill write-offs by technology companies such as JDS Uniphase make splashy headlines in the financial news, but they by no means represent the only way in which balance sheet assets suddenly and sharply decline in value. In the Old Economy, where countless manufacturers earn slender margins on low-tech industrial goods, companies are vulnerable to long-run erosion in profitability. Common pitfalls include fierce price competition and a failure, because of near-term pressures to conserve cash, to invest adequately in modernization of plants and equipment. As the rate of return on their fixed assets declines, producers of industrial commodities such as paper, chemicals, and steel must eventually face up to the permanent impairment of their reported asset values.

对于回报率长期偏低的企业而言，要精确预测未来会计价值的缩减幅度是不可能的。事实上，无法保证企业能完全纠正其虚高的净资产价值，尤其是在初次调整时。不过，分析师可以通过将资产负债表上显示的股东权益调整为可比公司通常获得的回报率，来估算未来减记的大致规模。

<!--en-->
It is not feasible, in the case of a chronically low rate-of-return company, to predict precisely the magnitude of a future reduction in accounting values.
The Balance Sheet
Indeed, there is no guarantee that a company will fully come to grips with its overstated net worth, especially on the first round. To estimate the expected order of magnitude of future write-offs, however, an analyst can adjust the shareholders' value shown on the balance sheet to the rate of return typically being earned by comparable corporations.

举例来说，假设Z公司过去五年的平均净利润为2400万美元。由于该公司的大部分盈利都用于发放股息，其股东权益一直停留在约3亿美元的水平。再假设在同一时期，标准普尔400指数中工业企业的平均回报率为14%。

<!--en-->
To illustrate, suppose Company Z's average net income over the past five years has been $24 million. With most of the company's modest earnings being paid out in dividends, shareholders' equity has been stagnant at around $300 million. Assume further that during the same period, the average return of companies in the Standard & Poor's 400 index of industrial corporations has been 14 percent.

3亿美元这个数字能否准确代表Z公司的股权价值呢？如果可以的话，那就意味着投资者愿意持有该公司的股票并接受仅8%的回报率（2400万美元除以3亿美元），即便其他股票能提供14%的回报率。然而，没有明显理由说明投资者会自愿做出这种牺牲。因此，Z公司的账面价值几乎肯定被高估了。

<!--en-->
Does the figure $300 million accurately represent Company Z's equity value? If so, the implication is that investors are willing to own the company's shares and accept a return of only 8 percent ($24 million divided by $300 million), even though a 14 percent return is available on other stocks. There is no obvious reason that investors would voluntarily make such a sacrifice, however. Therefore, Company Z's book value is almost certainly overstated.

对这家低利润公司真实股权价值的合理估算，应是能够产生相当于市场平均水平回报率的数值：

<!--en-->
A reasonable estimate of the low-profit company's true equity value would be the amount that produces a return on equity equivalent to the going rate:

$$ \frac{\text{Company Z average earnings stream}}{X} = \begin{array}{l} \text{Average return on equity} \\ \text{for U.S. corporations} \end{array} $$

$$ \frac{\$24 \text{ million}}{X} = 14\% $$

$$ X = \$171 \text{ million} $$

尽管作为一般性指导原则很有用，但这种调整业绩不佳公司股东权益的方法忽略了诸多重要的细微差别。一方面，Z公司可能被认为比普通公司风险更高。在这种情况下，股东会要求高于14%的回报率才会持有其股票。此外，现金流或许比净利润更能反映公司的经济表现。这意味着调整应基于现金流与市值的比率，而非股本回报率。再者，投资者的回报要求反映的是预期未来收益，而非过去业绩。根据该公司业务前景的不同，可以合理推测Z公司在未来五年内的利润要么会高于过去五年，要么会进一步下滑。同样，证券分析师可能预计，作为替代投资的同类股票组合在未来几年的回报率会高于或低于14%。看来，分析师越是试图探寻真实价值，这一概念就越显得模糊不清。《基本财务报表》

<!--en-->
Although useful as a general guideline, this method of adjusting the shareholders' equity of underperforming companies neglects a number of important subtleties. For one thing, Company Z may be considered riskier than the average company. In that case, shareholders would demand a return higher than 14 percent to hold its shares. Furthermore, cash flow may be a better indicator of the company's economic performance than net income. This would imply that the adjustment ought to be made to the ratio of cash flow to market capitalization, rather than return on equity. Furthermore, investors' rate-of-return requirements reflect expected future earnings, rather than past results. Depending on the outlook for its business, it might be reasonable to assume that Company Z will either realize higher profits in the next five years than in the past five or see its profits plunge further. By the same token, securities analysts may expect the peer group of stocks thatrepresent alternative investments to produce a return higher or lower than 14 percent in coming years. The further the analyst travels in search of true value, it seems, the murkier the notion becomes.
THE BASIC FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

## 真正的权益难以捉摸

<!--en-->
*TRUE EQUITY IS ELUSIVE*

金融分析师实际上所寻求却无法在财务报表中找到的，正是经济学家所定义的权益。在学术研究中，“权益”一词通常并非指会计账面价值，而是指归属于企业所有者的未来现金流的现值。试想一家企业凭借某项商标获得巨额收益，但由于该商标是**内部开发**而非收购所得，因此在会计上并无价值。该商标所带来的利润的现值会被纳入经济学家对权益的定义中，却不被会计师认可，这可能导致两者之间的差额高达数十亿美元。

<!--en-->
What financial analysts are actually seeking, but are unable to find in the financial statements, is equity as economists conceive of it. In scholarly studies, the term *equity* generally refers not to accounting book value, but to the present value of future cash flows accruing to the firm's owners. Consider a firm that is deriving huge earnings from a trademark that has no accounting value because it was developed **internally** rather than acquired. The present value of the profits derived from the trademark would be included in the economist's definition of equity but not in the accountant's, potentially creating a gap of billions of dollars between the two.

经济学家与会计师对权益概念的差异在“负权益”现象中表现得尤为明显。按照经济学家的说法，权益为负等同于破产。其逻辑在于：当公司的负债超过所有未来收入的**现值**时，所有者继续偿还债务便不再合乎理性。他们会停止向贷款人和贸易债权人支付到期款项，进而促使债权人通过迫使公司破产来追回债权。

<!--en-->
The contrast between the economist's and the accountant's notions of equity is dramatized by the phenomenon of negative equity. In the economist's terms, equity of less than zero is synonymous with bankruptcy. The reasoning is that when a company's liabilities exceed the **present value** of all future income, it is not rational for the owners to continue paying off the liabilities. They will stop making payments currently due to lenders and trade creditors, which will in turn prompt the holders of the liabilities to try to recover their claims by forcing the company into bankruptcy.

另一方面，假设一家非常成功的公司未来收入的现值远超其负债价值。如果该公司遭遇厄运，连续多年录得净亏损并注销部分业务，其资产的账面价值可能会低于负债价值。从会计角度看，结果就是股东权益为负。然而，资产的经济价值仍可能高于负债的账面值。在此情况下，公司没有理由暂停向债权人付款或申请破产。

<!--en-->
Suppose, on the other hand, that the present value of a highly successful company's future income exceeds the value of its liabilities by a substantial margin. If the company runs into a patch of bad luck, recording net losses for several years running and writing off selected operations, the book value of its assets may fall below the value of its liabilities. In accounting terms, the result is negative shareholders' equity. The economic value of the assets, however, may still exceed the stated value of the liabilities. Under such circumstances, the company has no reason to consider either suspending payments to creditors or filing for bankruptcy.

西联汇款公司于2006年9月从第一数据公司分拆出来的案例表明，会计意义上的负权益并不等同于资不抵债。此次分拆中，这家汇款服务提供商以现金和债务证券形式向第一数据公司支付了约35亿美元。扣除同期其他事项的影响后，截至2006年12月31日，股东权益从一年前的28亿美元降至-3.148亿美元。通过在随后三年里保持稳健盈利，西联汇款到2009年12月31日已将股东权益提升至3.535亿美元。

<!--en-->
The Western Union Company's September 2006 spin-off from First Data Corporation demonstrated that negative equity in an accounting sense is not synonymous with insolvency. In connection with the spin-off, the provider of money transfer services distributed approximately $3.5 billion to First Data in the form of cash and debt securities. Net of other events during the period, shareholders' equity fell to -$314.8 million on December 31, 2006, from $2.8 billion one year earlier. By producing solid earnings over the next three years, Western Union boosted shareholders' equity to $353.5 million by December 31, 2009.

任何将2006年底的负数数值误认为是西联汇款经济价值指标的人，都会认为其股票在每股18.85美元的价格下被严重高估。然而，截至2009年底，西联汇款的股价表现远优于整个股市。标准普尔500指数下跌了21.4%，而西联汇款的跌幅仅为15.9%。《资产负债表》

<!--en-->
Anyone who mistook the year-end2006 negative figure as an indication of Western Union's economic value would have deemed its stock grossly overvalued at $18.85 a share. Through the end of 2009, however, Western Union shares performed far better than the stock market as a whole. The Standard & Poor's 500 Index fell by 21.4 percent versus a decline of only 15.9 percent for Western Union.
The Balance Sheet

### 市场导向型权益数据的利弊

<!--en-->
*PROS AND CONS OF A MARKET-BASED EQUITY FIGURE*

依赖市值是一种实用的方法，金融分析师通常借此来估算经济学家所定义的、更为严谨的权益概念——即预期未来现金流的现值。若试图通过传统的财务报告系统得出这一数值，则会面临巨大的困难。问题在于，传统会计体系偏爱那些能够客观计量的项目；不幸的是，未来的盈利和现金流是无法直接观测的。此外，计算现值需要选定一个代表公司**资本成本**的**折现率**。确定资本成本在金融领域是个极具争议的话题，其中还涉及复杂的税务因素和风险调整。简而言之，用于计算经济学家所定义的权益的数值，并非会计师乐于处理的那种数字；他们理想中的数值是发票上的价格，且能通过已兑现的支票来独立验证。

<!--en-->
Relying on market capitalization is the practical means by which financial analysts commonly estimate the economists' more theoretically rigorous definition of equity as the present value of expected future cash flows. Monumental difficulties confront anyone who instead attempts to arrive at the figure through conventional financial reporting systems. The problem is that traditional accounting favors items that can be objectively measured. Unfortunately, future earnings and cash flows are unobservable. Moreover, calculating present value requires selecting a **discount rate** representing the company's **cost of capital**. Determining the cost of capital is a notoriously controversial subject in the financial field, complicated by thorny tax considerations and risk adjustments. The figures needed to calculate economists' equity are not, in short, the kind of numbers accountants like to deal with. Their ideal value is a price on an invoice that can be independently verified by a canceled check.

除了计算相对简便之外，市值还具有其他优势。一方面，它反映了大量分析师和投资者的共识——他们持续监测公司的未来盈利前景，并以此作为评估基础。

<!--en-->
Market capitalization has additional advantages beyond its comparative ease of calculation. For one thing, it represents the consensus of large numbers of analysts and investors who constantly monitor companies' future earnings prospects as the basis for their evaluations.

此外，股市开盘的任何一天都能计算出最新的市值数据。这与资产负债表中显示的股东权益相比具有显著优势，因为后者每三个月才更新一次。市值能迅速对各类新闻做出反应，比如竞争对手突然推出新产品、关键工厂因爆炸而停产，或是美联储突然上调利率等。相比之下，这些事件未必能在账面价值中以明确、可识别的方式体现出来。市值的坚定支持者认为，没有比这更精确的真正权益价值估算方法了。

<!--en-->
In addition, an up-to-the-minute market capitalization can be calculated on any day that the stock exchange is open. This represents a considerable advantage over the shareholders' equity shown on the balance sheet, which is updated only once every three months. Market capitalization adjusts instantaneously to news such as a surprise product launch by a competitor, an explosion that halts production at a key plant, or a sudden hike in interest rates by the Federal Reserve. In contrast, these events may never be reflected in book value in a discrete, identifiable manner. Ardent advocates of market capitalization cannot conceive of any more accurate estimate of true equity value.

然而，面对这些优势，分析师也必须权衡依赖市值来估算公司实际权益价值的若干弊端。虽然竞争性市场中形成的报价确实具有客观性，但这种报价仅适用于有公开交易股票的公司。对于私营企业，市值支持者通常会参考行业内的上市同行公司来推算其真实权益。例如，要计算一家私营造纸企业的权益，分析师可能会用上市同行公司的平均市盈率（参见第14章）乘以该私营企业的盈利额。

<!--en-->
Against these advantages, however, the analyst must weigh several drawbacks to relying on market capitalization to estimate a company's actual equity value. For one thing, while the objectivity of a price quotation established in a competitive market is indeed a benefit, it is obtainable only for corporations with publicly traded stocks. For privately owned companies,the proponents of market capitalization typically generate a proxy for true equity through reference to industry-peer public companies. For example, to calculate the equity of a privately owned paper producer, an analyst might multiply the publicly traded peer group's average price-earnings ratio (see Chapter 14) by the private company's earnings.

通常，同行公司的乘数基于**EBITDA**（参见第8章）而非净利润。这种方法还能将那些虽已不再上市但近期通过杠杆收购被纳入的企业纳入同行范围。不过，同行比较法的局限性在于它无法反映企业特有的因素，因此也就无法体现出使用市值作为实际权益价值衡量标准的主要优势。《基本财务报表》

<!--en-->
Often, the peer-group multiple is based on **EBITDA** (see Chapter 8) rather than net income. This method can expand the peer group to include companies no longer publicly traded but recently acquired in leveraged buyouts. A limitation of the peer-group approach is that it fails to capture company-specific factors and therefore does not reap one major benefit of using market capitalization as a gauge of actual equity value.
THE BASIC FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

即便分析师仅将市值应用于上市公司，仍可能遇到陷阱。例如，2008年10月22日，**道琼斯工业平均指数**下跌了190点，跌幅达5.7%。作为道指成分股的华特迪士尼公司股价暴跌8.9%，导致市值损失40亿美元，而当天该公司并未传出任何重大负面消息。不到一周时间，股市指数便收复了失地，迪士尼的股价也仅用了九天便回升至10月21日的水平。

<!--en-->
Even if analysts restrict their reliance on market capitalization to publicly traded companies, they will still encounter pitfalls. Consider, for example, that on October 22, 2008, the **Dow Jones Industrial Average** plunged by 190 points, or 5.7 percent. The price of Dow component Walt Disney plummeted by 8.9 percent, representing a $4 billion loss in market value, without any major negative news reported about the entertainment company that day. Less than a week later, the stock market gauge had fully recovered its loss, and Disney's shares took just nine days to rebound to their October 21 level.

尽管从理论上看，市值可以被视为公司的真实权益价值，但像2008年10月22日迪士尼所经历的那种短期剧烈波动，仍提醒我们需保持警惕。

<!--en-->
Notwithstanding the theoretical arguments for regarding market capitalization as a company's true equity value, short-run changes of the magnitude experienced by Disney on October 22, 2008, raise a caution.

从字面意义上理解，即便是市值出现巨大且突然的波动，也意味着公司盈利前景发生了变化。不过在极端情况下，公司股票总价值的暂时变动似乎更能反映股市的运行规律。这一观点得到了行为金融学领域大量研究的支持。与传统的金融经济学家不同，行为金融学家并不认为投资者总能准确处理信息，并按照经济学家定义的理性规则行事。行为金融学派的实证研究表明，市场价格往往会对新闻事件反应过度，而非如实反映公司的内在价值。尽管投资者理应根据预期未来股息来评估股票（见第14章），但行为金融学家发现，股市的波动性远远超出了股息变动所能解释的范围。⁶当然，这些结论仍存在争议。传统派对支撑这些结论的实证研究提出了质疑，从而引发了激烈的争论。不过，行为金融学的研究成果至少为那些难以相信“一天之内数十亿市值的蒸发就能比财务报表数据更真实地反映公司权益价值变化”的分析师提供了理论依据。

<!--en-->
In a literal interpretation, even a huge, sudden swing in market capitalization indicates a change in a company's earnings prospects. In extreme cases, though, a temporary shift in the aggregate value of a company's shares can appear to reveal more about the dynamics of the stock market. An inference along those lines is supported by extensive academic research conducted under the rubric of behavioral finance. In contrast to more traditional financial economists, the behavioralists doubt that investors invariably process information accurately and act on it according to rules of rationality, as defined by economists. Empirical studies by adherents of behavioral finance show that instead of faithfully tracking companies' intrinsic values, market prices frequently overreact to news events. Even though investors supposedly evaluate stocks on the basis of expected future dividends (see Chapter 14), the behavioralists find that the stock market is far more volatile than the variability of dividends can explain.⁶
To be sure, these conclusions remain controversial. Traditionalists have challenged the empirical studies that underlie them, producing a vigorous debate. Nevertheless, the findings of behavioral finance lend moral support to analysts who find it hard to believe that the one-day erasure of billions of market capitalization must automatically be a truer representation ofthe company's change in equity value than a figure derived from financial statement data.

因此，资产负债表和市值都是有用的工具，但不应盲目依赖。归根结底，真实的权益价值仍是一个难以确定的数字。分析师不应执着于理论上的纯粹性，而应采取灵活的态度，选择在特定场景下最适用的权益价值衡量方式。

<!--en-->
The Balance Sheet
Market capitalization, then, is a useful tool but not one to be heeded blindly. In the end, true equity remains an elusive number. Instead of striving for theoretical purity on the matter, analysts should adopt a flexible attitude, using the measure of equity value most useful to a particular application.

例如，资产负债表上主要基于历史成本的数据，在评估公司违反贷款契约风险时至关重要——这类契约通常要求维持最低的债务与净资产比率（见第12章）。而在旨在衡量债权人资产保障程度的清算分析中，历史成本数据的相关性则较低。也就是说，如果公司被出售以偿还债务，其成交价格很可能更接近市场对其资产的当前估值，而非这些资产的账面成本。

<!--en-->
For example, stated balance sheet figures, derived mainly from historical cost, are the ones that matter in estimating the risk that a company will violate a loan covenant requiring maintenance of a minimum ratio of debt to net worth (see Chapter 12). The historical cost figures are less relevant to a liquidation analysis aimed at gauging creditors' asset protection. That is, if a company were sold to pay off its debts, the price it would fetch would probably reflect the market's current valuation of its assets more nearly than the carrying cost of those assets.

然而，这两种衡量方式都难以精确等同于公司实际出售时所获得的资金。从决定出售到执行期间，由于股市波动的影响，公司的市值可能会发生显著变化。同样，某些资产的当前账面价值可能因价值减损未被及时确认而被高估，或因禁止对未易主资产进行增值调整而被低估。

<!--en-->
Neither measure, however, could be expected to equate precisely to the proceeds that would actually be realized in a sale of the company. Between the time that a sale was decided on and executed, its market capitalization might change significantly, purely as a function of the stock market's dynamics. By the same token, the current balance sheet values of certain assets could be overstated, through tardy recognition of impairments in value, or understated, reflecting the prohibition on writing up an asset that has not changed hands.

#### 通用格式的资产负债表

<!--en-->
*THE COMMON FORM BALANCE SHEET*

正如2001年科技公司的大规模资产减值所显示的那样，公司财务状况的恶化可能令投资者措手不及——因为这种变化是逐步发生的，却突然被披露出来。即便财务风险的增加已被及时报告，分析师也可能难以察觉。许多公司会以渐进的方式调整资产结构或融资方式。为了发现这些微妙却往往重要的变化，编制通用格式的资产负债表会很有帮助。

<!--en-->
As the technology companies' huge 2001 write-offs demonstrate, deterioration in a company's financial position may catch investors by surprise because it occurs gradually and is reported suddenly. It is also possible for an increase in financial risk to sneak up on analysts even though it is reported as it occurs. Many companies alter the mix of their assets, or their methods of financing them, in a gradual fashion. To spot these subtle yet frequently significant changes, it is helpful to prepare a common form balance sheet.

通用格式的资产负债表也被称为百分比资产负债表，它将每项资产转换为占总资产的百分比，将每项负债或权益项目转换为占总负债及股东权益的百分比。图表2.2将这一方法应用于星巴克2009年的资产负债表，该公司是一家咖啡加工与销售商。

<!--en-->
Also known as the percentage balance sheet, the common form balance sheet converts each asset into a percentage of total assets and each liability or component of equity into a percentage of total liabilities and shareholders' equity. Exhibit 2.2 applies this technique to the 2009 balance sheet of Starbucks, a processor and marketer of coffee.

分析师可以通过查看公司连续几个季度的通用格式资产负债表，来判断诸如存货占总资产的比例是否显著增加。这种增长可能预示着因意外需求放缓而导致的**非自愿性存货积压**。

<!--en-->
The analyst can view a company's common form balance sheets over several quarters to check, for example, whether inventory is increasing significantly as a percentage of total assets. An increase of that sort might signal **involuntary inventory buildup** resulting from an unanticipated slowdown in

sales. Similarly, a rise in accounts receivable as a percentage of assets may point to increasing reliance on the extension of credit to generate sales or a problem in collecting on credit previously extended. Over a longer period, a rise in the percentage of assets represented by a manufacturing company's property, plant, and equipment can signal that a company's business is becoming more capital-intensive. By implication, fixed costs are probably rising as a percentage of revenues, making the company's earnings more volatile.

## 结论

<!--en-->
*CONCLUSION*

通过仔细审视资产负债表中反映的基础价值，本章强调了采用批判性而非被动的方式来分析财务报表的必要性。关于股本回报率、商誉以及**杠杆性资本重组**的讨论，凸显了本章的核心主题——真实价值的难以捉摸。仅仅对历史成本惯例进行微调，无法使会计价值与经济学家所定义的权益相符，更无法达到财务分析师所期望的理想状态。在许多情况下，市值或许是一种更优的衡量方式。然而在某些情况下，公司股价作为价值标准的有效性可能会受到严重质疑。归根结底，财务报表使用者不能仅依赖某种方法得出的数字，而必须运用判断力来得出合理的结论。

<!--en-->
By closely examining the underlying values reflected in the balance sheet, this chapter emphasizes the need for a critical, rather than a passive, approach to financial statement analysis. The discussions of return on equity, goodwill, and **leveraged recapitalizations** underscore the chapter's dominant theme, the elusiveness of true value. Mere tinkering with the conventions of historical cost cannot bring accounting values into line with equity as economists define it and, more to the point, as financial analysts would ideally like it to be. Market capitalization probably represents a superior approach in many instances. Under certain circumstances, however, serious questions can be raised about the validity of a company's stock price as a standard of value. In the final analysis, users of financial statements cannot retreat behind the numbers derived by any one method. They must instead exercise judgment to draw sound conclusions.

第三章

<!--en-->
CHAPTER 3

### 利润表

<!--en-->
*The Income Statement*

分析利润表的目的，本质上在于判断其所反映的情况是好、坏还是一般。为实现这一目的，分析师会先得出一些初步结论，随后通过将该利润表与以往期间的利润表以及其他公司的利润表进行对比，来将其置于具体背景中加以考量。这些步骤将在本章题为“让数字说话”的部分中详细阐述。

<!--en-->
The goal of analyzing an income statement is essentially to determine whether the story it tells is good, bad, or indifferent. To accomplish this objective, the analyst draws a few initial conclusions, then puts the income statement into context by comparing it with income statements of earlier periods, as well as statements of other companies. These steps are described in the section of this chapter titled “Making the Numbers Talk.”

简单的分析技巧就能从利润表中提取大量信息，但信息的质量与数量同样重要。一位严谨的分析师必须确定该报表在多大程度上准确反映了发行方的收入、费用和盈利情况。这种更深层次的审视要求分析师意识到会计系统中可能扭曲经济现实的各种缺陷。

<!--en-->
Simple techniques of analysis can extract a great deal of information from an income statement, but the quality of the information is no less a concern than the quantity. A conscientious analyst must determine how accurately the statement reflects the issuer's revenues, expenses, and earnings. This deeper level of scrutiny requires an awareness of imperfections in the accounting system that can distort economic reality.

题为“数字的真实性究竟如何？”的部分记录了发行方为利用这些漏洞而不断想出新招的执着程度。分析师也必须具备同样的应变能力。尤其是财务报表研究者，必须紧跟那些将不断上涨的股票价值转化为质量存疑的收入的各种创新手段。

<!--en-->
The section titled “How Real Are the Numbers?” documents the indefatigability of issuers in devising novel gambits for exploiting these vulnerabilities. Analysts must be equally resourceful. In particular, students of financial statements must keep up with innovations in transforming rising stock values into revenues of dubious quality.

### 让数字说话

<!--en-->
*MAKING THE NUMBERS TALK*

仅通过观察原始形式的利润表，读者就能得出若干有用但有限的结论。例如，Peet's Coffee & Tea公司2009年的利润表（图表3.1）显示，该公司处于盈利而非亏损状态。该表还揭示了该公司的成本结构：销售成本（COGS）是总成本中最大的组成部分，约为销售、一般及行政费用（SG&A）的10倍；折旧与摊销在短期内属于固定费用，因此影响较小。

<!--en-->
By observing an income statement in its raw form, the reader can make several useful, albeit limited, observations. Peet's Coffee & Tea's income statement for 2009 (Exhibit 3.1) shows, for example, that the company was profitable rather than unprofitable. The statement also provides some sense of the firm's cost structure. Cost of goods sold (COGS) was the largest component of total costs, at about 10 times selling, general, and administrative expenses (SG&A). Depreciation and amortization, essentially a fixed expense in the short run, was a minor factor.

基于这些观察结果，我们可以推断：Peet's公司的盈利能力对原材料和劳动力价格的变化极为敏感。《基本财务报表》*图表3.1 Peet's Coffee & Tea Inc.利润表（单位：百万美元）*

<!--en-->
Based on these observations, we can infer that Peet's profitability is highly sensitive to changes in the prices of materials and labor that are

各项成本成分的相对重要性在很大程度上取决于皮特公司的业务模式。该公司的业务包括通过自有零售店、杂货店网络、宅配服务、办事处以及餐厅和餐饮服务商渠道销售茶叶、咖啡、特色食品及相关商品。对于需要大型生产设施的重型制造企业（如钢铁厂、汽车厂）而言，折旧在损益表中占比较大。皮特公司的损益表中没有研发和利息支出这两项对许多其他公司而言属于重要成本项目的类别。对于制药商以及从事电子产品和计算机软件开发与营销的公司来说，研发通常是重要的成本要素；同样，利息支出也是银行和金融公司以及电力公用事业公司的重要成本。与没有未偿债务的皮特公司不同，这些公司大量借贷，因此它们的利润对利率波动的敏感度比皮特公司更高。

<!--en-->
The relative importance of the various cost components is largely a function of Peet's business, which consists of selling tea, coffee, specialty foods, and related merchandise through its own retail stores, as well as a network of grocery stores, home delivery operations, offices, and restaurant and food service accounts. Depreciation is a larger component of the incomestatements of heavy manufacturing companies that require huge production facilities (e.g., steel mills, automobile plants).
The Income Statement
Peet's income statement is void in two categories that are significant cost items for many other companies—research and development (R&D) and interest expense. For pharmaceutical producers and companies that create and market electronics and computer software, R&D is generally a significant cost element. Similarly, interest expense is an important cost for banks and finance companies, as well as for electric utilities. Unlike Peet's, which has no debt outstanding, those companies borrow heavily, so their profits are more sensitive than Peet's to fluctuations in interest rates.

即便在同一行业内，由于商业模式和财务政策的不同，各公司的费用构成也会有所差异。图表3.2展示了这一点，该图比较了皮特咖啡茶公司、咖啡连锁店星巴克以及专营烘焙食品的潘娜拉面包公司这三家通过零售店销售产品的食品和饮料公司的损益表。为了便于比较，图表中将各公司损益表的组成部分转换为占营收的百分比。需要注意的是，百分比分解也有助于比较单家公司当年业绩与往年表现，或基于成本控制效率来对比两家不同的公司。

<!--en-->
Even within an industry, the breakdown of expenses can vary from company to company as a function of differing business models and financial policies. This is illustrated by Exhibit 3.2, which compares the income statements of Peet's Coffee & Tea and two other food and beverage companies that sell through retail stores, coffee shop operator Starbucks and Panera Bread, which specializes in baked goods. To facilitate the comparison, the exhibit converts the components of the companies' income statements to percentages of revenues. Note that percentage breakdowns are also helpful for comparing a single company's performance with its results in previous years and for comparing two different companies on the basis of their effectiveness in controlling costs.

与皮特公司类似，星巴克也通过零售店及其他营销渠道销售整豆咖啡、饮品相关配件及其他食品。然而，尽管同属一个行业，其成本结构却大不相同。星巴克的销货成本仅占营收的43.25%，而皮特公司这一比例则高达79.83%。另一方面，星巴克将营收的39.04%用于销售、一般及行政费用，而皮特公司这一比例仅为7.87%。

<!--en-->
Like Peet's, Starbucks roasts and sells whole-bean coffee, beverage-related accessories, and other food items through retail stores and other marketing channels. Despite being in the same line of business, however, it has a much different cost structure. Its COGS represents only 43.25 percent of revenue versus 79.83 percent for Peet's. On the other hand, Starbucks spends 39.04 percent of its revenue dollar on SGA versus only 7.87 percent for Peet's.

另一个区别在于星巴克使用了债务融资，因此会产生少量的利息支出。

<!--en-->
One other difference is that Starbucks employs debt and therefore incurs a modest amount of interest expense.

两家公司成本结构的显著差异反映了它们商业模式的不同。星巴克更侧重通过其遍布各地的门店进行咖啡零售，而皮特公司的销售则更多地依赖其他营销渠道。本质上讲，皮特公司更像是一家咖啡烘焙商，而星巴克则更侧重于现场为消费者冲泡咖啡。

<!--en-->
The dramatic difference in cost structures reflects differences in the two companies' business models. Starbucks more heavily emphasizes retailing of coffee through its ubiquitous stores, while Peet's sales are proportionately more concentrated in its other marketing channels. In essence, Peet's is more of a coffee roaster, and Starbucks is more involved in brewing coffee to serve to consumers on premise.

导致行业内成本结构差异的另一个因素可能是**规模经济**的存在，这一点将在后文讨论。不过，规模较大并不必然能带来更高的营业利润率。2009年，星巴克的营收是皮特公司的30多倍，其营业利润占营收的比例也确实更高，达到9.74%，而皮特公司为7.42%。另一方面，2009年潘娜拉面包公司的营收仅约为星巴克的七分之一，但其营业利润率却达到了10.62%，高于星巴克的9.74%。潘娜拉面包公司的*图表3.2 星巴克公司、潘娜拉面包公司和皮特咖啡茶公司的损益表（单位：百万美元）*

<!--en-->
Another factor that may give rise to differences in cost structures within an industry is the availability of **economies of scale**, as discussed later. Greater size does not invariably confer an advantage in operating margin, however. Starbucks had more than 30 times the revenue of Peet's in 2009 and did in fact achieve a higher percentage of operating income to revenues, 9.74 percent versus 7.42 percent. On the other hand, Panera Bread had only about one-seventh the revenues of Starbucks in 2009, yet achieved a 10.62 percent operating margin versus Starbucks's 9.74 percent. Panera's

THE BASIC FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

销售成本占销售额的比例高达66.82%，是星巴克43.25%的两倍多；但其销售、一般及行政费用比率却低得多，仅为6.14%，而星巴克则高达39.04%。

<!--en-->
COGS as a percentage of sales was half again as great as Starbucks's, at 66.82 percent versus 43.25 percent. Its advantage was in a far lower SG&A expense ratio, 6.14 percent versus 39.04 percent.

这种截然不同的成本结构反映了两家公司商业模式上的重大差异。截至2009年底，Panera的门店中42%为公司直营，58%为特许经营；相比之下，星巴克的连锁店则全部由公司拥有并运营。

<!--en-->
The contrasting cost structures reflected a major difference in the two companies' business models. At the end of 2009, 42 percent of Panera's stores were company owned, and 58 percent were franchised operations. The Starbucks chain, in contrast, was entirely company owned and operated.

即便在同一行业内，不同公司的成本占销售额比例也会因商业模式之外的因素而有所不同。有些公司运营效率更高，能以每单位支出创造更多收入。公司所处生命周期阶段也会产生影响。例如，2009年星巴克共有8,800家零售店，其扩张能力已受到限制；从2008年起，该公司关闭了多家门店，表明部分市场已趋于饱和。而Panera当时仅有1,380家咖啡馆，似乎尚未触及增长极限。

<!--en-->
Costs as percentages of sales also vary among companies within an industry for reasons other than differences in business models. Some companies operate more efficiently than others, generating more revenue from each dollar of expenditures. Where a company stands in its life cycle can also make a difference. For example, in 2009 Starbucks had a total of 8,800 retail stores and was encountering constraints on its ability to expand further. Beginning in 2008, the company closed a number of stores, suggesting that it had saturated some of its markets. Panera, on the other hand, had a total of 1,380 cafés and did not yet appear to be bumping up against limits on growth.

由于无需为了维持新店开业速度而选择利润较低的选址，其盈利能力得以提升。

<!--en-->
Its profitability was helped by not having to choose more marginal locations in order to maintain the pace of new store openings.

Peet’s、星巴克和Panera Bread在餐饮行业中所表现出的成本结构与利润率差异，在其他行业中同样存在。例如，一些制药商也生产和销售医疗器械、非处方保健品、洗护用品及美容产品。相比那些仅专注于处方药的企业，业务更为多元化的制造商往往会有更高的产品成本占比以及更低的研发费用占比。分析师必须注意，切勿将实际由商业战略导致的差异误认为是管理能力的优劣体现。

<!--en-->
The variation in cost structures and profit margins that Peet's, Starbucks, and Panera Bread exhibit within food and beverages is paralleled in other industries. For example, some pharmaceutical manufacturers also produce and market medical devices, nonprescription health products, toiletries, and beauty aids. A more widely diversified manufacturer can be expected to have a higher percentage of product costs, as well as a lower percentage of research and development expenses, than industry peers that focus exclusively on prescription drugs. Analysts must take care not to mistake a difference that is actually a function of business strategy as evidence of inferior or superior management skills.

财务报表附注中的分部报告数据有助于揭示那些常被归为一类的公司之间利润率的差异根源。遗憾的是，企业在定义业务分部时拥有较大自主权，导致缺乏标准化，从而难以进行比较。在这种情况下，分析师必须深入挖掘竞争对手的成本结构信息，尽可能从**投资者关系专员**处获取资料，并参考行业资料。

<!--en-->
Segment reporting data in the notes to financial statements can provide a measure of insight into the underlying differentiators of profit margins among companies that tend to be grouped together. Unfortunately, companies have considerable discretion in defining their segments, resulting in a lack of standardization that often makes comparisons difficult. In such cases, an analyst must dig deeper for an understanding of the competitors' cost structures by obtaining as much information as their **investor relations officers** will divulge and drawing on industry sources.

### 这些数字有多真实？

<!--en-->
*HOW REAL ARE THE NUMBERS?*

许多人被商业职业吸引，不仅因为金钱回报，还因为与其他许多职业不同，商业领域存在客观的评价标准。个人改善公司净利润的愿望，就像运动员追求打破世界纪录一样，激励着商业人士。损益表就是衡量公司表现的“秒表”；净利润则是公司在该“赛季”中的胜负记录。商业与体育之间的类比还体现在：仅凭出色的技能和团队合作并不足以赢得冠军。棒球教练可能会激烈抗议裁判的判罚以试图影响后续裁决，从而让有利于自己球队的结果出现；企业则有权解雇审计师，并利用这一权力影响那些属于判断范畴而非明确准则的会计决策。棒球队的管理层可以缩短主场右外野的围栏以偏袒左打者居多的阵容；企业管理层则可选择最能美化业绩的会计方法。

<!--en-->
Many individuals are attracted to business careers not only by monetary rewards but also by the opportunity, lacking in many other professions, tobe measured against an objective standard. The personal desire to improve the bottom line, that is, a company's net profit, challenges a businessperson in much the same way that an athlete is motivated by the quantifiable goal of breaking a world record. The income statement is the stopwatch against which a company runs; net profit is the corporation's record of wins and losses for the season.
The Income Statement
The analogy between business and athletics extends to the fact, which is apparent to any close observer, that superior skills and teamwork alone do not win championships. A baseball manager can intimidate the umpire by heatedly protesting a call on the base paths, hoping thereby to have the next close ruling go in his team's favor. A corporation has the power to fire its auditor and may use that power to influence accounting decisions that are matters of judgment rather than clear-cut reporting standards. A baseball team's front office can shorten the right-field fence in its home stadium to favor a lineup stocked with left-handed power hitters; a corporation's management can select the accounting method that shows its results in the most favorable light.

如果球队老板们认为本垒打和得分的增加会带动观众人数上升，他们便会共同游说规则委员会降低投手丘高度。同样，一些企业也会试图阻挠可能降低其账面收益的新会计准则的出台。

<!--en-->
Collectively, the team owners can urge the rules committee to lower the pitching mound if they believe that a predictable increase in base hits and runs will boost attendance. Similarly, a group of corporations can try to block the introduction of new accounting standards that might reduce their reported earnings.

当衡量成果的标准对参与者而言比该标准的准确性更为重要时，试图扭曲这一标准的行为便会变得尤为猖獗。遗憾的是，当企业试图通过将管理者薪酬与特定财务目标的实现挂钩来激励他们时，往往就会出现这种情况。那些奖金随每股收益同步增长的高管们，不仅有强烈的动机去创造真实的盈利，还会利用一切合法手段通过会计上的花招来虚增这些数字。

<!--en-->
Attempts to transform the yardstick become most vigorous when the measure of achievement becomes more important to participants than the accuracy of the measure itself. Regrettably, this is often the case when corporations seek to motivate managers by linking their compensation to the attainment of specific financial goals. Executives whose bonuses rise in tandem with earnings per share have a strong incentive not only to generate bona fide earnings but also to use every lawful means of inflating the figures through accounting sleight of hand.

要详细列举企业操纵会计规则以虚增盈利的所有方式，所需的篇幅将远超本章的分配量。因此，以下示例应足以向读者传达这种“规则变通”背后的思维逻辑。一旦理解了这些操纵者的思维方式，财务报表的使用者便能察觉到他们必然会使用的其他伎俩。

<!--en-->
It would take many more pages than are allotted to this chapter to detail all the ways that companies can manipulate the accounting rules to inflate their earnings. Instead, the following examples should convey to the reader the thought process involved in this rule bending. Equipped with an understanding of how the rule benders think, users of financial statements will be able to detect other ruses they are sure to encounter.

## 并非所有销售都是最终确定的

<!--en-->
*Not All Sales Are Final*

“只要管好营收这条线，净利润这条线自然会随之改善。”这是一句常见的商业格言，它强调了营业收入（即“营收线”）对净利润（即“净利线”）的重要性。其要点是：如果一家公司想解决盈利问题，就应专注于增加销售额。《基本财务报表》

<!--en-->
"Take care of the top line and the bottom line will take care of itself." So goes a business bromide, which underscores the importance of revenues (the top line) to net income (the bottom line). The point is that if a companywants to cure an earnings problem, it should concentrate on bringing in more sales.
THE BASIC FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

一般来说，只要所需的销售额是由销售团队实现的，这确实是条不错的建议。然而，如果财务人员通过会计上的小把戏来弥补营收缺口，公司的问题反而会进一步恶化。有些虚增营收的手段在公认会计原则（GAAP）的框架内是可行的，而另一些则明显超出了法律允许范围。不过，它们都会产生类似的不良后果：虚增的营收会抬高报告的盈利水平，却并未相应增加现金流。

<!--en-->
Generally, this is sound advice, as long as the needed sales are brought in by the sales force. A company can compound its problems, however, if the financial staff makes up the shortfall in revenues through accounting gimmicks. Some revenue-inflating tricks are achievable within generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) boundaries, whereas others clearly fall outside the law. They all produce similar ill effects, however. Enhancements to reported sales boost reported earnings without increasing cash flow commensurately.

通常，公司的盈利与现金流会出现不可持续的背离现象。最终结果就是对以往期间的财务报表进行突然调整。在此过程中，盈利与现金流虽重新趋于一致，但管理层的信誉却会一落千丈。即便没有发生此类冲击，通过随意性会计决策来夸大营收的做法对分析师而言仍是一种隐患。至少，它会降低公司各期财务报表之间的可比性。

<!--en-->
Often, a company's earnings and cash flow diverge to an extent that becomes unsustainable. The eventual result is an abrupt adjustment to the financial statements of previous periods. In the process, earnings and cash flow come back into alignment, but management's credibility plummets. Even when no such shock occurs, the practice of pumping up revenues through discretionary accounting decisions represents a hazard for analysts. At a minimum, it reduces the comparability of a company's financial statements from one period to the next.

### 对营收持怀疑态度的其他原因

<!--en-->
*Additional Reasons to Be Skeptical about Revenues*

对分析师而言不幸的是，企业并不总会在财务报表附注中说明其人为虚增营收的具体手段。例如，一家企业可能会降低对潜在客户的信贷标准，却不同时提高针对应收账款损失的准备金比例。其结果便是当期营收和盈利双双上升，而相应的信贷损失则要等到后期才会显现出来。或者，制造商可能会推出短期折扣，促使经销商或批发商提前下单。在这种情况下，当季的销售额和盈利确实会比没有这些激励措施时更高，但这种差异只不过是将营收从后期提前到了前期而已。如果分析师将这种虚增的季度销售额视为未来的预示，那他们将会大失所望。

<!--en-->
Unfortunately for analysts, companies do not always spell out in the notes to financial statements the means by which they have artificially inflated their revenues. A company might lower the credit standards it applies to prospective customers without simultaneously raising the percentage of reserves it establishes for losses on receivables. The result would be a rise in both revenues and earnings in the current period, with the corresponding increase in credit losses not becoming apparent until a later period. Alternatively, a manufacturer may institute short-term discounts that encourage its dealers or wholesalers to place orders earlier than they otherwise would. In this case, sales and earnings will be higher in the current quarter than they would be in the absence of the incentives, but the difference will represent merely a shifting of revenues from a later to an earlier period. Analysts will face disappointment if they regard such inflated quarterly sales as indicative of the future.

尽管当期损益表可能无法揭示企业是否采用了这些手段，但仍有几种技巧可以帮助分析师察觉营收的人为扩张现象。从回顾性角度看，信贷损失的激增或营收的意外不足，可能表明前期已利用前一段所述的方法虚增了营收。（这类线索并非毫无价值；若分析师发现历史上存在销售额被过度夸大的模式，便会对看似强劲的未来损益表持合理的怀疑态度。）从当期来看，如果一家公司的销售额增幅明显大于竞争对手，分析师就应引起注意。倘若与该公司的沟通以及从行业其他渠道获得的信息无法给出令人满意的解释（比如成功推出新产品），那么人为操纵手段很可能就是根源所在。行业人士也能直接提供关于如何将未来期间的营收提前至当期的相关信息。《损益表》

<!--en-->
Although the current-period income statement may offer no clues that these gambits have been used, several techniques can help the analyst detect artificial expansion of revenues. On a retrospective basis, a surge in credit losses or an unexpected shortfall in revenues may indicate that revenues were inflated in an earlier period with the techniques described in the preceding paragraph. (Hints of this kind are not without value; an analyst who finds a historical pattern of hyperbolized sales will be appropriately skeptical about future income statements that look surprisingly strong.) On a currentbasis, analysts should take notice if a company posts a substantially greater sales increase than its competitors. If discussions with the company and other industry sources fail to elicit a satisfactory explanation (such as the introduction of a successful new product), artificial methods may be the root of the matter. Industry sources can also provide direct testimony about tactics being used to shift revenues from future periods to the present.
The Income Statement

### 非经常性及特殊项目

<!--en-->
*Extraordinary and Nonrecurring Items*

对于大多数查看公司损益表的人来说，该文件的重要性不在于它反映的过去，而在于它对未来年份的预示意义。¹例如，去年的盈利对代表未来盈利折现的公司股价并无直接影响（参见第14章）。因此，股票投资者主要将前一年的损益表视为预测未来盈利的依据。同样，公司的债权人早在损益表出炉前就已经知道去年到期的利息是否得到支付；他们研究该文件的目的是为了判断公司在当年及今后支付利息的可能性。

<!--en-->
To most individuals who examine a company's income statement, the document is less important for what it tells about the past than for what it implies about future years.¹ Last year's earnings, for example, have no direct impact on a company's stock price, which represents a discounting of a future stream of earnings (see Chapter 14). An equity investor is therefore interested in a company's income statement from the preceding year primarily as a basis for forecasting future earnings. Similarly, a company's creditors already know whether they were paid the interest that came due in the previous year before the income statement arrives. Their motivation for studying the document is to form an opinion about the likelihood of payment in the current year and in years to come.

除了意识到损益表的读者主要将其视为未来的指标外，公司也清楚：营造更乐观的未来预期能够推高股价并降低借贷成本。因此，说服读者相信去年损害盈利的重大事件不会对未来盈利产生负面影响，符合公司的利益。

<!--en-->
In addition to recognizing that readers of its income statement will view the document primarily as an indicator of the future, a company knows that creating more favorable expectations about the future can raise its stock price and lower its borrowing cost. It is therefore in the company's interest to persuade readers that a major development that hurt earnings last year will not adversely affect earnings in future years.

实现这一目标的一种方式是声称公司遭受的任何重大损失都属于非正常经营范畴、具有异常性，因而不太可能再次发生。

<!--en-->
One way of achieving this is to suggest that any large loss suffered by the company was somehow outside the normal course of business, anomalous, and, by implication, unlikely to recur.

为了营造“该损失偏离公司正常经营模式”的印象，可以在损益表中单独列示该项损失，并将其标记为“非经常性项目”。需要注意的是，非经常性项目是按税后基础列示在持续经营损益线下方的。这种呈现方式最能给人留下该损失属于非日常经营活动的印象，从而最大限度地降低分析人士在预测未来业绩时对其重视程度。

<!--en-->
To create the desired impression that a loss was alien to the company's normal pattern of behavior, the loss can be shown on a separate line on the income statement and labeled an "extraordinary item." Note that an extraordinary item is reported on an after-tax basis, below the line of income (or loss) from continuing operations. This presentation creates the strongest possible impression that the loss was outside the ordinary course of business. It maximizes the probability that analysts of the income statement will give it little weight in forecasting future performance.

由于这种“线下处理”方式产生的效果极为显著，会计准则对其使用进行了严格限制。根据相关的**会计原则委员会（APB）**意见，要被认定为非经常性项目，相关事件必须“具有不寻常的性质且发生频率极低”。²这些标准并不容易满足。根据该意见，“不寻常性质”是指“相关事件或交易应具有高度异常性，且与实体在其经营环境中进行的常规典型活动明显无关或仅属偶然关联”。为防止“非经常性”标签被滥用，该意见禁止将几种按严格标准判定为性质异常的事件归类为非经常性项目。

<!--en-->
Because the effect created by a below-the-line treatment is so strong, the accounting rules carefully limit its use. To qualify as extraordinary under the relevant **Accounting Principles Board (APB)** opinion, events must be "distinguished by their unusual nature and by the infrequency of their occurrence."² These criteria are not easily satisfied. According to the opinion, *unusual nature* means that "the underlying event or transactionshould possess a high degree of abnormality and be of a type clearly unrelated to, or only incidentally related to, the ordinary and typical activities of the entity, taking into account the environment in which the entity operates.” Lest the *extraordinary* label be employed indiscriminately, the opinion prohibits its use for several types of events considered unusual in nature under the strict standard being applied.

其中包括：基本财务报表

<!--en-->
Among these are:
THE BASIC FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

* 应收账款和存货的核销。
* 外币折算产生的利得或损失（即使是由货币大幅贬值或升值引起的）。
* 处置业务分部，或出售、废弃固定资产所产生的利得或损失。即便2001年9月11日针对五角大楼和世界贸易中心的恐怖袭击事件，按照美国财务会计准则委员会（FASB）的严格标准来看，也并不属于“非经常性事项”。该工作组最初曾考虑允许企业将因灾难产生的费用列为“线后项目”，但最终投票决定不采纳这一做法。工作组主席兼FASB研究总监蒂莫西·S·卢卡斯指出，即便是明显受到事件影响的航空公司，也难以将袭击造成的影响与该期间的其他营收及盈利压力区分开来。³考虑到某项事项要被认定为“非经常性”需满足极为苛刻的条件，分析师在预测未来盈利时若完全忽略此类事项，或许可以认为自己的判断是稳妥的。毕竟，APB的意见书还强调：“发生频率极低”意味着相关事件或交易必须属于“在可预见的未来不太可能再次发生的类型”。人们或许会认为，偶尔会出现符合这一严格标准的事项，但几年后同一家公司又会发生性质截然不同却同样可被归类为“非经常性”并需作为“线后项目”列报的事件。更罕见的情况是，某非经常性事件发生后次年便又出现类似性质的事件，尽管根据会计准则，这种重复发生的情况本应“不在合理预期之内”。不过，从APB意见书中极为严格的表述来看，如果哪家公司在几年内两次以上计入非经常性事项，那将令人极为惊讶。然而，尽管看似不太可能，对Capital IQ数据库的检索却发现，在截至2009年的八年中，有30家公司至少三年记录了非经常性利得或损失。那些反复经历所谓“罕见且异常”事件的公司包括好事达、康尼格拉食品、金佰利克拉克、孟山都、西方石油以及时代华纳等巨头。美国电力公司在此期间共记录了六项非经常性事项。鉴于实际经验表明，无论管理层多么希望分析师能如此行事，他们都无法简单地把公司的未来盈利预测为仿佛从未发生过非经常性事件一般。实际上，企业在评估过往业绩以预测未来表现时，往往指望分析师能更加迁就自己。企业官员不仅鼓励财务报表使用者忽略那些被归类为“非经常性”的损失，还要求他们忽视某些仅因管理层宣称其为“异常”而对盈利造成的冲击。为了引导分析师朝着管理层所认定的真正（即更高）盈利趋势前行，企业会将所谓的“异常项”从其其他经营性盈利中分离出来。根据会计准则，这类拆分项目必须在“线前”（即税前基础上）列报，且禁止使用“非经常性”这一称谓。因此，企业会使用“非重复性”或“特殊性”等称呼。这些术语在GAAP中并无官方定义，但它们却给人一种印象：被标注的项目具有特殊性。有时，不符合非经常性事项标准的损失会被归入较为中性的“特别费用”栏目下。不过，即便使用这种术语，也会让人觉得公司已经解决了相关问题。 这种表述方式对企业管理者极具吸引力，以至于在Capital IQ数据库中检索发现：在标准普尔500指数所涵盖的公司中，有487家公司在2002年至2009年间的至少一半年份里报告了“非经常性项目”。其中近一半（230家）在这八年期间均记录了此类项目，包括埃克森美孚、摩根大通、麦当劳、微软和Sprint Nextel等蓝筹股公司。这些连续八年报告非经常性项目的公司中，许多既记录了正面的也记录了负面的非经常性项目，这强烈暗示它们试图向财务报表使用者表明：其真实的盈利发展轨迹比GAAP数据所显示的更为平稳。

随着时间的推移，“重组”一词已成为一种笼统的说法，用来指代那些企业希望分析师将其视为正常业务之外的事项、但又不符合“表外处理”条件的费用。该术语带有正面含义，暗示企业已经摒弃了亏损业务，为显著提升盈利能力做好了准备。但如果被滥用，将重组费用单独列示便可能描绘出过于乐观的过往业绩图景。它会误导缺乏经验的分析师，淡化那些反映管理层决策失误的业务举措的重要性。此外，与重组相关的损失可能会被归咎于公司的前任首席执行官，前提是这些损失在继任CEO任职初期就被计入账目。短短一年内，新任掌舵人便可因盈利状况相对于这笔可轻易归咎于前任的巨额损失而有所改善，从而将业绩好转的功劳归于自己。

更隐蔽的是，企业有时会冲销比实际经济损失更大的金额。企业管理者普遍认为：无论冲销15亿美元还是10亿美元，对其股价造成的损害程度并无显著差异。夸大损失的好处在于：随后几年中，这些多计的费用可以小额逐步转回，且无需进行专门披露。管理层便可利用这些收益来补充并平滑企业真正的营业利润。然而，财务报表使用者必须避免的最危险陷阱便是误以为“重组”一词意味着终结。有些企业有年年进行重组的坏习惯。对于这类公司，分析师预测未来盈利能力时应以扣除重组费用后的利润为准，而非扣除前的数据。宝洁公司（Procter & Gamble, P&G）便是典型例子。截至2001年4月，这家消费品公司已连续七个季度计提重组费用，总额达13亿美元。此外，管理层还表示计划继续计提这些看似非经常性的费用直至2004年中，最终总计冲销约40亿美元。

为辩解其报表处理方式，宝洁公司称美国证券交易委员会（SEC）的会计准则禁止其在1999年6月启动重组计划时一次性计提巨额费用；相反，公司必须在实际发生费用的期间予以记录。即便承认这一点，SEC也并未强制要求宝洁公司将关闭工厂和解雇员工的成本与其他运营费用区分开来。事实上，鉴于宝洁所处的高竞争性消费品行业中存在大量产品失败或过时的情况，将这些冲销项视为正常运营成本更为合理。然而，这些抽象的会计理论问题对券商分析师评估宝洁盈利记录的方式影响甚微。 所有跟踪该公司并向汤森金融/First Call提交每股收益预测的14位分析师，都在计算中排除了重组费用。宝洁公司管理层显然对华尔街对这种数据的解读感到满意。若计入所有看似非正常的损益项目，2000年四个季度的营业利润均出现下滑；而剔除管理层认为异常的项目后，除第一季度外，各季度净利润均有所上升。后一种解读无疑比那些令人沮丧的GAAP数据更能给投资者带来对宝洁公司前景的乐观预期。⁴

损益表

当然，当特殊项目属于收益而非损失时，企业往往会鼓励分析师在盈利计算中*纳入*这些项目。他们显然认为这种“以牙还牙”的做法合乎情理；从结果来看，许多证券分析师似乎也赞同这一观点。前述那14位华尔街分析师一致决定，将宝洁公司归类为非经常性或特殊收益的款项纳入其“核心净利润”指标中，即便他们同时排除了那些特殊及非经常性损失。

<!--en-->
* Write-offs of receivables and inventories.
* Gains or losses on foreign currency translation (even when they result from major devaluations or revaluations).
* Gains or losses on disposal of a segment of a business or the sale or abandonment of property, plant, or equipment.
Not even the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks on the Pentagon and World Trade Center qualified as an extraordinary event under the stringent criteria of the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB). After tentatively deciding that companies could break out costs arising from the disaster as below-the-line items, the task force on the subject voted not to allow the practice. The chairman of the task force, FASB Research Director Timothy S. Lucas, noted that even the airlines, which were plainly hurt by the events, would have difficulty separating the impact of the attacks from other revenue and earnings pressures during the period.³
Considering the exacting tests that an item must meet to be considered extraordinary, analysts may consider themselves on solid ground if they largely disregard any such item in forecasting future earnings. The APB opinion, after all, adds that “infrequency of occurrence” means that the event or transaction in question must be “of a type not reasonably expected to recur in the foreseeable future.” Occasionally, one would suppose, an event meeting this strict standard might be followed just a few years later by an event at the same company, radically different in nature but also qualifying for classification as extraordinary and below-the-line reporting. On even rarer occasions, an extraordinary event might be followed the very next year by a qualifying event of a similar nature, even though such a recurrence was “not reasonably expected,” to quote the accounting standard. Judging by the highly restrictive language of the APB opinion, however, it would be extremely surprising if any company ever booked an extraordinary item more than twice in a matter of several years.
Improbable though it might seem, however, a search of the Capital IQ database identified 30 companies that recorded extraordinary gains or losses in at least three of the eight years ending in 2009. Among the companies that repeatedly experienced events of an allegedly infrequent and unusual nature were such stalwarts as Allstate, Conagra Foods, Kimberly-Clark, Monsanto,Occidental Petroleum, and Time Warner. American Electric Power recorded six extraordinary items during the period. In light of actual experience, analysts cannot simply project a company's future earnings as though an extraordinary event had never occurred, however fervently management might wish them to do precisely that.
The Income Statement
Actually, companies lean on analysts to be even more accommodating when they evaluate past results to forecast future performance. Corporate officials not only encourage users of their financial statements to disregard losses that qualify for the label extraordinary but also ask them to ignore certain hits to earnings simply because management pronounces them aberrant. To steer analysts toward the true (that is, higher trajectory) trend of earnings deemed official by management fiat, companies break out the supposed aberrations from their other operating earnings. The accounting rules require such carve-outs to be reported above the line (that is, on a pretax basis) and prohibit use of the label *extraordinary*. Accordingly, companies employ designations such as *nonrecurring* or *unusual*. These terms have no official standing under GAAP, but they foster the impression that the highlighted items are exceptional in nature. Sometimes, losses that fail to meet the criteria of extraordinary items appear under the more neutral heading, "special charges." Even this terminology, however, leaves the impression that the company has put the problem behind itself. The semantics are so appealing to corporate managers that a search of the Capital IQ database revealed that 487 of the companies represented in Standard & Poor's 500 Index reported unusual items in at least half of the years from 2002 to 2009. Nearly half (230) recorded unusual items in all eight years of that span, including such blue chips as Exxon Mobil, JPMorgan Chase, McDonald's, Microsoft, and Sprint Nextel. Many of the eight-timers reported both positive and negative unusual items, strongly hinting at a desire to persuade users of financial statements that their true earnings progression was much smoother than the GAAP figures showed.
Over time, restructuring has become a catchall for charges that companies wish analysts to consider outside the normal course of business but that do not qualify for below-the-line treatment. The term has a positive connotation, implying that the corporation has cast off its money-losing operations and positioned itself for significantly improved profitability. If abused, the segregation of restructuring charges can create too rosy a picture of past performance. It can entrap the unwary analyst by downplaying the significance of failed business initiatives, which have a bearing on management's judgment. Additionally, the losses associated with a restructuring may be blamed on the company's previous chief executive officer, provided they are booked early in the successor CEO's tenure. Within a year's time, the new kingpin may be able to take credit for a turnaround, based on animprovement in earnings relative to a large loss that can be conveniently attributed to the predecessor regime.
THE BASIC FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
Even more insidiously, companies sometimes write off larger sums than warranted by their actual economic losses on a failed business. Corporate managers commonly perceive that the damage to their stock price will be no greater if they take (for sake of argument) a $1.5 billion write-off than if they write off $1.0 billion. The benefit of exaggerating the damage is that in subsequent years, the overcharges can be reversed in small amounts that do not generate any requirement for specific disclosure. Management can use these gains to supplement and smooth the corporation's bona fide operating earnings.
The most dangerous trap that users of financial statements must avoid, however, is inferring that the term *restructuring* connotes finality. Some corporations have a bad habit of remaking themselves year after year. For such companies, the analyst's baseline for forecasting future profitability should be earnings after, rather than before, restructuring charges.
Procter & Gamble (P&G) is a case in point. As of April 2001, the consumer goods company had booked restructuring charges in seven consecutive quarters, aggregating to $1.3 billion. Moreover, management indicated that it planned to continue taking these ostensibly nonrecurring charges until mid-2004, ultimately charging off approximately $4 billion.
Defending its reporting, P&G said that Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) accounting rules precluded it from taking one huge charge at the outset of the restructuring program launched in June 1999. Instead, the company was required to record the charges in the periods in which it actually incurred them. Granting the point, the SEC did not compel Procter & Gamble to segregate the costs of closing factories and laying off workers from its other operating expenses. Indeed, the arguments were stronger for treating the charge-offs as normal costs of operating in P&G's highly competitive consumer goods business, where countless products fail or become obsolete over time.
Abstract issues of accounting theory, however, had little impact on brokerage house securities analysts' treatment of P&G's earnings record. All 14 analysts who followed the company and submitted earnings per share forecasts to Thomson Financial/First Call excluded the restructuring charges from their calculations, and P&G management was bound to like Wall Street's interpretation of the numbers. Including all of the ostensibly unusual gains and losses, operating income declined in all four quarters of 2000. Leaving out all the items deemed aberrant by management, net income rose in all quarters but the first. The latter interpretation surely gave investors a more optimistic view of P&G's prospects than the sourpuss GAAP numbers.⁴
The Income Statement
Naturally, companies encourage analysts to *include* special items in their earnings calculations when they happen to be gains, rather than losses. They evidently reason that turnabout is fair play, and judging by the results, many securities analysts apparently agree. The 14 Wall Street analysts mentioned earlier unanimously chose to include in their “core net earnings” figures the gains that Procter & Gamble classified as nonrecurring or extraordinary, even as they excluded the extraordinary and nonrecurring losses.

### 将股市收益转化为营业收入

<!--en-->
*Transforming Stock Market Proceeds into Revenues*

在企业管理者用新策略补充传统盈利手段的同时，近年来他们也更加专注于提升营业收入。对于希望向投资者展示最佳形象（即便未必完全准确）的企业而言，这种做法极具意义。如果一家公司能够实现其营收目标，那么其在盈利方面的胜利便已注定过半。当然，成功还取决于对成本的控制。然而，如果没有强劲的营业收入作为基础，企业便无法靠节约成本来创造可观的净利润。

<!--en-->
At the same time that corporate managers have been supplementing their traditional tactics with new adjustments to earnings, they have also concentrated in recent years on applying their ingenuity to revenues. This focus makes eminent sense for corporations that want to present the best possible, if not necessarily most accurate, profile to investors. If a company achieves its revenue objectives, its battle for profitability is more than half won. To be sure, success also depends on controlling expenses. Without a robust top line, however, the company cannot economize its way to a respectable bottom line.

开拓销售业务不仅是一项至关重要的任务，也是一项艰巨的工作。竞争对手总是试图通过推出更优质的产品或降低价格来抢夺市场份额。从为消费者创造最大价值及促进经济效率的角度出发，管理层应对这一挑战的最佳方式就是升级自身产品并降低成本，从而让利于客户。增加广告开支或扩充销售团队也能带来营收增长。不过，除了有效执行产品设计或营销计划外，还有另一种选择：管理层可以通过属于企业财务范畴的手段来促进销售。

<!--en-->
Garnering sales is not only a vital task, but a tough job as well. Competitors are forever striving to snatch away revenues by introducing superior products or devising means of lowering prices to customers. From the standpoint of maximizing value to consumers and promoting economic efficiency, management's optimal response to this challenge is to upgrade its own products and generate cost savings that it can pass along to customers. Stepping up expenditures on advertising or expanding the sales force can also lead to increased revenues. Along with effective execution of product design or marketing plans, however, another option exists. Management can boost sales through techniques that more properly fall into the category of corporate finance.

通过并购来提高营收增速是最常见的例子。企业可以通过收购其他公司并将其销售额并入自身来实现销售增长的加速。尽管有时缺乏警惕的投资者难以察觉其中的区别，但通过并购为股东创造真正价值其实更为困难。

<!--en-->
Raising the rate of revenue increases through mergers and acquisitions is the most common example. A corporation can easily accelerate its sales growth by buying other companies and adding their sales to its own. Creating genuine value for shareholders through acquisitions is more difficult, although unwary investors sometimes fail to recognize the distinction.

在图表3.3中的虚构案例中，Big Time Corporation在第一年至第二年间的销售额增长了5%。同行业的较小型私营公司Small Change也实现了5%的年度销售增长。假设Big Time在第一年年末用自身股票收购了Small Change。在此假设下（“收购情景”），Big Time的损益表显示销售额增长了10%。

<!--en-->

<!--en-->
increase between Year 1 and Year 2. (Note that Year 1 is shown as originally reported, with Small Change still an independent company, while in Year 2, the results of the acquired company, Small Change, are consolidated into the parent's financial reporting. 表面上看，年增长率达10%的公司比仅增长5%的公司更具吸引力。然而需要注意的是，以净利润占销售额的百分比来衡量，Big Time的盈利能力并未因此次收购而得到改善。两家利润率均为3%的公司合并后，虽然公司规模变大，但销售利润率仍保持在3%。正如图表3.3中的补充数据所示，股东在此过程中并未获得任何额外收益。

<!--en-->
On the face of it, a company growing at 10 percent a year is sexier than one growing at only 5 percent a year. Observe, however, that Big Time's profitability, measured by net income as a percentage of sales, does not improve as a result of the acquisition. Combining two companies with equivalent profit margins of 3 percent produces a larger company that also earns 3 percent on sales. Shareholders do not gain anything in the process, as the supplementary figures in Exhibit 3.3 demonstrate.

如果Big Time决定不收购Small Change，其已发行股份数将维持在7500万股。第1年的盈利额为1.5亿美元，第2年增长至1.575亿美元，因此每股收益从2.00美元上升至2.10美元。

<!--en-->
If Big Time decides not to acquire Small Change, its number of shares outstanding remains at 75.0 million. The earnings increase from $150.0 million in Year 1 to $157.5 million in Year 2 raises earnings per share from $2.00 to $2.10.

由于市盈率保持在14倍这一行业平均水平，Big Time的股价将从每股28.00美元上涨至29.40美元。

<!--en-->
With the price-earnings multiple constant at 14 times, equivalent to the average of the company's industry peers, Big Time's stock price rises from $28.00 to $29.40 a share.

而在收购情形下，Big Time按照14倍的行业平均市盈率来支付Small Change的收购价款，总收购价格为710万美元×14=9940万美元。按Big Time第1年的股价28.00美元计算，此次收购需增发9940万美元÷28.00美元=360万股股票。加上Small Change的净利润后，Big Time在第2年的盈利额达到1.65亿美元。将该数字除以增加的已发行股份数（7860万股），可得每股收益为2.10美元。在14倍的市盈率下，Big Time的每股价值即为29.40美元，这一数值与非收购情景下的计算结果完全一致。仅仅是将年度销售额增长率从5%提高到10%，并未给股东带来实质益处；无论Big Time是否收购Small Change，其股价涨幅都仅为5%。

<!--en-->
In the Acquisition Scenario, on the other hand, Big Time pays its industry-average earnings multiple of 14 times for Small Change, for a total acquisition price of $7.1 million × 14 = $99.4 million. At Big Time's Year 1 share price of $28.00, the purchase therefore requires the issuance of $99.4 million ÷ $28.00 = 3.6 million shares. With the addition of Small Change's net income, Big Time earns $165.0 million in Year 2. Dividing that figure by the increased number of shares outstanding (78.6 million) produces earnings per share of $2.10. At a price-earnings multiple of 14 times, Big Time is worth $29.40 a share, precisely the price calculated in the Nonacquisition Scenario. The mere increase in annual sales growth from 5 percent to 10 percent has not benefited shareholders, whose shares increase in value by 5 percent whether Big Time acquires Small Change or not.

分析师应注意，此分析对各类情景背后的假设条件较为敏感。例如，假设Big Time并非通过发行股票，而是用借款来筹措收购Small Change所需的资金。

<!--en-->
Analysts should note that this analysis is sensitive to the assumptions underlying the scenarios. Suppose, for instance, that instead of issuing stock, Big Time finances the acquisition of Small Change with borrowed money.

假设Big Time需为9940万美元的新借款支付8%的利息。在收购情形下，第2年的利息费用将从1亿美元增至1.18亿美元。税前利润因此从2.5亿美元降至2.42亿美元；按34%的实际税率计算，净利润则从1.65亿美元减少至1.597亿美元。不过，交易完成后已发行股份数仅为7500万股，而非股票收购情形下的7860万股。结果，Big Time的每股收益上升至1.597亿美元÷7500万股=2.13美元。基本财务报表

<!--en-->
Let us suppose that Big Time must pay interest at a rate of 8 percent on the $99.4 million of new borrowings. Interest expense in Year 2 of the Acquisition Scenario is now $118.0 million, rather than $100.0 million. Pretax income therefore falls from $250.0 million to $242.0 million, reducing net income from $165.0 million to $159.7 million at the company's effective tax rate of 34 percent. Only 75.0 million shares are outstanding at the conclusion of the transaction, however, rather than the 78.6 million observedin the acquisition-for-stock case. As a result, Big Time's earnings per share rise to $159.7 million ÷ 75.0 million = $2.13.

假设市场继续给予Big Time的盈利14倍的估值倍数，该股票当前价值为29.82美元，略高于“不收购情景”下的价值。实际上，投资者可能会略微下调Big Time的市盈率，以反映其利息保障能力减弱所带来的更高风险。（根据第13章所列公式，在股票收购情形下，息税前利润与利息费用之比为3.3倍（360.0百万美元 ÷ 110.0百万美元）；而在债务融资收购情形下，这一比例降至3.1倍（360.0百万美元 ÷ 118.0百万美元）。）如果由于债务保护能力的下降，市盈率仅从14倍降至13.8倍，那么在这种情形下Big Time的股价将再次达到29.40美元，相当于“不收购情景”下的第2年股价。

<!--en-->
Assuming the market continues to assign a multiple of 14 times to Big Time's earnings, the stock is now worth $29.82, a bit more than in the Nonacquisition Scenario. In practice, the investors may reduce Big Time's price-earnings multiple slightly to reflect the heightened risk represented by its decreased interest coverage. (Following the formulas laid out in Chapter 13, income before interest and taxes declines from $360.0 million ÷ $110.0 million = 3.3 times in the stock-acquisition case to $360.0 million ÷ $118.0 million = 3.1 times in the debt-financed-acquisition case.) If the price-earnings multiple falls only from 14 to 13.8 times as a result of this decline in debt protection, Big Time's stock price in this variant again comes to $29.40, equivalent to the Year 2 price in the Nonacquisition Scenario.

正如Big Time通过发行股票来收购Small Change的情况一样，如果投资者对公司债务增加对其信用质量的影响十分敏感，那么即便Big Time借入所需资金进行收购，股东也无法从中获益。

<!--en-->
As in the case of Big Time paying with stock for the acquisition of Small Change, shareholders do not benefit if Big Time instead borrows the requisite funds, assuming investors are sensitive to the impact of the company's increased debt load on its credit quality.

### 内部增长与外部增长

<!--en-->
*Internal versus External Growth*

比精细调整计算结果更为重要的是这样一个原则：企业若想在不提高盈利能力的前提下加速营收增长，便无法真正增加股东财富。但这并未阻止企业试图通过收购其他公司并将其销售额并入自身报表，从而用高销售增长率来迷惑分析师。分析师可能因未能区分**内部增长**与**外部增长**，而中了这种圈套。

<!--en-->
More important than the fine-tuning of the calculations is the principle that a company cannot truly increase shareholders' wealth by accelerating its revenue growth without also improving profitability. This does not dissuade companies from attempting to mesmerize analysts with high rates of sales growth generated by grafting other companies' sales onto their own through acquisitions. Analysts may fall for the trick by failing to distinguish between **internal growth** and **external growth**.

内部增长是指源于企业现有业务的销售额增加，而外部增长则指通过收购带来的新增销售额。若一家企业的内部（或有机）增长率高于行业平均水平，则表明它正在从竞争对手手中夺取市场份额。为谨慎起见，分析师必须进一步查明管理层是否只是通过降低毛利率来增加销量。倘若并非如此，该企业或许确实正在改善其竞争地位，并最终提升自身价值。另一方面，如果A公司通过收购B公司实现外部增长，但A公司及新子公司均未提高盈利能力，那么合并后企业的内在价值并不会超过两家公司价值之和。

<!--en-->
Internal growth consists of sales increases generated from a company's existing operations, while the latter represents incremental sales brought in through acquisitions. An internal (or organic) growth rate greater than the average recorded for the industry implies that the company is gaining market share from its competitors. As a precaution, the analyst must probe further to determine whether management has merely increased unit sales by accepting lower gross margins. If that is not the case, however, the company may in fact be improving its competitive position and, ultimately, increasing its value. On the other hand, if Company A generates external growth by acquiring Company B and neither Company A nor its new subsidiary increases its profitability, then the intrinsic value of the merged companies is no greater than the sum of the two companies' values.

不过，如果并购能够带来盈利能力的提升，外部增长确实可以增加股东财富。这种效应通常被称为*协同效应*。这个词常被那些承诺通过收购实现运营效率提升却拿不出具体实例的企业滥用，毕竟这些收购看似并不具备此类潜力。尽管如此，即便是那些多年来目睹所谓协同效应从未兑现而变得愤世嫉俗的分析师，也会承认确实存在几种通过外部增长来提高企业利润率的有效途径。首先，企业可以通过扩大采购规模来降低单位成本。供应商通常会为大额客户提供更优惠的价格，且能比小批量订购的客户更高效地提供服务。如果在竞争环境稳定的情况下，生产每个产品的原材料、燃料及运输成本下降，而产品售价保持不变，企业的毛利率便会上升。

<!--en-->
External growth can increase shareholders' wealth, however, if the mergers and acquisitions lead to improvements in profitability. This effect is commonly referred to as *synergy*. It is a term much abused by companiesthat promise to achieve operating efficiencies, without offering many specific examples, through acquisitions that appear to offer few such opportunities. Nevertheless, even analysts who have grown cynical after years of seeing purported synergies remain unrealized will acknowledge the existence of several bona fide means of raising a company's profit margins through external growth.
The Income Statement
For one thing, a company may be able to reduce its cost per unit by increasing the size of its purchases. Suppliers commonly offer volume discounts to their large customers, which they can service more efficiently than customers who order in small quantities. If the cost of materials, fuel, and transportation required to produce each widget goes down while the selling price of widgets remains unchanged in a stable competitive environment, the company's gross margin increases.

通过外部增长来提高盈利能力的另一种方式涉及**范围经济**。

<!--en-->
Another way to increase profitability through external growth involves **economies of scope**.

举个简单的例子：一家薯片制造商会派遣销售团队拜访零售店。相关费用中很大一部分是销售人员往返各店铺所产生的时间和交通成本，以及他们的健康保险和其他福利开支。现在假设这家薯片制造商收购了一家椒盐脆饼制造商。为便于说明，假设这家椒盐脆饼公司此前依赖食品经纪人而非内部销售团队。收购方终止与经纪人的合同，并将椒盐脆饼纳入薯片销售团队的产品线。由于新增了椒盐脆饼产品线，每次销售访问带来的收入和毛利润随之上升。每位销售人员的销售访问次数基本保持不变，因为处理新产品的订单所耗费的时间很少。因此，每次销售访问的时间和交通成本并未显著增加，而健康保险及其他福利成本则完全没有增加。综合来看，通过同一分销渠道销售薯片和椒盐脆饼所获得的盈利能力，要高于仅销售单一零食产品时的盈利能力。

<!--en-->
In a simple illustration, a manufacturer of potato chips has a sales force calling on retail stores. Much of the associated expense represents the time and transportation costs incurred as the salespeople travel from store to store, as well as the salespeople's health insurance and other benefits. Now suppose that the potato chip manufacturer acquires a pretzel manufacturer. For the sake of explication, assume that the pretzel company formerly relied on food brokers rather than an in-house sales force. The acquiring company terminates the contracts with the brokers and adds pretzels to its potato chip sales force's product line. Revenues and gross profits per sales call rise with the addition of the pretzel line. The number of sales calls per salesperson remains essentially constant, because taking orders for the additional product consumes little time. Accordingly, time and transportation costs per sales call do not rise materially, while the cost of health insurance and other benefits does not rise at all. Adding it all up, the profitability of selling both potato chips and pretzels through the same distribution channel is greater than the profitability of selling one snack food only.

分析师应当注意：关于潜在范围经济性的说法往往事后证明被夸大了。例如，几十年来，银行、证券公司和保险公司经常宣称“金融超市”时代的到来——即单一分销渠道就能高效地向消费者提供各类金融服务。虽然这些企业之间确实发生了相当程度的整合，但企业间的文化障碍比企业规划者预想的更为棘手。销售人员需要接受大量培训，才能适应从节奏快速的股票交易业务转向较为繁琐的保险产品销售过程。总体而言，合并企业的业务相关性越低，实现预期范围经济性的可能性就越小。当不同行业的企业为了追求新的协同效应而合并时，分析师应对管理层编制的预测性损益表中显示的利润率增长数据持极度谨慎的态度。**基本财务报表**

<!--en-->
Analysts should be forewarned that claims of potential economies of scope often prove, in retrospect, to be exaggerated. Over a period of several decades, for example, banks, brokerage houses, and insurance companies have frequently proclaimed the advent of the financial supermarket, in which a single distribution channel will efficiently deliver all classes of financial services to consumers. A fair amount of integration between these businesses has certainly occurred, but cultural barriers between the businesses have turned out to be more formidable than corporate planners have foreseen. Considerable training is required to teach salespeople how to shift gears between the fast-paced business of dealing in stocks and the more painstaking process of selling insurance policies. In general, the less closely related the combining businesses are, the less certain it is that the hoped-for economiesof scope will be realized. When disparate companies combine in pursuit of novel synergies, analysts should treat with extreme caution the margin increases shown in pro forma income statements produced by management.
THE BASIC FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

#### 利用规模经济

<!--en-->
*Capturing Economies of Scale*

最后，或许也是最著名的例子是：并购确实可以通过规模经济来真正提升盈利能力和股东财富。如图表3.4所示，Central Widget目前仅利用了其生产能力的83.3%。在当前的生产水平下，该公司的**固定成本**为3亿美元÷2.5亿单位=每单位1.20美元，占每美元销售额的12%。这些无法削减的成本严重制约了该公司的净利润率——仅为2.0%，进而也限制了其股本回报率（见第13章），后者仅为11.1%。*图表3.4 规模经济*

<!--en-->
Finally, and perhaps most famously, mergers can genuinely increase profitability and shareholder wealth through economies of scale. As illustrated in Exhibit 3.4, Central Widget is currently utilizing only 83.3 percent of itsproductive capacity. At the present production level, the company's **fixed costs** amount to $300 million ÷ 250 million = $1.20 per unit, or 12 percent of each sales dollar. These irreducible costs represent a major constraint on the company's net profit margin, just 2.0 percent, and in turn its return on equity (see Chapter 13), which is an unexciting 11.1 percent.
*EXHIBIT 3.4 Economies of Scale*
