现金流量表反映了公司的资金运用情况。内部产生的资金还足以支付公司42亿美元的股息。沃尔玛并未通过资本市场筹资，反而实现了长期债务和短期债务的净减少，并赎回了73亿美元的普通股。

<!--en-->
The Statement of Cash Flows spending program. Internally generated funds also covered the company's $4.2 billion of dividends. Instead of going to the capital markets to raise money, Wal-Mart achieved net reductions in its long-term and short-term debt, along with a net retirement of $7.3 billion of common stock.

沃尔玛能够自行为其扩张融资，这是一大优势。有时，由于高利率或股价低迷，新的融资成本会高得令人难以承受；而在商业世界偶尔出现的信贷紧缩期间，外部融资甚至无论付出何种代价都难以获得。

<!--en-->
Wal-Mart's ability to self-finance its expansion is a great advantage. At times, new financing becomes painfully expensive, as a function of high interest rates or depressed stock prices. During the credit crunches that occasionally befall the business world, external financing is unavailable at any price.

沃尔玛对外部资金依赖度较低的基础，在于其盈利能力极强的折扣店业务。如果由于经济衰退或竞争加剧导致这一业务暂时放缓，公司将面临两种选择：要么放慢新店开设速度并削减用于提升利润的技术投资，要么更加依赖外部融资。

<!--en-->
Underlying Wal-Mart's lack of dependence on external funds is a highly profitable discount store business. If this engine were to slow down for a time, as a result of an economic contraction or increased competitive pressures, the company would have two choices. It could reduce its rate of store additions and profit-enhancing investments in technology, or it could become more dependent on external financing.

前一种做法可能会进一步损害盈利能力，而后一种选择则会使沃尔玛更大比例的EBITDA被用于支付利息和股息。简而言之，财务灵活性的丧失会导致进一步的财务灵活性缺失。

<!--en-->
The former approach could further impair profitability, while the latter option would earmark a greater portion of Wal-Mart's EBITDA for interest and dividends. Loss of financial flexibility, in short, leads to further loss of financial flexibility.

当企业面临严重的财务压力时，董事会可能会采取较为极端的措施——削减或取消股息。（比取消股息更极端的措施仅有严厉的开支缩减——即出售核心资产以换取现金，以及停止支付利息或违约。）企业会极力避免削减股息，因为担心因此失去投资者的青睐，进而导致资本成本上升。有时，董事会甚至会借钱来维持现有的股息水平。但这种做法无法长期持续，否则利息成本会不断上升，而内部现金生成却停滞不前，最终可能导致资不抵债。

<!--en-->
If a corporation's financial strain becomes acute, the board of directors may take the comparatively extreme step of cutting or eliminating the dividend. (About the only measures more extreme than elimination of the dividend are severe retrenchment, entailing a sell-off of core assets to generate cash, and cessation of interest payments, or default.) Reducing the dividend is a step that corporations try very hard to avoid, for fear of losing favor with investors and consequently suffering an increase in cost of capital. Boards sometimes go so far as to borrow to maintain a dividend at its existing rate. This tactic cannot continue over an extended period, lest interest costs rise while internal cash generation stagnates, ultimately leading to insolvency.

尽管企业有时会竭尽全力维持股息，但削减股息仍应被视为在盈利低迷时期保持财务灵活性的一种潜在手段。

<!--en-->
Notwithstanding the lengths to which corporations sometimes go to preserve dividends, reducing the dividend must be viewed as a potential means of maintaining financial flexibility in a period of depressed earnings.

毕竟，“可自由支配”这一术语用于描述扣除运营费用和资本支出后剩余的现金流，它强调了股息并非强制性支付，而是由董事会酌情决定的。当维持股息会危及公司的财务健康时，股东实际上可能会敦促董事会削减**派息**，以此作为长期提升股票价值的手段。

<!--en-->
After all, the term *discretionary*, applied to the cash flow that remains available after operating expenses and capital expenditures, emphasizes that dividends are not contractual payments, but disbursed at the board's discretion. When preservation of the dividend jeopardizes a company's financial well-being, shareholders may actually urge the board to cut the **payout** as a means of enhancing the stock value over the longer term.

为了评估股息的安全性，分析师可以计算可自由支配现金流覆盖股息的程度。以沃尔玛为例，该比率高达140.65亿美元 ÷ 42.17亿美元 = 3.34倍，可谓极为充裕。事实上，即便沃尔玛当年净利润为零，仍能支付股息。仅折旧一项就达71.57亿美元（图表4.10中未显示），已经超过了股息数额。基本财务报表

<!--en-->
To gauge the safety of the dividend, analysts can calculate the margin by which discretionary cash flow covers it. In Wal-Mart's case, the ratio is an extremely comfortable $14.065 billion ÷ $4.217 billion = 3.34X. In fact, if Wal-Mart had earned a zero profit for the year, it still would havecovered its dividend. Depreciation alone, at $7.157 billion (not shown in Exhibit 4.10), exceeded dividends.
THE BASIC FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

沃尔玛的财务灵活性堪称卓越。对于许多其他公司而言，净利润的轻微下降就足以使其可自由支配现金流低于计划中的股息支付水平。不过，这些公司通常还有额外的缓冲空间，即削减资本预算。零售商不仅可以放慢新店开设速度，还可以推迟现有门店的计划性翻新。

<!--en-->
Wal-Mart's degree of financial flexibility is exceptional. A modest drop in the net income of many other companies would reduce their discretionary cash flow below the level of planned dividend payments. These companies typically have an additional cushion, however, in the form of potential cut-backs in their capital budgets. A retailer could not only reduce the pace of store additions but also defer planned refurbishment of existing stores.

不过，后一种做法可能会削弱未来的竞争力。零售商发现，如果店铺外观显得陈旧，其销售额就会下降。同样，如果一家工业企业长期将资本支出降至仅够维持现有设备正常运转的水平，它也会失去竞争优势——这种支出仅用于保持现有厂房和设备的良好运行状态，而不用于扩大产能或升级设施以提高生产力。顺便说一句，分析师应寻求独立渠道来确认管理层所称的维护水平数据，或许可以请教熟悉该业务的工程师。企业可能会在经济衰退期间夸大其削减资本支出以节省现金的程度。

<!--en-->
The latter measure, though, could cut into future competitiveness. Retailers find that their sales drop off if their stores start to look tired. Similarly, an industrial company can lose its competitive edge if it drops back to maintenance-level capital spending for any extended period. This is the amount required just to keep existing plant and equipment in good working order, with no expenditures for adding to capacity or modernizing facilities to enhance productivity. Analysts, by the way, should seek independent confirmation of the figure that management cites as the maintenance level, possibly from an engineer familiar with the business. Companies may exaggerate the extent to which they can reduce capital spending to conserve cash in the event of a downturn.

评估财务灵活性的最后一个因素是调整后营运资本的变化。与传统营运资本（流动资产减去流动负债）不同，这一数字排除了应付票据、现金及短期投资。在图表4.10中，前者被纳入短期债务的净变动部分，而当期现金的增减则被视为财务灵活性分析中的余项。

<!--en-->
A final factor in assessing financial flexibility is the change in adjusted working capital. Unlike conventional working capital (current assets minus current liabilities), this figure excludes notes payable, as well as cash and short-term investments. In Exhibit 4.10, the former is part of the net change in short-term debt, while the period's increase or decrease in cash is treated as a residual in the analysis of financial flexibility.

对沃尔玛而言，该财年调整后的营运资本需求所占用的资金规模（43.68亿美元）远小于资本支出。通常来说，随着销售增长，企业的存货和应收账款也会相应增加。资产负债表稳健的企业可以通过增加应付账款（供应商提供的信用）来满足大部分资金需求。然而，如果未售出商品积压导致存货增速远超销售增速，就可能需要外部融资。同样，如果客户付款速度变慢，应收账款也会加大营运资本需求与可用贸易信贷之间的缺口。由此导致的信贷质量指标恶化（参见第13章），又可能促使供应商减少所提供的信用额度。如此一来，财务灵活性的丧失便会陷入恶性循环。

<!--en-->
For Wal-Mart, the fiscal year's adjusted working capital requirement represented a much smaller ($4.368 billion) use of funds than capital expenditures. In general, a company's inventories and receivables expand as sales grow over time. A company with a strong balance sheet can fund much of that cash need by increasing its trade payables (credit extended by vendors). External financing may be required, however, if accumulation of unsold goods causes inventories to rise disproportionately to sales. Similarly, if customers begin paying more slowly than formerly, receivables can widen the gap between working capital requirements and trade credit availability. The resulting deterioration in credit quality measures (see Chapter 13), in turn, may cause vendors to reduce the amount of credit they are willing to provide. Once again, loss of financial flexibility can feed on itself.

### 为“冗余资金”辩护

<!--en-->
*IN DEFENSE OF SLACK*

当信贷稀缺时，无论是因为金融市场整体环境所致，还是由于企业自身债务质量指标恶化，经营环境已经足够艰难。有时情况会更糟：企业甚至被禁止借款。银行信贷协议通常会设定限制性条款，可能包括对总负债的限制（参见第12章“预测财务灵活性”一节）。一旦触及这些条款规定的限度，受约束的企业便无法继续借款以履行义务。《现金流量表》105

<!--en-->
Conditions are tough enough when credit is scarce, either because of general conditions in the financial markets or as a result of deterioration in acompany's debt quality measures. Sometimes the situation is much worse, as a company finds itself actually prohibited from borrowing. Bank credit agreements typically impose restrictive covenants, which may include limitations on total indebtedness (see "Projecting Financial Flexibility" in Chapter 12). Beyond a certain point, a firm bound by such covenants cannot continue borrowing to meet its obligations.
The Statement of Cash Flows
105

违反债务契约或为避免破产而采取的典型后果是：管理层削减可自由支配的支出以防止失去控制权。许多企业在短期内可以削减却不影响运营的项目，对其长期健康发展却至关重要。广告和研发显然是削减对象——它们的效益要在未来才能显现，而成本却在当期就体现出来。多年以来，习惯性压缩此类支出的企业会损害其竞争力，进而将短期问题转化为长期问题。

<!--en-->
A typical consequence of violating debt covenants or striving to head off bankruptcy is that management reduces discretionary expenditures to avoid losing control. Many items that a company can cut without disrupting operations in the short run are essential to its long-term health. Advertising and research are obvious targets for cutbacks. Their benefits are visible only in future periods, while their costs are apparent in the current period. Over many years, a company that habitually scrimps on such expenditures can impair its competitiveness, thereby transforming a short-term problem into a long-term one.

避免这种衰退模式正是财务灵活性的主要益处。如果在景气时期企业能够产生正的融资前现金流，就不必砍掉那些对未来具有投资价值的资本支出及其他开支。同样，保持一定“冗余资金”的企业也不太可能在压力下被迫取消股息发放。如此一来，企业就能避免在资本市场中损害自身形象，并降低未来融资成本。

<!--en-->
Avoiding this pattern of decline is the primary benefit of financial flexibility. If during good times a company can generate positive cash flow before financing, it will not have to chop capital expenditures and other outlays that represent investments in its future. Nor, in all likelihood, will a company that maintains some **slack** be forced to eliminate its dividend under duress. The company will consequently avoid tarnishing its image in the capital markets and raising the cost of future financings.

尽管财务灵活性带来诸多好处，但维持资金缓冲并不被普遍视为明智的企业政策。反对观点基于这样的定义：*自由现金流*是指“超出企业为所有具有正**净现值**的项目所需资金的现金流，这些项目按相关资本成本进行**折现**后仍为正值。”³根据这一论点，管理层应将所有多余的现金流作为股息分配给股东。唯一替代方案是将它们投资于低回报项目（甚至可能是回报更低的可交易证券），从而阻碍股东对其部分资本获得合理回报。持这种观点的人认为，如果任由管理者自行决定，他们往往会将现金困在低回报投资中——因为他们的薪酬往往与其所控制资产的规模增长正相关。

<!--en-->
Despite the blessings that financial flexibility confers, however, maintaining a funds cushion is not universally regarded as a wise corporate policy. The opposing view is based on a definition of *free cash flow* as "cash flow in excess of that required to fund all of a firm's projects that have positive **net present values** when **discounted** at the relevant cost of capital."³ According to this argument, management should dividend all excess cash flow to shareholders. The only alternative is to invest it in low-return projects (or possibly even lower-return marketable securities), thereby preventing shareholders from earning fair returns on a portion of their capital. Left to their own devices, argue the proponents of this view, managers will trap cash in low-return investments because their compensation tends to be positively related to the growth of assets under their control.

因此，应当鼓励管理层将所有多余的现金返还给股东。那些低估财务灵活性价值的人认为，如果这种鼓励措施无效，就应动用**恶意收购**的威胁手段。

<!--en-->
Therefore, management should be encouraged to remit all excess cash to shareholders. If encouragement fails to do the trick, the threat of **hostile takeover** should be employed, say those who minimize the value of financial flexibility.

反对保留多余现金流的观点听起来确实合乎逻辑。此外，众多研究⁴也支持这一观点，这些研究表明企业即便在耗尽优质投资机会后仍会继续投资。不过，由于这一论点源于经济理论，在实践中必须谨慎应用。过度投资无疑已在许多行业中导致长期的产能过剩，进而造成持续的低盈利水平。回顾起来，涉事企业若增加股息支付或回购股票，而非兴建新厂，反而会更好地服务于股东利益。然而，这种判断是基于事后视角得出的。管理者之所以过度投资，可能是因为他们相信了最终被证明过于乐观的经济增长预测。倘若需求按预期速度增长，那些拒绝扩大产能的企业或许就无法维持其市场份额。

<!--en-->
The argument against retaining excess cash flow certainly sounds logical. It is supported, moreover, by numerous studies⁴ indicating the tendency of companies to continue investing even after they have exhausted their good opportunities. Growing as it does out of economic theory, though, the argument must be applied judiciously in practice. Overinvestment has unquestionably led, in many industries, to prolonged periods of excess capacity,producing in turn chronically poor profitability. In retrospect, the firms involved would have served their shareholders better if they had increased their dividend payouts or repurchased stock, instead of constructing new plants. That judgment, however, benefits from hindsight. Managers may have over-invested because they believed forecasts of economic growth that ultimately proved too optimistic. Had demand grown at the expected rate, a firm that had declined to expand capacity might have been unable to maintain its market share.

从长远来看，无法跟上那些更具扩张意愿的竞争对手所实现的规模经济，对股东的伤害可能比几年的产能过剩更为严重。金融分析师的职责包括在不依赖事后信息的情况下，对企业再投资政策作出判断；他们不应被动接受那种认为短期内低回报意味着行业已无值得开发的机会的普遍观点。《基本财务报表》

<!--en-->
In the long run, failing to keep up with the scale economies achieved by more expansion-minded competitors could have harmed shareholders more than a few years of excess capacity. The financial analyst's job includes making judgments about a firm's reinvestment policies—without the benefit of hindsight—and does not consist of passively accepting the prevailing wisdom that low returns in the near term prove that an industry has no future opportunities worth exploiting.
THE BASIC FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

理论家们难以捕捉到的一个更微妙之处在于：财务灵活性可以直接转化为运营灵活性。当信贷环境紧张、难以筹措营运资金时，将现金投资于可变现证券能使企业相对于那些精打细算的竞争对手获得优势。放弃财务灵活性的另一个不太明显的风险是：经济衰退引发的临时裁员可能导致企业永久失去经验丰富的熟练工人。由于被裁掉的熟练员工另谋高就，随后的经济复苏期生产率便会受损。因此，继续运营工厂并刻意增加存货，以留住有价值的员工，可能是更为经济的做法。

<!--en-->
A subtler point not easily captured by theorists is that financial flexibility can translate directly into operating flexibility. Keeping cash trapped in marketable securities can enable a firm to gain an edge over lean-and-mean competitors when tight credit conditions make it difficult to finance working capital needs. Another less obvious risk of eschewing financial flexibility is the danger of permanently losing experienced skilled workers through temporary layoffs occasioned by recessions. Productivity suffers during the subsequent recovery as a consequence of laid-off skilled employees finding permanent jobs elsewhere. It may therefore be economical to continue to run plants, thereby deliberately building up inventory, to keep valued workers on the payroll.

如果没有应对营运资金融资需求突然增加的能力，这一战略便难以实施。

<!--en-->
This strategy is difficult to implement without some capability of adjusting to a sudden increase in working capital financing requirements.

## 结论

<!--en-->
*CONCLUSION*

过去四十年间，现金流量表已成为其他报表的重要补充。在资产负债表和损益表只能提供有限信息的许多情况下，它显得尤为宝贵。例如，对于一家受高度杠杆影响且管理层旨在最小化而非最大化账面利润的企业而言，损益表并非衡量其成功与否的可靠指标。同样，对于净资产已经大幅缩水的企业来说，本季度股东权益较上一季度减少10%这一事实也基本无关紧要。此时投资者或债权人最关心的是：企业能否通过继续履行短期义务来争取足够时间以解决经营难题。《现金流量表》107

<!--en-->
Over the past four decades, the statement of cash flows has become a valuable complement to the other statements. It is invaluable in many situations where the balance sheet and income statement provide only limited insight. For example, the income statement is a dubious measure of the success of a highly leveraged company that is being managed to minimize, rather than maximize, reported profits. Similarly, it is largely irrelevant whether the balance sheet of a company with an already substantially depleted net worth shows 10 percent lower equity in the current quarter than in the previous one. The primary concern of the investor or creditor at such times is whether the company can buy enough time to solve its operating problems by continuing to meet its near-term obligations.
The Statement of Cash Flows
107

现金流量表的作用不仅在于深化对那些损益表和资产负债表无法充分反映的风险与机遇的分析，它还有助于确定企业所属的生命周期阶段。在发展的各个阶段，财务灵活性对于应对各类典型挑战都至关重要。现金流量表是衡量灵活性的最佳工具；与普遍看法相反，灵活性并非仅仅是给胆怯投资者提供的保护伞。在积极进取但审慎的管理层手中，现金流缓冲能够帮助企业在其竞争对手被迫削减开支时，依然维持必要的长期投资。

<!--en-->
The cash flow statement does more than enrich the analysis of companies encountering risks and opportunities that the income statement and balance sheet are not designed to portray. It also helps to identify the life cycle categories into which companies fit. At all stages of development, financial flexibility is essential to meeting the types of challenges that typically arise. The cash flow statement is the best tool for measuring flexibility, which, contrary to a widely held view, is not merely a security blanket for squeamish investors. In the hands of aggressive but prudent management, a cash flow cushion can enable a company to sustain essential long-term investment spending when competitors are forced to cut back.

## 第五章

<!--en-->
*CHAPTER 5*

# 什么是利润？

<!--en-->
*What Is Profit?*

在商业世界和经济理论中，利润占据着至关重要的地位。追求利润的需求为企业组织带来了秩序与纪律。它推动了降低成本的创新，进而促进稀缺资源的有效利用。盈利动机还鼓励储蓄和承担风险，这两者是经济发展不可或缺的因素。最后，盈利能力是商人衡量自身成就、证明薪酬合理性的标尺。

<!--en-->
Profits hold an exalted place in the business world and in economic theory. The necessity of producing profits imposes order and discipline on business organizations. It fosters cost-reducing innovations, which in turn promote the efficient use of scarce resources. The profit motive also encourages savings and risk taking, two indispensable elements of economic development. Finally, profitability is a yardstick by which businesspeople can measure their achievements and justify their claims to compensation.

鉴于上述这些重要的经济功能，人们或许会认为财务报表的使用者早已制定出普遍认可的利润定义。然而，实际情况仅在以下极其基础层面上如此：

<!--en-->
In view of all these essential economic functions, one might suppose that users of financial statements would have long since devised a universally agreed-upon definition of profit. This is the case, however, only at the following, extremely rudimentary level:

$$
\text{Profit} = \text{Revenue} - \text{Costs}
$$

不过，以这种方式定义利润只会引发更多疑问：什么是收入？哪些成本才算数？或者更准确地说，哪些成本现在算数，哪些以后才算数？由于这些问题可以有多种答案，因此市面上存在无数种利润定义。对于财务报表分析师而言，最需要理解的区别在于真实利润与会计利润之间。

<!--en-->
Defining profit in such a manner merely stirs up questions, however: What is revenue? Which costs count? Or, more precisely, which costs count now, and which count later? Because these questions can be answered in many different ways, countless definitions of profit are in common use. For analysts of financial statements, the most important distinction to understand is between bona fide profits and accounting profits.

## 真实利润与会计利润

<!--en-->
*BONA FIDE PROFITS VERSUS ACCOUNTING PROFITS*

在定义真实利润时，“收入减去成本”这一简单公式是一个有用的起点。计算此类利润时，分析师必须确保只考虑真实的收入，并扣除所有相关成本。成本清单包括但不限于劳动力、原材料、场地费用、购买的服务、设备折旧以及税费。无论分析师的计算多么细致，除非能通过一项关键检验，否则任何利润计算结果都无法令人满意：

<!--en-->
In defining bona fide profits, the simple formula, revenue minus costs, represents a useful starting point. When calculating this kind of profit, the analyst must take care to consider only genuine revenues and to deduct all relevant costs. A nonexhaustive list of costs includes labor, materials, occupancy, services purchased, depreciation of equipment, and taxes. No matterhow meticulously the analyst carries out these computations, however, no calculation of profit can be satisfactory unless it passes a litmus test:

深入剖析利润情况

<!--en-->
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

*企业获得真实利润后，其所有者的财富会比之前更丰厚。* 为了强调这一点：没有财富的增加，就不算真实利润。真实利润才是财务分析中真正重要的利润类型。

<!--en-->
*After a company earns a bona fide profit, its owners are wealthier than they were beforehand.*
To underscore the point, there can be no bona fide profit without an increase in wealth. Bona fide profits are the only kind of profits that truly matter in financial analysis.

至于会计利润，公认会计原则（GAAP）为其计算制定了详尽且精确的规则。不过对财务分析师而言，“会计利润”的实际定义很简单：

<!--en-->
As for accounting profits, generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) define voluminous rules for calculating them with extraordinary precision. For financial analysts, however, the practical definition of an *accounting profit* is simple:

*会计利润就是会计准则所认定的那个数字。* 如果在特定时期内，企业并未增加所有者的财富，但会计准则却认定其产生了利润，那就足够了。这种并未反映真实财富增长的会计利润，对许多股市投资者来说已经足够。他们欣然为任何经知名会计师事务所认定并宣布为“利润”的数字赋予市盈率倍数。

<!--en-->
*An accounting profit is whatever the accounting rules say it is.*
If, during a stated interval, a business adds nothing to its owners' wealth, but the accounting rules state that it has earned a profit, that is good enough. An accounting profit that reflects no genuine increase in wealth is certainly sufficient for many stock market investors. They cheerfully assign a price-earnings multiple to any number that a reputable accounting firm waves its magic wand over and declares to be a profit.

### 什么是收入？

<!--en-->
*WHAT IS REVENUE?*

例如，假设某企业家创办了一家餐饮特许经营公司。虚构的Salsa Meister International并不经营任何Salsa Meister餐厅，它只是向其他企业家出售特许经营权并收取加盟费。

<!--en-->
Suppose, for example, that an entrepreneur launches a restaurant-franchising business. The fictitious Salsa Meister International does not operate any Salsa Meister restaurants. It merely sells franchises to other entrepreneurs and collects franchise fees.

遗憾的是，这些加盟餐厅持续亏损。不过这一事实并不影响Salsa Meister International的会计利润。这些餐厅的运营不属于Salsa Meister International，它们的收入不是该公司的收入，成本也不是该公司的成本。Salsa Meister International的收入完全来自加盟费，这些费用源于其为加盟商提供的菜单开发、会计系统支持、员工培训以及广告宣传等服务。

<!--en-->
The franchised restaurants, sad to say, consistently lose money. That fact has no bearing on Salsa Meister International's accounting profit, however. The restaurants' operations are not part of Salsa Meister International, their revenues are not its revenues, and their costs are not its costs. Salsa Meister International's income consists entirely of franchise fees, which it earns by rendering the franchisees such services as developing menus, providing accounting systems, training restaurant employees, and creating advertising campaigns.

精明的分析师会追问：那些亏损的加盟商从何处筹得现金来支付加盟费？图表5.1解答了这一问题。Salsa Meister International向公众发售股票，随后将所得资金借给加盟商。加盟商则以“加盟费”的名义将现金送回给Salsa Meister International。Salsa Meister International心安理得地收下这些费用——它们超过了维持公司总部运转所需的微薄成本——并将其重新命名为收入。

<!--en-->
An astute analyst will ask how money-losing franchisees come up with cash to pay fees. The diagram in Exhibit 5.1 answers this riddle. Salsa Meister International sells stock to the public and then lends the proceeds to the franchisees. The franchisees send the cash right back to Salsa MeisterInternational under the rubric of fees. Salsa Meister International gratefully accepts the fees, which exceed the modest costs of running a corporate headquarters, and renames them revenue.

什么是利润？

<!--en-->
What Is Profit?

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/212df2607dd2c3252a4dd057bc2f334c.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261012%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261012T065612Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=bb82d4b4cfcd58052f2d0beb95705e9d10ba80f14f926a62565af628034baff9)

***图表5.1：将股市融资转化为收入* 根据GAAP规定，Salsa Meister International确实创造了利润。投资者依据会计利润乘以市盈率来估值，该公司便借此机会进行下一次公开发行。募集资金再次用于支付加盟商的加盟费，随着Salsa Meister连锁店向新地区扩张，加盟商数量也随之增加。会计利润随之上升，将股市融资先标记为加盟费、最终标记为盈利的循环便再度开始。

<!--en-->
***EXHIBIT 5.1** Turning Stock Market Proceeds into Revenue*
According to GAAP, Salsa Meister International has earned a profit. Investors apply a price-earnings multiple to the accounting profit. On the strength of that valuation, the company goes forward with its next public stock offering. Once again, the proceeds finance the payment of fees by franchisees, whose numbers have meanwhile increased in connection with the Salsa Meister chain's expansion into new regions. Accounting profits rise, and the cycle of relabeling stock market proceeds, first as fees and finally as earnings, starts all over again.

然而，精明的分析师却为此感到困扰。透过交易的形式看本质，可以明显看出Salsa Meister International的财富并未增加。资金只是从股东流向公司，再流向特许经营商，最后又回到公司，期间经历了几次名称上的变更而已。

<!--en-->
The astute analyst is troubled, however. Cutting through the form of the transactions to the substance, it is clear that Salsa Meister International's wealth has not increased. Cash has simply traveled from the shareholders to the company, to the franchisees, and then back to the company, undergoing a few name changes along the way.

显然，仅仅让资金循环并不能增加财富。如果杰克给吉尔一美元，而她立刻又将其还给他，那么在这次所谓的交易之后，双方的情况并不会比交易前更好。从定义上讲，杰克和吉尔都没有获得真正的利润。无论GAAP对会计利润如何界定，Salsa Meister International同样没有获得真正的利润。更深入地审视利润问题。

<!--en-->
Merely circulating funds, it is clear, does not increase wealth. If Jack hands Jill a dollar, which she promptly hands right back to him, neither party is better off after the so-called transaction than before it. By definition,neither Jack nor Jill has earned a bona fide profit. Salsa Meister International has not earned a bona fide profit either, regardless of what GAAP may say about accounting profits.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

迟早，投资者会意识到这一点。一旦如此，该公司便将失去通过在股市筹集新资金来制造会计利润的能力。届时，Salsa Meister的股价将会跌至其内在价值——零。投资者将蒙受重大损失，而这些损失本可以通过询问公司所报告的利润是否真正反映了财富的增加来避免。此外，除非投资者开始明白真正的利润有时与会计利润存在巨大差异，否则他们还会继续犯下类似的错误。

<!--en-->
Sooner or later, investors will come to this realization. When that happens, the company will lose its ability to manufacture accounting profits by raising new funds in the stock market. Salsa Meister's stock price will then fall to its intrinsic value—zero. Investors will suffer heavy losses, which they could have avoided by asking whether the company's reported profits truly reflected increases in wealth. Moreover, the investors will continue making similar mistakes unless they begin to understand that bona fide profits sometimes differ radically from accounting profits.

### 哪些成本才算数？

<!--en-->
*WHICH COSTS COUNT?*

愿意不把会计利润视为表面数值，是进行真正有用的财务报表分析的关键要素。同样重要的是，分析师在决定用什么来替代GAAP对利润的定义时必须谨慎行事。一旦他们脱离GAAP所规定的统一规则体系，分析师便进入了思想的自由市场，在那里众多机构会推销各种相互竞争的盈利指标。

<!--en-->
The willingness to take accounting profits at something other than face value is an essential element of genuinely useful financial statement analysis. It is likewise imperative that analysts exercise care in deciding what to substitute for a GAAP definition of profit. Once they leave the GAAP world of agreed-upon rules, analysts enter a free market of ideas, where numerous parties hawk competing versions of earnings.

许多变体都取决于在确定最具分析价值的盈利定义时该扣除哪些成本。虽然其中一些流行的变体能为财务报表分析中的棘手问题提供见解，但另一些却反而会使事实变得模糊不清。许多财务报表的编制者试图利用人们对GAAP的不满，鼓动分析师采用那些能使自身利润看起来高于会计利润或真正利润的盈利指标。

<!--en-->
Many of the variations hang on the question of which costs to deduct in deriving the most analytically informative definition of earnings. While some of the popular variants offer insight into knotty problems of financial statement analysis, others have the opposite effect of obscuring the facts. Many issuers of financial statements attempt to exploit dissatisfaction with GAAP by encouraging analysts to adopt earnings measures that make their own profits appear higher than either their accounting profits or their bona fide profits.

当今大多数替代性盈利指标的原型是一种将折旧加回的指标。早在1930年，一位投资专家就曾敦促投资者忽略基于会计数据的盈利，他这样说道：

<!--en-->
The archetype for most of today's alternative earnings measures is a version that adds back depreciation. As far back as 1930, an investment expert urged investors to ignore accounting-based earnings in the following words:

> 教科书会建议投资者关注已扣除折旧费用后的盈利数据。但归根结底，折旧仅仅是一项会计项目，在一定范围内可以被调整，以呈现出所期望的净利润。因此，如果可能的话，投资者最好获取未扣除折旧前的盈利数据，再自行估算折旧费用，从而得出近似的净利润。¹ 什么是利润？需要注意的是，作者并不否认折旧在盈利计算中的相关性；他反对的是折旧数据过于容易被人操控。² 报表编制者只需利用自身权限，设定较短或较长的资产使用年限，就能随意调高或调低报告的盈利数字。对于公司向潜在投资者提交的财务报表而言，可以合理推测，“所期望的净利润”往往高于公司实际的真实利润。因此，必要的调整就是*增加*折旧费用，进而*减少*盈利。作者赞同当今那些提倡替代性盈利指标的人士的观点，认为合理的分析需要对报告收益进行调整；但他绝没有主张分析师完全忽略折旧。另一方面，许多报告盈利微薄的公司宣传员却毫不羞于鼓动投资者无视折旧。这种对**权责发生制会计**根基的大胆挑战，其灵感源自私人房地产领域——在那里，管理上市公司的逻辑被彻底颠倒过来。私人房地产所有者并非利用会计规则中的一切弹性来最大化报告盈利，反而力求最小化报告收入，进而减少所得税。因此，当私人投资者购置一栋建筑（可折旧资产）及其所占用的土地（不可折旧）时，通常会尽可能将较高的购买价格分摊到建筑上。这种处理方式能最大化折旧费用，从而减少业主的税负。假设该建筑的年度租金收入恰好抵消业主的实际支出，如维护费、修缮费、房产税以及房贷利息；换句话说，在不考虑非现金性质的折旧费用前，业主处于收支平衡状态。一旦计入折旧，该物业便显示出年度亏损，从而降低业主的所得税额。再假设几年后，业主出售了土地和建筑。还清房贷后，由于房地产价值随时间推移而上涨，她最终获得的现金比最初投资额还要多。总结这位房地产投资者的经历：她以高于购入价的价格售出了物业，且在此过程中并未因运营而产生净现金支出；相反，非现金性质的折旧费用所带来的税收节省反而促成了其财富的增长。关键在于，这位投资者比购买建筑前更加富有。根据我们的定义，尽管她每年都报告亏损，但她确实实现了真正的利润。更令人费解的是，她还能通过出售物业获得收益。经济理论认为，投资之所以有价值，是因为它能产生利润；进而，只有利润增加，价值才能提升。然而在本例中，尽管物业持续出现亏损，其价值却依然上涨。 更深入地审视利润问题：当然，这些奇特现象背后有合理的解释。税法允许业主摊销物业成本的比率，实际上高估了资产的实际损耗程度。在一栋建筑通常很长的使用寿命期内，出于税务目的，它可能会被多次计提折旧。 经济折旧与税收折旧之间的差异，可以被视为对社会性生产性投资的补贴。或者，它也可以被看作是房地产运营商对制定税法的立法者施加影响的一种体现。无论如何，传统的损益表都无法准确反映买卖建筑物的盈利能力。更接近现实的做法是干脆忽略折旧费用，转而关注**现金回报率**。简单来说，业主在投资初期投入一笔资金，在期末收回更多资金，同时还能在持有建筑物期间通过节省税款来获得现金流。

<!--en-->
> Textbooks will advise the investor to look for earnings figures which give effect to depreciation charges. But depreciation, after all, is a purely accounting item, and can be adjusted, within limits, to show such net earnings as are desired. Therefore it would seem preferable for the investor to obtain, if possible, earnings before depreciation, and to make his own estimate of depreciation in arriving at approximate net earnings.¹
What Is Profit?
Observe that the author does not dispute the relevance of depreciation to the calculation of earnings. Rather, he objects that they are too malleable.² The issuer of the statements can raise or lower its reported earnings simply by using its latitude to assume shorter or longer average lives for its depreciable assets.
It is fair to assume, in the case of financial statements that companies present to potential investors, that “such net earnings as are desired” are higher than the company’s bona fide profits. Therefore, the necessary adjustment is to *increase* depreciation and thereby *reduce* earnings. The author agrees with today’s boosters of alternative earnings measures that proper analysis requires adjustments to reported income, but he is very far from urging analysts to ignore depreciation altogether.
Promoters of many companies with negligible reported earnings, on the other hand, are not bashful about urging investors to disregard depreciation. This audacious assault on the very foundations of **accrual accounting** draws its inspiration from the world of privately owned real estate, where the logic of managing a public company is turned upside down. Instead of exploiting every bit of latitude in the accounting rules to maximize reported earnings, private owners of real estate strive to minimize reported income and, by extension, income taxes. Accordingly, when a private investor acquires a building (a depreciable asset) and the land that it sits on (which is not depreciable), she typically attributes as large a portion of the purchase price as possible to the building. That treatment maximizes the depreciation expense and minimizes the owner’s taxes.
Let us suppose that annual rental revenue on the building offsets the landlord’s out-of-pocket expenses, such as maintenance, repairs, property taxes, and interest on the property’s mortgage. The owner, in other words, is breaking even, before taking into account the noncash expense of depreciation. Including depreciation, the property shows an annual loss, which reduces the owner’s income tax bill. Let us also assume that after a few years, the owner sells the land and building. After paying off the mortgage balance, she walks away with more cash than she originally invested, thanks to the tendency of real estate values to rise over time.
Recapping the real estate investor’s experience, she has sold the property for more than she paid. Her gain has not been reduced along the way by net cash outlays on operations. On the contrary, the tax savings produced by the noncash depreciation expense have contributed to the rise in her wealth. The key point is that the investor is wealthier than she was before she bought the building. According to our definition, she has realized a bona fide profit, despite reporting losses every single year. Adding to the paradox is the investor’s success in selling the property for a gain. Economic theorystates that an investment has value only because it produces profits. By extension, the value can increase only if the profits increase. In this instance, however, the property's value rose despite an uninterrupted flow of red ink.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS
Naturally, these curious events have a rational explanation. The rate at which the tax code allows owners to write off property overstates actual wear and tear. Over the typically very long life of a building, it may get depreciated several times over for tax purposes. The disparity between economic depreciation and tax-based depreciation may be viewed as a subsidy for socially productive investment. Alternatively, it can be seen as a testament to the real estate operators' influence over the legislators who write the tax code.
Either way, a conventional income statement provides a cockeyed view of the profitability of buying and selling buildings. A closer approximation of reality ignores the depreciation expense altogether and focuses on **cash-on-cash-profit**. In the simplest terms, the owner lays out a sum at the beginning of the investment and takes out a bigger sum at the end, while also generating cash—through tax savings—during the period in which she owns the building.

### 这一概念能被延伸多远？

<!--en-->
*HOW FAR CAN THE CONCEPT BE STRETCHED?*

在有限程度上，忽略折旧的盈利分析也可应用于房地产领域之外。在广播行业，企业所记录的折旧与摊销费用往往远超资产的实际损耗。例如，当一家公司收购广播电台或电视台时，其价格中属于厂房及设备的部分所占比例相对较小；电台价值的更大组成部分源于其对部分广播频谱的独占使用权——这种稀缺资源的价值往往会随时间推移而上升。正如房地产案例所示，尽管广播公司在扣除折旧后可能连年亏损，但最终出售电台时却能获得丰厚利润。分析师不应仅基于传统净利润来分析广播公司，而应重点关注**广播现金流**，其通常定义为：

<!--en-->
To a limited extent, a profitability analysis that ignores depreciation is applicable outside the world of real estate. In the broadcasting business, companies typically record depreciation and amortization expense that far exceeds physical wear and tear on assets. For example, when a company buys a radio or television station, the price reflects a comparatively small component of plant and equipment. The larger portion of the station's value derives from its exclusive right to utilize part of the broadcasting spectrum, a scarce resource that tends to become more valuable over time. Much as in the real estate illustration, the broadcaster may show perennial losses after depreciation, yet realize a handsome profit when it finally sells the station. Instead of analyzing broadcasters on the basis of conventional net income, it is appropriate for analysts to focus on **broadcast cash flow**, usually defined as:

$$
\text{operating income} + \text{depreciation and amortization} + \text{corporate overhead}
$$

（更精确的广播现金流计算会扣除购买新节目的现金支出，同时加回此前购置节目的摊销费用；这两项数据均可在现金流量表中找到。）什么是利润？显然，有意忽略折旧是一种需谨慎使用的分析手段。在许多行业中，固定资产主要由机器或车辆构成，它们确实会因使用而贬值。分析误差的主要风险并不在于报告的折旧费用远超经济折旧，而是恰恰相反。

<!--en-->
(A more meticulous calculation of broadcast cash flow deducts cash outlays for acquisition of new programming while adding back the amortization of the cost of previously acquired programming; both items can be found on the statement of cash flows.)
What Is Profit?
Clearly, the deliberate neglect of depreciation is an analytical option that should be used with discretion. In many industries, fixed assets consist mainly of machines or vehicles that really do diminish in value through use. The major risk of analytical error does not arise from the possibility that reported depreciation expense will substantially exceed economic depreciation, but the reverse.

通过类比房地产和广播行业，任何资本密集型行业中勉强盈利的公司都能宣称自己实现了盈利。其窍门不过是宣称分析师不应再考虑折旧而已。不过，以这种方式产生的所谓“盈利”既算不上会计利润，也算不上真正的利润。

<!--en-->
Through a false analogy with real estate and broadcasting, any marginally unprofitable company in a capital-intensive business can declare itself to be in the black. The trick is simply to proclaim that analysts should no longer consider depreciation. Supposed earnings generated in such fashion qualify as neither accounting profits nor bona fide profits, however.

## 结论

<!--en-->
*CONCLUSION*

尽管衡量利润至关重要，但商界人士却无法给出适用于所有情况的完美定义。就连“收入减去成本”这一简单公式，也会因会计口径下收入和成本的易变性而失效。正如第6章和第7章所展示的，这些衡量企业绩效的基本指标极易被操纵和扭曲，因此不能轻信其表面数值。此外，我们对房地产和杠杆收购的简要讨论也表明：即便净利润的计算完全符合GAAP准则，它与投资者的实际回报率也可能并无关联。

<!--en-->
Despite the critical importance of measuring profit, businesspeople cannot produce a definition that is satisfactory in every situation. Even the simple formula of revenue minus costs founders on the malleability of accounting-based revenues and costs. As Chapters 6 and 7 demonstrate, these basic measures of corporate performance are far too subject to manipulation and distortion to be taken at face value. Also, our brief discussions of real estate and leveraged buyouts show that net earnings can be calculated in perfect accordance with GAAP yet bear little relation to an investor's rate of return.

鉴于上述情况，财务分析师必须把握微妙的平衡：一方面，他们不能拘泥于会计教条而脱离经济现实；另一方面，也不能接受那些寻求廉价资本者强加给他们的“现实版本”。分析师应对此类说法持怀疑态度——即声称企业的所谓成本不过是会计惯例，而持不同意见者便是守旧之人。

<!--en-->
In light of such observations, financial analysts must walk a fine line. On the one hand, they must not lose touch with economic reality by hewing to accounting orthodoxy. On the other hand, they must not accept the version of reality that seekers of cheap capital would like to foist on them. Analysts should be skeptical of claims that a business's alleged costs are mere accounting conventions and that anyone who believes otherwise is a fuddy-duddy.

## 第6章

<!--en-->
*CHAPTER 6*

# 收入确认

<!--en-->
*Revenue Recognition*

经验告诉我们，即便经过审计，直接采信报告的收入数据也可能十分危险。许多企业采用极具侵略性的收入确认方式，虽符合GAAP准则，却扭曲了背后的经济现实。有时，一心想达成业绩目标的高管甚至会越过底线，进行欺诈性收入确认。通常，表面上的巨大成功往往预示着此前报告的收入很可能被向下修正。在维持股价的巨大压力下，销售增长极其迅猛的公司似乎尤其容易采取此类做法。

<!--en-->
Experience teaches that it can be dangerous to accept reported revenues at face value, even if they have been audited. Many corporations employ highly aggressive recognition practices that comply with GAAP yet distort the underlying economic reality. Sometimes, executives hell-bent on making their numbers will cross the line into fraudulent revenue recognition. Often, outward signs of exceptional success indicate, in reality, a high probability of downward revisions of previously reported revenues. Under intense pressure to maintain their stock prices, companies characterized by extremely rapid sales growth seem particularly prone to take liberties.

### 制药行业的渠道填塞行为

<!--en-->
*CHANNEL-STUFFING IN THE DRUG BUSINESS*

2002年4月3日，百时美施贵宝公司的股价在盘后交易中暴跌14%，原因是该公司宣布第一季度营业利润为每股0.44至0.47美元。而Thomson Financial/First Call调查的分析师此前预期为每股0.56美元。这家制药商还称，全年利润将比2001年的每股2.41美元至少下降25%。

<!--en-->
On April 3, 2002, Bristol-Myers Squibb shares plummeted by as much as 14 percent in after-hours trading after the company said first-quarter earnings from operations would be $0.44 to $0.47 a share. Analysts surveyed by Thomson Financial/First Call had been expecting $0.56. For the full year, said the pharmaceutical producer, earnings would drop by at least 25 percent from 2001's $2.41 a share.

在这一意外消息公布后，首席执行官彼得·多兰亲自接管全球药品业务。该业务的前负责人随即离职。两周后，公司又宣布首席财务官也将辞职。

<!--en-->
In the wake of the negative surprise, Chief Executive Officer Peter Dolan assumed direct responsibility for the worldwide medicines business. The previous head of the unit left the company. Two weeks later, the company announced that its chief financial officer would step down as well.

预计收益突然下滑的原因是：2001年，百时美施贵宝公司向批发商提供折扣，以促使他们以远超药店处方需求的速度购买产品。这推高了2001年某些药物的营收，因为对批发商的销售额超过了消费者的终端需求。然而到了2002年，批发商并未重新订货，而是消耗掉积压的库存以满足药店客户的需求。因此，百时美施贵宝公司对批发商的销售随之放缓。

<!--en-->
The explanation for the sudden drop in projected earnings was that in 2001 Bristol-Myers gave wholesalers discounts to induce them to buy its products at a much faster rate than necessary to fill prescriptions at pharmacies. That boosted revenues for certain drugs in 2001, as sales to wholesalers ran above end demand by consumers. In 2002, however, instead of reordering, wholesalers worked down their bloated inventories to supply their pharmacy customers. Bristol-Myers's sales to wholesalers consequentlyslackened.

多兰告诉分析师和投资者，公司正在削减发货量，2002年的利润将取决于批发商库存水平下降的速度。更深入地看利润情况……

<!--en-->
Dolan told analysts and investors that the company was cutting back shipments and that 2002 profits would depend on how quickly the wholesalers' inventory levels could be reduced.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

“渠道填塞”是证券分析师用来描述百时美施贵宝公司所采用的财务报告手段的术语，其目的是将未来收入提前计入当期。只要所获折扣足以覆盖相关的**持有成本**，药品批发商就乐意持有超出实际需求的库存。他们入库药品的保质期通常还有约两年时间，因此这些产品在批发商仓库中贬值的风险很小。此外，以当前价格购入额外药品的批发商还能从制造商随后的零售价上调中获益；这种涨价使他们能够对按旧价购进的库存收取更高的加价。

<!--en-->
*Channel-stuffing* is a security analysts' term for the financial reporting gimmick that Bristol-Myers employed to accelerate future revenues to the current period. Drug wholesalers were happy to hold more inventory than they needed, as long as the discounts they received were large enough to cover the related **carrying costs**. Expiration dates for the drugs they took into inventory were typically about two years in the future, so there was little risk that the products would lose their value while sitting in the wholesalers' warehouses. Furthermore, wholesalers that bought extra drugs at the current price stood to gain from subsequent increases in the retail price by the manufacturer. The price hikes would allow them to take higher markups on inventory purchased at the old price.

不过，为何百时美施贵宝公司要费心去填满其批发分销渠道呢？尤其是考虑到这些折扣意味着放弃本可收回的销售款项。批发商所能吸收的冗余库存也是有限的。

<!--en-->
Why, though, would Bristol-Myers bother to stuff its wholesale distribution channels, especially considering that the discounts represented sales dollars forgone and never to be recovered? Wholesalers could absorb only so much redundant inventory.

迟早，这种手段必将终结，从而暴露出该公司通过挪用未来期间的销售来虚增收益的事实。

<!--en-->
Sooner or later, the scheme would have to end, making it apparent that the company had overstated earnings by borrowing sales from future periods.

这正是百时美施贵宝公司发生的情况。2003年3月10日，该公司重新编制了1999年至2001年的财务报表，以纠正“错误和不恰当的会计处理”。公司将持续经营业务的收益减少了约9亿美元，不过2002年的数据则被向上修正以部分抵消这一影响。此前，公司曾向投资者表示，此次重新编制报表只是将已报告的收入从早期期间转移到2002年和2003年。但最终，公司从早期年份中扣除了25亿美元，而在后期年份中仅确认了19亿美元；公司解释称其中6亿美元的差异“主要是由于销售退货、回扣等应计项目的变化”¹以及会计政策调整所致。百时美施贵宝公司的股价在2000年底曾达到70.37美元的高峰，此后却跌至22.51美元。即便在对投资者造成如此损失之后，百时美施贵宝公司仍未停止修订行为。2004年3月16日，公司再次重新编制1999年至2002年以及2003年的收益数据，并将其向上修正。

<!--en-->
That is exactly what happened to Bristol-Myers. On March 10, 2003, the company restated its financial statements for 1999 through 2001 to correct “errors and inappropriate accounting.” The company chopped earnings from continuing operations by about $900 million, partially offset by an upward revision for 2002. Earlier, the company had told investors that its planned restatement would merely shift reported revenues from earlier periods to 2002 and 2003. As it turned out, however, the company deleted $2.5 billion from the earlier years and booked only $1.9 billion in the later years, explaining that the disappearance of $0.6 billion was “primarily due to changes in accruals from sales returns, rebates,”¹ and accounting changes. Bristol-Myers stock, which had reached a peak of $70.37 at the end of 2000, closed at $22.51. Even after this damage to investors, Bristol-Myers was not done with its revisions. On March 16, 2004, the company restated its 1999 through 2002 earnings and its 2003 earnings upward.

#### 注定失败的计划背景

<!--en-->
*Background of a Doomed Scheme*

2001年和2002年间股价的急剧下跌有助于解释为何百时美施贵宝公司会采取这种注定无法持续的盈余操纵手段。与其他制药商一样，由于难以开发出能替代专利即将到期产品的新药，百时美施贵宝公司面临着盈利压力。自1989年百时美与施贵宝合并以来，公司在耗费数十亿美元研发经费后仍未推出一款重磅药物。公司最大的希望——降压药Vanlev——在发现不良副作用后，于2000年未能获得美国食品药品监督管理局的批准。2001年，公司因同意支付20亿美元收购抗癌药Erbitux而蒙受尴尬，该药由生物技术公司ImClone Systems研发，后来也未能获得美国食品药品监督管理局的批准。收入确认 121

<!--en-->
The stock's precipitous decline during 2001 and 2002 helped to explain why Bristol-Myers manipulated its earnings in a manner that was sure to prove unsustainable. Along with other pharmaceutical producers, Bristol-Myers was feeling profit pressures due to difficulties in developing new drugs to replace sales of products on which patent protection was expiring. Thecompany had not generated a single major drug from billions of research dollars since the 1989 merger of Bristol-Myers and Squibb. Management's biggest hope, the hypertension drug Vanlev, failed to obtain Food and Drug Administration approval in 2000 after adverse side effects were discovered. In 2001, the company suffered embarrassment when it agreed to pay $2 billion for cancer drug Erbitux, a discovery of biotechnology company ImClone Systems that later failed to obtain Food and Drug Administration approval.
Revenue Recognition
121

1996年，时任首席执行官查尔斯·海姆博尔德二世向投资者承诺，到2000年年度收益增长率将达到12%。但随着行业竞争加剧以及低价仿制药威胁到百时美施贵宝公司一款畅销抗癌药的销售，这一目标难以实现。1999年底的一次会议后，海姆博尔德取代了医药部门负责人唐纳德·海顿二世。

<!--en-->
In 1996, then-CEO Charles Heimbold Jr. promised investors 12 percent annual earnings growth through 2000. That target proved elusive as industry competition escalated and a low-priced generic alternative threatened sales of a top-selling Bristol-Myers cancer drug. Following a late 1999 meeting, Heimbold replaced Donald Haydon Jr., the head of the medicines group.

根据《华尔街日报》采访的历任及现任公司高管所述，²海顿以直言不讳地谈论百时美施贵宝公司不断下滑的销售前景而闻名。因此，他的调职被视为一种信号：高管必须不惜一切代价完成销售指标。从那时起，医药部门开始向批发商提供折扣，以诱使他们订购超出药店处方预期水平的货物。

<!--en-->
According to past and present company executives interviewed by the *Wall Street Journal*,² Haydon was known for speaking candidly about Bristol-Myers's declining sales prospects. Consequently, his reassignment was taken as a message that executives must meet their sales quotas at all costs. At that point, the medicines group began offering wholesalers discounts to induce them to order at higher levels than expected pharmacy prescriptions justified.

此外，根据受访高管的说法，百时美施贵宝公司开始将通过动用前期计提的重组准备金来虚增利润。这一做法违反了美国证券交易委员会（SEC）在1999年公报中重申的会计政策——即此类准备金必须专款专用，禁止将其分批计入利润。同样可疑的是，百时美施贵宝公司屡次计提的重组准备金数额恰好等于资产出售所产生的收益。此外，这些高管称，该公司经常通过出售小型产品线所获得的收益，人为地将每股收益（EPS）增加一两美分，却既不披露相关资产剥离情况，也不将其列为一次性事件。

<!--en-->
In addition, according to the interviewed executives, Bristol-Myers started to pump up the bottom line by taking into earnings portions of restructuring reserves created in earlier periods. This was contrary to Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) accounting policy, reiterated in a 1999 bulletin, requiring that such reserves be used exclusively for specified purposes and prohibiting them from being taken into earnings in small amounts over time. Also suspect was Bristol-Myers's repeated practice of establishing restructuring reserves that exactly equaled gains on asset sales. In addition, the executives said, the company frequently added a penny or two to earnings per share (EPS) through gains on sales of small product lines, without reporting the divestments or highlighting them as one-time events.

SEC对以“不具重要性”为由隐瞒此类交易信息的行为表示不满，并指出：即便某笔小额交易可以合理忽略，但未能披露多笔此类交易仍可能构成具有误导性的陈述。最后，部分受访高管认为，2001年中，百时美施贵宝公司高估了其收购杜邦制药业务所涉及的78亿美元金额中属于在研开发费用的部分；根据GAAP准则，这部分费用本可立即予以冲销。SEC长期以来一直指责企业高估在研开发费用，以减少可能导致后续资产减值的商誉金额。《华尔街日报》采访的高管们则认为，该公司夸大在研开发费用的冲销额，是为了将来有可能逆转部分冲销结果，从而进一步操纵报告利润。“深入审视利润”

<!--en-->
The SEC frowned on withholding information about such transactions on claims of immateriality and stated that even if one small transaction could be legitimately ignored, failing to disclose a number of them could be materially misleading. Finally, some of the interviewed executives contended that in mid-2001, Bristol-Myers overstated the portion of its $7.8 billion acquisition of DuPont's drug business that was attributable to in-process research and development and therefore qualified for immediate write-off under GAAP. The SEC had long claimed that companies were overvaluing in-process R&D to minimize the amount of goodwill that might cause a subsequent write-down. Executives interviewed by the *Wall Street Journal* contended that the company overstated the in-process R&D write-off tocreate the possibility of reversing portions of it in the future, as yet one more way to tweak reported earnings.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

公司官员极力否认其会计政策旨在操纵利润，或借此最大化那些薪酬与公司股价挂钩的高管们的报酬。然而，百时美施贵宝公司在2003年3月10日进行的资产减值处理，正值SEC和联邦调查局加强对公司高层在不当会计行为中所起作用调查之际。

<!--en-->
Company officials strenuously denied that its accounting policies were geared toward managing earnings or, by extension, maximizing the compensation of senior executives whose compensation was linked to the company's stock price. Bristol-Myers's March 10, 2003, write-down, however, came in the context of accelerating SEC and Federal Bureau of Investigation inquiries into senior management's role in the improper accounting.

2004年8月，百时美施贵宝公司同意支付1.5亿美元以解决SEC提出的会计欺诈指控。随后在2005年6月，该公司又因存货操纵问题支付了3亿美元以和解司法部的指控。该公司还同意让首席执行官多兰辞去董事长职务，并承诺在塞顿霍尔大学法学院设立商业伦理讲席教授职位。后来当选新泽西州州长的纽瓦克联邦检察官克里斯托弗·J·克里斯蒂指出，这一骗局反映出一种不惜一切代价追求更高销售额的企业文化。“这些人掌握着本应向投资者公开的信息，但他们却没有披露，”克里斯蒂评论道，“这不是简单的渠道填塞问题，而是故意隐瞒信息的问题。”³

<!--en-->
In August 2004, Bristol-Myers agreed to pay $150 million to settle SEC charges of accounting fraud. This was followed in June 2005 by a $300 million settlement of Justice Department charges that also arose from inventory manipulation. The company further agreed that CEO Dolan would surrender the title of chairman and pledged to endow a chair in business ethics at Seton Hall University Law School. Christopher J. Christie, the U.S. attorney in Newark who was subsequently elected governor of New Jersey, said the scheme reflected a corporate culture that emphasized higher sales at all costs. “These people had knowledge which they should have disclosed to the investing public, which they did not,” Christie commented. “It’s not a channel-stuffing case. It’s a failure-to-disclose case.”³

### 识别过度存货

<!--en-->
*Detecting Excessive Inventory*

并非所有人都对百时美施贵宝公司披露的渠道堵塞问题感到意外。在该公司于2002年4月3日发布公告前几天，美林证券分析师史蒂文·泰格就写道：该公司排名前十的核心零售品牌的批发渠道存货可能高达5亿至8亿美元。⁴这一数字相当于平均每周销售额的2.42倍，属于异常高水平。泰格估计，由此导致的销售放缓将在2002年第一季度使百时美施贵宝公司的每股收益减少0.02至0.03美元。

<!--en-->
Not everyone was caught entirely off guard by Bristol-Myers's revelation of clogged-up distribution channels. Several days before the company's April 3, 2002, announcement, Merrill Lynch analyst Steven Tighe wrote that the inventory in the wholesale distribution chain for the company's top 10 core retail brands could total $500 million to $800 million.⁴ That would approximate 2.42 times average weekly sales, an abnormally high level. Tighe estimated that the resulting sales deceleration would penalize Bristol-Myers earnings per share by $0.02 to $0.03 in 2002's first quarter.

这位分析师依据医疗保健数据供应商IMS Health提供的价格和处方统计数据，估算出百时美施贵宝公司10种主要药品的批发存货量；这些药品占其制药业务收入的50%。例如，IMS数据显示，降胆固醇药物普伐他汀在2001年的药店层面销售额增长了8%，零售价格则上涨了6%；而百时美施贵宝公司报告的当年销售额增幅却达到21%，这意味着与药店实际销售情况相比存在7%的差距。⁵其中最大的销售差异出现在口服降糖药格华止上，差额高达17亿美元。

<!--en-->
The analyst derived his estimate of wholesale inventories for Bristol-Myers's 10 major drugs, representing 50 percent of pharmaceutical revenues, from price and prescription statistics of IMS Health, a vendor of health care data. For example, IMS reported that pharmacy-level sales of Pravachol, a cholesterol-reducing drug, grew by 8 percent in 2001 and the retail price increased by 6 percent. Bristol-Myers reported a 21 percent sales gain for the year, implying a gap of 7 percent versus the sell-through at pharmacies.⁵ The largest such sales disparity, amounting to $1.7 billion, involved Glucophage, an oral antidiabetic.

根据IMS的数据，处方量减少了8%，抵消了8%的零售价格上涨带来的影响，但百时美施贵宝的销售额却增长了18%。Tighe认为，格华止的批发库存量竟高达他估计的该品牌2002年销售额的78%。收入确认方面，事实证明库存积压及其对盈利的影响比Tighe的分析更为严重。不过，渠道囤货现象的被发现，确实敲响了股价即将下跌的警钟。更令人惊讶的是，UBS Warburg分析师C.J. Sylvester早在2001年9月就警告称公司存在价值约5.5亿美元的积压库存，这比公司公布这一重磅消息的时间早了半年。

<!--en-->
According to IMS, prescriptions declined by 8 percent, offsetting an 8 percent retail price increase, yet Bristol-Myers recorded an 18 percent sales gain. Tighe reckoned that Glucophage wholesale inventories equaled a staggering 78 percent of his estimated 2002 sales for the brand.
Revenue Recognition
It turned out that the inventory bloat and resulting earnings impact were even greater than Tighe's analysis suggested. Still, the detection of channel-stuffing was an alarm bell for the impending stock price decline. More impressively still, UBS Warburg analyst C. J. Sylvester warned of excess inventory on the order of $550 million in September 2001, half a year before the company dropped its bombshell.

对大多数财务报表使用者而言，像IMS和NDCHealth这类公司提供的用于此类分析所需数据的年度订阅费用高达数万美元。不过，百时美施贵宝的案例仍说明了将公司报告的盈利数据与独立提供的信息进行比对的重要性。某些行业（如汽车业和博彩业）公开的销售统计数据也能提供有益的验证。

<!--en-->
Unfortunately for most users of financial statements, annual subscriptions to the data required for this sort of analysis, provided by companies such as IMS and NDCHealth, run into tens of thousands of dollars. The Bristol-Myers Squibb case study nevertheless illustrates the value of testing a company's reported earnings against independently provided information. Publicly available statistics for sales in certain industries, such as automobiles and casinos, can provide a helpful check.

### 对盈利的再审视

<!--en-->
*A SECOND TAKE ON EARNINGS*

*我喜欢做的事情就是开车四处转，然后顺手劫掠一番。你可以把人从车里拖出来痛打一顿，抢走他们的钱和车。能拥有这种能力还挺有意思的。⁶* 这些话并非出自职业罪犯之口，而是来自《侠盗猎车手3》的众多玩家之一——这款游戏由Take-Two Interactive Software发行。在这款极受欢迎的游戏中，另一种得分方式是与妓女发生性关系，随后将其杀害并抢走她的钱财。其他常见策略还包括随意枪击行人，或用棒球棍猛击他们。正是这些内容使得《侠盗猎车手3》在澳大利亚被禁止发行。

<!--en-->
*What I like to do is get in the car and drive around and do drive-by shootings. You can haul someone out of their car and beat on them and steal their money and their car. It's kind of amusing that you have that ability.⁶*
These are not the words of a career criminal, but of one of the many devotees of *Grand Theft Auto 3*, a video game produced by Take-Two Interactive Software. Another way that players score in the hugely popular game is to have sex with a prostitute, then murder her and steal her money. Other popular strategies consist of shooting random pedestrians and bludgeoning them with a baseball bat. Such features have earned *Grand Theft Auto 3* the distinction of being banned in Australia.

虽然没那么残忍，但同样真实存在的不当行为让Take-Two在财务造假史上留下了一笔。事情始于该公司股价在不到六个月的时间内翻了一番多。即便如此，一些专家仍认为相对于Electronic Arts和Activision等行业同行而言，其股票被低估了，因此推测微软可能会将其收购。

<!--en-->
Less brutal, but nonimaginary, misdeeds won Take-Two a place in the annals of financial misrepresentation. The story began to unfold after the company's share price more than doubled in less than six months. Even at that, some experts considered the stock undervalued relative to industry peers such as Electronic Arts and Activision, giving rise to speculation that Take-Two might be an attractive candidate for acquisition by Microsoft.

人们对该股持续上涨的短期预期在2001年12月14日被打破。

<!--en-->
Near-term dreams of continued upward momentum in the stock were shattered on December 14, 2001.

受公司可能需重述盈利数据的传言影响，Take-Two股价暴跌4.72美元至10.33美元，跌幅达31%。传言最终被证实属实。Take-Two于12月17日宣布，将重述截至2001年10月31日的财年前三个季度的盈利数据。管理层称，调整原因是公司将出售给“某些独立第三方经销商”的部分游戏收入计入营收，但这些游戏后来又被退回或由Take-Two回购。公司估计，2000财年的每股收益将从0.88美元调整为0.75–0.77美元。对利润的深入剖析

<!--en-->
Take-Two plunged by $4.72 to $10.33, a 31 percent drop, on rumors that the company might have to restate its earnings. The rumors proved on the mark. Take-Two announced on December 17 that it would restate its earnings for the first three quarters of the fiscal year ending October 31, 2001. According to management, the adjustment arose because the company recorded revenue on some games it sold to"certain independent third-party distributors" but which were later returned to or repurchased by Take-Two. The company estimated that earnings per share for fiscal 2000 would be restated from $0.88 to $0.75–$0.77.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

令一些观察者惊讶的是，12月17日Take-Two股价反而上涨3.23美元至13.56美元，涨幅达31%。对于Rocker Partners的卖空者Marc Cohodes而言，公司的公告恰恰表明其依赖会计手段来粉饰报表。用他的话说，Take-Two是在向自己销售产品，并将这些销售计入营收。⁷ 然而，总裁Paul Eibeler则抱怨说，这些重述掩盖了Take-Two的“内在实力”⁸，并称公司在2002财年的前景依然乐观。一些华尔街分析师也持相同观点。

<!--en-->
Surprisingly to some observers, Take-Two's stock rose by $3.23 to $13.56, a 31 percent gain, on December 17. To short seller Marc Cohodes of Rocker Partners, the company's announcement was evidence that it was relying on accounting gimmickry. As he characterized it, Take-Two had been selling products to itself and including those sales in its revenues.⁷ President Paul Eibeler, however, complained that the restatements were overshadowing Take-Two's "underlying strength"⁸ and that the company's prospects for fiscal 2002 were strong. Some Wall Street analysts shared that view.

Wedbush Morgan Securities的Miguel Iribarren重申了其买入建议，一年目标价定为25美元。Commerce Capital Markets的Richard Zimmerman也维持其强烈买入评级，目标价为20美元。

<!--en-->
Wedbush Morgan Securities' Miguel Iribarren reiterated his buy recommendation with a one-year price target of $25. Commerce Capital Markets' Richard Zimmerman confirmed his strong buy with a target of $20.

接下来的几个月里，财务报告方面的消息愈发糟糕。2002年1月22日，Take-Two宣布推迟发布第四季度及财年末业绩报告。纳斯达克股市随即暂停了Take-Two股票的交易。2月12日，公司将其2001财年的每股收益从0.88美元调整为0.23美元，同时还将2002财年前九个月的每股亏损额从0.11美元略微缩减至0.09美元。此外，Take-Two透露美国证监会已对其会计问题展开调查。次日，又一个典型的警示信号出现了：公司首席财务官Albert Pastino辞职。

<!--en-->
For the next few months, the financial reporting news got worse. On January 22, 2002, Take-Two announced that it would postpone the release of its fourth quarter and fiscal year-end results. The Nasdaq stock market promptly halted trading in Take-Two's shares. On February 12, the company restated its fiscal year 2001 earnings per share from $0.88 to $0.23, while also slightly reducing its reported per-share loss for the first nine months of fiscal 2002 from ($0.11) to ($0.09). In addition, Take-Two disclosed that the SEC had launched an investigation of its accounting. The following day, another classic red flag appeared, as the company's chief financial officer, Albert Pastino, resigned.

尽管有这些不利情况，但当Take-Two的股票于2月15日恢复交易时，一些分析师仍持乐观态度。摩根·基根公司的鲍勃·德莱恩评论道：“从负面来看，管理层缺乏可信度，且该公司历来存在激进的会计处理方式。但展望未来，他们凭借几款热门游戏取得了成功，资产负债表也将显著改善。”⁹ 他将该股评级为“跑赢大盘”，六个月目标价为30–35美元。

<!--en-->
Despite these adverse developments, when trading in Take-Two shares resumed on February 15, some analysts remained upbeat. Morgan Keegan's Bob DeLean commented, "On the negative side, management has no credibility and you have historically aggressive accounting. But going forward, they are having success with a couple of big hits and the balance sheet is going to look a lot better."⁹ He rated the stock outperform, with a six-month target of $30–$35.

罗克合伙公司的科霍德斯则依然持怀疑态度，他认为：“这些数字肯定是编造的，这一点我们确信无疑。其他一切都是猜测而已。”¹⁰ 与许多其他财务造假案例所呈现的教训相反，接受这家信誉受损的管理层关于公司前景光明的保证反而带来了回报。分析师伊里巴伦设定的2002年12月达到20美元的目标，在当年4月便已实现；在此期间标准普尔500指数几乎未发生变化。德莱恩设定的30–35美元六个月目标区间的下限，也于2002年11月被触及，尽管此时标普指数已下跌15%。尽管收入确认方面的造假行为最终比公司在2002年披露的范围更广，但股东们仍收获了这些好消息。2004年1月31日，Take-Two宣布将重新编制自1999财年以来的财务报表。最新的差异涉及价格折让准备金的处理问题。

<!--en-->
Rocker Partners' Cohodes remained the skeptical, arguing, "The numbers have been made up, that we know for sure. Everything else is speculation."¹⁰
In this instance, contrary to the lesson taught by many other cases of financial misreporting, it paid to accept the discredited management's assurances that the company's business prospects looked bright. Analyst Iribarren's target of $20 by December 2002 was achieved in April of that year, with the Standard & Poor's 500 Index nearly unchanged over the period. The lower end of DeLean's six-month target of $30–$35 by August 2002 was likewise reached, albeit tardily, in November 2002, notwithstanding a 15 percent drop in the S&P.
Revenue Recognition
All this good news for shareholders came despite the fact that the revenue recognition misreporting ultimately turned out to be more extensive than the company disclosed in 2002. On January 31, 2004, Take-Two announced it would restate earnings back as far as fiscal 1999. The latest discrepancies involved the recording of reserves for price concessions.

2005年6月9日，Take-Two同意支付750万美元的罚款，以和解美国证监会提出的会计欺诈指控。前董事长瑞安·布兰特同意支付50万美元罚款，并退还及支付310万美元的预支利息——这些款项是基于最初报告的利润而发放的奖金。

<!--en-->
On June 9, 2005, Take-Two agreed to a penalty of $7.5 million to settle SEC charges of accounting fraud. Former Chairman Ryan Brant consented to a penalty of $500,000 and disgorgement and prejudgment interest of $3.1 million, representing bonuses based on the originally reported earnings.

前首席运营官拉里·穆勒和前首席财务官詹姆斯·大卫二世也同意接受罚款并退还相关奖金。

<!--en-->
Former Chief Operating Officer Larry Muller and former Chief Financial Officer James David Jr. also agreed to penalties and disgorgement of bonuses.

涉事各方均未承认或否认美国证监会指控中的内容，但这些指控本身就像《侠盗猎车手3》中描述的混乱场面一样令人震惊。证监会指控称，Take-Two通过大约180项所谓的“寄售安排”系统性地确认收入。证监会认为，在财政年度或季度末，该公司向分销商发送数十万份视频游戏，而这些分销商并无付款义务；随后公司将这些发货虚假地记为销售，并在此后期间接受这些产品的退货。美国证监会称，在许多情况下，管理层还伪造发票，将退货伪装成“各类产品的采购”。¹¹ 此外，根据指控，Take-Two对仍在生产、尚未发货的游戏不当确认了收入。最后，证监会还指责该公司对收购两家视频游戏发行商的处理不当，且未能为其游戏零售价格的下调设立适当的准备金。

<!--en-->
None of the parties admitted or denied the allegations in the SEC's complaint, but those allegations were as disturbing, in their own way, as descriptions of mayhem in *Grand Theft Auto 3*. The commission charged that Take-Two systematically booked revenue from approximately 180 separate so-called parking arrangements. At or around the end of fiscal years or quarters, the commission contended, the company shipped hundreds of thousands of video games to distributors who were under no obligation to pay for them, fraudulently booked the shipments as if they were sales, then accepted returns of the products in later periods. In many instances, the SEC claimed, management created fraudulent invoices to disguise the returns as "purchases of assorted product."¹¹ Furthermore, according to the complaint, Take-Two improperly recognized revenues on games that were still being manufactured and therefore could not be shipped. Finally, the SEC charged, the company accounted improperly for the acquisition of two video game publishers and failed to establish proper reserves for reductions in the retail prices of its games.

这让人想起该公司最著名的游戏中无辜旁观者所遭受的对待：公认会计原则在Take-Two管理层手中遭到了类似棒球棍般的摧残。

<!--en-->
Reminiscent of the treatment of innocent bystanders in the company's most notorious game, GAAP received the equivalent of a beating with a baseball bat at the hands of Take-Two's management.

### 收入与现金之间的差异

<!--en-->
*An Income versus Cash Disparity*

对财务报表使用者而言令人欣慰的是，那些不当确认收入的管理者往往会被其留下的数字痕迹所暴露。以某电脑制造商的财务报表为例，它提前预示了该领域的潜在问题。在肯德尔广场研究公司于1993年10月修正此前公布的利润数据之前，《财务报表警报》这一研究服务机构就警告称，该公司确认收入的时间过早。

<!--en-->
Encouragingly for users of financial statements, managers who improperly recognize revenues are often betrayed by the number trails they create. Consider how the financial statements of one computer manufacturer telegraphed future problems in this area. Shortly before Kendall Square Research's October 1993 revision of its previously reported earnings, a research service known as *Financial Statement Alert* warned that the company was recognizing revenues too early.

肯德尔广场公司在1992年3月上市后的前六个季度中实现了4540万美元的收入。《财务报表警报》的联合出版人洛伦·凯洛格将这一损益表数据与该公司现金流量表中的数字进行了对比。在同样的18个月里，肯德尔广场公司“从客户处收到的现金”仅为2570万美元。凯洛格认为，这两个数字之间1970万美元的差异表明，肯德尔广场所确认的大部分销售存在疑点。更仔细地审视利润情况

<!--en-->
Kendall Square reported $45.4 million in revenue in the first six quarters after it went public in March 1992. Loren Kellogg, copublisher of *Financial**Statement Alert*, compared this income statement information with a figure from the company's statement of cash flows. Over the same 18-month period, Kendall Square's "cash received from customers" was just $25.7 million. Kellogg viewed the $19.7 million disparity between the two numbers as evidence that a large proportion of sales being booked by Kendall were dubious.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

这一警告后来被证明极具预见性。凯洛格的分析刊登在《华尔街日报》上不到一个月，肯德尔广场便宣布其1993年第三季度的收入将“远低于”证券分析师的预期。

<!--en-->
The warning proved prescient. Less than a month after Kellogg's analysis was reported in the *Wall Street Journal*, Kendall Square disclosed that its third-quarter 1993 revenues would be "substantially below" securities analysts' expectations.

该公司原本预计每股收益为0.11美元（根据预测跟踪机构Zacks Investment Research的数据，这也是市场共识预期），但如今却表示将出现亏损。此外，Kendall Square推迟了第三季度财报的发布，并宣布其刚上任一个月的高级副总裁兼财务主管辞职。顺便说一句，所有这些迹象都是公司存在严重问题的典型表现。

<!--en-->
In lieu of earnings per share of $0.11 (the consensus forecast according to the forecast-tracking firm of Zacks Investment Research), the company said that it would report a loss. Additionally, Kendall Square delayed the release of its third-quarter earnings and announced the resignation of its senior vice president and treasurer, who had joined the company only a month earlier. All these developments, by the way, were classic indications of serious corporate problems.

收入确认争议是Kendall Square陷入困境的核心原因。该公司称，尽管第三季度的发货量“基本符合预期”，但对于应从这些发货中确认多少收入仍存在疑问。所罗门兄弟公司的分析师Jeffry Canin推测公司内部可能存在分歧；他认为，一些高管可能反对将给予那些同意升级至Kendall下一代电脑产品的客户的回扣计入收入。Smith Barney Shearson的分析师Barry Bosak则提出，Kendall Square可能因过度依赖对大学的销售而受到影响。

<!--en-->
Revenue recognition controversies were central to Kendall Square's difficulties. The company indicated that although third-quarter shipments were "generally in line with expectations," there was some question about the proper amount of revenue to recognize from the shipments. Jeffry Canin, an analyst at Salomon Brothers, speculated about a possible area of disagreement within the company. It was possible, he suggested, that some officials objected to counting as revenue rebates that might have been given to customers who agreed to upgrade to Kendall's next generation of computers. Smith Barney Shearson analyst Barry Bosak proposed the possibility that Kendall Square had been hurt by its reliance on sales to universities.

这些大学反过来又依赖于日益减少的政府拨款，最终无力支付货款。事实上，一些批评者暗示Kendall Square向教育机构提供研究经费，以此作为获取订单的交换条件，但公司管理层否认了这一指控。

<!--en-->
A number of these institutions, which were in turn dependent on diminishing government funding, proved unable to pay. Indeed, some critics insinuated that Kendall Square had made research grants to educational institutions as quid pro quos for orders, a charge that management denied.

无论如何，Kendall Square的麻烦仍在继续：审计机构普华永道撤回了对该公司1992年度财务报表的无保留意见。管理层透露，当年最初报告的2050万美元销售额中，有420万美元属于“不当确认”的收入。公司还补充说，1993年上半年的未经审计数据也需重新表述。

<!--en-->
At any rate, Kendall Square's troubles continued, as auditor Price Waterhouse withdrew its clean opinion from the company's 1992 financial statements. Management revealed that the year's sales figure, originally reported as $20.5 million, included $4.2 million of "improperly recognized" revenue. Unaudited numbers for the first half of 1993 would also require restatement, the company added.

在这些公告发布后，Kendall Square解除了其总裁、首席财务官以及技术产品部门负责人的职务。该公司的代理首席执行官宣布，今后Kendall Square将专注于按订单生产电脑，而非提前备货以等待订单。这一改革有望减少与收入确认相关的问题，但等到其实施之时，财务报表使用者已经遭受了重大损失。

<!--en-->
In the wake of these announcements, Kendall Square demoted and then fired its president, its chief financial officer, and the head of its technical products group. The company's acting chief executive officer announced that henceforth, Kendall Square would concentrate on building computers to order instead of creating inventories in anticipation of orders. That reform was likely to reduce problems associated with revenue recognition, but bythe time it was introduced, the damage to users of financial statements was substantial.

股价跌至7½美元，较三个月前的高点已下跌约70%。¹² 收入确认

<!--en-->
At 7½, the company's stock price was down by about 70 percent from its peak three months earlier.¹²
Revenue Recognition

### 分期付款购物的歧途

<!--en-->
*ASTRAY ON LAYAWAY*

2000年8月9日，沃尔玛百货公司公布了截至7月31日的第二财季业绩：净利润同比增长28%；稀释后每股收益达到0.36美元，增幅为29%。销售额增长了20%，其中开业超过一年的门店销售额增长了5%。

<!--en-->
On August 9, 2000, Wal-Mart Stores reported a 28 percent year-over-year increase in net income for its fiscal second quarter ending July 31. At $0.36, earnings per share (diluted) were up by 29 percent. Sales rose by a healthy 20 percent, climbing 5 percent at Wal-Mart units open for more than one year.

鉴于一位分析师将其称为“非常出色的一个季度”，人们本以为这家折扣零售商的股价会上涨。至少，由于每股收益的增长与First Call/Thomson Financial所报道的华尔街分析师共识预期相符，投资者会期望股价能保持稳定。然而实际上，沃尔玛的股价却下跌了4.375美元，至53.125美元。这相当于当日股价下跌8%，而当天道琼斯工业平均指数仅小幅下跌0.6%。

<!--en-->
In light of these results, which one analyst characterized as “a very good quarter,” the discount chain’s share price might have been expected to rise. At the very least, investors would have expected the stock to hold steady, given that the EPS increase was in line with Wall Street analysts’ consensus forecast, as reported by First Call/Thomson Financial. As it turned out, however, Wal-Mart’s shares fell by $4.375 to $53.125. That represented an 8 percent decline on a day on which the Dow Jones Industrial Average changed only modestly (down 0.6 percent).

《华尔街日报》¹³和彭博新闻社¹⁴均将沃尔玛股价的这种反常下跌归因于一项会计政策变更——该变更预计将减少随后（第三）季度的盈利。零售商管理层建议分析师将8月至10月期间的每股收益预估下调1.5至2美分，以反映公司在分期付款销售方面的会计处理方法的变化。

<!--en-->
Both the *Wall Street Journal*¹³ and the *Bloomberg* newswire¹⁴ linked the paradoxical drop in Wal-Mart’s stock to an accounting change that was expected to reduce the following (third) quarter’s earnings. The retailer’s management advised analysts to lower their earnings per share estimates for the August-to-October period by 1.5 to 2 cents, to reflect a shift in the company’s method of accounting for layaway sales.

在此类交易中，顾客先支付定金来预留商品，随后在指定时间内分期付款，待付清全部款项后方可取走商品。在财务会计准则第101号（FAS 101）强制要求更改会计做法之前，沃尔玛会在将商品列入分期付款清单时便确认销售收入。按照这种更为保守的新方法，公司只有在顾客付清全部款项并提取商品后才会确认销售。

<!--en-->
In such transactions, customers reserve goods with down payments, then make additional payments over a specified period, receiving their merchandise when they have paid in full. Prior to the change in accounting practice, which Financial Accounting Standard (FAS) 101 made mandatory, Wal-Mart booked layaway sales as soon as it placed the merchandise on layaway. Under the new and more conservative method, the company began to recognize the sales only when customers completed the required payments and took possession of the goods.

据一位分析师称，沃尔玛股价8%的跌幅属于“某种程度的过度反应”。实际上，此次股价下跌完全是过度反应。会计方法的变更并未改变零售商最终收到的现金金额或收款时间。因此，沃尔玛计划中的收入确认流程变更并不会导致货币的时间价值损失。为防止有人继续错误地将经济意义归因于收入确认的时间点，沃尔玛解释称，第三财季报告的盈利小幅减少将在第四财季得到弥补。此外，管理层早在8月9日的电话会议前就已宣布了这项会计变更。

<!--en-->
According to one analyst, Wal-Mart’s 8 percent stock price decline represented “somewhat of an overreaction.” In reality, the price drop was an overreaction in its entirety. Changing the accounting method altered neither the amount of cash ultimately received by the retailer nor the timing of its receipt. The planned change in Wal-Mart’s revenue recognition process therefore entailed no loss in time value of money. Lest anyone mistakenly continue to attribute economic significance to the timing of the revenue recognition, Wal-Mart explained that the small reduction in reported earnings in the third fiscal quarter would be made up in the fourth. On top ofeverything else, management had already announced the accounting change prior to its August 9 conference call.

深入剖析利润情况

<!--en-->
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

一位机构投资组合经理所言不虚：他将市场对所谓新闻的反应称为“与其说是其他什么，不如说是混乱”。若从表面上看，媒体报道暗示投资者因这些既过时又无关紧要的“新闻”而抛售股票。或者，投资者可能有其他原因导致股价下跌。一方面，截至7月31日的三个月内，门店客流量较上一季度有所下降；另一方面，德国业务亏损额超过了管理层的预期。如果这些事件才是沃尔玛股价下跌的真正原因，那么《华尔街日报》和彭博社将抛售归因于毫无实际经济影响的会计变更便是错误的。无论如何，市场一片混乱；唯一的问题是，混淆视听的是投资者还是记者。

<!--en-->
An institutional portfolio manager spoke truly when he called the market's reaction to the supposed news “more confusion than anything else.” If taken at face value, the press reports indicate that investors bid the shares down on so-called news that was both dated and irrelevant. Alternatively, investors may have had other reasons for driving down the shares. For one thing, store traffic declined in the three months ended July 31 from the preceding quarter's level. Additionally, German operations posted a larger loss than management had forecast. If these events were the true causes of Wal-Mart's slide, then the *Wall Street Journal* and the *Bloomberg* newswire erred in attributing the sell-off to an accounting change with no real economic impact. Either way, confusion reigned; the only question is whether it was the investors or the journalists who were confused.

## 会员费的确认

<!--en-->
*RECOGNIZING MEMBERSHIP FEES*

贝利健身俱乐部提供了另一个案例：关于收入确认的问题导致了股市对该公司看似乐观的盈利消息作出不利反应。1998年7月30日，这家健身连锁店公布的稀释后每股收益为0.08美元，而上年同期则为亏损0.59美元。据《华尔街日报》报道，¹⁵ 利润的改善“出乎意料地令人鼓舞”，这表明该公司较新且更高端的门店正在推动整体业绩的提升。然而，在财报发布后的一个月内，贝利公司的股价下跌了44%，同期道琼斯工业平均指数跌幅仅为16%。此外，在贝利发布财报后，卖空交易（即押注股价会下跌的交易）占流通股的15%。1998年第一季度，该公司的**空头头寸比率**在3%至5%之间波动。

<!--en-->
Bally Total Fitness provided another case in which questions about revenue recognition contributed to an unfavorable stock market reaction to seemingly upbeat earnings news. On July 30, 1998, the health club chain reported diluted earnings per share of $0.08, up from a year-earlier loss of $0.59. According to the *Wall Street Journal*,¹⁵ the improved profits were “unexpectedly encouraging.” They suggested that the success of the company's newer, more upscale clubs was bolstering overall performance. In the month following the earnings report, however, Bally's shares declined by 44 percent. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell by a less severe 16 percent over the same period. In the wake of Bally's report, moreover, short sales (representing bets that the price would fall) accounted for 15 percent of all outstanding shares. During the first quarter of 1998, the company's **short interest ratio** fluctuated in a range of 3 percent to 5 percent.

由于贝利公司越来越依赖通过融资方式收取的会员费而非现金销售，投资者不愿轻信其盈利增长的数据。贝利公司为客户的初始会员费提供长达36个月的融资，费用范围在600美元至1,400美元之间，年利率为16%至18%。¹⁶ （持续缴纳的会费仅占净收入的27.9%，1998年时约90%的会员每月平均仅支付7美元左右。）总体而言，随着融资会员费在总收入中所占比重的增加，公司报告的利润率也随之受益。

<!--en-->
Investors were unwilling to accept Bally's earnings increase at face value because of the company's growing reliance on memberships that it financed, as opposed to selling for cash. Bally's financed customers' initial membership fees, which ranged from $600 to $1,400, for up to 36 months, charging annual interest rates of 16 percent to 18 percent.¹⁶ (Ongoing dues represented just 27.9 percent of net revenues, with approximately 90 percent of members paying an average of only about $7 a month in 1998.) On the whole, the company's reported profit margins benefited from the increase in financed memberships as a percentage of total revenues.

然而，所报告的盈利是基于对最终无法付清所有分期付款的客户比例的假设。收入确认 129

<!--en-->
The reported earnings, however, rested on assumptions regarding the percentage of customers who would ultimately fail to make all of the scheduled installments.
Revenue Recognition
129

即使在最佳情况下，任何健身俱乐部的新会员中也有相当一部分会在支付初始费用后放弃会员资格。正如纽约大学会计学教授保罗·布朗所指出的：“人们放弃健身俱乐部会员资格几乎没有什么损失。我们谈论的又不是健康保险计划，甚至不是他们可能需要的汽车。”¹⁷ 当然，贝利公司按照良好的会计惯例为无法收回的款项计提了准备金。不过，准备金的数额需要基于对新会员信用质量的判断。由于融资会员费对贝利公司而言并非全新事物，管理层在做出假设时有一定经验可循。此外，近年来该公司成功提高了电子资金转账支付选项的使用率。与通过月度账单收费的会员相比，信用卡或银行账户被自动扣费的会员还款率更高。

<!--en-->
Even under the best of circumstances, a considerable portion of any health club's new members let their memberships lapse, despite paying an initial fee. As New York University accounting professor Paul Brown notes, "People have little to lose from walking away from a health-club membership. It's not a health-care plan we're talking about, or even a car, which they might need for transportation."¹⁷
To be sure, Bally set aside reserves for uncollectible amounts, consistent with good accounting practice. The size of the reserves, however, required judgment about the credit quality of the new members. Because financed memberships were not entirely new to Bally, management had some experience on which to base its assumptions. In addition, the company had succeeded in increasing the use of an electronic funds transfer payment option in recent years. Collection rates were higher for members whose credit cards or bank accounts were automatically charged for fees than for those billed through monthly statements.

不过，增加对需要借贷才能入会的客户的依赖也存在风险。与任何销售情形一样，积极开拓新业务可能会导致接纳资质较差的客户。总体而言，新会员在财务能力和健身积极性方面可能不如以往购买分期付款会员资格的客户。如果拖欠款项的会员数量超出管理层的预期，从事后来看，Bally在收入确认上就过于激进，不得不撤销此前报告的收入。

<!--en-->
There were risks, though, in stepping up reliance on customers who needed to borrow in order to join. As in any sales situation, aggressive pursuit of new business could result in acceptance of more marginally qualified customers. On average, the newer members might prove to be less financially capable or less committed to physical fitness than the previous purchasers of financed memberships. If more members failed on their payments than management assumed, Bally would prove in hindsight to have been too aggressive in recognizing revenue and would have to rescind previously reported income.

对1998年第二季度财报持保留态度，并不意味着财务报表使用者是在质疑Bally的管理层。相反，他们只是出于合理考虑，在对一家历来存在可疑收入确认做法的服务行业公司进行评估时保持谨慎。在《华尔街日报》发表批评性文章后，一些分析师为Bally辩护，指出该公司于1997年7月应美国证券交易委员会工作人员的要求采用了更为保守的会计做法。此前，Bally会在会员资格出售时便全额确认初始会员费。

<!--en-->
By taking the second-quarter 1998 earnings with a grain of salt, users of financial statements were not necessarily casting aspersions on Bally's management. Rather, they were understandably applying caution in evaluating a company in a service industry historically identified with questionable revenue recognition practices. Some analysts sprang to Bally's defense following the *Wall Street Journal*'s critical article by highlighting the company's adoption of a conservative practice at the Securities and Exchange Commission staff's behest in July 1997. Previously, Bally had fully recognized initial membership fees at the time that the memberships were sold.

健身俱乐部运营商可能会滥用这种做法，通过高压手段为那些极有可能无法按时付款的人预订分期付款的会员资格。依赖财务报表的外部人士会看到收入增长，但这种增长最终将被证明是不可持续的。根据新的会计处理方式，Bally将初始费用产生的收入在其预计的会员期内进行分摊——现金即时支付的销售为36个月，分期付款销售则为22个月。

<!--en-->
A health club operator could abuse this approach by using high-pressure tactics to book financed memberships for individuals who were highly unlikely to keep up their payments. Outsiders relying on the financial statements would perceive a growth in revenues that must, in time, prove unsustainable. Under the new accounting treatment, Bally spread the revenues from the initial fees over the expected membership lives—36 months for sales made for cash on the barrelhead and 22 months for financed sales.

美国证券交易委员会敦促Bally分摊会员费的确认时间，这只是超越健身俱乐部行业的更广泛举措的一部分。会计原则本身并未改变，即配比原则。对于健身俱乐部而言，会员预付的费用代表了其在会员期内所享受服务的对价。因此，俱乐部运营商应在提供服务的期间内确认收入。20世纪90年代末，这一基本理论并未发生变化，但美国证券交易委员会在确定部分公司对规则的解释过于宽松后，加强了对会员费的监管力度。受到更严格审查的行业包括会员制零售店。

<!--en-->
The SEC's urging of Bally to spread out its recognition of membership fees was part of a broader effort extending beyond the health club industry. There was no change in the accounting principle, namely, the matchingconcept. In the case of a health club, members' up-front fees represent payments for services received over the term of their membership. Club operators should therefore recognize the revenue over the period in which they render the service. During the late 1990s, the underlying theory underwent no change, but the SEC intensified its focus on membership fees after determining that some companies were interpreting the rules too liberally. Among the industries that came under increased scrutiny were the membership club retailers.

在这类经营模式中，消费者需预先支付费用，以获得在销售打折商品的商店购物的特权。**深入了解利润情况**

<!--en-->
In this type of operation, consumers pay up-front fees for the privilege of shopping at stores that sell discounted merchandise.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

1998年10月19日，BJ's Wholesale Club将其年度会员费（通常可供两名家庭成员使用，费用为35美元）的即时确认方式，改为在整个会员期（通常为12个月）内逐步确认。伴随会计政策的变更，BJ's重新计算了截至8月1日的财政上半年净利润，结果为1040万美元，较此前报告的2860万美元下降了64%。此次重述反映了会计变更对往年累计影响的一次性费用，以及因对新店开业前费用采用更保守的会计处理方法而产生的110万美元税后费用。

<!--en-->
On October 19, 1998, BJ's Wholesale Club switched from immediate recognition of its annual membership fee (typically $35 for two family members) to incremental recognition of the fee over the full membership term, generally 12 months. In conjunction with the change in accounting policy, BJ's restated its net income for the fiscal first half ending August 1 to $10.4 million. That was down 64 percent from the previously reported $28.6 million. The restatement reflected a one-time charge for the accounting change's cumulative effect on preceding years, as well as a $1.1 million after-tax charge arising from a change to more conservative accounting for new-store preopening expenses.

就在这些事件发生前一个半月，BJ's曾发布新闻稿称，其即时确认年度会员费的做法符合GAAP标准。¹⁸管理层还辩称无需进行递延处理，理由是BJ's仅允许会员在入会后的90天内取消会员资格并获退款。

<!--en-->
Just a month and a half before these events, BJ's had issued a press release asserting that its practice of immediately recognizing annual membership fees was consistent with GAAP.¹⁸ Management had also argued that no deferral was required, on the grounds that BJ's offered its members the right to cancel and receive refunds for only 90 days after enrollment.

实际上，只有0.5%的会员要求退款。此外，与Bally Total Fitness的情况不同，会员费在BJ's的收入中仅占很小一部分，其98%的收入来自商品销售。

<!--en-->
A mere 0.5 percent of members actually requested refunds. In contrast to the situation at Bally Total Fitness, moreover, membership fees represented a minor portion of BJ's revenues, 98 percent of which derived from merchandise sales.
