然而，根据GAAP规定，一般要求将会员费分摊到整个会员期内。如果公司提供退款服务，那么在退款期结束前，它不能确认任何收入，除非有足够长的历史数据能让管理层有把握地预测未来情况。最多而言，BJ's的退款记录可能允许公司在会员注册之日就开始确认费用。无论如何，将收入确认分摊到会员期内都是强制性的。¹⁹ 1999年12月，美国证监会（SEC）通过发布《工作人员会计公告第101号——财务报表中的收入确认》（SAB 101）澄清了这一点。该机构明确表示，希望公司在退款权到期前不确认会员费收入。MemberWorks是一家提供会员计划的供应商，其服务涵盖医疗保健、个人理财及旅游等多个领域；为响应SAB 101的要求，该公司于2000年7月1日起更改了其会计处理方式。

<!--en-->
Under GAAP, however, the general requirement was to spread membership fees over the full membership period. If a company offered refunds, it could not book *any* of the revenue until the refund period expired, unless there was a sufficiently long history to enable management to estimate future experience with reasonable confidence. At most, BJ's refund record might have entitled the company to begin booking the fees on the date that members enrolled. Spreading the revenue recognition over the membership period would have been mandatory in any case.¹⁹
In December 1999, the SEC staff clarified the point by issuing “Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 101—Revenue Recognition in Financial Statements” (SAB 101). The staff stated its preference that companies not book membership fees until refund privileges expired. MemberWorks, a provider of membership programs offering services and discounts in a wide range of fields including health care, personal finance, and travel, altered its accounting in response to SAB 101, effective July 1, 2000.

由此产生了2570万美元的一次性非现金费用，这反映了此前已确认的会员费被递延所致。²⁰ 收入确认

<!--en-->
A one-time noncashcharge of $25.7 million resulted, reflecting the deferral of previously recognized membership fees.²⁰
Revenue Recognition

### 五花八门的宽松收入确认手法

<!--en-->
*A POTPOURRI OF LIBERAL REVENUE RECOGNITION TECHNIQUES*

通过强化对SAB 101中所规定的收入确认规则的执行力度，SEC制止了那些被视作过于激进的会计手法。Professional Detailing是一家为制药公司招募并管理销售人员的公司，它不得不停止将客户支付的招聘广告费用计入收入。短短一个月内，该公司股价下跌了31%。National Data Corporation旗下的Physician & Hospital Systems & Services部门放弃了其一贯的做法：不仅在工作完成前就确认后台服务的收入，甚至在寄出账单前就确认收入。National Data终止了这一做法，并为此计提了1380万美元的一次性费用以纠正此前虚增的收入。First American Financial在采纳配比原则后，开始将贷款服务的收入按贷款期限逐步确认，而非立即确认，由此累计计提了5560万美元的费用。²¹

<!--en-->
By intensifying its enforcement of established revenue recognition rules in SAB 101, the SEC put a stop to techniques that the staff considered overly aggressive. Professional Detailing, a recruiter and manager of sales staff for pharmaceutical companies, had to stop including in revenues the reimbursements that it received from clients for placing help-wanted ads. Within a month, the company's share price fell by 31 percent. Physician & Hospital Systems & Services, a unit of National Data Corporation, abandoned its long-standing policy of booking revenues for its back-office services not merely before it completed the work, but before it mailed out bills. National Data ended the practice and took a $13.8 million one-time charge to correct the previous pumping up of revenues. First American Financial took a cumulative $55.6 million charge when it embraced the matching principle by beginning to book revenues for loan services over the loan's duration, rather than immediately.²¹

#### 完工百分比法

<!--en-->
*Percentage-of-Completion Method*

在特定情况下，从事长期合同工作的公司可以在向客户开具账单前就确认收入。这一结果源于GAAP为解决建筑公司中常见的账目不匹配问题而提出的方案。各类服务公司、国防承包商以及资本货物制造商都会面临同样的会计难题。

<!--en-->
Under certain circumstances, a company engaged in long-term contract work can book revenue before billing its customer. This result arises from GAAP's solution to a mismatch commonly observed at construction firms. A variety of service companies, defense contractors, and capital goods manufacturers come up against the same accounting issue.

通常，公司会在合同期内分几次向客户开具账单。开具账单的时间可能会滞后于公司为履行义务而产生的支出时间。如果不采取某种措施来纠正这种不匹配现象，那么在合同初期报告的利润会偏高，而在后期则会偏低。

<!--en-->
Typically, the company agrees to bill its customers in several installments over the life of the contract. The billing may lag behind the company's incurring of expenses to fulfill its obligations. Without some means of correcting this mismatch, reported profit will be inappropriately high in the contract's early stages and inappropriately low in the late stages.

完工百分比法正是GAAP解决这一问题的方法。它允许公司按照已完成工作的比例来确认收入，而不是依据开票情况。完工百分比法虽然能纠正这种不匹配现象，但也可能涉及相当大的主观性。尤其是当公司专门致力于为特定客户的独特问题寻找创造性解决方案时，这类工作很难用工程标准来衡量。管理层可以通过做出较为宽松的假设来加速此类合同的收入确认，而这些假设又难以被审计师从客观角度否定。与人为加速会计处理的常见情况一样，随意调整完工百分比实际上是在挪用未来的收入，最终必然会导致收入缺口的出现。更深入地审视利润问题

<!--en-->
The percentage-of-completion method is how GAAP addresses the problem. It permits the company to recognize revenue in proportion to the amount of work completed, rather than in line with its billing. The percentage-of-completion method can rectify the mismatch but may also entail considerable subjectivity. This is particularly so when the company specializes in finding creative solutions to particular companies' unique problems, a sort of work that cannot be readily measured by engineering standards. Management can speed up revenue recognition on such contracts bymaking assumptions that are liberal yet difficult for the auditors to reject on objective grounds. As is generally the case with artificial acceleration, taking liberties with the percentage of completion borrows future revenues, making a surprise shortfall inevitable at some point.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

## 越界行为

<!--en-->
*Crossing the Line*

在上述案例中，监管机构只是抱怨这些公司现有的收入确认政策过于乐观，但在其他情况下，管理层则被指控存在虚假陈述行为。例如，1996年，SEC指控计算机制造商Sequoia Systems及其四位前高管参与了旨在夸大公司收入和利润的“欺诈计划”。根据在华盛顿联邦地区法院提交的诉状，前董事长及其他三名高管将意向书视为收入入账，篡改部分采购订单日期，并向客户授予Sequoia从未披露的特殊条款。SEC还称，这些高管在公司真实财务状况曝光前出售股票，从中获利。该公司及其前高管最终在未承认也未否认有罪的情况下，与SEC达成了民事和解。²²

<!--en-->
In the foregoing cases, the regulators merely complained that the companies' existing revenue recognition policies painted too rosy a picture, but in other instances, management has been accused of misrepresentation. For example, in 1996, the SEC claimed that computer manufacturer Sequoia Systems and four former executives engaged in a "fraudulent scheme" aimed at inflating the company's revenue and income. According to the complaint filed in U.S. District Court in Washington, the ex-chairman and three other officials booked letters of intent as revenue, backdated some purchase orders, and granted customers special terms that Sequoia never disclosed. Furthermore, charged the SEC, the executives profited from the scheme by selling stock before a true picture of the company's financial condition emerged. The company and its former officials settled the SEC's civil charges without admitting or denying guilt.²²

### 用“空热量”来虚增盈利

<!--en-->
*FATTENING EARNINGS WITH EMPTY CALORIES*

甜甜圈制造商Krispy Kreme于2000年4月上市，发行价为每股21美元。其股价在交易首日便飙升76%，达到37美元。这使得该公司的市盈率高达78倍，这一数字超过了标准普尔食品指数约23倍的平均水平三倍多。

<!--en-->
Doughnut maker Krispy Kreme went public at $21 a share in April 2000. Its stock soared by 76 percent to $37 on the first day of trading. That put its price-earnings ratio at 78 times, more than triple the multiple on the Standard & Poor's Food Index of around 23 times.

尽管Krispy Kreme的甜甜圈确实具有令人上瘾的特性，但一些分析师认为其股价已经涨得过高。不过，投资者还是被该公司远超一般食品企业的增长率所鼓舞。在截至1月30日的2000财年中，同店销售额增长了14%。自1998财年末以来，门店数量更是激增20%，达到144家——其中58家为直营店，86家为加盟店。每当新店开业时，渴望品尝的顾客总会成群结队地排队，以便在开门瞬间满足口腹之欲。在消费者对糖分的狂热推动下，Krispy Kreme的股价持续上涨，于2000年11月达到108.50美元。

<!--en-->
Notwithstanding the undeniably addictive quality of its doughnuts, some analysts thought Krispy Kreme's shares had risen too high. Investors were encouraged, however, by a growth rate far in excess of the typical food company. Same-store sales had jumped by 14 percent in fiscal 2000 (ended January 30). The number of stores had vaulted 20 percent to 144—58 company-owned and 86 franchised—since the end of fiscal 1998. Whenever a new store was slated to launch, eager customers lined up in droves to satisfy their cravings the instant the doors opened. Propelled by consumers' sugar high, Krispy Kreme shares continued to surge, reaching $108.50 in November 2000.

这种狂热不可能永远持续下去。2003年，新店开业的速度放缓，这令Krispy Kreme作为“超级成长股”的估值受到质疑。根据美国证券交易委员会于2009年发布的指控，此时Krispy Kreme修改了高管薪酬计划。²³从那时起，除非公司每个季度的每股收益能超出预期指引至少0.01美元，否则高管将拿不到奖金。为了继续达到自己设定的标准，SEC称管理层开始操纵某些费用计提方式，以使每股收益至少比指引高出一美分。最终，Krispy Kreme连续13个季度都超出了这一门槛。此外，SEC还指出，Krispy Kreme不当记录了涉及公司回购加盟店的可疑交易。

<!--en-->
The mania could not last forever. In 2003, the pace of new store openings slackened, throwing into question Krispy Kreme's valuation as a super growth stock. At this point, according to a Securities and Exchange Commission complaint released in 2009, Krispy Kreme revised its senior executive compensation plan.²³ Henceforth, officers would receive no bonuses unlessthe company reported earnings in each quarter that exceeded its earnings per share guidance by at least $0.01.
Revenue Recognition
To continue to clear the bar that it set for itself, the SEC said, management began to manipulate certain expense accruals to produce EPS at least one penny above the guidance. Ultimately, Krispy Kreme strung together 13 consecutive quarters in which it exceeded that threshold. In addition, said the SEC, Krispy Kreme improperly recorded questionable transactions involving company purchases of franchised stores.

## 漫长的下跌开始了

<!--en-->
*The Long Slide Begins*

2004年5月7日，该公司发布了有史以来首次盈利预警，告知投资者其盈利将比此前预期低10%。Krispy Kreme将利润下滑归咎于低碳饮食的兴起，但一些分析师怀疑真正的原因是过度扩张。他们注意到，竞争对手Dunkin' Donuts的业务并未受到低碳饮食趋势的明显影响。曾在2001年进行过两次拆股的Krispy Kreme股价，在听到这一消息后当天便下跌了29%。当月晚些时候，《华尔街日报》根据一位熟悉相关交易的人士提供的信息，详细披露了此次加盟店回购中的可疑之处。²⁴报道称，2003年Krispy Kreme开始谈判，拟回购其在密歇根州经营不佳的七家加盟店。据称，Dough-Re-Mi欠Krispy Kreme数百万美元的加盟费、设备及原材料款项，且早已拖欠不还。《华尔街日报》报道说，双方达成了初步协议：Krispy Kreme要求该加盟商承担关闭两家业绩不佳门店的费用，并偿还拖欠的利息；随后，据该报消息来源称，Krispy Kreme同意将购买价格提高，以涵盖这些额外成本。

<!--en-->
On May 7, 2004, the company issued a first-ever profit warning, telling investors that its earnings would be 10 percent lower than it previously expected. Krispy Kreme blamed its faltering profits on the new popularity of low-carbohydrate diets, but some analysts suspected that the real problem was overexpansion. They noted that there was no sign of carb consciousness hurting business at rival Dunkin' Donuts. Krispy Kreme shares, which had split twice in 2001, suffered a one-day, 29 percent decline on the news. Later that month, the *Wall Street Journal* detailed questionable aspects of the franchise repurchases, based on information by a person familiar with the transactions.²⁴
In 2003, according to the account, Krispy Kreme began a negotiation to buy back its struggling seven-store Michigan franchise. Dough-Re-Mi reportedly owed Krispy Kreme several million dollars for franchise fees, equipment, and ingredients and was delinquent on its payments. The *Journal* reported that the parties reached a preliminary agreement in which Krispy Kreme asked its franchisee to absorb the cost of closing down two underperforming stores and to repay past-due interest. Then, according to the *Journal*'s informant, Krispy Kreme agreed to increase the purchase price by the amount of these additional costs.

为什么Krispy Kreme要设法收回门店关闭成本和逾期利息，却又立刻把这笔钱付回去呢？其动机可能是为了虚增账面盈利。如果交易如《华尔街日报》所述那样运作，支付给Dough-Re-Mi的额外款项就会成为无形资产——即重新获得的加盟权，而这类资产无需摊销。也就是说，不会有按计划逐步冲减的方式去减少未来的盈利。另一方面，当同样一笔钱回到Krispy Kreme手中时，它会被记为利息收入。本质上，按照《华尔街日报》的描述，Krispy Kreme只是把钱从一个口袋取出，再放进另一个口袋，从而制造出虚假的盈利。

<!--en-->
Why would Krispy Kreme try to recover the store-closing costs and overdue interest, only to pay it right back? The motivation might have been to increase reported earnings. If the transaction was structured as the *Journal* stated, the extra money paid out to Dough-Re-Mi became part of an intangible asset, reacquired franchise rights, which would not amortize. That is, no scheduled, bit-by-bit write-down would reduce future earnings. On the other hand, when the very same dollars came back to Krispy Kreme, they would be recorded as interest income. In essence, according to the *Wall Street Journal*'s story, Krispy Kreme manufactured earnings by taking money out of one pocket and putting it into another.

假设《华尔街日报》的报道属实，那么给Dough-Re-Mi用于支付关闭费用的钱也会变成无形资产。倘若Krispy Kreme先回购加盟权再关闭门店，就会产生相应费用。问题在于，资产理应是指能创造未来经济价值的东西。而已关闭的门店显然不符合这一定义。细看盈利真相：Krispy Kreme对其会计处理的辩解堪称此类案例中的典型。

<!--en-->
The money given to Dough-Re-Mi to cover the closing costs also became an intangible asset, again assuming the *Journal*'s account was accurate. Had Krispy Kreme instead repurchased the franchises and then closed the stores,it would have incurred an expense. The catch is that an asset is supposed to be something that creates future economic value. Terminated stores would not seem to satisfy that definition.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS
Krispy Kreme's defense of its accounting was a classic of the genre.

首先，该公司称审计师认可了其对相关项目的处理方式。不过，从企业审计师每年批准的诸多边缘性操作来看，这一理由并不充分。其次，Krispy Kreme辩称，Dough-Re-Mi的利息支付与此次收购无关。然而巧合的是，这笔款项恰好在同一天支付，且从Krispy Kreme付给特许经营商的最终汇款中扣除。

<!--en-->
To begin with, said the company, the auditor approved its handling of the items. This was not a strong justification, judging by the many borderline actions that corporations' auditors approve every year. Second, argued Krispy Kreme, Dough-Re-Mi's interest payment was unrelated to the acquisition. By a remarkable coincidence, however, it occurred on the very same day, and it was deducted from Krispy Kreme's final remittance to the franchise seller.

这笔交易还有另一个奇怪之处。最初，Krispy Kreme表示将支付相当于2450万美元的金额来购买密歇根州的特许经营权。后来，价格竟上涨了26%，达到3210万美元。该公司的首席财务官声称，这种差异源于最初对交易成本的评估不完整。他称，Krispy Kreme本应在价格中计入一笔潜在额外费用——即Dough-Re-Mi的高层管理人员兼大股东为同意推迟支付其应缴的购款并继续担任Krispy Kreme员工而收取的期票所产生的费用。然而，交易完成后不久，Krispy Kreme便解雇了该高管，导致实际支付的金额比原定的期票金额多出500万美元。

<!--en-->
There was yet another strange aspect to the deal. Originally, Krispy Kreme said it would pay the equivalent of $24.5 million for the Michigan franchise. Later on, the price jumped by 26 percent to $32.1 million. The company's chief financial officer claimed that the disparity arose from an initially incomplete assessment of the costs of the transaction. Krispy Kreme, he said, should have included in the price the potential added costs of a promissory note that Dough-Re-Mi's top executive and major shareholder took in exchange for agreeing to defer his portion of the purchase price while he stayed on as a Krispy Kreme employee. Krispy Kreme, however, dismissed the executive soon after the transaction closed, triggering a payment $5 million greater than the amount originally attributed to the promissory note.

这笔额外款项同样被计入名为“重新获得的特许经营权”的非摊销无形资产之中。交易与追加付款之间的时间间隔如此之短，不禁让人怀疑其中至少有一部分实质上是支付给该高管的遣散费。如果按此入账，Krispy Kreme将立即确认一笔费用。Krispy Kreme牵强的辩解是：这笔款项并非遣散费，因为它付给了Dough-Re-Mi，而非直接给该高管本人。

<!--en-->
This extra money, too, became part of the nonamortizing, intangible asset known as reacquired franchise rights. The shortness of the interval between the transaction and the increased payment raised the question whether at least a portion of the disbursement was in substance a severance payment to the executive. If it had been booked that way, Krispy Kreme would have realized an immediate expense. Krispy Kreme's dubious rebuttal was that the payment was not severance because it went to Dough-Re-Mi, rather than directly to the executive.

进一步削弱Krispy Kreme可信度的是其在北加州进行的第二次特许经营权回购细节。2002年5月提交的10-K报告中称，截至2001年1月，首席执行官斯科特·利文古德持有该特许经营权的3%股份。实际上，他的持股比例高达6%；2001年8月，作为离婚协议的一部分，他将其中3%的股份转让给了妻子。这对夫妇于2002年6月离婚。Krispy Kreme的一位发言人将10-K报告中的差异归咎于校对错误，但该公司可能有动机希望尽量压低这一数字。允许高管在特许经营中持有可观股份的做法并不常见；其他一些特许经营餐饮企业禁止此类行为，认为这属于利益冲突。

<!--en-->
Further undercutting Krispy Kreme's credibility were details of a second franchise repurchase, in northern California. The 10-K filed in May 2002 reported that as of January 2001 CEO Scott Livengood held a 3 percent share of the franchise. In reality, his stake amounted to 6 percent, but in August 2001 he ceded 3 percent to his wife as part of a separation agreement. The couple divorced in June 2002. A Krispy Kreme spokeswoman blamed the 10-K discrepancy on a proofreading error, but the company had a potential motive for wanting to state as low a figure as possible. Allowing executives to hold nontrivial stakes in franchises was unusual. Some other franchised food companies prohibited the practice, viewing it as a conflict of interest.

2004年7月29日，Krispy Kreme披露美国证监会已对其会计做法展开非正式调查。消息传出后，该公司股价暴跌16%。调查的重点之一是特许经营权的回购。Camelback Research Alliance指出，Krispy Kreme不摊销所购回的特许经营权这种做法在特许经营行业并不常见。该公司辩称，他们认为特许经营权具有无限寿命，因此不应随时间逐步注销。Camelback的联合创始人唐恩·W·维克里还指出，Krispy Kreme在某些特许经营回购中支付了虚高的价格。他提到，2003年该公司以6750万美元的价格购回了由两名前董事拥有的达拉斯和什里夫波特地区的特许经营权。这些资产包括五家门店和一家为外部客户供货的生产设施。与此同时，Krispy Kreme却拒绝回购位于南加州、售价据称达8000万美元且拥有22家门店的特许经营权。维克里质疑：加州的门店真的会价值如此之低吗？关于特许经营回购估值的疑问，引发了人们对关联方交易存在疑点的担忧。

<!--en-->
On July 29, 2004, Krispy Kreme disclosed that the SEC had opened an informal inquiry into its accounting practices. The company's stock plungedby 16 percent on the news. One focus of the investigation was franchise repurchases. Camelback Research Alliance noted that Krispy Kreme's practice of not amortizing the reacquired rights was nonstandard in the franchising industry. The company parried that it believed the franchise rights had indefinite lives and therefore should not be written off over time.
Revenue Recognition
Camelback co-founder Donn W. Vickrey also suggested that Krispy Kreme had paid inflated prices in some franchise repurchases.²⁵ He noted that in 2003 the company paid $67.5 million for franchises in Dallas and Shreveport owned by two former directors. The assets included five stores and one commissary, a production facility that served off-premises customers. At the same time, Krispy Kreme was declining to buy back a southern California franchise that was for sale for a reported $80 million and held 22 stores. Vickrey questioned whether the California stores could truly be so much less valuable. The questions about valuation of the franchise repurchases raised the specter of questionable transactions with related parties.

综合考量Krispy Kreme的所有会计做法，Camelback给予该公司“盈利质量F级”的评价。这一评级通常是该研究公司仅授予具备以下三个特征的公司：

<!--en-->
Taking into account all of Krispy Kreme's accounting practices, Camelback gave the company an F for earnings quality, a designation the research firm customarily awarded only to companies with three characteristics:

1. 基本面平稳或呈下降趋势，从而有动机美化财务报表。
2. 存在明显的不寻常或不当会计操作及交易迹象。
3. 公司治理薄弱的证据。

<!--en-->
1. Flat or declining fundamentals, providing a motivation to prettify the financials.
2. Visible evidence of unusual or improper accounting or transactions.
3. Evidence of weak corporate governance.

### 局势愈发紧张

<!--en-->
*The Heat Goes Up*

维克里的批评被证明是敏锐的。不到一个月后，Krispy Kreme的首席运营官便辞职了；这一高层人事变动被Thomas Weisel Partners的分析师斯基普·卡彭特视为更多问题即将浮现的迹象。²⁶同月晚些时候，公司财报表现大幅不及预期。该公司拒绝提供盈利指引，这通常是一个令人担忧的信号。Rocker Partners的大卫·罗克进一步指出，Krispy Kreme资产负债表上的现金，即便不是全部，也似乎主要来自售后回租交易，而非经营活动所得。²⁷2004年9月12日，审计机构普华永道拒绝完成对最新季度财务报表的审核，直到董事会聘请的外部律师事务所完成审计方要求的某些程序为止。

<!--en-->
Vickrey's criticisms proved astute. Krispy Kreme's chief operating officer resigned less than a month later, a top-level executive change that analyst Skip Carpenter of Thomas Weisel Partners viewed as a sign of more problems to come.²⁶ A major earnings disappointment followed later the same month. The company declined to provide earnings guidance, which is usually a reason to worry. David Rocker of Rocker Partners further noted that most, if not all, of the cash on Krispy Kreme's balance sheet appeared to have come from a sale-and-leaseback transaction, rather than from operations.²⁷ On September 12, 2004, auditor PricewaterhouseCoopers refused to complete its review of the latest quarter's financial statements until an outside law firm hired by the board completed certain procedures that the auditor requested.

2004年10月8日，美国证监会将针对Krispy Kreme财务报告做法的调查升级为正式立案调查。不到一周后，两名前董事被起诉，指控他们通过获取一份从未认真考虑过的外部报价，人为抬高了Krispy Kreme为其所拥有的达拉斯-什里夫波特特许经营店支付的价格。

<!--en-->
On October 8, 2004, the SEC upgraded its inquiry to a formal investigation of Krispy Kreme's financial reporting practices. Less than a week later, two former directors were slapped with a lawsuit alleging that they pumped up the price Krispy Kreme agreed to pay for the Dallas-Shreveport franchise, which they owned, by obtaining an outside bid that they neverseriously considered.

2004年11月22日，由于该公司宣布上市以来的首次亏损，Krispy Kreme股价下跌16%至9.64美元。这一价格较2003年8月经拆股调整后的峰值49.74美元已大幅缩水。其他令人沮丧的数据还包括：同店销售额下降了超过6%；公司为应对证监会的调查和未决诉讼花费了300万美元。与往常的财报电话会议不同，管理层拒绝回答任何问题，并撤销了此前关于2005年销售额增长15%的预测。更深入地审视利润情况

<!--en-->
On November 22, 2004, Krispy Kreme stock fell 16 percent to $9.64 as the company announced its first-ever loss as a public company. That was down from an August 2003 peak, adjusted for splits, of $49.74. Among other depressing statistics, same-store sales declined by more than 6 percent, and it cost the company $3 million to deal with the SEC probe and pending litigation. Departing from customary practice for earnings calls, management declined to answer any questions and withdrew its previous projection of 15 percent sales growth in 2005.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

Krispy Kreme再也无法将其困境归咎于逐渐消退的低碳水化合物饮食热潮。Legg Mason的一名分析师指责该公司在选择新店址时粗心大意，且未能妥善培训新的加盟商。此外，该公司通过在超市和便利店销售甜品导致市场饱和。在圣安东尼奥的一家新Krispy Kreme门店，店主开门时发现的并非排着长队、睡在睡袋里的顾客，而只有等待他的员工。该市已有三家Krispy Kreme门店，其甜甜圈也在Albertsons和H-E-B超市出售。

<!--en-->
Krispy Kreme could no longer pin its troubles on the low-carbohydrate diet fad, which appeared to be fading. A Legg Mason analyst charged the company with carelessness in selecting new store locations and failure to train new franchisees properly. In addition, the company had saturated the market by selling its goodies in supermarkets and convenience stores. Instead of a long line of customers camped out in sleeping bags, the manager of a new Krispy Kreme store in San Antonio found only his employees waiting for him when he arrived to open up. The city already had three other Krispy Kreme outlets, and its doughnuts were being sold in Albertsons and H-E-B supermarkets.

加盟商之间也可能出现了紧张迹象。一家中西部加盟商行使了将其所持11%股份卖回给公司的期权；Krispy Kreme还披露了因两名加盟商导致的200万美元坏账计提。

<!--en-->
There were also possible signs of strain among franchisees. A Midwestern franchisee exercised an option to sell 11 percent of its shares back to the company, and Krispy Kreme disclosed a $2 million charge for doubtful accounts from two franchisees.

2004年12月16日，Krispy Kreme承认，支付给Dough-Re-Mi前业主的部分款项本应被计入薪酬费用。不过，董事会聘请的律师并未发现此事中存在故意不当行为。管理层也承认在收购加州一家加盟店时的会计处理存在错误。受此消息影响，Krispy Kreme股价上涨8.7%；分析师们欣喜地认为披露的情况并未更糟。然而，普华永道仍拒绝完成对前两个季度业绩的审核，直至董事会特别委员会及外部律师事务所正在进行的调查结束为止。

<!--en-->
On December 16, 2004, Krispy Kreme conceded that some of the payment to Dough-Re-Mi's former owner should have been treated as compensation expense. Lawyers hired by the board, however, found no intentionally improper conduct in the incident. Management also acknowledged errors in its accounting for the acquisition of a California franchise. Krispy Kreme stock rose by 8.7 percent on the news, as analysts rejoiced that the disclosures were not worse. PricewaterhouseCoopers, however, continued to refuse to complete its review of results for two prior quarters, pending completion of the ongoing investigation by a special committee of the board and the outside law firm.

很快便显而易见的是，该公司尚未脱离困境。2005年1月4日，Krispy Kreme宣布将调低上一年度报告的盈利数额，并且由于未能提交财务报表以及盈利下滑，该公司或将违约其1.5亿美元的银行信贷额度。

<!--en-->
It quickly became clear that the company was not yet out of the woods. On January 4, 2005, Krispy Kreme said it would reduce its previous year's reported profit and that it would be in default on its $150 million bank credit line due to its failure to file financial statements and probably also as a result of its earnings decline.

Krispy Kreme称，由于无法继续动用银行信贷额度，公司将无法履行对加盟商债务的担保责任，其中1670万美元已经违约。2月份，该公司表示需要在3月底前获得额外信贷才能维持运营。此时，针对该公司的股东诉讼已累计超过十几起；其中一起诉讼指控Krispy Kreme为了满足投资者对盈利增长的期望，竟指示部分员工运送比批发客户订购量更多的甜甜圈。收入确认 137

<!--en-->
Without the ability to draw further on its bank line, said Krispy Kreme, it would be unable to honor its guarantees of franchisees' debts, of which $16.7 million was in default. In February, the company said that it needed additional credit by the end of March to remain in business. By this time, more than a dozen shareholder lawsuits had piled up, including one alleging that Krispy Kreme had tried to meet investors' expectations for earnings growth by ordering some employees to ship more doughnuts than wholesale customers had ordered.
Revenue Recognition
137

面对日益恶化的局势，Krispy Kreme将首席执行官斯科特·利文古德替换为一位擅长企业扭亏为盈的专家。2005年2月24日，美国纽约南区联邦检察官办公室在SEC正在进行的调查基础上展开了进一步调查。2005年4月9日，财务报告中披露的问题出现了新情况：Krispy Kreme将其2004财年财务数据的修正幅度从380万美元至490万美元区间上调至520万美元至620万美元区间。此前未披露的问题涉及衍生品交易、租赁及租赁相关改良的会计处理错误，以及Krispy Kreme收购某特许经营业务之前向加盟商出售设备所产生的收入冲回问题。

<!--en-->
In response to its deteriorating situation, Krispy Kreme replaced chief executive Scott Livengood with a turnaround specialist. On February 24, 2005, the U.S. attorney's office for the Southern District of New York launched an investigation on top of the SEC's ongoing probe. Several new elements entered the disclosures of financial reporting problems on April 9, 2005, when Krispy Kreme increased the size of the corrections to its fiscal 2004 results from the $3.8 million to $4.9 million range to a range of $5.2 million to $6.2 million. The previously undisclosed problems involved derivatives transactions, errors in accounting for leases and improvements related to leases, and reversal of income related to equipment sold to a franchisee before Krispy Kreme bought that operation.

管理层表示，针对最后一项问题可能还需要进一步重述财务报表，因为确认收入的基础将从发货或交付日期改为设备安装日期。

<!--en-->
Management said further restatements probably would be needed on the last item, as the basis for recognizing the revenue would be changed to the installation date of the equipment, rather than the shipping or delivery date.

### 解决方案

<!--en-->
*The Resolution*

经过10个月的时间，董事会特别委员会提交了调查报告。这份措辞谨慎的文件指出，尽管所有接受访谈的员工和加盟商都否认故意歪曲Krispy Kreme的盈利数据或奉命行事，但“这些会计错误的数量、性质和时间点强烈表明它们源于刻意操纵盈利的意图。”²⁸报告批评了所谓的“循环交易”现象——资金先流向加盟商，随后又流回公司并被记为收入，从而使管理层能够实现比预期高出0.01美元的盈利目标。

<!--en-->
After 10 months, the board special committee submitted a report of its investigation. The carefully worded document indicated that although all employees and franchisees who were interviewed denied deliberately distorting Krispy Kreme's earnings or being ordered to do so, "the number, nature, and timing of the accounting errors strongly suggest that they resulted from an intent to manage earnings."²⁸ The report criticized "round-trip transactions" in which money flowed out to franchise sellers, then flowed back in and was booked as revenue, enabling management to achieve its bogey of $0.01 above guidance.

最终结局出现在2009年：前首席执行官利文古德以及前首席财务官约翰·泰特和兰迪·卡斯蒂文斯就SEC的指控达成和解。他们被指控在一项旨在增加自身薪酬的计划中操纵Krispy Kreme的盈利数据。他们既不承认也不否认这些指控，但同意交出SEC认定的非法所得款项、支付民事罚款，并被永久禁止再犯类似违规行为。SEC的诉状还称，Krispy Kreme管理层在与证券分析师的通话中提供了误导性信息，从而维持了股价，使其高于没有这种财务操纵时的水平；SEC指出高管们对此心知肚明却未予披露。利文古德、泰特和卡斯蒂文斯于2003年8月出售了约324,000股股票，当时正值股价峰值附近。

<!--en-->
The denouement came in 2009, when former CEO Livengood and former CFOs John Tate and Randy Casstevens settled SEC charges that they were instrumental in inflating Krispy Kreme's earnings in an alleged scheme to increase their compensation. They did not admit or deny the allegations but agreed to surrender money the SEC said they earned illegally, pay civil penalties, and be permanently enjoined from committing future violations. The SEC complaint also alleged that Krispy Kreme management conducted misleading conference calls with securities analysts, helping to keep the stock price higher than it would have been without the alleged financial manipulation, which the SEC said the executives knew about but failed to disclose. Livengood, Tate, and Casstevens collectively sold approximately 324,000 shares of stock in August 2003, close to the price peak.

### 从甜甜圈事件中吸取教训

<!--en-->
*Learning Lessons from Doughnuts*

Krispy Kreme并非属于虚构巨额盈利的案例。相反，SEC的诉状描述了一个通过多种财务报表项目逐步“积少成多”的过程，以便每个季度都能将盈利超出预期0.01美元。证券分析师在公布的财务数据中并未发现明确证据表明利润数据不准确。不过，财务报表使用者仍可从中汲取一些可供未来参考的经验教训。**更深入地审视盈利情况**

<!--en-->
Krispy Kreme was not a case of massively fictitious earnings. Rather, the SEC complaint depicted a process of nickel-and-diming, through a widerange of financial statement items, to beat earnings guidance by $0.01 in every single quarter. Security analysts found no clear-cut evidence within the reported numbers that stated profits were inaccurate. Still, users of financial statements can draw some lessons for future reference.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

首先，如果一家企业长期持续超出盈利预期或实现季度盈利的同比增长，这就值得怀疑其是否存在盈利管理行为。企业的成长往往是不均衡的，这反映出经济周期、竞争压力的变化以及投入成本的波动等因素的影响。Krispy Kreme案例带来的第二个教训是：关联方交易与误导性财务报告常常相伴而生。最后，当管理层为盈利下滑提出的借口经不起推敲时——正如Krispy Kreme以低碳热潮为由解释一样——他们很可能是在利用财务报告手段来掩盖真正原因。

<!--en-->
To begin with, an exceptionally long record of beating guidance or posting year-over-year gains in quarterly earnings is a reason to suspect earnings management. Businesses tend to grow unevenly over time, reflecting such factors as the business cycle, waxing and waning of competitive pressures, and fluctuations in input costs. A second lesson of the Krispy Kreme case is that related-party transactions and deceptive financial reporting often go hand in hand. Finally, when management offers an excuse for deteriorating earnings that does not stand up to scrutiny, as Krispy Kreme did by citing the low-carb craze, it may be using financial reporting tricks to try to conceal the true causes.

## 哈里伯顿公司的延迟披露问题

<!--en-->
*TARDY DISCLOSURE AT HALLIBURTON*

2002年，《纽约时报》报道了哈里伯顿公司在1998年更改会计政策一事，该政策使这家工业建筑公司能够将超过1亿美元的有争议成本记为收入。²⁹哈里伯顿直到一年多后才披露这一成本超支处理方式的变更。显然，作为对《纽约时报》文章的回应，美国证券交易委员会启动了调查，最终对该公司提出了提交具有重大误导性的财务报告等指控。

<!--en-->
In 2002, the *New York Times* reported on a 1998 change in accounting policies by the Halliburton Corporation that enabled the industrial construction company to book more than $100 million of disputed costs as revenue.²⁹ Halliburton did not disclose the change in its treatment of cost overruns until more than a year later. Apparently in response to the *Times* article, the Securities and Exchange Commission initiated an investigation that eventually led to charges of filing materially misleading financial reports.

由于该事件发生时在任的首席执行官身份特殊，哈里伯顿公司的这起会计争议虽并非极其严重，却可能受到了过度关注。当哈里伯顿公司迟来的披露信息被公之于众时，首席执行官迪克·切尼早已转任美国副总统。对白宫而言不巧的是，就在乔治·W·布什总统呼吁打击会计违规行为次日，便有股东提起诉讼，指控切尼及其他哈里伯顿高管策划了大规模的欺诈投资者计划。布什主张对参与欺诈的企业高管处以更严厉的监禁刑罚，并加强美国证监会揭露财务报告骗局的能力。

<!--en-->
The Halliburton affair probably attracted disproportionate attention for an accounting controversy of less than gargantuan proportions because of the identity of the chief executive officer on whose watch it occurred. By the time Halliburton's tardy disclosure became public knowledge, CEO Dick Cheney had moved on to become vice president of the United States. Inconveniently for the White House, a shareholder lawsuit alleging a massive scheme to defraud investors was filed against Cheney and other Halliburton executives on the day after President George W. Bush called for a crack-down on accounting abuses. Bush advocated tougher prison sentences for corporate officials engaging in fraud and a strengthening of the SEC's ability to uncover financial reporting scams.

令政府更加尴尬的是，切尼与安达信会计师事务所关系密切。该事务所因对安然公司的审计问题而饱受批评，最终倒闭。在2000年给同事的一份备忘录中，安达信的特里·哈切特吹嘘说，他与切尼的关系极为紧密，以至于他离开达拉斯办事处负责亚洲业务后，仍继续担任哈里伯顿账户的主管合伙人。Revenue Recognition 139

<!--en-->
Additional embarrassment for the administration arose from Cheney's close ties to Arthur Andersen, which incurred massive criticism for its auditing of Enron and ultimately went out of business. In a 2000 memo to his colleagues, Arthur Andersen's Terry Hatchett boasted that his relationship with Cheney was so tight that he remained lead partner on the Halliburton account even after leaving the Dallas office to head Asian operations.
Revenue Recognition
139

此外，切尼还出现在一则宣传视频中，称赞安达信的能力。

<!--en-->
Additionally, Cheney appeared in a marketing video hailing Arthur Andersen's capabilities.

## 会计问题

<!--en-->
*The Accounting Issues*

这些会计问题涉及建设项目中产生的成本超支。根据合同条款及超支性质的不同，哈里伯顿有可能从客户处收回相关费用。1998年以前，该公司会在解决索赔请求的当季度确认来自超支成本回收的收入。然而从1998年第二季度开始，哈里伯顿背离了其传统做法，开始通过将某些项目的损失与尚未解决的索赔中预计可收回的金额相抵来确认收入。

<!--en-->
The accounting issues involved cost overruns incurred in construction projects. Depending on the terms of the contract and the nature of the overrun, Halliburton could potentially recover the associated cost from a customer. Prior to 1998, the company recognized income from recovery of overrun costs in the quarter in which it resolved the claim. Beginning in the second quarter of 1998, however, Halliburton departed from its traditional practice and began recognizing revenues by offsetting its losses on certain projects with estimated probable recoveries on claims that it had not yet resolved.

无论旧的处理方式还是新的处理方式，均符合美国通用会计准则的要求。不过，新方式使得1998年第二季度至1999年第三季度期间的列报税前利润增加了2亿美元。1998年第四季度，会计政策变更使列报税前利润增长了46%。投资者在此期间看到的数字与以往期间的数据不具备可比性，因此无法准确了解哈里伯顿的利润趋势。直到2000年3月，该公司才在1999年的10-K年度报告中透露其已更改会计政策。

<!--en-->
Both the old and the new accounting treatment were acceptable under GAAP. The new treatment, however, boosted reported pretax income by $200 million between the second quarter of 1998 and the third quarter of 1999. In the fourth quarter of 1998, the change in accounting policy raised reported pretax profits by 46 percent. The numbers that investors saw during this period were not comparable to those reported for earlier periods, meaning they did not obtain an accurate picture of Halliburton's profit trend. Not until March 2000 did the company reveal, in its 1999 Form 10-K filing, that it had changed its accounting policy.

2001年，哈里伯顿采取了更为激进的收入确认方式。对于某些项目，哈里伯顿甚至在向客户开具账单前数月就开始确认销售收入。此前，公司的政策是只有在预计一个月内能向客户收款时才确认收入。此外，公司还将一些有争议的账单在账面上保留一年多时间，而非将其冲销并计入损失。以往的政策是只有确信能在一年内收回大部分款项时才不予冲销。由于这一变化，有争议的索赔金额从2000年的1.13亿美元翻倍至2001年的2.34亿美元。

<!--en-->
In 2001, Halliburton adopted an even more aggressive approach to recognizing revenue. For some projects, Halliburton began reporting sales months before billing customers for the work. Previously, the policy was to book revenues only if the company expected to bill clients within one month. In addition, the company began keeping some disputed bills on the books for over a year instead of writing them off and reporting losses. The previous policy was to refrain from a write-off only if it believed it would collect most of the claim within one year. As a result of this change, disputed claims doubled from $113 million in 2000 to $234 million in 2001.

首席财务官道格·福西表示，他无法想象切尼曾特别批准1998年的会计政策变更。他将此描述为因公司业务结构变化而做出的常规商业决策。20世纪90年代末以前，哈里伯顿主要承接成本加成类合同，即无论发生何种成本，公司都能保证获得一定利润。到1998年，大多数合同转为固定价格模式。在这种安排下，公司必须按预定费用完成工作，否则就需就成本超支以及工程规格变更所产生的费用进行协商补偿。

<!--en-->
Chief Financial Officer Doug Foshee said he could not imagine that Cheney had specifically approved the 1998 change in accounting policy. He characterized it as a routine business decision prompted by a shift in the company's business mix. Up until the late 1990s, Halliburton worked mostly under cost-plus contracts, in which it was guaranteed a profit over whatever costs it incurred. By 1998, most contracts were on a fixed-price basis. Under this arrangement, the company had to complete the work for a predetermined fee or else negotiate repayment for cost overruns and for costs arising from changes in specifications of the work.

深入剖析利润情况

<!--en-->
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

上述环境变化或许确实影响了哈里伯顿的会计政策，但更为宽松的收入确认政策的采用，是在1998年与德雷塞尔工业公司合并后公司股价承压的背景下发生的。德雷塞尔公司面临潜在的巨额石棉相关诉讼赔偿责任。此外，哈里伯顿的能源服务业务也面临困境。1998年第四季度，全公司的销售额和利润较去年同期均有所下降。

<!--en-->
Those changed circumstances may well have affected Halliburton's accounting policies, but the adoption of a more liberal revenue recognition policy occurred in the context of pressure on the company's stock price due to its 1998 merger with Dresser Industries. Dresser faced potentially large legal liabilities from asbestos-related litigation. Furthermore, conditions were difficult in Halliburton's energy services business. Corporate-wide sales and profits fell in the fourth quarter of 1998 from the year-earlier period.

哈里伯顿的财务报表进一步表明，为应对这些压力，该公司刻意以有利的方式呈现其业绩。1995年10月切尼出任首席执行官时，公司每1美元季度收入对应的应收账款约为0.95美元；到2000年7月他离任时，这一数字上升到了1.20美元。这种增长似乎并未反映行业环境的普遍变化——在同一时期，五家主要竞争对手的应收账款与销售额之比从0.92降至0.86。表面上看，哈里伯顿在收到款项前就更加积极地确认收入，这正是虚增账面盈利的经典手段。³⁰

<!--en-->
Halliburton's financial statements provided further hints that in response to these pressures the company took liberties to present its results in a favorable light. When Cheney became CEO in October 1995, the company had about $0.95 of receivables for each dollar of quarterly revenues. At the end of his tenure, in July 2000, the figure stood at $1.20. This increase did not appear to reflect a general change in industry conditions. Over that same span, the average ratio of receivables to sales at five major competitors declined from $0.92 to $0.86. On the face of it, Halliburton became more aggressive about booking revenues before getting paid, a classic technique for pumping up reported earnings.³⁰

### 解决方案

<!--en-->
*The Resolution*

2004年8月3日，美国证监会宣布，哈里伯顿及其前财务主管罗伯特·C·马奇莫尔二世已同意分别支付750万美元和5万美元的罚款，以此了结关于提交具有重大误导性财务报表的指控。证监会沃斯堡办事处负责人哈罗德·F·德根哈特评论道：“证监会今天的行动强调了企业财务披露中保持完全透明的重要性。即便相关业绩是按照公认会计原则（GAAP）计算的，涉及公司业绩的重要信息也应清晰、及时地予以披露。”³¹ 该公司与马奇莫尔既未承认也未否认证监会的指控。副总统切尼的律师指出，证监会对此事进行了彻底调查，并未发现董事会或首席执行官在信息披露方面存在责任；对于切尼是否知晓会计变更对哈里伯顿利润的影响这一问题，该律师拒绝回答。

<!--en-->
On August 3, 2004, the SEC announced that Halliburton and its former controller, Robert C. Muchmore Jr., had agreed to settle charges of filing materially misleading financial statements by paying penalties of $7.5 million and $50,000, respectively. The administrator of the commission's Fort Worth office, Harold F. Degenhardt, commented, "The SEC's action today emphasizes the importance of complete transparency in a company's financial disclosures. Important information bearing on a company's results should be clearly and timely disclosed, even if those results are calculated in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP)."³¹
The company and Muchmore neither admitted to nor denied the SEC charges. Vice President Cheney's attorney noted that the SEC had investigated the matter very thoroughly and had found no responsibility for nondisclosure on the part of either the board or the CEO. He declined to answer a question about whether Cheney knew of the effect of the accounting change on Halliburton's profits.

## 来自哈里伯顿的教训

<!--en-->
*Lessons from Halliburton*

审计师的认可并不能保证企业的财务报告一定可靠。安达信会计师事务所顺从了哈里伯顿的决定，未在当年披露重要的会计政策变更。通常，这种决策的理由是“不具重要性”，然而在1998年第四季度，由于成本超支会计处理方式的变化，税前利润被高估了近50%。顺便提一下，哈里伯顿于2002年4月解雇了安达信会计师事务所，就在《纽约时报》对该公司的会计做法提出质疑的前一个月。《纽约时报》当时质疑了哈里伯顿的会计做法。收入确认方面，即便财务报表的使用者看到由权势人物最终负责数据真实性，也不应掉以轻心。哈里伯顿首席执行官迪克·切尼曾是国会议员、白宫办公厅主任和国防部长；据某些说法，他属于那种不干预日常管理的领导者，不会关心最终导致与证监会达成和解的会计决策。另一方面，他显然对会计事务相当熟悉，甚至在一则营销视频中称赞安达信的工作。无论如何，如果一家公司在行业不景气期间仍表现出异常强劲的盈利水平，财务报表使用者绝不应自动排除操纵性会计手段导致这种差异的可能性。

<!--en-->
An auditor's seal of approval does not guarantee that a company's financial reporting is reliable. Arthur Andersen went along with Halliburton's decision not to disclose an important change in accounting policies in the year in which it was made. Immateriality is a common rationale for such a decision,yet in the fourth quarter of 1998, the change in accounting for cost overruns produced nearly a 50 percent overstatement of pretax earnings. By the by, Halliburton fired Arthur Andersen in April 2002, the month before the *New York Times* raised questions about the company's accounting practices.
Revenue Recognition
Neither should users of financial statements be complacent just because a prestigious individual has ultimate responsibility for the integrity of the numbers. Halliburton CEO Dick Cheney was a former congressman, White House chief of staff, and secretary of defense. By some accounts, he was a hands-off manager who would not have concerned himself with the accounting decision that eventually resulted in a settlement with the Securities and Exchange Commission. On the other hand, he evidently felt familiar enough with accounting matters to praise Arthur Andersen's work in a marketing video. In any case, if earnings look suspiciously strong during a rough patch for the company's industry, users of financial statements should never automatically rule out the possibility that manipulative accounting explains the disparity.

### 利用“应急储备”来调节盈利

<!--en-->
*MANAGING EARNINGS WITH RAINY DAY RESERVES*

通过提前确认销售来虚增短期账面盈利，是与收入相关的、最为人诟病的舞弊行为。不过，分析师也必须警惕另一种相反的操纵手段：管理层会故意推迟收入确认，以压低短期利润。这种看似矛盾的行为背后的动机，是为了呈现出平稳的年度盈利增长态势，从而让股票投资者给予更高的市盈率倍数（参见第14章）。

<!--en-->
Overstating near-term reported earnings by recognizing sales prematurely is the revenue-related abuse that creates the greatest notoriety. Analysts must also watch out for the opposite sort of finagling, however. Sometimes, management *delays* revenue recognition to *understate* short-run profits. The motive for this paradoxical behavior is a desire to report the sort of smooth year-to-year earnings growth that equity investors reward with high price-earnings multiples (see Chapter 14).

稳定的盈利增长很少能自然发生。不过，企业可以通过设立“应急储备”来人为制造这种增长。当净利润超出预期时，管理层会将其中一部分存入应急储备；日后当需要提升业绩以达到既定目标时，再将这笔盈利取出使用。平滑利润表并非罕见现象，但企业对这类话题往往十分敏感。

<!--en-->
Steady earnings growth rarely occurs naturally. A company can produce it artificially, however, by creating a rainy day reserve. When net profit happens to be running above expectations, management stows part of it in a rainy day reserve. Later on, when the income is needed to boost results to targeted levels, management pulls the earnings out of storage. Smoothing the bottom line is not uncommon, but companies are touchy about the subject.

化工生产商W.R.格雷斯公司在被指控通过不当储备来调节盈利时反应强烈。1998年12月22日，美国证监会指控该公司及六名前高管在过去五年内通过不当转移收入的方式虚假报告盈利。

<!--en-->
Chemical producer W. R. Grace reacted with indignation when it was accused of managing its earnings through improper reserves. On December 22, 1998, the Securities and Exchange Commission charged the company and six of its former executives with falsely reporting earnings over the preceding five years by improperly shifting revenue.

格雷斯公司遵循常规做法，宣称将“坚决抗辩”³²这些指控，声称其财务报告是合规的，并指出外部审计师对会计处理并未提出任何异议。作为被指控的高管之一，前格雷斯首席执行官J.P.博尔杜克的律师表示，他的当事人将对抗这些指控，并相信自己会被证明无罪。该律师抱怨称，美国证监会试图因博尔杜克履行其职责而惩罚他。更深入地看利润问题

<!--en-->
Grace followed the standard script, declaring that it would “vigorously contest”³² the charges, stating its belief that its financial reporting was proper and pointing out that its outside auditors had raised no objections to the accounting. An attorney for former Grace Chief Executive Officer J. P. Bolduc, who was among theaccused executives, said that his client would fight the charges and expected to be vindicated. The SEC, complained the lawyer, was trying to punish Bolduc for carrying out his duties exactly as he should have.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

美国证监会特别指出，格雷斯公司拒绝报告其肾透析服务子公司National Medical Care（NMC）在20世纪90年代初因医疗保险报销规则变更而获得的1000万美元至2000万美元收入。根据证监会的执法部门的说法，格雷斯高管认为由于当时盈利水平已经符合华尔街分析师的预期，这笔意外之财并不会对股价产生帮助。这种推断与投资者通常对一次性事件所产生的利润和亏损持轻视态度的做法一致（参见第3章）。

<!--en-->
The SEC specifically alleged that Grace had declined to report $10 million to $20 million of revenue that its kidney dialysis services subsidiary, National Medical Care (NMC), received in the early 1990s as the result of a change in Medicare reimbursement rules. According to the commission's enforcement division, the Grace executives reckoned that with earnings already meeting Wall Street analysts' forecasts, the windfall would not help the company's stock price. Such an inference would have been consistent with investors' customary downplaying of profits and losses that they perceive to be generated by one-time events (see Chapter 3).

事实上，这笔意外收入反而可能在未来导致NMC的利润增加30%，这一超出目标且不可持续的水平，进而对股价造成负面影响。

<!--en-->
In fact, it was possible that the unexpected revenue would actually hurt the stock price down the road by causing NMC's profits to increase by 30 percent, an above-target and unsustainable level.

为了解决NMC利润过高的问题，据称格雷斯管理层将这笔额外收入记入另一个账户，随后在1993年至1995年间利用它来虚增该医疗保健集团的申报收入。美国证监会称，例如，格雷斯的高级管理人员曾要求NMC的管理人员在1994年第四季度多报150万美元的收入，因为当时公司需要提升盈利数据。

<!--en-->
To solve the perceived problem of excessively high profits at NMC, Grace's management allegedly placed the extra revenue in another account, which it later drew on to increase the health care group's reported revenues between 1993 and 1995. As an example, claimed the SEC, senior managers of Grace asked NMC's managers to report an extra $1.5 million of income in the fourth quarter of 1994, when corporate earnings needed a boost.

直到1995年7月一直担任格雷斯首席财务官的布莱恩·J·史密斯在证词中称，由于肾透析部门的盈利增长无法持续，“我们认为降低增长率是审慎之举”。³³不过，他的律师否认此举是为了取悦华尔街分析师、保持申报盈利数据的平稳，正如前格雷斯及NMC员工所声称的那样。该律师称，史密斯考虑的是真正的负债问题。

<!--en-->
Brian J. Smith, who was Grace's chief financial officer until July 1995, testified in a deposition that because the kidney dialysis unit could not maintain its pace of earnings increases, "We believed that it was prudent to reduce the growth rates."³³ His attorney denied, however, that the goal was to please Wall Street analysts by keeping reported earnings smooth, as former Grace and NMC employees asserted. Smith had bona fide liabilities in mind, claimed the attorney.

格雷斯公司的审计机构普华会计师事务所的一位高级合伙人并不认为设立准备金的做法是恰当的。

<!--en-->
A senior partner at Grace's auditing firm, Price Waterhouse, did not agree that the additions to reserves were appropriate.

尤金·高恩作证称，他在1991年指出，会计准则明确规定利润只能用于应对可预见且可量化的负债；公认会计原则并未赋予企业设立应急基金的自主权。

<!--en-->
Eugene Gaughan testified that in 1991, he pointed out that the accounting rules clearly stated that profits could be set aside only for foreseeable and quantifiable liabilities; GAAP did not give companies discretion to create rainy day funds.

在年度审计中，普华会计师事务所提议撤销这些准备金，但管理层予以拒绝。根据审计机构的记录，格雷斯高管表示他们希望为“*不可预见的*未来事件”³⁴预留一笔缓冲资金（斜体为原文所加）。最终，普华会计师事务所允许保留这些准备金。审计人员的决定基于这样的判断：从格雷斯公司整体来看，存入准备金的金额并不重要；不过如果NMC是一家独立公司的话，这一数额就会显得重要。（当时，审计人员通常认为，若某项事项对盈利的影响达到5%或10%，则属于重要事项。美国证监会后来确定，若某事项会影响投资者的决策，则视为重要事项。）关于收入确认问题，据高恩称，普华会计师事务所在1992年底再次提出异议，原因是他们看到一份备忘录，其中描述了格雷斯公司利用准备金来操纵申报利润增长，同时将NMC高管的激励薪酬与实际业绩挂钩。另一位普华合伙人托马斯·斯坎伦称，他曾告诉格雷斯首席执行官博尔杜克，囤积准备金是错误的，必须停止这种做法。

<!--en-->
In its year-end audit, Price Waterhouse proposed reversing the reserves, but management refused. According to the auditing firm's records, the Grace executives said that they wanted a "cushion for *unforeseen* future events"³⁴ (italics added). Eventually, Price Waterhouse allowed the additions to reserves to stand. The auditors' decision reflected a finding that the amount placed in the reserve was not material from Grace's corporate-wide standpoint, although it would be if NMC were a stand-alone company. (At the time, auditors generally judged an item material if it affected earnings by5 percent or 10 percent. The Securities and Exchange Commission later established the criterion that an event was material if it would affect an investor's decision.)
Revenue Recognition
According to Gaughan, Price Waterhouse objected again around the end of 1992, after seeing a memo that described Grace's use of reserves to influence reported growth in profits, while gearing NMC executives' incentive compensation to "actual results." Another Price Waterhouse partner, Thomas Scanlon, said that he told Grace CEO Bolduc that stockpiling reserves was wrong and would have to stop.

到那时为止，这笔应急准备金的数额已增至约5500万美元。

<!--en-->
By that time, the contents of the rainy day reserve had grown to about $55 million.

简而言之，格雷斯公司1998年声称其审计师对医疗保险补偿带来的意外之财的会计处理没有提出异议，这一说法仅在技术层面上成立——即普华会计师事务所基于重要性原则出具了无保留意见的财务报表。正如该审计事务所的一位发言人所指出的，这种意见并不意味着认可报表中的所有内容。然而直到1999年4月，格雷斯公司仍坚称普华会计师事务所对其会计处理“毫无保留地予以认可”。³⁵ 1999年6月30日，格雷斯公司在不承认也不否认美国证监会指控的情况下达成了和解。该公司同意停止进一步的证券法违规行为，并设立一笔100万美元的教育基金，用于普及有关财务报表及公认会计原则的知识。按照惯常的说辞，该公司解释称和解是“因为我们认为，将此事抛在脑后并继续前进符合员工和股东的最佳利益”。³⁶ 格雷斯事件提醒我们：几乎在所有情况下，一旦有人指控企业财务报告存在违规行为，企业总会以激烈且千篇一律的方式加以否认。

<!--en-->
It appears, in short, that Grace's 1998 statement that its auditors had raised no objections to its accounting for the Medicare reimbursement windfall was true only in the technical sense that Price Waterhouse issued clean financials, based on materiality considerations. As a spokeswoman for the auditing firm pointed out, such an opinion does not imply agreement with everything in the statements. As late as April 1999, however, Grace was still insisting that Price Waterhouse had approved its accounting "without reservation."³⁵
On June 30, 1999, Grace settled the case without admitting or denying the SEC's charges. The company agreed to cease and desist from further securities law violations and also to set up a $1 million education fund to promote awareness of and education about financial statements and generally accepted accounting principles. Adhering again to the standard script, the corporation explained that it settled the case "because we think it is in the best interests of our employees and shareholders to put this matter behind us and move forward."³⁶
The Grace affair serves as a reminder that almost invariably, an allegation of irregularities in corporate financial reporting is followed by a vehement, formulaic denial.

无论企业如何宣称自己因诚信受到质疑而深感愤慨，分析师都应对其所谓“清白无辜”的辩解持保留态度。历史记录并未表明，那些极力为自己会计做法辩护的企业最终一定能证明自己并无过错。

<!--en-->
No matter how offended the company purports to be about having its integrity questioned, analysts should take the protests of innocence with a grain of salt. The record does not suggest that the companies that bray loudest in defending their accounting practices are sure to be vindicated in the end.

## 篡改数据：一个系统性问题

<!--en-->
*FUDGING THE NUMBERS: A SYSTEMATIC PROBLEM*

前述例子表明，虚报营业收入的现象其实相当普遍。不过读者或许会疑惑：这种论述是否过于悲观地看待人性？毕竟大多数人本质上不是诚实的吗？对于从未遭遇过先前公布的销售数据被修正且发现其具有误导性或欺诈性的新手分析师而言，对每家公司的损益表都心存疑虑或许显得多疑。更深入地审视利润问题

<!--en-->
As the preceding examples demonstrate, manipulation of reported revenue is distressingly common. Readers may nevertheless wonder whether this discussion presents too bleak a picture of human nature. Are not most people basically honest, after all? To a novice analyst who has never been blindsided by revisions of previously reported sales figures that proved misleading orfraudulent, it may seem paranoid to view every company's income statement with suspicion.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

哈佛商学院名誉教授迈克尔·C·詹森指出，在员工薪酬公式中设定预算目标，必然会导致营业收入的虚报。³⁷ 詹森写道：“告诉管理者，一旦达成目标就能获得奖金，结果会有两件事发生：首先，管理者会试图设定容易实现的目标；其次，一旦目标确定，他们就会竭尽全力确保目标达成，哪怕这会损害公司利益。”他列举了一些管理者通过以下手段“竭尽全力”达到目标的真实案例：

<!--en-->
Harvard Business School Professor Emeritus Michael C. Jensen observes, however, that misrepresenting revenues is the inevitable consequence of using budget targets in employee compensation formulas.³⁷ “Tell a manager that he will get a bonus when targets are realized and two things will happen,” writes Jensen. “First, managers will attempt to set easy targets, and, second, once these are set, they will do their best to see that they are met even if it damages the company.” He cites real-life examples of managers who “did their best” through such stratagems as:

- 运送重量与产品完全相同的水果篮，并将其记为销售收入。
- 宣布自1月2日起涨价，以此促使客户在年底前下单，从而帮助管理者实现销售目标。这一涨价行为使该公司与竞争对手相比处于不利地位。
- 将尚未组装完成的重型设备从英国的一家工厂发往荷兰（以便在目标季度确认收入）。制造商随后花费巨额成本并历经诸多不便，才在其客户附近的仓库完成设备的组装工作。除了管理者操纵收入的行为外，一些企业客户也乐于配合这种操作。“很多时候，如果没有客户的协助，公司根本无法实施此类欺诈行为，”美国证券交易委员会的地区管理员海伦·L·莫里森指出。³⁸例如，无线通讯供应商Hybrid Networks在1997年第四季度的收入中，有三分之一来自报告期最后一天向分销商Ikon Office Solutions的销售业务。尽管Ikon明知自己没有客户需要这些设备，仍同意从Hybrid购买价值150万美元的调制解调器。Hybrid通过提供一份附加协议来促成这笔交易，该协议实际上允许Ikon无需付款即可退回这些调制解调器。Ikon于1998年行使了这一权利，但负责此次采购的Ikon高管罗纳德·戴维斯却给Hybrid发送电子邮件，声称自己对那份附加协议毫不知情。不幸的是，Hybrid后来将附加协议的副本交给了审计人员。随后，美国证监会起诉了Hybrid，后者被迫重新陈述财务数据，以剔除这笔并未实际完成的调制解调器销售业务。此外，戴维斯还收到了停止进一步违反证券法的禁令。在其他一些涉及不当确认销售的执法行动中，美国证监会也指控企业客户的高管存在共谋行为。

收入确认：那些能让管理者获利却损害公司真实利润的收入确认手段究竟有多普遍？据Ikon高管戴维斯称：“制造商经常打电话给你说：‘我需要达到季度业绩指标，你能否给我一张价值10万美元的采购订单？’”³⁹在围绕W. R. Grace公司涉嫌推迟收入确认以平滑盈利的诉讼中，首席财务官的律师为客户的做法辩护道：“任何地方的首席财务官都会以某种方式操控盈利数据，而如今美国证监会却据此认定其为欺诈行为。”⁴⁰迈克尔·詹森补充道：“几乎每家公司都采用一种预算制度，这种制度奖励员工说谎，却惩罚他们说真话。”他提议通过切断预算目标与薪酬之间的关联来改革这一制度。不过现实是，激进的改革短期内不太可能实现。因此，分析师必须仔细审查他们所分析的每家公司的收入情况。即便对于最优质的蓝筹股公司而言，监控应收账款或存货相对于销售额的增长水平也应成为常规操作。无论管理层如何保证，应收账款和递延收入的显著增长都是危险的信号。当会员制公司的注册人数与其报告销售额之间出现偏离常规的关系时，分析师必须及时发出警示。詹森指出：“预算操纵现象十分普遍，而在大多数企业文化中，这种行为甚至被视为理所当然，甚至受到赞扬。”分析师务必保持警惕。

收入及盈利数据的重新陈述出现在各种情形之中。许多备受瞩目的案例涉及处于相对较新行业中的初创公司。在潜在的滥用行为被揭露之前，管理层可能会采取比审计人员日后所能容忍的更为随意的做法。另一方面，一些历史悠久的大型企业在确认销售收入时有时也会过于激进。成熟企业可能出于满足此前快速增长所形成的高期望之需，而刻意夸大收入。 事后，各公司通常将财报数据虚高归因于判断失误、会计错误、个别经理的故意歪曲，或是这三者的组合。经验丰富的分析师们曾多次因营收数据被修正而吃亏，因此往往不相信这些夸大陈述只是无心的差错。为了了解这些资深人士的观点——即便未必认同他们对人性的悲观看法——回顾几个营收数据造假的典型案例还是很有必要的。

2002年11月，Enterasys Networks公司重新核算了2000年和2001年共19个月期间的营收数据，发现其实际营收比原先报告的数字低11%，公司将其归咎于会计错误。在此期间，该公司的净亏损额也相应增加了同样的比例。（之所以出现不寻常的19个月区间，是因为财政年度发生了变化。）导致1.53亿美元销售额被剔除的错误包括：在错误的期间入账、对作为产品付款而收到的股票估值过高，以及本应计入营收但在这19个月期间并未实际到账的款项。Enterasys是Cabletron Systems的主要存续子公司，由克雷格·本森共同创立；就在营收数据被修正的消息公布时，本森刚刚当选新罕布什尔州州长。《华尔街日报》试图联系当选州长本森过渡团队的发言人，但未获回应；本森自2000年6月起便担任Enterasys的审计委员会成员。

**深入剖析利润问题**  
辛辛那提米拉克龙公司称，该公司是通过匿名举报才发现有230万美元的销售额被虚报，时间发生在1993年上半年。公司称这一“孤立”事件源于Sano塑料机械部门未能遵守“销售截止”规则。与辛辛那提米拉克龙公司的政策相悖的是，Sano将尚未发货的产品也算入了销售额。最终只有一名高级经理被解雇，其他人仅受到训斥。⁴¹

第一财务管理公司则将1991年前九个月的营收数据修正归咎于会计错误，而非违反政策。（不过，负有责任的部分员工还是被解雇了。）问题出在Basis Information Technologies子公司身上，该公司是由第一财务管理公司合并19家独立企业后组建的。据报道，Basis Information Technologies未能准确记录某些随合同到期而应冲减的应计收入。在查明这一混乱状况的同时，第一财务管理公司还发现某些与收购相关的费用被不当摊销。⁴²

在2003年6月接受《财富》杂志采访时，朗讯科技公司的外部律师对该公司在一笔交易中所确认的1.25亿美元营收发表了评论，美国证券交易委员会曾对该笔交易的营收确认提出质疑。克拉瓦思、斯韦恩与摩尔律师事务所的保罗·桑德斯将朗讯与Winstar公司之间的这笔交易视为“沟通不畅”，而非会计欺诈。当被问及这种失误是否故意为之时，桑德斯回答：“我不知道，我认为不是。”⁴³ 一个月后，朗讯被迫发布撤回声明，承认桑德斯的言论不准确，且公司确实伪造了相关文件。

2004年5月17日，朗讯公司及三名前高管同意达成和解，他们既不承认也不否认美国证券交易委员会的指控。SEC指控称，朗讯在2000财年虚假且不当确认了约11.48亿美元的营收和4.7亿美元的税前利润。SEC的诉状指出，九名现任及前任朗讯高管为了完成内部销售目标并获取基于销售的奖金，不当授予或隐瞒了各种附加协议及其他激励措施，以此诱使客户购买公司产品。 此外，美国证监会指出，这些高管违反了内部会计控制规定，并就合同外承诺的存在情况误导了公司的财务和会计人员。虽然此案并未导致财务业绩的重新列报，但美国证监会因朗讯公司不配合调查而对其处以2500万美元的罚款。收入确认 147

<!--en-->
- Shipping fruit baskets that weighed exactly the same amount as their product and booking them as sales.
- Announcing a price increase, effective January 2, to induce customers to order before year-end and thereby help managers achieve their sales targets. The price hike put the company out of line with the competition.
- Shipping unfinished heavy equipment from a plant in England (resulting in revenue recognition in the desired quarter) to the Netherlands. At considerable cost and inconvenience, the manufacturer then completed the assembly in a warehouse located near its customer.
Compounding the problem of managers who play games with their revenues is the willingness of some corporate customers to play along. “All too often, companies wouldn’t be able to accomplish the frauds without the assistance of their customers,” observes Helane L. Morrison, a district administrator for the Securities and Exchange Commission.³⁸ For example, one-third of wireless communications provider Hybrid Networks’ revenue in the fourth quarter of 1997 consisted of a sale made on the final day of the reporting period to a distributor, Ikon Office Solutions. Ikon agreed to purchase $1.5 million worth of modems from Hybrid, despite knowing that it had no customers for the equipment. Hybrid closed the sale by providing a side letter essentially permitting Ikon to return the modems without paying for them. Ikon exercised that option in 1998, yet Ronald Davies, the Ikon executive who handled the purchase, sent an e-mail to Hybrid denying any knowledge of the side letter. Unfortunately, Hybrid later gave a copy of the side letter to its auditors. The SEC then sued Hybrid, which was forced to restate its revenues to eliminate the nonfinal sale of modems to Ikon. Furthermore, Davies received a cease-and-desist order to refrain from further violations of the securities laws. In certain other enforcement actions alleging improper recognition of sales as well, the SEC has charged executives of corporate customers with collusion.
Revenue Recognition
How widespread are revenue recognition gambits that enrich managers but impair bona fide profits? According to Ikon executive Davies, “It’s very common for a manufacturer to call you up and say, ‘I need to hit my quarterly number, would you mind giving me a purchase order for $100,000?’”³⁹ In the litigation surrounding W. R. Grace’s alleged delay of revenue recognition to smooth earnings, the chief financial officer’s attorney defended his client’s action by arguing, “Any CFO anywhere has managed earnings in a way the SEC is now jumping up and down and calling fraud.”⁴⁰ Michael Jensen chimes in, “Almost every company uses a budget system that rewards employees for lying and punishes them for telling the truth.” He proposes reforming the system by severing the link between budget targets and compensation. Realistically, however, radical reforms are not likely to occur any time soon.
Analysts therefore need to scrutinize carefully the revenues of every company they examine. Even in the case of the bluest of the blue chips, watching for rising levels of accounts receivable or inventory, relative to sales, should be standard operating procedure. Regardless of management’s programmed reassurances, conspicuous surges in unbilled receivables and deferred income are telltale danger signals. It is imperative that analysts raise a red flag when a membership-based company’s registrations deviate from their customary relationship with reported sales. “Budget-gaming is rife,” says Jensen, and “in most corporate cultures, much of this is expected, even praised.” Let the analyst beware.
Restatements of revenues and earnings arise in a wide range of circumstances. Many well-publicized cases involve young companies in comparatively new industries. Until the potential abuses have been demonstrated, management may be able to take greater liberties than the auditors will countenance at a later point. On the other hand, major, long-established corporations are sometimes overzealous in booking sales. Mature companies may pump up revenues out of a desire to meet high expectations created by earlier rapid growth.
After the fact, companies variously attribute excesses in reporting to misjudgment, bookkeeping errors, deliberate misrepresentation by rogue managers, or some combination of the three. Seasoned analysts, having been burned on many occasions by revenue revisions, tend to doubt that overstatements are ever innocent mistakes. To gain some of the veterans’ perspective, if not necessarily their jaundiced view of human nature, it is worthwhile to review a few case histories of misstated revenues.
In November 2002, Enterasys Networks restated its revenue downward by 11 percent for a 19-month period in 2000 and 2001, blaming accounting mistakes. The network equipment maker’s net loss for the period rose by the same amount. (A change in the fiscal year accounted for the unusual19-month interval.) The purported mistakes that contributed to the elimination of $153 million of sales included revenues booked in the wrong periods, inflated valuations of stock received as payment for products, and expected payments that were booked as revenues but failed to materialize during the 19-month interval. Enterasys was the major surviving subsidiary of Cabletron Systems, cofounded by Craig Benson, who had just been elected governor of New Hampshire when the revisions were announced. The *Wall Street Journal* received no response to its call to a spokesman for the transition team of governor-elect Benson, who had served on the Enterasys audit committee since June 2000.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS
Cincinnati Milacron credited an anonymous tip for its uncovering of a $2.3 million overstatement of sales in the first half of 1993. The “isolated” incident, said the company, involved a failure by the Sano plastic machinery unit to observe the “sales cutoff” rule. Contrary to Cincinnati Milacron’s policy, Sano had counted in sales units that had not been shipped. The obligatory firing centered on a senior manager, while others escaped with reprimands.⁴¹
First Financial Management blamed accounting errors, rather than policy violations, for its restatement of revenues for the first nine months of 1991. (Some of the employees at fault were fired, all the same.) The problem arose in the Basis Information Technologies subsidiary, a unit that First Financial had formed by consolidating 19 separate companies. Basis Information Technologies reportedly lost track of certain accruals of revenue, which should have been reduced as contracts expired. While uncovering the mess, First Financial also found that certain acquisition-related expenses had been amortized improperly.⁴²
In a June 2003 interview with *Fortune*, Lucent Technologies’ outside counsel commented on the company’s booking of $125 million of revenue in a deal that the Securities and Exchange Commission had questioned. Paul Sanders of Cravath, Swaine & Moore characterized the telecommunications equipment manufacturer’s handling of the transaction with Winstar as a “failure of communication,” rather than as accounting fraud. Asked if the failure was intentional, Sanders replied, “I don’t know. I don’t think so.”⁴³ One month later, Lucent was forced to publish a retraction in which it acknowledged that Sanders’s comments were inaccurate and that it had falsified documents. On May 17, 2004, Lucent and three former executives agreed to settle, without admitting or denying the allegations, SEC charges that the company fraudulently and improperly recognized about $1.148 billion of revenue and $470 million in pretax earnings during fiscal 2000. The SEC complaint asserted that nine current and former Lucent executives improperly granted or failed to disclose side agreements and other incentives to induce customers to buy the company’s products, all in order tomeet internal sales targets and obtain sales-based bonuses. Furthermore, the SEC charged, the executives violated internal accounting controls and misled corporate finance and accounting personnel about the existence of extracontractual commitments. This case did not result in a restatement of financial results, but the SEC fined Lucent $25 million for not cooperating with its investigation.

## 结论

<!--en-->
*CONCLUSION*

励志演说家向听众保证：只要他们能想象出成功的景象，成功便会随之而来。一些信奉自助理念的企业高管将这一建议奉为圭臬。看到有条件的销售和可疑的会员制模式后，他们便幻想出符合公认会计原则（GAAP）的营收数据，以为现实会随之实现。他们将这种虚幻的图景搬进财务报表中，以此抬高公司看似的市场价值和信用质量。当这种凭空想象的营收未能兑现时，管理者可能会诉诸欺诈手段来维持这一假象。然而，早期那种夸大营收的积极心态，与后期实施的欺诈行为一样具有破坏性。一旦发现有过度激进的营收确认迹象，分析师必须迅速而果断地采取行动，以免被管理者那种危险的乐观情绪所影响。

<!--en-->
Motivational speakers assure their audiences that if they visualize success, success will follow. Some of the corporate executives who live by the self-help creed take this advice a bit too literally. Seeing conditional sales and dubious memberships, they visualize GAAP revenues, believing that reality will follow. They transfer their own mirage to the financial statements, pumping up their companies' perceived market value and credit quality. When the revenues derived from wishful thinking fail to materialize, the managers may resort to fraud to maintain the illusion. The positive mental attitude that overstates revenues in the early stage is no less damaging, however, than the fraud responsible at a later point. When evidence of overly aggressive revenue recognition appears, analysts must act swiftly and decisively, lest they become infected by the managers' dangerous optimism.

# 第七章

<!--en-->
*CHAPTER 7*

# 费用确认

<!--en-->
*Expense Recognition*

正如第六章所述，企业可以通过激进的营收确认来严重扭曲其盈利状况。对财务报表保持适当怀疑态度的分析师，自然会质疑企业是否也通过随意处理费用来虚增净利润。答案无疑是肯定的。企业管理者在压低和延迟费用确认方面，与他们在最大化及加速营收确认方面的手段同样“巧妙”。

<!--en-->
As Chapter 6 illustrated, companies can grossly distort their earnings through aggressive revenue recognition. Analysts who arm themselves with appropriate skepticism about financial statements are bound to wonder whether companies also pump up the bottom line by taking liberties in booking expenses. The answer is resoundingly affirmative. Corporate managers are just as creative in minimizing and slowing down the recognition of expenses as they are in maximizing and speeding up the recognition of revenues.

## 北电网络的递延利润计划

<!--en-->
*NORTEL'S DEFERRED PROFIT PLAN*

北电网络展示了应计项目所具有的扭曲能力，这也是财务报告中最容易被滥用的特征之一。该公司成立于1882年，最初是加拿大贝尔电话公司下属的电话及电话设备制造部门；1895年，该部门被剥离出来，成为北方电气制造有限公司。此后历经多次所有权和名称变更，最终定名为北电网络，以彰显其主导全球公共及私人电信网络市场的雄心。

<!--en-->
Nortel Networks illustrated the distorting power of accruals, one of the most abused features of financial reporting. Founded in 1882 as the Bell Telephone Company of Canada's department for manufacturing telephones and telephone equipment, the unit was spun off as the Northern Electric and Manufacturing Company Limited in 1895. It went through various ownership and name changes, eventually becoming known as Nortel Networks to signify the company's quest to dominate the global market for public and private telecommunications networks.

北电网络逐渐发展成为北美最大的电信设备制造商，并搭乘了20世纪90年代末光纤设备行业的繁荣快车。从1990年代中期到2000年代中期，其市值增长了十多倍，公司还斥资300亿美元用于收购。北电网络在广告中请来了埃尔顿·约翰等名人代言。

<!--en-->
Nortel grew into North America's largest telecommunications equipment manufacturer and rode the late-1990s boom in fiber optics equipment. From the mid-1990s until mid-2000, its market capitalization soared more than tenfold, and the company shelled out $30 billion for acquisitions. Nortel's showy advertisements featured celebrities such as Elton John.

2000年的科技泡沫破裂终结了那些辉煌岁月。人们发现，与许多高科技同行一样，这家加拿大工业的标杆企业支付了过高的价格进行草率收购，向客户提供了不靠谱的信贷条件，并做出了过于乐观的盈利预测。从2000年9月到2002年8月，北电网络的市值缩水了99%，导致大量投资于其股票的加拿大养老基金遭受重创。【更深入地审视利润】

<!--en-->
The Tech Wreck brought those heady days to an end in 2000. It became apparent that like many of its high-tech peers, the showpiece of Canadian industry had paid exorbitant prices for ill-considered acquisitions, extended credit to customers on unsound terms, and made overly optimistic earnings forecasts. Between September 2000 and August 2002, Nortel's marketcapitalization sank by 99 percent, devastating Canadian pension plans that were heavily invested in its shares.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

### 会计差异的最初迹象

<!--en-->
*First Indications of Accounting Discrepancies*

新任首席执行官弗兰克·邓恩采取积极措施稳定公司局面，将员工人数从95,000人削减至35,000人，并退出几项主要业务。然而，2003年10月23日，转型进程遭遇阻碍。北电网络宣布，公司在会计上出现了“错误”，导致2000年、2001年、2002年以及2003年上半年所报告的亏损额需减少7.4亿美元。审查发现，在此期间公司的资产负债表多计了9亿美元的负债，而相应的亏损部分被1.6亿美元的税收抵免所抵消。此外，公司重新核查账目后发现，三年半时间内产生的9,200万美元营收本应递延到以后期间确认。

<!--en-->
New CEO Frank Dunn moved aggressively to stabilize the company, slashing the workforce from 95,000 to 35,000 and exiting several major businesses. The turnaround ran into a snag on October 23, 2003, however. Nortel announced that it had made accounting “mistakes” that required a reduction of previously stated losses totaling $740 million for 2000, 2001, 2002, and the first half of 2003. A review found that the company’s balance sheet overstated liabilities by $900 million for the period in question, with the associated losses partly offset by $160 million in corresponding tax benefits. In addition, the company’s second look at its books revealed that $92 million in revenues from the three-and-a-half-year span should have been deferred to later periods.

曾在2000年及2001年大部分时间担任首席财务官的邓恩解释称，这些错误发生在高科技行业动荡不安的时期。“我想向北电网络的利益相关者保证，我们决心查明错误根源，并采取适当措施确保此类问题不再发生。”¹ 但股东们并未完全放心，因为北电网络的股价在盘后交易中下跌了6%。

<!--en-->
Dunn, who had been chief financial officer in 2000 and much of 2001, explained that the errors were made during a volatile period for the high-tech industry. “I want to assure Nortel Networks stakeholders that we are committed to working to identify the causes of the mistakes,” said Dunn, “and to implement the appropriate measures to ensure that the problems will not recur in the future.”¹ Shareholders were not entirely reassured, as Nortel’s shares fell by 6 percent in after-hours trading.

不过总体而言，投资者认为由于拟进行的账务调整幅度不大且能减少此前报告的亏损，因此这一消息并不算太糟。

<!--en-->
On the whole, though, investors concluded that because the planned restatements were modest and would reduce previous losses, the news was not all that bad.

三个月后，北电网络及其首席执行官似乎已经挽回了在投资者心中的失地，因为该公司宣布了六年来首次年度盈利。“执行得非常出色，”一位华尔街分析师欣喜地说，“数据看起来相当不错。”² 遗憾的是，这些数据并不像看上去那么好。2004年3月10日，北电网络透露，其审计委员会的调查可能会导致对过往盈利数据的再次调整。结果，该公司不得不推迟提交2003年度财务报告，从而发出了关于其财务报表可信度的警示信号。随后一周，北电网络将首席财务官道格拉斯·C·比蒂和财务总监迈克尔·J·戈洛格利安排为无限期带薪休假。从让高管休假而非直接解雇这一不同寻常的做法来看，会计专家怀疑公司的问题十分严重，甚至可能与审计机构德勤会计师事务所存在分歧。

<!--en-->
Three months later, Nortel and its CEO appeared to have regained any lost ground with investors as the company announced its first annual profit in six years. “Great execution,” exulted one Wall Street analyst. “The numbers look really good.”²
Unfortunately, the numbers proved not to be as good as they looked. On March 10, 2004, Nortel disclosed that an investigation by its audit committee was likely to necessitate another revision of past earnings. As a result, the company had to wave a classic red flag with respect to the credibility of its financial statements by delaying the filing of its 2003 financial reports. The following week, Nortel placed Chief Financial Officer Douglas C. Beatty and Controller Michael J. Gollogly on indefinite paid leaves of absence. Based on the unusual procedure of putting the executives on leave, rather than firing them, accounting experts suspected the company’s problems were acute and might involve a disagreement with auditor Deloitte & Touche.

不过，一些券商分析师仍对该公司的前景表示乐观。

<!--en-->
Some brokerage house analysts, however, continued to express confidence in the company’s outlook.

“在我看来，北电网络过去确实犯过错误，但我愿意相信他们已经吸取了教训，”³ 一位坚持推荐买入的分析师评论道。一家独立股票研究公司的分析师承认管理层存在信任问题，但希望此次会计调整幅度较小，对北电网络股价的影响有限。“既然只是调整往年数据，那又有什么关系呢？我今天就要买入这只股票，”⁴ 该分析师说。费用确认 151

<!--en-->
“In my opinion Nortel has made mistakesin the past, but I'd like to believe that they learned their lesson,"³ commented one analyst who maintained his buy recommendation. An analyst at an independent equities research firm acknowledged there was an issue of trust in management but expressed hope that the accounting changes would be minor and have little impact on Nortel's share price. "When you're adjusting prior year numbers, who cares, I'm buying the stock today,"⁴ the analyst said.

事实证明，这种看法大错特错。持更怀疑态度的观察人士开始质疑，最近的这些会计差错是否真的属于无意之失。2003年，北电网络推出了一项特别奖金计划：高管的奖金与利润挂钩。据多伦多的《环球邮报》报道，共有16名高管通过该计划共获得了4360万美元的奖金。据报道，邓恩和比蒂分别获得了215万美元和83.1万美元。⁵

<!--en-->
That remark would prove misguided by a long shot. More skeptical observers were apt to wonder whether the latest accounting inaccuracies were truly inadvertent errors. In 2003, Nortel had introduced a special bonus scheme. Senior executives' bonuses were tied to profits, and according to Toronto's *Globe and Mail*, 16 executives had collected a total of $43.6 million under the plan. Dunn and Beatty had reportedly received $2.15 million and $831,000, respectively.⁵

## 每况愈下

<!--en-->
*From Bad to Worse*

2004年3月5日，北电网络是纽约证券交易所交易量最大的股票，当日股价下跌3.7%。美国证券交易委员会（SEC）宣布，已将对该公司会计问题的调查升级为正式立案调查。监管研究机构SEC Insight Inc.的总裁约翰·加文评论称，SEC此次升级调查并赋予其发出传票的权力，可能意味着北电网络“并未如其所言那样积极配合”。安大略省证券委员会也在调查北电网络的财务报告情况，而加拿大皇家骑警随后的调查也演变成了刑事侦查。

<!--en-->
Nortel was the most heavily traded stock on the New York Stock Exchange on March 5, 2004, falling by 3.7 percent, as the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) announced that it had upgraded its inquiry into the company's accounting to a formal investigation. John Gavin, president of the regulatory research firm SEC Insight Inc., commented that the SEC's upgrading of its probe, which empowered the commission to issue subpoenas, might indicate that Nortel was "not cooperating as much as they say they are."⁶ The Ontario Securities Commission also was looking into Nortel's financial reporting, and an inquiry by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police later evolved into a criminal investigation.

那些轻视会计问题严重性的分析师在2004年4月28日遭到了打击。北电网络宣布将此前公布的2003年7.32亿美元盈利数字削减50%。该公司称部分利润将被重新计入此前出现亏损的年份。北电网络还推迟公布2003年第一季度业绩，进一步损害了自身的信誉。

<!--en-->
Analysts who had downplayed the significance of the accounting revelations were dealt a blow on April 28, 2004. Nortel dropped a bombshell in the form of a 50 percent cut in its previously announced 2003 earnings of $732 million. The company said some of those profits would be shifted to earlier years, for which it reported losses. Nortel also delayed the reporting of its results for the first quarter of 2003, further damaging its credibility.

除了令市场期待的新一轮会计调整幅度较小的希望破灭外，北电网络还因解雇首席执行官邓恩、首席财务官比蒂和财务总监戈洛格利而震动市场。

<!--en-->
In addition to dashing hopes that the new round of accounting statements would be minor, Nortel rattled the market by firing CEO Dunn, CFO Beatty, and controller Gollogly.

他们被以“有过失”为由解雇，但根据加拿大法律，这一表述包括无能的情况，因此解雇并不一定意味着存在犯罪行为。北电网络还将其四个业务部门的财务负责人安排为带薪休假。该公司股价下跌了28%，标准普尔公司也将该公司的企业信用评级从B下调至B-。利润详析

<!--en-->
They were terminated for cause, but under Canadian law that phrase included incompetence, so the dismissal did not necessarily imply any criminal acts. Nortel also placed the finance chiefs of its four operating divisions on paid leave. The company's stock price dropped by 28 percent, and Standard & Poor's downgraded its corporate credit rating from B to B-.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

一些观察人士认为，这些高管不过是董事会未能有效监督公司会计实践的替罪羊。邓恩在应对2001年经济衰退时的表现仍备受赞誉。此外，行业专家认为从技术层面看，该公司处于有利地位。

<!--en-->
Some observers suggested that the senior executives were scapegoats for the board's failure to police the company's accounting practices. Dunn continued to receive high marks for his response to the 2001 business downturn. Furthermore, industry experts considered the company well positioned from a technological standpoint.

尽管有这些所谓的运营优势，北电网络财务报告的可信度仍在持续恶化。2004年6月2日，该公司表示，2003年盈利数字被削减50%未必是最后一次调整。随着北电网络开始处理2003年下半年的报告数据，进一步重述的可能性也随之出现。

<!--en-->
Notwithstanding these purported operational strengths, the credibility of Nortel's financial reporting continued to deteriorate. On June 2, 2004, the company indicated that the 50 percent cut in its 2003 earnings would not necessarily be the last revision. The possibility of further restatements arose as Nortel turned its attention to its reporting for the second half of 2003.

由于该公司不断推迟发布最终盈利重述结果的日期，管理层的可信度继续下降。

<!--en-->
Management's credibility continued to shrink as the company kept pushing back its target date for producing definitive earnings restatements.

北电网络有650名员工专门负责此项工作，此外还有众多外部审计师和顾问协助。到2004年8月，他们的努力仅产生了“估算出的有限初步未经审计”数据。⁷三个月后，该公司仍未公布2004年的任何业绩，并再次推迟财务报告的发布。2004年8月11日，新的一页被翻开：此前专注于应计项目和准备金核算的北电网络调查，转向了收入确认问题。公司称，原定于2000年确认、但计划推迟到以后年度计入的25亿美元收入中，有2.5亿美元将被完全剔除。这一金额的错误确认源于多种原因：包括未将法定所有权转移给客户、未达到发货前确认收入的标准、收款可能性存疑以及其他不当操作。多伦多Terra Capital基金的基金经理邓肯·斯图尔特表示，北电网络的高层管理人员因未能遵守自行设定的财务报表提交期限，且在经过数月调查后才公布重大的财务报告问题，简直“像小丑一样”⁸。

<!--en-->
Nortel had 650 employees devoted to the task, augmented by a host of outside auditors and consultants. By August 2004, their efforts had produced only "estimated limited preliminary unaudited" numbers.⁷
Three months later, the company still had not reported any results for 2004, and it once again delayed the release of its financials. On August 11, 2004, a new chapter opened. Nortel's investigation, which previously had focused on accruals and provisions, had turned to revenue recognition. The company said that $250 million of the $2.5 billion in 2000 revenue that had been slated for shifting to later years would be eliminated altogether. Incorrect recognition of that amount resulted from a combination of nontransfer of legal title to customers, failure to meet criteria for recognizing revenue prior to shipment, the collectibility questions, and other incorrect steps. Duncan Stewart, a fund manager with Terra Capital in Toronto, said Nortel's senior managers were "looking like clowns"⁸ for failing to meet self-imposed deadlines for filing financial statements and for announcing major new financial reporting problems after many months of investigating.

2005年1月10日，北电网络终于提交了2003年度的财务报表。

<!--en-->
On January 10, 2005, Nortel finally filed its 2003 financial statements.

鉴于董事会对公司会计工作的监管受到严厉批评，五位董事表示不会寻求连任，尽管他们并未被指控有任何不当行为。在一个极为罕见的举措中，12名高管同意退还他们根据错误会计数据获得的860万美元奖金。

<!--en-->
Reflecting the heavy criticism of the board's oversight of the company's accounting, five directors said they would not seek reelection, although they were not charged with any wrongdoing. In a highly unusual step, 12 senior executives agreed to return $8.6 million in bonuses they received based on erroneous accounting.

北电网络以3500万美元的和解金解决了美国证监会提出的会计欺诈民事指控，但有关其财务状况不佳的传言仍持续不断。该公司未能获得政府的财政援助，而21世纪头十年的经济衰退更是雪上加霜。2009年1月19日，北电网络在美国、加拿大和英国申请破产。公司最初希望重组并摆脱破产困境，但在2009年6月宣布将清算所有资产。费用确认 153

<!--en-->
Nortel settled SEC civil charges of accounting fraud for $35 million, but rumors of poor financial condition persisted. The company was unable to obtain governmental financial assistance, and the recession of the late 2000s struck a further blow. On January 19, 2009, Nortel filed for bankruptcy in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. The companyinitially hoped to reorganize and emerge from bankruptcy, but in June 2009 announced that it would instead liquidate all of its assets.
