2001年11月19日，该公司告知投资者：到2002年底将有91.5亿美元的债务到期，而可用的现金和信贷额度仅约17.5亿美元。这一信息出现在迟交五天的截至9月30日的季度10-Q报告中——这又是财务报告舞弊的典型预警信号。

<!--en-->
On November 19, 2001, the company told investors that it had $9.15 billion in debt coming due by the end of 2002 and only about $1.75 billion of cash and credit lines available. This disclosure came in the 10-Q for the quarter ending September 30, which was filed five days late—another classic warning sign of financial reporting malfeasance.

11月21日，惠誉评级指出，安然公司BBB-的评级——属于投资级中的最低等级——取决于与Dynegy的收购交易能否完成。该评级机构警告称，如果交易失败，安然申请破产的可能性极大。在接下来的几天里，标准普尔、穆迪投资者服务公司和惠誉均将安然的评级维持在投资级，因为该公司试图协商重组银行债务。11月28日，谈判破裂，这三家机构遂将安然的评级下调至投机级。Dynegy终止了拟议中的收购计划，12月2日，安然便成为了当时有史以来规模最大的企业破产案。

<!--en-->
On November 21, Fitch stated that its Enron rating of BBB-, the lowest in the investment grade tier, depended on the Dynegy acquisition being consummated. The rating agency warned that if the deal broke down, a bankruptcy filing was highly possible. For the next few days, Standard & Poor's, Moody's Investors Service, and Fitch kept their ratings in the investment grade category as the company attempted to negotiate a restructuring of its bank debt. On November 28, the talks broke down, and all three agencies lowered Enron to speculative grade. Dynegy terminated its proposed acquisition, and on December 2, Enron became, by a wide margin, the biggest corporate bankruptcy ever, up to that time.

在12月12日的国会听证会上，安达信会计师事务所首席执行官约瑟夫·P·贝拉迪诺暗示安然可能违反了证券法。法斯托承认了电信欺诈和证券欺诈罪名。

<!--en-->
In congressional hearings on December 12, Arthur Andersen CEO Joseph P. Berardino suggested that Enron might have violated securities laws. Fastow pleaded guilty to wire and securities fraud.

莱和斯基林被判犯有欺诈罪和共谋罪，不过由于莱在即将服刑前去世，其定罪被撤销。欺诈行为是否可被察觉？

<!--en-->
Lay and Skilling were convicted of fraud and conspiracy, although Lay's conviction was rescinded when he died shortly before he was to begin his prison sentence.
Is Fraud Detectable?

### 安然如何误导投资者

<!--en-->
*How Enron Misled Investors*

安然掩盖其真实财务状况的关键之一在于缺乏坦诚。安然的许多披露虽然符合法律条文要求，但据《华尔街日报》报道，一些顶尖会计学教授表示他们根本无法理解安然与法斯托之间的交易及其背后的动机。同一份刊物的另一篇文章指出，大多数证券分析师也承认他们并不清楚安然是如何盈利的。

<!--en-->
One key to Enron's concealment of its true financial condition was simply a lack of forthrightness. Many of Enron's disclosures met the letter of the law, but according to a *Wall Street Journal* article, some top-flight professors of accounting said they could not make heads or tails of Enron's transactions with Fastow or the company's reasons for entering into them. Another article in the same publication stated that most securities analysts readily conceded that they did not know how Enron made money.

该公司对其业务的描述不仅没有阐明真相，反而造成了混淆。安然超过90%的申报收入来自其称之为“批发服务”的交易活动。该公司对这项业务的解释如下：

<!--en-->
The company's description of its business shed no light and instead spread confusion. Enron derived more than 90 percent of its reported revenue from trading, which it called "wholesale services." It explained that business as follows:

> *安然公司通过构建由选择性资产所有权、对第三方资产的合同使用权以及做市商活动组成的网络，来发展批发业务。*《福布斯网》的丹·阿克曼写道，这句话读起来“就像是用德语写成，经波兰语中转后再译回英语一样。”⁷ 安然公司还利用会计准则中的漏洞来误导投资者。该公司按照合约总值而非净值来确认能源相关衍生工具的营收，而其他证券交易通常按净值计算营收。例如，如果一家经纪公司为客户交易10,000股价格为50美元的股票，它计入营收的要么是佣金，要么是买卖价差，总额约为500美元。而对于一份总值同样为500,000美元、佣金或价差却很小的能源合约，安然公司却将其营收记为500,000美元——这一数字比经纪公司记录的营收高出一千倍。这种会计处理方式使安然公司在2000年的报告营收翻了一番，从而超越那些经济影响力更大的企业，自称是“美国第七大公司”。对**市价计价会计**规则的过度滥用，构成了安然公司虚假陈述的又一例证。根据美国通用会计准则（GAAP），将预计在未来长达20年内实现的能源相关合约及其他衍生工具利润计入当期收益是合法的。每个季度末，该公司会估算每份未平仓电力或天然气买卖合约的公允价值。合约价值的后续变动会被加入或扣除当期收益。由于只有期限在几年内的合约才有公开的市场报价作为估值依据，因此长期合约缺乏独立的估值基准。在这种情况下，安然公司被允许使用未公开的假设和定价模型来自行确定估值。  
>
> **深入剖析利润情况**  
> 当然，安然公司首席会计师理查德·考西向投资者保证，公司的估值估计是保守的。他还声称，未实现收益并未集中在估值不确定性最大的长期合约中。不过分析师们仍对安然公司在2001年第二季度计入7.47亿美元未实现收益这一数据感到担忧——该数字甚至超过了公司6.09亿美元的EBITDA值。（对于没有披露类似数据的竞争对手，分析师会通过比较风险管理活动引起的净资产价值变动来进行季度对比。）首席执行官杰弗里·斯基林比考西更甚，他不仅试图打消人们对安然公司报告盈利真实性的怀疑，甚至采取了恐吓手段。在一次讨论安然公司盈利情况的电话会议上，分析师理查德·格鲁布曼抱怨说，该公司是唯一一家不在盈利报告中附上资产负债表的企业。斯基林回应道：“嗯，非常感谢，我们很感激……[粗俗用语]。”⁸  
>
> 当安然公司试图通过出售给Dynegy公司来挽救自身时，其欺骗手段的又一线索浮出水面。《纽约时报》的弗洛伊德·诺里斯报道称，2001年10月23日——即公司解雇首席财务官安德鲁·法斯托的前一天——财务会计准则委员会（FASB）的新兴问题工作组收到了一个紧急提问：假设有一家名为“大型能源公司”的企业，它拥有一家天然气管道子公司和一家能源交易子公司。该公司能否只报告其中一个子公司的盈利，而隐瞒另一个子公司的亏损呢？正如安然公司的损益表掩盖了其报告盈利的实质一样，其资产负债表也歪曲了真实的财务状况。 从肯·莱将一家天然气交易公司转变为能源交易巨头之初，就需要巨额债务支持。根据当时的会计准则，表外实体可以将债务排除在公司账目之外，而安然公司可以借此声称自己并未对这些实体行使控制权。经验丰富的信贷分析师们无视这些会计技术细节，重新计入安然公司在表外实体中所承担的相应债务份额。即便如此，这些表外工具加上不透明的信息披露，仍使该公司看起来比实际负债水平要低。从严重依赖表外融资，到法斯托所参与的那些利润丰厚且存在利益冲突的合伙关系，这一发展过程并不令人意外。安然公司还通过使用一种名为“预付掉期”的衍生品交易来掩盖其债务规模。与普通掉期不同，这种交易要求交易对手方预先付款，而安然公司的付款则分摊到多年期内。一家参与此类预付掉期交易的银行的发言人指出，该交易的现金流模式与浮动利率贷款类似；因此，银行将其记为贷款，而安然公司却将其视为掉期交易。
>
> 欺诈行为能否被察觉？207 虽然安然公司通过曲解规则严重误导了投资者，但其欺骗行为很大程度上源于对基本会计准则的公然违反，且得到了审计师的默许。安达信会计师事务所同意以“金额不重要”为由放弃追究的事项中，就包括2000年计入股东权益的1.72亿美元。这笔款项实际上是公司因向四个特殊目的实体发行股票而收到的应收票据。根据美国通用会计准则（GAAP），公司发行股票时只有在收到现金后才能确认权益。2001年10月，当安然公司修订财务报表时，竟轻描淡写地将这一违反GAAP的行为称为会计错误。另一项违反GAAP的行为则使安然公司得以将某关联公司的债务排除在资产负债表之外。在国会作证时，安达信首席执行官贝拉迪诺称，安然公司并未向审计师披露：它为该金融机构对其特殊目的实体Chewco Investments所进行的3%投资中的一半提供了担保。根据GAAP，这种安排意味着安然公司未能满足避免合并Chewco的条件。随着安然丑闻持续占据新闻头条，有关严重欺诈行为的报道也不断涌现。员工称，1998年管理层曾带他们前往空荡荡的交易大厅，让他们假装成忙碌的销售人员，以应付来访的证券分析师。同样拙劣的手段还包括：据报道，安然公司从银行借入5亿美元购买国库券，几天后又出售这些国库券并偿还银行，却将这笔毫无实质意义的交易所得记为经营活动产生的现金流。

<!--en-->
> *Enron builds wholesale businesses through the creation of networks involving selective asset ownership, contractual access to third-party assets, and market-making activities.*
This statement, wrote Dan Ackman of *Forbes.com*, read "like something written in German, translated to Chinese and back to English by way of Polish."⁷
Enron also misled investors by aggressively exploiting wiggle room in the accounting rules. The company booked revenue from its energy-related derivatives contracts on the basis of gross value, rather than net value, as is the norm for other securities transactions. For instance, if a brokerage firm trades 10,000 shares of a $50 stock for a customer, it books as revenue either its commission or the spread between the bid and asked price, which might total $500. Trading an energy contract with the same gross value of $500,000 and a similarly small commission or spread, Enron booked revenue of $500,000—a thousand times what a brokerage firm would record. This accounting treatment enabled Enron to double its reported revenue in 2000, leapfrogging companies with far greater economic impact to call itself the "seventh largest company in America."
Excessive liberties with **mark-to-market accounting** rules constituted yet one more element of Enron's misrepresentation. Under GAAP, it was legitimate to include in current earnings the profits on energy-related contracts and other derivatives that it expected to earn over future periods that could be as long as 20 years. At the end of each quarter, the company estimated the fair value of each open contract to buy or sell electricity or natural gas at a stated price. A subsequent change in the value of a contract would be added to or subtracted from earnings. The potential for abuse arose from the factthat quoted market prices were available only for contracts extending out a few years. No such independent basis for valuation existed for longer-dated contracts. In such cases, Enron was allowed to generate its own valuations, using undisclosed assumptions and pricing models.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS
Naturally, Enron Chief Accounting Officer Richard Causey assured investors that the company's valuation estimates were conservative. He also maintained that the unrealized gains were not heavily concentrated in long-term contracts, where uncertainty regarding valuation was greatest. Analysts nevertheless worried about Enron's disclosure that it booked $747 million in unrealized gains in the second quarter of 2001. That figure exceeded the company's EBITDA of $609 million. (For competitors that did not disclose a comparable number, analysts made quarterly comparisons of the changes in values of net assets from risk management activities.)
President Jeffrey Skilling went further than Causey in discouraging skepticism about the veracity of Enron's reported earnings, venturing into outright intimidation. On a conference call dealing with Enron's earnings, analyst Richard Grubman complained that the company was unique in refusing to include a balance sheet in its earnings release. Skilling replied, "Well thank you very much, we appreciate that . . . [obscene epithet]."⁸
Another hint about Enron's deceptive methods emerged as the company was attempting to save itself through a sale to Dynegy. Floyd Norris of the *New York Times* reported that on October 23, 2001, the day before the company forced out Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow, the Financial Accounting Standards Board's (FASB) Emerging Issues Task Force received a rush question: A hypothetical "Big Energy Corporation" has a natural gas pipeline subsidiary and an energy trading subsidiary. May the company report profits earned in one subsidiary but not report losses incurred at the other?
Just as Enron's income statement concealed the nature of its reported earnings, its balance sheet misrepresented the reality of its financial position. From the outset of Ken Lay's transformation of a trading natural gas utility into a trading powerhouse, massive amounts of debt had been required. Off-balance-sheet entities kept debt off the company's books, based on accounting rules under which Enron could assert that it did not exert control. Experienced credit analysts ignored the accounting technicalities and added back Enron's proportionate share of the off-balance-sheet entities' debt. Still, the off-balance-sheet vehicles, combined with nontransparent disclosures, enabled the company to make itself look less debt-laden than it really was. From heavy reliance on off-balance-sheet financing, it was not a wholly surprising progression to Fastow's lucrative and conflicted partnerships.
Enron also disguised the magnitude of its debt burden by extensive use of a derivatives trade called a "prepaid swap." Unlike an ordinary swap,this transaction required Enron's counterparty to make its payments up-front, while Enron's payments were spread over a multiyear period. The spokesman for one bank that engaged in a prepaid swap noted that the cash flows replicated a floating-rate loan. Therefore, he said, the bank booked the transaction as a loan. Enron, in contrast, treated it as a swap.
Is Fraud Detectable?
207
While Enron grossly misled investors by stretching the rules, a large part of its deception consisted of outright violation of basic accounting standards, with the acquiescence of its auditor. Among the objections that Arthur Andersen agreed to waive on grounds of immateriality was a $172 million addition to shareholders' equity in 2000. The amount represented a note receivable that the company received in exchange for shares of stock that it issued to four special purpose entities. Under GAAP, when a company issues stock, it can record equity only when it receives cash. When Enron revised its financial statements in October 2001, it blithely labeled this violation of GAAP an accounting error.
Another violation of GAAP improperly enabled Enron to keep debt of an affiliate off its balance sheet. In testimony before Congress, Arthur Andersen CEO Berardino said that Enron failed to disclose to its auditor that it had guaranteed half of a 3 percent investment by a financial institution in its special purpose entity, Chewco Investments. Under GAAP, that arrangement meant Enron failed to meet a test for avoiding consolidation of Chewco.
As the Enron scandal continued to generate headlines, reports emerged of grossly fraudulent activities. Employees claimed that in 1998, management took them to an empty trading floor and had them pretend to be salespeople busily engaged in selling energy contracts, all to impress visiting securities analysts. Equally crude was a scheme in which Enron reportedly borrowed $500 million from a bank and bought Treasury bills. A few days later, it sold the Treasury bills and repaid the bank, reporting the proceeds from the meaningless transaction as operating cash flow.

### 分析师们是否察觉到了欺诈行为？

<!--en-->
*Did Analysts Detect the Fraud?*

安然公司倒闭事件备受瞩目，这使得任何能声称自己提前发现欺诈行为的人都能名利双收。投资者肯定会追捧那些被认为有望揭露未来虚假利润的方法论者。然而记录显示，就连仔细审查安然财务报表的人也未能认清欺诈的严重程度。管理层成功隐瞒了最恶劣的行径，直到大多数投资者的资金已经损失殆尽。

<!--en-->
The high profile of Enron's collapse spelled fame and fortune for anyone who could legitimately claim to have spotted the fraud in advance. Investors were sure to flock to anyone with a methodology deemed likely to uncover future faked profits. The record indicates, however, that not even diligent scrutinizers of Enron's financial statements recognized the depths of the fraud. Management successfully concealed the worst of its misdeeds until most of the investors' money had been lost.

诚然，在危机爆发前，安然财务报表中缺乏透明度的问题早已引起注意。2000年9月20日，《华尔街日报》对安然股价年内近乎翻倍至84.875美元、相当于盈利的60倍这一现象表示担忧。文章指出，未实现的非现金收益对安然及其他大型能源交易公司的账面盈利贡献巨大。“可能存在盈利质量方面的问题，”密歇根州立大学会计学教授汤姆·林斯迈尔说，“当然也可能出现剧烈波动，导致如今看似确定的盈利在未来无法兑现。”⁹ 安然公允价值假设的不透明性是一个重大隐患。

<!--en-->
To be sure, the lack of transparency in Enron's financial statements attracted notice well before the debacle. On September 20, 2000, the Wall*Street Journal* raised concerns about the year-to-date near-doubling of Enron's share price to $84.875, some 60 times earnings. The article drew attention to the major contribution of unrealized, noncash gains to the reported earnings of Enron and other companies with large energy-trading units. "There could be a quality-of-earnings issue," said Michigan State University accounting professor Tom Linsmeier. "There certainly might be great volatility that could cause what now looks like a winning, locked-in gain to not arise sometime in the future."⁹ The opacity of Enron's fair value assumptions was a major concern.

“归根结底，他们只是告诉你他们认为的答案，却没说明得出该答案的过程，”商业估值服务公司的分析师斯蒂芬·坎贝尔抱怨道，“这本质上就是在说‘请相信我’。”¹⁰ 深入剖析利润情况

<!--en-->
"Ultimately they're telling you what they think the answer is, but they're not telling you how they got to that answer," Business Valuation Services analyst Stephen Campbell complained. "That is essentially saying 'trust me.'"¹⁰
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

《华尔街日报》对公允价值计量会计问题的详细讨论，引起了空仓卖空者、Kynikos Associates公司的詹姆斯·查诺斯的注意，他察觉到安然股票潜在的下跌风险。以擅长剖析财务报表著称的查诺斯，在后来谈及安然的崩溃时对自己的发现显得颇为谦逊。他表示，直到2001年夏天，他以为不过是盈利被高估而已。“从[安然的]文件中只能看出这一点，”他说。¹¹ 查诺斯认为股价会下跌，但没想到会跌至每股几美分。

<!--en-->
The *Wall Street Journal*'s detailed discussion of the mark-to-market accounting issue alerted short seller James Chanos of Kynikos Associates to the potential downside in Enron's stock. Renowned for his skill as a dissector of financial statements, Chanos was modest about his discoveries when he later discussed Enron's fall. Up until the summer of 2001, Chanos stated, he suspected nothing worse than a case of overstated earnings. "That is all you could tell from [Enron's] documents," he said.¹¹ Chanos thought that the stock price would decline but not that it would plunge to pennies a share.

其他仔细研究财务报表的人也得出了类似结论。例如，2001年5月，Off Wall Street Consulting公司建议卖空当时交易价格约为59美元的安然股票。这家分析公司指出了财务报表中可识别的两个因素：非交易资产的公允价值计量以及与私人合伙企业的关联方交易。

<!--en-->
Others who pored over the financials achieved similar results. For instance, in May 2001, Off Wall Street Consulting recommended a short sale of Enron, then trading around $59. The analytical firm cited two factors identifiable from the financial statements, namely, the mark-to-market on nontraded assets and related-party transactions with private partnerships.

当安然股价跌至26美元，略低于Off Wall Street Consulting设定的30美元目标价时，该公司撤销了卖出建议。从短期来看，这一决策颇为明智，因为股价随后反弹至36美元，才进入最终的崩盘阶段。不过，如果Off Wall Street Consulting知晓安然欺诈的全貌，想必会将目标价定在远低于30美元的水平。

<!--en-->
When Enron fell to $26, a little below Off Wall Street Consulting's $30 target price, the firm removed its sell recommendation. That proved astute in the short run, as the stock rallied to $36 before entering its final death spiral. If Off Wall Street had known the full scope of Enron's deception, however, it presumably would have set a target price well below $30.

2001年8月，法国巴黎银行分析师丹尼尔·斯科托发布了一份题为《压力重重却无路可走》的报告，敦促投资者无论怎样都要抛售安然的股票和债券。十个月前，斯科托曾暂停对包括安然在内所有在加州开展业务的公司的评级。不过此举是基于他担心这些公司在州政府放松管制计划下无法从监管机构处获得递延能源账户的全额补偿。简而言之，斯科托建议在部分最大损失发生前让投资者退出，这一点值得肯定，但他的警告是在2000年8月股价触及90美元峰值之后很久才发出的。

<!--en-->
In August 2001, BNP Paribas analyst Daniel Scotto issued a report titled "All Stressed Up and No Place to Go," which urged investors to sell Enron's stock and bonds no matter what. Ten months earlier, Scotto suspended his ratings on all companies conducting business in California, including Enron. That action, however, was based on his concern that the companies would not be fully compensated by regulators for deferred energy accounts under the state's deregulation plan. In short, Scotto deserved credit for advising investors to bail out before some of the biggest losses, but his warning came long after the $90 peak of August 2000.

另一例所谓提前察觉安然财务造假的情况涉及Cayuga基金，该基金由康奈尔大学约翰逊管理学院的学生协助管理。

<!--en-->
Another purported instance of advance detection of Enron's misreporting involved the Cayuga Fund, managed with the assistance of students at theCornell University Johnson Graduate School of Management.

2000年12月1日，也就是申请破产前一年零一天，该基金以67.38美元的价格清仓了全部安然股票。这使得该基金从低价购入的股票中获得了129%的回报。欺诈行为能否被察觉？主张全额卖出的费迪尔姆·博伊尔和泰格·帕克这两名学生指出，Beneish财务模型显示出盈利操纵的可能性。此外，这些学生分析师还发现能源交易业务产生的盈利缺乏透明度。最后，他们无法理解年报中的附注，他们的教授也认为这些附注晦涩难懂。帕克回忆起投资大师沃伦·巴菲特的一句话：如果你看不懂附注，那是因为管理层不想让你看懂。

<!--en-->
On December 1, 2000, a year and a day before the bankruptcy filing, the fund liquidated its entire Enron position at $67.38. That enabled the fund to book a return of 129 percent on shares it had purchased much more cheaply.
Is Fraud Detectable?
Feidhlim Boyle and Tyger Park, the students who advocated a 100 percent sale, noted that the Beneish financial model indicated a possibility of earnings manipulation. In addition, the student-analysts observed a lack of clarity in the earnings generated by the energy trading business. Finally, they could not understand the footnotes in the annual report, and their professor likewise found them obscure. Park recalled a remark by master investor Warren Buffett that if you cannot understand the footnotes, it is because management does not want you to.

然而，康奈尔大学的学生们并未察觉到安然的欺诈行为。事实上，他们低估了Beneish模型发出的信号的重要性。学生们基于当时的股价建议卖出，但对安然的长期评级仍为中性——如果他们怀疑存在大规模造假行为，肯定不会如此评级。

<!--en-->
The Cornell students did not detect Enron's fraud, however. In fact, they downplayed the importance of the Beneish model's signal. The students recommended a sale based on the stock's prevailing price but rated Enron neutral over the long term, which they surely would not have done if they suspected massive falsification.

McCullough Research出色地发现了Enron财务报表中的不一致之处。

<!--en-->
McCullough Research did an excellent job of spotting inconsistencies in Enron's financials.

Enron Online在截至2001年9月30日的九个月季度财报中声称其名义营收达到5440亿美元（涉及电力和天然气输送），但其在同期向联邦能源监管委员会提交的文件却显示，能源购销额仅为6.93亿美元。McCullough还发现，报告的盈利减去股息后的数额与留存收益的增加额之间存在差异。此外，该公司指出，Enron所报告的现金流中包含了必须日后退还给客户的加州押金；扣除该项后，现金流实际上为负值。这些都是扎实的财务报表分析成果，但相关问题直到Enron申请破产前一个月才浮出水面。

<!--en-->
Enron Online's quarterly earnings report for the nine months ending September 30, 2001, claimed $544 billion of notional revenue (representing electricity and gas transmitted), yet its Federal Energy Regulatory Commission filing for the same period showed only $693 million of energy purchases and sales. McCullough also found a discrepancy between reported earnings less dividends and additions to retained earnings. Finally, the firm noted that Enron's reported cash flow included customer deposits in California that had to be repaid at a later point. Net of that item, cash flow was negative. This was all solid financial statement analysis, but the problems came to light only in the month before Enron's bankruptcy filing.

最后，Egan-Jones评级公司因比穆迪和标准普尔等大型竞争对手更快地将Enron债券评级下调至投机级而广受认可。不过，Egan-Jones给出的BB级评级仅意味着该债券在一年内违约的概率约为1%。而且，这一评级下调发生在Enron申请破产前仅37天，尽管该公司的虚假陈述行为至少可追溯至1997年。

<!--en-->
Finally, Egan-Jones Ratings Company gained widespread recognition for being swifter to downgrade Enron's bonds to speculative grade than larger competitors such as Moody's and Standard & Poor's. The BB rating to which Egan-Jones lowered the debt, however, connoted only about a 1 percent probability of default within one year. Moreover, the downgrade occurred just 37 days before Enron filed for bankruptcy, although the company's misrepresentations dated back to at least 1997.

Egan-Jones因其严谨的分析而值得称赞，但与其他机构一样，它也无法真正宣称自己发现了足以摧毁该公司的欺诈行为。

<!--en-->
Egan-Jones deserved credit for its analytical rigor, but like the others, it cannot truly claim that it unearthed a fraud deep enough to destroy the company.

### 给财务分析师的启示

<!--en-->
*Lessons for Financial Analysts*

Enron能够长期维持其欺诈行为，这警示我们财务报表分析的局限性。审计师未能制止对公认会计原则的公然滥用，给分析师带来了巨大障碍。除此之外，该公司还竭力使其财务报告难以理解。“他们对自己如何赚钱并不愿多说，”Sanders, Morris & Harris公司的研究主管约翰·奥尔森说道，“我认识的分析师中，没一个能真正深入分析Enron的财务状况。”¹² 对利润的深入剖析

<!--en-->
Enron's success in sustaining its fraud over a long period represents a cautionary tale of the limitations of financial statement analysis. The auditors'failure to curb flagrant abuses of GAAP posed a huge obstacle to analysts. On top of that, the company did its best to make its financial reports unfathomable. “They’re not very forthcoming about how they make their money,” said John Olson, who headed research at Sanders, Morris & Harris. “I don’t know an analyst worth his salt who can seriously analyze Enron.”¹²
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

在此类案例中，即便对数字进行最细致的调查，也可能在公司倒闭前无法找到确凿证据。因此，当Beneish模型等工具显示出强烈的财务操纵迹象，同时伴随不透明的财务报告时，分析师应格外警惕。市场上有许多值得投资的公司，无需将资本冒险投入那些经不起推敲的企业。

<!--en-->
In a case of this sort, the most diligent investigation of the numbers may not turn up a smoking gun before the company collapses. Accordingly, analysts should be especially wary when a strong likelihood of financial manipulation, as indicated by tools such as the Beneish model, coincides with nontransparent financial reporting. There are many companies to invest in without risking capital on those that fail the smell test.

### HealthSouth的艰难历程

<!--en-->
*HEALTHSOUTH’S EXCRUCIATING ORDEAL*

在担任理疗师以及德克萨斯州一家小型医院连锁店的初级管理人员之后，30岁的理查德·斯克鲁希（发音为“SCROO-shee”）于1984年创立了HealthSouth。由于联邦医疗保险对老年人康复治疗的慷慨报销政策，这家企业取得了巨大成功。在二十年间，斯克鲁希将这家位于阿拉巴马州伯明翰的公司发展成为美国规模最大的康复医院连锁机构，拥有1500家医院。

<!--en-->
After working as a physical therapist and a junior executive of a small Texas hospital chain, 30-year-old Richard Scrushy (pronounced “SCROO-shee”) founded HealthSouth in 1984. The business proved highly successful, thanks in large measure to a generous Medicare reimbursement policy for physical rehabilitation of an aging population keen on sports and exercise. Over two decades, Scrushy built the Birmingham, Alabama, company into the largest chain of its kind in the United States, with 1,500 rehabilitation hospitals.

在此过程中，斯克鲁希积累了巨额财富，被誉为“伯明翰的唐纳德·特朗普”。他购置了七架商务喷气机，并经常亲自驾驶。几家受益于HealthSouth慷慨捐助的慈善机构还以斯克鲁希的名字命名建筑。他还作为自己乡村音乐乐队的主唱而备受瞩目。著名运动员约翰·斯莫尔茨和丹·马里诺曾被邀请在HealthSouth赞助的儿童巡回演出中发言。

<!--en-->
In the process, Scrushy amassed immense wealth, becoming known as the Donald Trump of Birmingham. He acquired seven corporate jets, which he frequently piloted. Several philanthropies that benefited from HealthSouth’s generosity named buildings after Scrushy. He also captured attention as the lead singer of his own country music band. Famed athletes John Smoltz and Dan Marino were hired to speak at a children’s road show sponsored by HealthSouth.

斯克鲁希的崛起一帆风顺，直到1997年国会大幅削减了对医院的联邦医疗保险报销额度。在接下来的两年里，HealthSouth的营业利润率和盈利水平急剧下滑。斯克鲁希通过削减薪资以及出售无利可图的业务来应对这一局面。

<!--en-->
Scrushy’s ascent proceeded without a hitch until 1997, when Congress sharply cut back Medicare reimbursements to hospitals. During the next two years, HealthSouth’s operating margins and profits plummeted. Scrushy responded by slashing salaries and divesting unprofitable sidelines.

当这些措施仍无法扭转盈利下滑势头时，他进一步收紧运营，将平均患者住院时间从21.5天缩短至17.5天。即便如此，该公司仍难以达到华尔街证券分析师设定的高额盈利预期。

<!--en-->
When those measures failed to revive profits, he tightened operations, cutting average patient’s stays from 21.5 to 17.5 days. Still, the company struggled to meet Wall Street securities analysts’ lofty earnings estimates.

最终，HealthSouth只是靠歪曲事实才勉强达到分析师的预期。2003年3月19日，美国证券交易委员会指控HealthSouth自1999年以来虚报了14亿美元的盈利。后来检察官将这一数字上调至近25亿美元。丑闻曝光后新聘请的审计机构普华永道最终又追加了5亿美元的错误商誉及其他收购相关项目账目，以及1994年至1999年间因“激进会计手段”而产生的8亿至16亿美元虚增利润。2005年，HealthSouth重新申报了2001–2002年度的财务结果，将营收减少了约15亿美元，并将原先报告的4.81亿美元盈利修正为5.55亿美元亏损。欺诈行为能否被察觉？根据SEC的指控，HealthSouth的造假行为始于1986年公司上市之后。证券监管机构还称，董事长兼首席执行官斯克鲁希通过出售至少780万股自家股票，并凭借虚假利润获得650万美元奖金，从中谋取了个人利益。

<!--en-->
In the end, HealthSouth met the analysts’ expectations only by stretching the truth. On March 19, 2003, the Securities and Exchange Commission charged that HealthSouth had overstated earnings by $1.4 billion since 1999. Prosecutors later raised the figure to nearly $2.5 billion. PriceWaterhouseCoopers, the new auditor chosen after the scandal broke, eventually added to this total $500 million in incorrect accounting for goodwill and other acquisition-related items in the period 1994 through 1999,plus $800 million to $1.6 billion in “aggressive accounting” from 1992 to March 2003. In 2005, HealthSouth restated its results for 2001–2002, reducing revenue by about $1.5 billion and changing its originally reported $481 million of earnings for the two years to $555 million of losses.
Is Fraud Detectable?
According to the SEC’s complaint, HealthSouth’s falsification began shortly after the company went public in 1986. The securities regulator also claimed that Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Scrushy had personally profited from the fraud by selling at least 7.8 million of his own shares and by receiving a $6.5 million bonus based on the false profits.

在SEC爆出丑闻后，斯克鲁希被停职，不久便遭解雇；他是在针对内幕交易指控进行的六个月调查结束后，才刚刚重返CEO职位。

<!--en-->
Scrushy, who was placed on leave following the SEC bombshell and fired soon thereafter, had only recently returned to his CEO post after a six-month investigation of insider trading allegations.

针对新指控，他的律师评论道：“斯克鲁希先生对政府过去两天采取的出乎意料的行动感到震惊和意外。”¹³即便在公司历史上曾受雇于斯克鲁希的五位首席财务官都承认参与了欺诈行为，辩护团队仍坚称斯克鲁希对财务报表操纵并不知情。“我不是会计师，”被告在随后与此相关的民事审判中如此陈述。

<!--en-->
Regarding the new charges, his lawyers commented, “Mr. Scrushy was shocked and surprised at the unexpected actions taken by the government over the past two days.”¹³ Even after all five chief financial officers who worked under Scrushy during the company’s history confessed to participating in the fraud, the defense team maintained that Scrushy was unaware of the financial statement manipulation. “I’m not an accountant,” the defendant stated in a later civil trial related to the allegations.

无论出现何种证据，斯克鲁希始终一味否认，这成为HealthSouth事件中的一贯基调。他在《60分钟》电视节目采访中否认自己负有任何责任；但在国会听证会上被要求重申其清白声明时，他却援引第五修正案赋予的免于自证其罪的权利。后来，在欺诈审判期间，斯克鲁希表示如果被判无罪，他将试图重新担任HealthSouth的首席执行官，尽管美国证券交易委员会对他仍有未决的执法行动。

<!--en-->
Flat denial by Scrushy, regardless of the evidence that emerged, was a consistent theme as the HealthSouth story unfolded. Scrushy disavowed any culpability in an interview on the *60 Minutes* network television program, but when asked to repeat his declaration of innocence in a congressional hearing, he invoked his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination. Later, during his trial for fraud, Scrushy said that if acquitted, he would try to regain his position as chief executive officer of HealthSouth, notwithstanding a Securities and Exchange Commission enforcement action pending against him.

一位曾为斯克鲁希妻子担任私人购物员的女性这样评价这对夫妇：“他们的生活简直完全脱离现实。”¹⁴ 更巧的是，一本吹捧HealthSouth惊人成功之书恰好在SEC提出指控前便已上市。《HealthSouth的故事》由杰弗里·L·罗登格伦撰写，出版方为专门从事企业史编写的Write Stuff Syndicate公司。犹他州参议员奥林·哈奇与爱荷华州参议员汤姆·哈金为该书撰写了赞赏性前言，他们当时并未察觉即将到来的风暴。（这两位参议员还参加了斯克鲁希1997年的婚礼，哈奇甚至为婚礼创作了一首歌。）

<!--en-->
A woman who worked as a personal shopper for Scrushy’s wife said of the couple, “Their life was about as uninhibited by reality as one could imagine.”¹⁴
In a monumental case of unfortunate timing, a book hailing HealthSouth’s phenomenal success reached bookstores shortly before the SEC filed its allegations. *The Story of HealthSouth*, by Jeffrey L. Rodengren, was published by Write Stuff Syndicate, a firm specializing in corporate histories. Senators Orrin Hatch of Utah and Tom Harkin of Iowa had contributed an admiring foreword, unaware of the impending storm. (The two senators also participated in Scrushy’s 1997 wedding, with Hatch writing a song for the occasion.)

### 虚假陈述的手法

<!--en-->
*Methods of Misrepresentation*

据HealthSouth举报人韦斯顿·L·史密斯称，斯克鲁希经常召集所谓的“家庭会议”，指示公司高管夸大上报的盈利数据以符合证券分析师的预测。这些虚假会计分录被称为“垃圾账”。¹⁵史密斯对四项联邦刑事指控认罪，他曾在2002年8月前担任HealthSouth的首席财务官，之后转任住院业务主管。诉状指出，当HealthSouth的官员和会计师敦促斯克鲁希停止虚增利润时，他的回应实际上是：“除非我先卖掉我的股票。”¹⁶ 深入剖析利润数据

<!--en-->
According to HealthSouth whistleblower Weston L. Smith, Scrushy regularly convened so-called family meetings in which he directed companyexecutives to inflate reported earnings to meet securities analysts' estimates. The fake accounting entries were called “dirt.”¹⁵ Smith, who pleaded guilty to four federal criminal charges, had been HealthSouth's chief financial officer until August 2002, before switching to head of inpatient operations. The complaint stated that when HealthSouth officials and accountants urged Scrushy to cease inflating profits, he replied, in effect, “Not until I sell my stock.”¹⁶
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

史密斯承认的虚假申报中包括一份声称提交给SEC的财务报表属实的证明。此举违反了2002年在安然和世通公司发生大规模财务报告欺诈后颁布的《萨班斯-奥克斯利法案》。该法案要求首席财务官和首席执行官对财务报表的准确性予以担保，这为检察官打击造假者提供了强大武器；但HealthSouth的欺诈行为却粉碎了人们认为这项严厉的新法律能彻底杜绝财务错报的想法。

<!--en-->
Among the false filings Smith admitted to was a certification that financial statements sent to the SEC were true. Doing so was a violation of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act, enacted in 2002 following massive financial reporting frauds at Enron and WorldCom. The Sarbox provision requiring CFOs and CEOs to attest to the accuracy of financial statements gave prosecutors a powerful weapon to wield against falsifiers, but HealthSouth's fraud dispelled any notion that the tough new law would end financial misreporting altogether.

HealthSouth通过低估治疗成本与患者保险赔付额之间的差额来夸大其盈利。

<!--en-->
HealthSouth exaggerated its earnings by understating the gap between the cost of a treatment and the amount that the patient's insurance would cover.

这使得该公司能够拨备一笔少得离谱的坏账准备金。每次该公司以这种方式虚增净营收和利润时，都会相应调整资产负债表，从而抬高固定资产（如房产、厂房及设备）的价值。另一位承认参与会计欺诈的HealthSouth高管称，公司会超额计提某些被内部称为“socks”的准备金账户金额，随后再将这些金额“转入”营收中。¹⁷为了逃避监管，HealthSouth并未进行大规模、集中的账目调整，而是将其分散到存货、无形资产以及房产、厂房及设备（PP&E）等多个类别中。由于审计人员只有在固定资产增加额超过一定金额时才会提出质疑，公司管理层特意确保不超出这一阈值。

<!--en-->
That enabled the company to set aside an unrealistically small allowance for uncollectible accounts. Each time the company overstated its net revenue and earnings in this way, it made a corresponding balance sheet adjustment, raising the value of an asset such as property, plant, and equipment. Another HealthSouth executive who pleaded guilty to participating in accounting fraud said the company overbooked certain reserve accounts referred to internally as “socks,” then later “bled them out” into revenue.¹⁷
To avoid detection, HealthSouth made no large, concentrated adjustments but instead spread them over several different categories, including inventory, intangible assets, and property, plant, and equipment (PP&E). Knowing that the auditors would question an addition to fixed assets only if it was greater than a certain dollar amount, the company officials were careful not to exceed that threshold.

到2002年中期，通过这种逐步操作的方式，该公司成功将PP&E价值虚增了50%以上。雷曼兄弟公司的会计分析师罗伯特·威伦后来评论道：“他们很聪明，意识到只要增幅不大，审计人员就不会偏离他们通常采用的抽样审查方式。”¹⁸如果审计人员确实对某项账目提出质疑，据说HealthSouth的高管们会伪造文件来为该项账目辩护。

<!--en-->
By mid-2002, using this little-by-little approach, the company managed to overstate its PP&E by more than 50 percent. Lehman Brothers accounting analyst Robert Willens later commented, “They were smart enough to realize that, as long as the increases weren’t dramatic, the auditors were not going to deviate from the sampling approach they typically take.”¹⁸ If the auditors did question an accounting entry, HealthSouth executives reportedly created a phony document to validate the item.

HealthSouth还通过不注销那些几乎无法收回的应收账款来抬高利润。这种惯用的伎俩导致了内部调查所发现的5亿美元可疑账目中的大部分；这一数字不包括普华永道所查出的明显造假行为。此外，公司在出售已贬值的资产时也不确认损失。还有一次，财务报表竟将带有HealthSouth标志的四肢支架列为存货，尽管公司并不会因在医疗中心免费发放这些产品而产生任何营收。欺诈行为能被察觉吗？证券持有者为HealthSouth的财务操纵付出了沉重代价。2003年3月19日SEC首次指控其存在财务报告违规行为后，HealthSouth便失去了12.5亿美元的信贷额度。由于一笔3.54亿美元的可转换债券将在一周多后到期，该公司似乎很难在不申请破产的情况下筹集新贷款来偿还债务。（作为破产后的债权人，银行将优先索取HealthSouth的资产。）据KDP投资顾问公司的普雷米拉·彼得斯称，该公司总负债达35亿美元，但按其现金流计算，其实际价值仅为24亿美元。¹⁹由于公司证券交易于3月19日被暂停，股东和债券持有人起初无法脱身。

<!--en-->
HealthSouth also propped up profits by failing to write off receivables with little chance of being collected. That classic dodge accounted for most of the $500 million of questionable accounting uncovered by an internal investigation, separate from PriceWaterhouseCoopers' study of outright falsification. In addition, the company did not recognize losses when it soldassets that had declined in value. Also, in one instance, the financial statements treated arm and leg braces bearing the HealthSouth logo as inventory, even though the company would generate no revenue from handing them out free at its medical centers.
Is Fraud Detectable?
Securities holders paid a heavy price for HealthSouth's financial hankypanky. Following the SEC's initial accusation of financial reporting violations on March 19, 2003, HealthSouth lost access to a $1.25 billion line of credit. With a $354 million convertible bond coming due in a little over a week, it appeared doubtful that the company could arrange a new loan to cover the debt maturity without first filing for bankruptcy. (As postbankruptcy lenders, the banks would get first claim on HealthSouth's assets.) According to Premila Peters of KDP Investment Advisors, the company owed $3.5 billion in total, but based on its cash flow, its value was only $2.4 billion.¹⁹
Shareholders and bondholders were initially trapped in their positions because trading in the company's securities was suspended on March 19.

（误读暂停交易的债券市场参与者在3月20日进行了几笔交易，但SEC随后取消了这些交易。）当公司债务交易于3月21日恢复时，可转换次级债券的收盘价跌至20，而本周早些时候曾高达98。HealthSouth的高级债券价格也从80多美元跌至约44美元。对债券持有人而言，更糟的消息是银行阻止公司按计划在4月1日偿还可转换债券的本金。至于股票，交易以场外交易方式恢复，股价在3月底收于8.5美分，而交易暂停前股价还为3.91美元。

<!--en-->
(Bond market participants who misinterpreted the suspension made a few trades on March 20, but the SEC nullified those transactions.) When trading in the company debt resumed on March 21, the convertible **subordinated** bonds closed at 20, down from as high as 98 earlier in the week. HealthSouth's senior bonds were down from the mid-80s to about 44. Additional bad news for bondholders arrived as bankers blocked the company from making the April 1 principal repayment on the convertible bonds. As for the stock, trading resumed on an over-the-counter basis, and the shares ended March at 8.5 cents, down from $3.91 before the trading halt.

### 人民诉斯克鲁希案

<!--en-->
*The People versus Scrushy*

截至2003年10月15日，共有15名HealthSouth高管承认参与了财务造假。其中几人作证称斯克鲁希知晓或主导了此次会计欺诈行为。“多米诺骨牌正在倒下，而且倒得很快，”一名参与调查的人员说，“这是调查人员的梦想。”²⁰前SEC律师克里斯托弗·贝贝尔补充道：“斯克鲁希的前景十分黯淡。”²¹令斯克鲁希的法律困境雪上加霜的是，联邦检察官于2003年7月披露，他们发现了有关税务欺诈、妨碍司法、恐吓证人、洗钱以及公共腐败的证据。同时还有消息称，联邦调查局正在调查威廉·马西二世的自杀事件；马西负责管理斯克鲁希私人企业的控股公司。马西自杀前两个月曾匆忙前往巴哈马群岛出差。FBI怀疑斯克鲁希设立离岸银行账户是为了逃税。更深入地审视利润问题

<!--en-->
By October 15, 2003, a total of 15 HealthSouth executives had pleaded guilty to involvement in fraudulent reporting. Several had testified that Scrushy knew about or directed the accounting fraud. “The dominoes are falling, and they are falling fast,” said one person involved in the investigation. “It’s an investigator’s dream.”²⁰ Former SEC attorney Christopher Bebel added, “Scrushy’s prospects look bleak.”²¹
Compounding Scrushy's legal problems, federal prosecutors disclosed in July 2003 that they had uncovered evidence of tax fraud, obstruction of justice, witness intimidation, money laundering, and public corruption. It also emerged that the Federal Bureau of Investigation was looking into the suicide of William Massey Jr., who managed an umbrella company for Scrushy's personal businesses. Two months before taking his own life, Massey made a hasty business trip to the Bahamas. The FBI suspected Scrushy of setting up offshore bank accounts as a tax dodge.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

2003年11月4日，联邦检察官以85项与虚假会计计划相关的指控起诉理查德·斯克鲁希，这些指控包括共谋、证券欺诈、邮件及电信欺诈以及洗钱。次年又新增了伪证罪和妨碍司法公正罪，修订后的起诉书将指控总数合并为58项。

<!--en-->
On November 4, 2003, federal prosecutors charged Richard Scrushy with 85 charges related to a false accounting scheme, including conspiracy, securities fraud, mail and wire fraud, and money laundering. Perjury and obstruction of justice were added the following year, when a revised indictment consolidated the charges into a total of 58.

2003年的起诉书使斯克鲁希成为首位被控违反《萨班斯-奥克斯利法案》的首席执行官，因为他签署了财务报表。他对所有指控均拒不认罪，声称尽管自己以事无巨细的管理风格著称，却对这起大规模欺诈行为毫不知情。尽管在认罪的两名HealthSouth高管中，有15人指认了他，但斯克鲁希的律师仍对检方证据不屑一顾。“他们没什么证据，”他说，“他们的主要论点很薄弱。”²² 在这场看似艰难的抗辩中，斯克鲁希利用了检方自信地决定不在伯明翰更换审判地点的有利条件——他在当地被视为成功的本地人。斯克鲁希进一步利用这一优势，在伯明翰的一家电视台主持了一档新电视节目。他声称此举并非为了为自己辩护，而是保留反驳“明显错误”陈述的权利。²³ 该节目在Word of Truth Productions录制，该机构隶属于一所黑人教会的外展事工部门，斯克鲁希于2003年加入了该教会。

<!--en-->
The 2003 indictment made Scrushy the first CEO accused of violating the Sarbanes-Oxley Act because he had signed the financial statements. He pleaded not guilty to all charges, claiming that notwithstanding his reputation as a micromanager, he was oblivious to the massive fraud. Even though several of the 15 HealthSouth executives who pleaded guilty had implicated him, Scrushy's attorney brushed off the prosecutors' evidence. "They don't have much," he said. "Their primary case is weak."²²
In his seemingly uphill battle to beat the rap, Scrushy capitalized on the confident prosecutors' decision not to seek a change in venue from Birmingham, where he was admired as a local boy who made good. Scrushy pushed this advantage by hosting a new television series on a Birmingham station. He claimed that the purpose was not to present his own side of the case against him, but he reserved the right to counter "blatantly wrong" statements.²³ The program was taped at Word of Truth Productions, part of the outreach ministry of a predominantly black church that Scrushy joined in 2003.

他加入教会以及参与电视节目的举动引发了外界猜测：他希望在这座非裔美国人占人口73%的城市中赢得陪审团的同情。

<!--en-->
Both his membership in the congregation and the TV show raised speculation that he hoped to win sympathy from jurors in a city where African Americans constituted 73 percent of the population.

斯克鲁希打出了宗教牌，他成为了一名无宗派传教士，并在几家当地教堂担任客座牧师。斯克鲁希的一位前商业伙伴称，他从未在HealthSouth看到过黑人高管，并补充道：“我第一次听到宗教与理查德·斯克鲁希被提及在同一句话中，是在读到他前往Guiding Light Church的消息时。”²⁴ 另有说法称，斯克鲁希年轻时曾深陷基督教信仰，但后来逐渐疏远。面对批评，斯克鲁希始终坚称：“我对所受指控纯属无辜，且蒙主赐福，有能力应对指控我的人。”²⁵ 审判期间，斯克鲁希及其律师坚称他们与另一档在当地播出的节目《The Scrushy Trial with Nikki Preede》无关。该节目由斯克鲁希的女婿拥有的电视台播出，其主持人曾为斯克鲁希的律师事务所从事公关工作。一位前斯克鲁希律师是该节目的常客评论员，而电视台总经理曾在斯克鲁希的乡村西部乐队中弹奏吉他和提琴。法官不得不指示陪审团不要观看任何涉及斯克鲁希和HealthSouth的电视节目。

<!--en-->
Scrushy played the religion card by becoming a nondenominational preacher and delivering guest sermons at several local churches. A former business associate of Scrushy's commented that he had never observed any black executives at HealthSouth and added, "The first time I heard religion and Richard Scrushy mentioned in the same sentence was when I read about him going to Guiding Light Church."²⁴ According to other accounts, Scrushy was deeply involved in Christianity as a youth but later drifted away. Scrushy remained steadfast in the face of criticism: "I am innocent of the accusations against me," he said, "and have been blessed by the Lord in having the resources to confront my accusers."²⁵
During the trial, Scrushy and his lawyers insisted they had nothing to do with another locally telecast program, *The Scrushy Trial with Nikki Preede*. This program aired on a station owned by Scrushy's son-in-law, and its host had done public relations work for Scrushy's law firm. A former Scrushy attorney was a frequent commentator on the show, and the station's general manager had played guitar and fiddle in Scrushy's country-western band. The judge felt obliged to instruct the jury not to watch any television programs dealing with Scrushy and HealthSouth.

欺诈行为能被察觉吗？斯克鲁希的辩护还采用了更传统的策略，比如攻击某位政府证人存在婚外情。他的律师着重强调那些认罪并作证指控斯克鲁希的HealthSouth高管所受到的轻判。或许同样奏效的是，首席辩护律师佩戴了一条印有老鼠吃奶酪图案的领带出庭，这与他对关键控方证人品格的描述相呼应。在检察官看来，斯克鲁希还得益于法官在冗长的会计相关证词期间开玩笑的习惯，认为这可能致使部分陪审团对庭审的重视程度不够。

<!--en-->
Is Fraud Detectable?
Scrushy's defense also employed more conventional tactics, such as attacking one government witness for marital infidelity. His lawyers hammered at the light sentences meted out to HealthSouth executives who confessed and testified against Scrushy. Perhaps effective as well was the lead defense attorney's appearance in a necktie decorated with an image of rats eating cheese, echoing his description of a key prosecution witness's character. In the prosecutors' view, Scrushy benefited as well from the judge's habit of cracking jokes during long stretches of accounting-related testimony, arguing that it may have caused some jurors to take the proceedings less seriously than they ought.

无论如何，2005年6月28日，理查德·斯克鲁希被裁定所有指控不成立。“原因在于审判地点，”前联邦检察官乔治·B·纽豪斯二世说道。²⁶ 他与多位法律专家观点一致，认为如果检察官在伯明翰以外的地区审理此案，被告早就会被定罪。

<!--en-->
In any event, on June 28, 2005, Richard Scrushy was acquitted of all charges. "It was venue," said former federal prosecutor George B. Newhouse Jr.²⁶ He echoed a number of legal experts who asserted that the defendant would have been convicted had prosecutors tried him anyplace other than Birmingham.

然而，斯克鲁希的无罪判决并未结束他的法律麻烦。四个月后，他因行贿前阿拉巴马州州长、以使其任命自己进入负责审批医院建设的州委员会而被起诉。

<!--en-->
Scrushy's acquittal did not end his legal troubles, however. Four months later, he was indicted on charges of bribing the former governor of Alabama to appoint him to the state board responsible for approving hospital construction.

此外，他还面临因会计欺诈引发的股东诉讼和美国证监会（SEC）的民事指控。最终，斯克鲁希在未承认有罪的情况下与SEC达成和解，同意放弃7750万美元的股票收益，并支付350万美元罚款。股东诉讼中的法官则判令他赔偿28亿美元。最后，斯克鲁希被判犯有行贿罪，被判处10年零6个月监禁。法官驳回了他的辩解——即若入狱，他作为牧师的良好工作将会受到影响。

<!--en-->
In addition, he faced a shareholder suit and SEC civil charges arising from the accounting fraud. Scrushy eventually settled the SEC case without admitting guilt, agreeing to give up $77.5 million in stock gains and pay a $3.5 million penalty. The judge in the shareholder suit ordered him to pay $2.8 billion. Finally, Scrushy was convicted of the bribery charge and sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison. The judge rejected his plea that if he were incarcerated, his good work as a minister would suffer.

### HealthSouth的审计失败

<!--en-->
*Audit Failure at HealthSouth*

HealthSouth的审计机构安永会计师事务所最令人失望的表现，就是未能对现金余额的突然大幅增加提出质疑。美国司法部称，该公司2002年第二季度报告的5.45亿美元现金余额较上一季度增长了50%以上，但实际数额被高估了超过3亿美元。雷曼兄弟公司的会计分析师威伦斯指出，审计人员本应通过抽样方式核实现金余额。“这是最容易审计的项目之一，但结果却令人惊讶，”威伦斯说，“不过抽样检查可能让他们误以为一切正常。”²⁷其他警示信号显然也被忽视了。2002年3月离开HealthSouth会计部门的簿记员迈克尔·维恩斯曾向安永警告存在会计欺诈行为，但该审计公司却认定该公司的会计处理是合法的。此外，一位HealthSouth的内部审计师告诉安永，她无法全面查阅公司的账簿。据另一位合伙人透露，独立审计师对此并未采取任何行动。更仔细地审视利润情况

<!--en-->
The most dismaying aspect of the performance of HealthSouth's auditor, Ernst & Young, was its failure to challenge a sudden, large increase in cash. The Justice Department claimed that the company's reported $545 million **cash balance** in 2002's second quarter, a jump of more than 50 percent from the preceding quarter, was overstated by more than $300 million. Lehman Brothers accounting analyst Willens noted that auditors were supposed to confirm cash balances by obtaining a sample. "It's one of the easiest things to audit and it does seem amazing," said Willens. "But a sample may have led them to conclude that everything was in order."²⁷
Other red flags apparently were ignored. Michael Vines, a bookkeeper who left HealthSouth's accounting department in March 2002, warned Ernst & Young about accounting fraud, but the auditing firm concluded that the company's accounting was legitimate. Additionally, a HealthSouth internal auditor told Ernst & Young that she could not get full access to thecompany's books. The independent auditor took no action in response to that disturbing statement, according to another partner.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

在该领域的专家看来，HealthSouth的内部制衡机制也出现了崩溃。

<!--en-->
In the view of experts in the field, internal checks and balances also broke down at HealthSouth.

董事会的审计委员会在2001年仅召开了一次会议，这一次数比美国证监会建议的最低次数少了三次。这本应提醒公司的独立审计师：公司的内部控制缺乏有效监督，可能存在不可靠性。哥伦比亚大学会计学教授伊扎克·沙拉夫认为，审计委员会如此不频繁地开会，意味着它“实际上形同虚设”。²⁸还有其他理由让人怀疑HealthSouth的董事会是否足够独立以履行其监督职责。“HealthSouth董事会的失职程度简直堪称严重疏忽，”公司治理中心主任保罗·拉皮德斯断言。²⁹尤其令人担忧的是董事们与HealthSouth及斯卡希之间的交易往来：一名董事每年从公司领取25万美元的咨询费；另一名董事获得了价值560万美元的合同，负责为HealthSouth建造的医院安装玻璃；还有一名董事与斯卡希共同购买了一处价值39.5万美元的度假房产。六名董事以及第七名董事的妻子参与了一项在线医疗用品业务（有时通过关联实体进行），而HealthSouth向该业务输送了超过1.74亿美元的业务量。

<!--en-->
The board's audit committee met only once during 2001, three times less than the minimum recommended by the SEC. That should have alerted the company's independent auditor that the company's internal controls were not adequately supervised and might be unreliable. Such infrequent convening of the audit committee meant it was "nonexistent, for all practical purposes," according to Columbia University accounting professor Itzhak Sharav.²⁸
Other reasons existed for questioning whether HealthSouth's board was sufficiently independent to fulfill its watchdog responsibilities. "There has been so much sleeping on the job at the HealthSouth board that it could rise to gross negligence," asserted Paul Lapides, head of the Corporate Governance Center.²⁹ Particularly troubling were directors' transactions with HealthSouth and Scrushy. One director earned $250,000 a year in consulting fees from the company, and another received a $5.6 million contract to install glass at a hospital constructed by HealthSouth. Another director bought a $395,000 resort property in conjunction with Scrushy. Six directors and a seventh's wife were participants (in some instances through related entities) in an online medical supply venture to which HealthSouth directed more than $174 million in business.

此外，多年来，同一个董事会委员会同时负责企业审计和薪酬管理。公司治理专家在其他大型公司中找不到类似的安排，考虑到审计失败恰恰导致了斯卡希薪酬的增加，这种安排尤为成问题。

<!--en-->
Moreover, for several years, a single board committee oversaw both corporate audit and compensation. Corporate governance experts could find no parallel at another major company for this arrangement, which was especially problematic considering that the audit failure fattened Scrushy's pay package.

## 早期预警信号

<!--en-->
*Early Warning Signs*

1999年至2000年间，当斯卡希引入类似流水线式的流程以加快患者流转速度时，营业利润激增了143%，而销售额仅增长了3%。调查人员后来认定，这种不合常理的巨大差距源于虚构的利润数字。财务报表使用者应对此类收入与利润之间的巨大差异保持警惕。

<!--en-->
In 1999–2000, when Scrushy instituted an assembly-line-like process to move patients through the system more swiftly, operating earnings skyrocketed by 143 percent. Sales, however, inched up by just 3 percent. Investigators later concluded that this implausibly large gap was a product of fabricated profit numbers. Users of financial statements should be skeptical of such wide disparities between changes in revenue and profit.

负面意外也可能是一种警示信号，正如HealthSouth所展示的那样。美国证监会指控称，2002年8月27日斯卡希向投资者宣称医疗保险报销政策的变化将使公司每年损失1.75亿美元，但他实际夸大了真实影响约1.5亿美元。据美国证监会称，其他HealthSouth高管担心，根据新实施的《萨班斯-奥克斯利法案》，他们因需对虚假财务报表签字认证而可能面临监禁。这些高管声称，为了降低证券分析师的预期、从而减轻造假压力，他们说服斯卡希停止财务造假，并向分析师发布虚假的利润预警。结果，HealthSouth的股价在一天之内暴跌44%。欺诈行为能否被察觉？在股价暴跌前三个月，斯卡希大量抛售股票的行为引起了美国证监会对内幕交易的怀疑。这一线索最终指向了意想不到的财务报告欺诈方向。对财务报表使用者而言，教训是：那些在其他方面显得不可信的管理层很可能也在篡改账目。

<!--en-->
Negative surprises can also be a warning sign, as HealthSouth demonstrated. The SEC complaint claimed that when Scrushy told investors on August 27, 2002, that a change in Medicare reimbursements would cost the company $175 million annually, he was overstating the true impact by about $150 million. According to the SEC, other HealthSouth executives were worried that under the newly enacted Sarbanes-Oxley Act, therequirement to certify the company's false financial statements meant they might face prison sentences. The executives claimed that to lower security analysts' expectations and thereby relieve the pressure to falsify, they persuaded Scrushy to abandon the reporting fraud and give securities analysts a bogus profit warning. In response, HealthSouth's stock plunged 44 percent in a single day.
Is Fraud Detectable?
A large stock sale by Scrushy three months before that precipitous drop aroused the SEC's suspicions of insider trading. That trail ultimately led in the unexpected direction of financial reporting fraud. For users of financial statements, the lesson is that a management that appears untrustworthy on other grounds may be tampering with the books as well.

### 牛奶及其他流动资产

<!--en-->
*MILK AND OTHER LIQUID ASSETS*

帕玛拉特公司从1961年开始崛起，最终成为意大利最大的食品生产商以及全球最大的乳制品企业。当时，卡利斯托·坦齐继承了一家火腿和萨拉米香肠企业。两年后，坦齐创立了帕玛拉特牛奶品牌。他通过引进将牛奶包装在独特的长方形纸盒中、且无需冷藏即可保存长达六个月的技术，将其打造为行业领导者。到1970年，该品牌在国际上被誉为“冠军之奶”，公司也开始赞助滑雪赛事。坦齐随后将产品线扩展到甜点、酱料、饼干和果汁领域，并将企业赞助范围扩大至赛车运动和足球。20世纪90年代，帕玛拉特上市，并在意大利、美国、拉丁美洲和亚洲展开一系列收购活动。该公司知名的品牌包括Archway饼干、Pomi意大利面酱和Sunnydale Farms牛奶。在此过程中，坦齐成为政治竞选的重要捐助者，并获颁意大利国家骑士勋章。

<!--en-->
Parmalat SpA's rise to the rank of Italy's largest food producer and the world's largest dairy company began in 1961, when Calisto Tanzi inherited a ham and salami business. Two years later, Tanzi created the Parmalat milk brand. He built it into an industry leader by importing technology for packaging milk in distinctive rectangular cartons and preserving it for up to six months without refrigeration. By 1970, the brand was internationally known as the “milk of champions,” and the company started sponsoring ski events. Tanzi expanded the product line to desserts, sauces, cookies, and fruit juices and the corporate sponsorship to auto racing and soccer. In the 1990s, Parmalat went public and launched a series of acquisitions in Italy, the United States, Latin America, and Asia. The company's well-known brands included Archway cookies, Pomi pasta sauces, and Sunnydale Farms milk. Along the way, Tanzi became a major contributor to political campaigns and received a knighthood from the Italian state.

2003年12月19日，美国银行称，显示帕玛拉特账户中有47亿美元余额的文件并非真实文件。标准普尔随即把帕玛拉特的债务评级下调至D级，意味着其已违约。

<!--en-->
On December 19, 2003, Bank of America said documents indicating a $4.7 billion balance in a Parmalat account were not authentic. Standard & Poor's promptly downgraded Parmalat's debt to D, indicating default.

四天后，控股公司Parmalat Finanziaria SpA宣布计划申请破产。随着财务欺诈证据浮出水面，坦齐被捕。他估计帕玛拉特资产负债表上的资金缺口高达100亿美元，承认自己至少十年来一直在伪造财务报表，并承认他非法从帕玛拉特转移了至少6.4亿美元给由其家族控制的亏损旅游企业。最终，坦齐被判入狱10年。

<!--en-->
Four days later, holding company Parmalat Finanziaria SpA announced plans to file for bankruptcy. As evidence of financial fraud emerged, Tanzi was arrested. He estimated the hole in Parmalat's balance sheet at $10 billion, said he had been falsifying the financial statements for at least a decade, and admitted that he had unlawfully shifted at least $640 million from Parmalat to money-losing travel businesses controlled by his family. Tanzi ultimately received a 10-year prison sentence.

事实证明，这种欺诈行为不仅限于帕玛拉特资产负债表上的虚假流动性。2004年1月发布的初步报告显示，该公司的净债务约为180亿美元，其中近160亿美元此前并未被披露。普华永道还发现，截至2003年9月30日的九个月内，该公司的营收仅为40亿欧元，而非报告的54亿欧元。据受命调查此案的会计师事务所称，原本报告为6.51亿欧元的EBITDA实际上只有1.21亿欧元。丑闻爆发前，帕玛拉特的市场资本额超过20亿欧元，但根据意大利政府任命的特别管理人恩里科·邦迪的报告，2003年底该公司的实际资产总额不足10亿欧元。

<!--en-->
As it turned out, the fraud extended beyond the phantom liquidity on Parmalat's balance sheet. A preliminary report issued in January 2004revealed that the company had net debt of approximately $18 billion, almost $16 billion of which had not been disclosed previously. PricewaterhouseCoopers also found that the company's revenues for the nine months ended September 30, 2003, were only €4 billion, rather than the reported €5.4 billion. Reported as €651 million, EBITDA was actually just €121 million, according to the accounting firm, which was brought in to investigate after the scandal broke. Parmalat's market capitalization prior to the scandal exceeded €2 billion, but according to a report by Enrico Bondi, the special administrator appointed by the Italian government, actual assets totaled less than €1 billion at the end of 2003.

颇具讽刺意味的是，公司高管竟试图用锤子砸毁用于实施欺诈的电脑。更深入地审视利润情况……

<!--en-->
In a bizarre touch, company executives attempted to destroy a computer used in the fraud by smashing it with a hammer.
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

直到帕玛拉特倒闭前一个月，投资者才收到有关危机的正式警告。早在2003年10月，德意志银行的股票研究小组仍将该公司股票评为“买入”级，强调其强劲的现金流表现；花旗银行也在11月发布了乐观的报告。此外，直到申请破产前九天，该公司的债务仍享有投资级评级。不过，早在此之前就已出现一些典型的警示信号，即便该公司表面上看似经营顺利。

<!--en-->
Investors had little official warning of trouble until the month before Parmalat's collapse. As late as October 2003, Deutsche Bank's equity research group rated the company's stock a buy, highlighting its strong reported cash flow, and Citibank put out an optimistic report in November. Furthermore, the company's debt carried an investment grade rating until nine days before the bankruptcy filing. Earlier on, however, there were classic warning signs that may indicate trouble even if a company outwardly appears successful.

一个重要的警示信号是帕玛拉特对债务的过度依赖，尽管它声称拥有巨额现金储备。当被问及此事时，首席财务官福斯托·托纳总是回应称公司正处于收购阶段，且现金余额能带来可观回报。该公司主要牛奶厂的员工代表也得到了类似的答复，他们还被威胁若公开暗示财务不当行为将面临诉讼。同样，卡利斯托·坦齐指责包括雷曼兄弟在内的金融机构散布有关会计违规的谣言，以压低其股价。

<!--en-->
A major red flag was Parmalat's voracious appetite for debt, despite claiming to have a huge cash balance. When challenged on this point, Chief Financial Officer Fausto Tonna consistently replied that the company was on the acquisition trail and that its liquid balances were earning good returns. Union officials at the company's main milk plant received a similar answer and were threatened with a lawsuit if they made any public suggestion of financial improprieties. In a similar vein, Calisto Tanzi charged that financial institutions, including Lehman Brothers, were spreading rumors of accounting irregularities to drive down the price of its stock.

这种回应方式在从事财务欺诈的公司中十分常见。一位曾拒绝与帕玛拉特合作的投资银行家告诉《商业周刊》，自20世纪80年代中期以来，该公司的情况就“很奇怪”。“感觉不对劲，”他透露道。³⁰ 一些观察者认为，高得离谱的盈利能力其实是一个危险信号。一位米兰的银行家指出，一家管理良好的同类企业，其营业利润率通常在6%到7%之间，而帕玛拉特却报告了12%的营业利润率。³¹ 财务报告的透明度不足也是另一个警示信号。“帕玛拉特属于‘应回避’的对象，”巴克莱资本的高收益债券分析师罗伯特·琼斯说，“根本没有足够的信息来形成基本的信贷评估。”³² 不过，并非所有人都避而远之。“做过研究的人都知道这家公司并非清白之辈，”苏格兰皇家银行的消费品行业分析师罗布·奥曼评论道，“但许多人看到利差³³后便想：一家乳制品公司能有多大的问题呢？”³⁴ 欺诈行为能被察觉吗？219

<!--en-->
This sort of response is typical of companies engaged in financial fraud. One investment banker who had declined to deal with Parmalat told *BusinessWeek* that things had “been strange” at the company since the mid-1980s. “It smelled bad,” he confided.³⁰
Suspiciously high profitability constituted a danger sign to some observers. A Milan banker noted that a very well-managed company in Parmalat's business would achieve an operating margin of 6 to 7 percent, yet Parmalat was reporting 12 percent.³¹ Lack of transparency in financial reporting was another warning. “Parmalat was an ‘avoid’ recommendation,” said BarCap high yield bond analyst Robert Jones. “There simply wasn't enough information to form a fundamental credit view.”³² Not everybody steered clear, however. “Everyone who did their research knew this wasn'tthe cleanest company,” commented RBS consumer products analyst Rob Orman, “but many people looked at the spread³³ and thought, how far wrong can you go with a dairy company?”³⁴
Is Fraud Detectable?
219

帕玛拉特巴西子公司Parmalat Participacoes do Brasil Ltda.在2002年的财务报表中，暴露出该公司通过复杂的金融手段美化资产负债表的证据。

<!--en-->
The 2002 financial statements of Parmalat’s Brazilian unit, Parmalat Participacoes do Brasil Ltda., included evidence that Parmalat was prettying up its balance sheet through elaborate financial engineering.

在这家巴西子公司的财务报表附注中，有一处披露：2002年1月18日，该子公司发行了价值5亿欧元的可转换证券。与普通可转换债券的持有者不同，后者有权选择是否转换，而此次证券的购买者却“做出了不可撤销的承诺”，将在2008年到期时转换为股票。Parmalat Participacoes do Brasil Ltda.将这笔交易（以美元计价）记为5.238亿美元的“增资资金”；这笔款项被归入一项总额为7.64亿美元的综合性资产负债表项目，其中包括少数股东权益、增资资金以及股东权益。

<!--en-->
Deep in the footnotes of the Brazilian subsidiary’s statements was a disclosure that on January 18, 2002, the subsidiary issued a €500 million security convertible into company shares. Unlike the owner of a standard convertible bond, for whom conversion is optional, the buyer of this instrument “made an irrevocable commitment to convert” into shares at the 2008 maturity. Parmalat Participacoes do Brasil Ltda. accounted for the transaction (in U.S. dollars) as $523.8 million of “funds for capital increase,” part of an undifferentiated $764 million balance sheet entry encompassing minority interest, funds for capital increase, and shareholders equity.

当这一项目在母公司层面合并时，它仅仅被计入股东权益。此外，分析师们怀疑这种可转换证券的购买方其实是另一家帕玛拉特子公司。就在发行可转换证券的同一天，Parmalat Finance Corp. BV还发行了3亿欧元的债券。这意味着该公司通过在一个子公司出售债务、在另一个子公司购入债务的方式，增加了自身的股东权益。交易曝光后，管理层拒绝置评；遗憾的是，这家巴西子公司的财务报表并非公开文件，外界因此无法借此发现帕玛拉特的种种伎俩。

<!--en-->
When this item was consolidated at the parent level, it was simply part of shareholders’ equity. Furthermore, analysts suspected that the buyer of the convertible security was another Parmalat unit. On the same day that the convertible was issued, Parmalat Finance Corp. BV issued a €300 million bond. This would mean that by selling debt in one unit and buying it in another, the company increased its shareholders’ equity. Management declined to comment when the transaction subsequently came to light, and unfortunately, the Brazilian subsidiary’s financial statement was not a public document, so outsiders could not have used it to get wind of Parmalat’s hanky-panky.

幕后还有这样的信息：帕玛拉特的各子公司与关联方进行货币套期保值操作。但这种交易实际上并不具备真正的套期保值效果。

<!--en-->
Behind the scenes as well was the information that Parmalat units engaged in currency hedges with related parties. The economic impact of such a transaction does not truly constitute a hedge.

对于细心的投资者而言，另一些警示信号出现在部分券商的研究报告中。2002年12月，美林证券的分析师乔安娜·斯皮德和尼克·索乔夫斯基将帕玛拉特的评级下调为“卖出”，指出该公司频繁进入债券市场融资，却同时宣称拥有巨额现金，这让人对其现金创造能力产生质疑。分析师们还敏锐地认为，帕玛拉特庞大的现金余额其实是个负面因素。他们正确地指出，持有大量现金却产生较低的利息收益，却不利用这些现金来偿还债务，属于“低效的资产负债管理”。³⁵ 这种不经济行为的背后原因竟是这些现金根本不存在。2003年1月24日，Auerbach Grayson & Co.的一名分析师估计，帕玛拉特的净金融债务实际上高达45亿美元，而非该公司所报告的23亿美元。³⁶ 特别管理员邦迪认为，只需将该公司公布的债务总额与其独立发行的债券数据相比较，就能轻易判断出其真实的财务状况。

<!--en-->
Additional straws in the wind for attentive investors appeared in selected brokerage firm research reports. In December 2002, Merrill Lynch analysts Joanna Speed and Nic Sochovsky downgraded Parmalat to sell, saying that the company’s frequent recourse to the bond market, while reporting high cash balances, threw into question its cash-generating ability. The analysts also presciently viewed Parmalat’s exceptionally large cash balance as a negative. They appropriately argued that maintaining vast amounts of debt while holding cash that generated a lower interest rate, rather than using the cash to reduce debt, represented “inefficient balance sheet management.”³⁵ The explanation for this uneconomic behavior turned out to be that the cash was fictitious. On January 24, 2003, an analyst at Auerbach Grayson & Co. estimated that Parmalat’s net financial debt was $4.5 billion, rather than the $2.3 billion reported by the company.³⁶ Special administrator Bondi contended that Parmalat’s true financial condition was easily determinableby comparing its published debt totals with independently produced data on the amount of bonds it had issued.

<!--en-->
A CLOSER LOOK AT PROFITS

另一个危险信号出现在2003年2月26日，当时帕玛拉特突然取消了发行30年期债券的计划。潜在买家对该公司在声称拥有53亿美元现金的同时仍需借贷的做法表示担忧。公司随后表示将改为发行期限为7年的债券，这一举动表明市场对帕玛拉特长期稳定性的信心不如管理层所预期的那样强。这一消息导致该公司股价跌至七年来的最低点。2月28日，帕玛拉特最终取消了7年期债券的发行计划。

<!--en-->
Another hazard signal emerged on February 26, 2003, when Parmalat suddenly canceled its plan to sell 30-year bonds. Potential buyers of the issue were voicing uneasiness about the company's need to borrow at the same time that it claimed to have $5.3 billion in cash. The company said it would instead issue bonds with maturities of just seven years, suggesting the market had less confidence in Parmalat's long-run stability than management had thought. This news triggered a fall in the company's stock price to a seven-year low. On February 28, Parmalat called off the seven-year issue.

在申请破产前的最后两个月里，危机迹象愈发明显。11月6日，意大利股市监管机构Consob要求Parmalat提供关于其如何投资35亿欧元以及计划如何偿还2004年底到期的债券的详细信息。11月11日，审计机构德勤披露，他们无法确认Parmalat是否正确地记录了某份与货币相关的衍生品合约所产生的1.35亿美元收益。11月14日，公司出现了典型的风险信号——高层管理人员变动：首席财务官一年内第二次辞职。

<!--en-->
In the last two months before the bankruptcy filing, the signs of trouble multiplied. On November 6, Consob, the Italian stock market regulator, requested details on how Parmalat had invested €3.5 billion and how it planned to pay back bonds scheduled to mature by the end of 2004. On November 11, auditor Deloitte & Touche disclosed that it was unable to confirm that Parmalat had accounted correctly for a $135 million gain on a currency-related derivatives contract. A classic danger sign, senior management turnover, surfaced on November 14 with the second resignation within a year by a chief financial officer.

接着，在11月27日，该公司宣布已以5.899亿美元的价格出售其在开曼群岛的一家对冲基金中的股份，但到了12月8日却透露这笔资金无法收回。此时，该公司面临流动性紧缩的局面已显而易见。12月9日，Parmalat未能支付1.5亿欧元的债券到期款。虽然公司在12月12日支付了所需的本金，但那时标准普尔已经将其债务评级下调至投机级。

<!--en-->
Next, on November 27, the company announced that it had sold its stake in a hedge fund based in the Cayman Islands for $589.9 million but on December 8 revealed that the proceeds were not recoverable. By that time, it was clear that the company was facing a liquidity squeeze. On December 9, Parmalat failed to pay a €150 million bond maturity. The company made the required principal payment on December 12, but by then, Standard & Poor's had downgraded its debt to speculative grade.

奇怪的是，最早察觉到Parmalat骗局的人并非金融分析师，而是一位喜剧演员。在2002年9月的一场戏剧演出中——也就是申请破产前一年多——著名的意大利艺人贝佩·格里洛向观众讲述道，一位Parmalat高管曾告诉他，该公司的债务为130亿欧元，资产同样为130亿欧元。作为意大利政府和商业惯例的尖锐批评者，格里洛调侃Parmalat说：“在一个正常的国家里，它早就崩溃、破产了。”³⁷在他的玩笑成真后，格里洛的单人表演录像带在意大利电视台播出。

<!--en-->
Oddly, the person who achieved the greatest renown for early recognition of the Parmalat's house of cards was not a financial analyst, but a comedian. During a theater presentation in September 2002, more than a year before the bankruptcy filing, the popular Italian entertainer Beppe Grillo recounted to his audience that a Parmalat executive had told him the company had €13 billion in debts and €13 billion in assets. Grillo, an acerbic critic of Italian government and business practices, quipped about Parmalat: "In a normal country, it would collapse, bankrupt."³⁷ A videotape of Grillo's one-man show was broadcast on Italian television after his joke became reality.

格里洛声称他的叙述属实，但拒绝透露消息来源。

<!--en-->
Grillo claimed his anecdote was true but declined to name his informant.

不过后来，他还是被传唤在针对Parmalat丑闻的司法调查中作证。当被问及他是如何预见到公司会破产时，他表示任何人都能看出Parmalat资产负债表中的漏洞，因为财务报告很容易获取。不过，格里洛比普通民众略占优势：在成为喜剧演员之前，他获得了会计学位。《欺诈可察觉吗？》第221页

<!--en-->
Later, though, he was called to testify in the judicial investigation of the Parmalat scandal. Asked to explain how he had managed to foresee the bankruptcy, he stated that anyone could have seen the holes in Parmalat's balance sheet, given that the financial reports were easily accessible. Grillohad a bit of an advantage over the average citizen, however. Prior to becoming a comedian, he earned a degree in accounting.

## 结论

<!--en-->
*CONCLUSION*

以此作为我们探讨“欺诈是否可察觉”这一话题的结尾再合适不过。贝佩·格里洛为Parmalat案增添了喜剧色彩，而理查德·斯克鲁西则把针对他的法律程序变成了闹剧。安然公司的管理层垮台带有悲剧色彩，因而适合搬上舞台。那些能从预示这些欺诈事件发生的征兆中吸取教训的分析师，或许能成为未来财务报告剧中的英雄。

<!--en-->
This is a fitting note on which to conclude our discussion of whether fraud is detectable. Beppe Grillo lent a comic twist to the Parmalat case, and Richard Scrushy made a farce of the legal proceedings against him. The downfall of Enron's management contained elements of tragedy that made it adaptable to the stage. Analysts who learn the lessons of events that foreshadowed the revelation of these frauds may become the heroes of future financial reporting dramas.

第12章

<!--en-->
CHAPTER 12

### 财务报表预测

<!--en-->
*Forecasting Financial Statements*

正如第2至4章所述，对公司当前财务报表的分析虽具启发性，但远不及对其*未来*财务报表的分析来得重要。毕竟，决定公司股票价值的是未来的盈利和股息（参见第14章），而决定信贷质量的是未来按时偿债的相对可能性（参见第13章）。诚然，投资者在一定程度上会依据过去来预测未来。但由于已公布的财务数据人人可得，研究它们不太可能为投资者带来相对于竞争对手的显著优势。要想捕捉尚未反映在证券价格中的内在价值，分析师必须依据未来报表中出现的盈利和信贷质量指标来采取行动。

<!--en-->
Analysis of a company's current financial statements, as described in Chapters 2 through 4, is enlightening, but not as enlightening as the analysis of its *future* financial statements. After all, it is future earnings and dividends that determine the value of a company's stock (see Chapter 14) and the relative likelihood of future timely payments of debt service that determines credit quality (see Chapter 13). To be sure, investors rely to some extent on the past as an indication of the future. Because already-reported financials are available to everyone, however, studying them is unlikely to provide any significant advantage over competing investors. To capture fundamental value that is not already reflected in securities prices, the analyst must act on the earnings and credit quality measures that will appear on future statements.

当然，分析师无法确切知道公司未来的财务报表会是什么样子。不过，财务预测也并非纯粹的猜测。这一过程是对历史模式和关系的延伸，建立在对未来经济状况、市场行为以及管理层行动的假设之上。

<!--en-->
Naturally, the analyst cannot know with certainty what a company's future financial statements will look like. Neither are financial projections mere guesswork, however. The process is an extension of historical patterns and relationships, based on assumptions about future economic conditions, market behavior, and managerial actions.

财务预测只有在其假设成立的情况下才能与实际结果相符。因此，分析师应积极收集报表之外的信息。他们必须不断通过与所分析公司的客户、供应商及竞争对手建立联系，来提升自身假设的准确性。

<!--en-->
Financial projections will correspond to actual future results only to the extent that the assumptions prove accurate. Analysts should therefore energetically gather information beyond the statements themselves. They must constantly seek to improve the quality of their assumptions by expanding their contacts among customers, suppliers, and competitors of the companies they analyze.

#### 典型的一年期预测

<!--en-->
*A TYPICAL ONE-YEAR PROJECTION*

以下的一年期预测分析了分析师的假设对三份基本财务报表的影响。要理解损益表、现金流量表和资产负债表之间的相互关联性，没有比按此方式追踪数字更好的方法了。225 预测与证券分析

<!--en-->
The following one-year projection works through the effects of the analyst's assumptions on all three basic financial statements. There is probably no better way than following the numbers in this manner to appreciate theinterrelatedness of the income statement, the cash flow statement, and the balance sheet.
225
FORECASTS AND SECURITY ANALYSIS

图表12.1展示了虚构公司Colossal Chemical Corporation当前的财务报表。历史报表为预测提供了起点，有助于验证有关未来财务业绩假设的合理性。在关于Colossal Chemical预测的讨论中，我们假定分析师不仅研究了该公司过去一年的业绩，还研究了过去几年的数据。

<!--en-->
Exhibit 12.1 displays the current financial statements of a fictitious company, Colossal Chemical Corporation. The historical statements constitute a starting point for the projection by affirming the reasonableness of assumptions about future financial performance. We will assume throughout the commentary on the Colossal Chemical projection that the analyst has studied the company's results over not only the preceding year but also over the past several years.

#### 预测损益表

<!--en-->
*Projected Income Statement*

财务预测始于盈利预测（图表12.2）。预测损益表中的两个关键数字——净利润和折旧——稍后将纳入预测的现金流量表。而现金流量表又会为编制预测资产负债表提供数据。在每个后续阶段，分析师都需要做出额外的假设。不过，逻辑流程始终是从盈利预测开始的，它将显著影响这三份报表的内容。

<!--en-->
The financial projection begins with an earnings forecast (Exhibit 12.2). Two key figures from the projected income statement, net income and depreciation, will later be incorporated into a projected statement of cash flows. The cash flow statement, in turn, will supply data for constructing a projected balance sheet. At each succeeding stage, the analyst will have to make additional assumptions. The logical flow, however, begins with a forecast of earnings, which will significantly shape the appearance of all three statements.

紧接着将按顺序从顶部（销售额）到底部（净利润）逐一讨论损益表中各项所对应的假设。

<!--en-->
Immediately following is a discussion of the assumptions underlying each line in the income statement, presented in order from top (sales) to bottom (net income).

**销售额**：2011年的预测值为21.1亿美元，较图表12.1中显示的2010年实际数值增长了6%。其中，出货量增长贡献了2%，价格上涨贡献了4%。

<!--en-->
**Sales** The projected $2.110 billion for 2011 represents an assumed rise of 6 percent over the actual figure for 2010 shown in Exhibit 12.1. Of this increase, higher shipments will account for 2 percent and higher prices for 4 percent.

为了得出这些数字，分析师会利用图表12.3中所显示的历史细分数据来逐步构建预测模型。该公司各业务领域——基础化工品、塑料及工业化学品——的销售预测可借助行业出版物、行业协会以及提供计量经济预测模型的公司等资料来制定。所有这些预测都基于对未来一年经济增长（国内生产总值增加）的某种假设。分析师必须仔细确认预测者所依据的假设，并判断其是否合理。

<!--en-->
To arrive at these figures, the analyst builds a forecast from the ground up, using the historical segment data shown in Exhibit 12.3. Sales projections for the company's business—basic chemicals, plastics, and industrial chemicals—can be developed with the help of such sources as trade publications, trade associations, and firms that sell econometric forecasting models. Certain assumptions about economic growth (increase in gross domestic product) in the coming year underlie all such forecasts. The analyst must be careful to ascertain the forecaster's underlying assumptions and judge whether they seem realistic.

如果要求分析师做出的盈利预测需与公司内部的经济预测保持一致，那么确立关键指标与公司各业务板块出货量之间的历史关系就至关重要。例如，某个业务板块的出货量历史上可能以工业整体增速的1.5倍速度增长。*图表12.1 Colossal Chemical Corporation截至2010年12月31日的财务报表（单位：百万美元，省略零）*

<!--en-->
If the analyst is expected to produce an earnings projection that is consistent with an in-house economic forecast, then it will be critical to establish a historical relationship between key indicators and the shipments of the company's various business segments. For example, a particular segment's shipments may have historically grown at 1.5 times the rate of industrial

化工、造纸和资本货物等基础行业最适合采用此处所述的基于宏观经济的方法。而在技术驱动型行业以及电影、玩具等受热门趋势影响的行业中，销售业绩与整体经济趋势之间的关联往往较为松散。在这种情况下，预测工作很大程度上依赖于与目标行业内的相关人士建立联系。其目的在于对公司新产品可能取得的成功做出明智的推测。

<!--en-->
Basic industries such as chemicals, paper, and capital goods tend to lend themselves best to the macroeconomic-based approach described here. In technology-driven industries and hits-driven businesses such as motion pictures and toys, the connection between sales and the general economic trend will tend to be looser. Forecasting in such circumstances depends largely on developing contacts within the industry being studied. The objective is to make intelligent guesses about the probable success of a company's new products.

按地理区域划分的销售历史数据（图表12.4）为销售预测提供了另一项参考依据。分析师可以调整从行业细分预测中得出的数字，以反映全球特定地区异常强劲或异常疲软的经济表现预期。同样，某公司可能在某个地区面临特殊问题，比如与外国政府的纠纷。通过地理销售数据分解，可以大致了解此类事件可能产生的影响程度。

<!--en-->
A history of sales by geographic area (Exhibit 12.4) provides another input into the sales projection. An analyst can modify the figures derived from industry segment forecasts to reflect expectations of unusually strong or unusually weak economic performance in a particular region of the globe. Likewise, a company may be experiencing an unusual problem in a certain region, such as a dispute with a foreign government. The geographic sales breakdown can furnish some insight into the magnitude of the expected impact of such occurrences.

FORECASTS AND SECURITY ANALYSIS

毛利率为34%，较上一年的33%略有提升。一家公司的预期毛利率反映了对其劳动力及原材料成本变化的预判。影响毛利率预测的还有行业竞争的激烈程度，这会决定企业能否将成本上涨转嫁给客户，或保留成本下降带来的好处。

<!--en-->
margin of 34 percent, a slight improvement over the preceding year's 33 percent. The projected gross margin for a company in turn reflects expectations about changes in costs of labor and material. Also influencing the gross margin forecast is the expected intensity of industry competition, which affects a company's ability to pass cost increases on to customers or to retain cost decreases.

在基础化工等资本密集型行业中，公司及行业的预计产能利用率是关键变量。当产能被充分利用时，固定成本会被分摊到最大的生产量上，从而将单位成本降至最低。此外，如果需求超过产能导致所有生产商满负荷运转，便无人有动机通过降价来扩大销量。在此类情况下，成本上涨会被完全（甚至超额）转嫁出去，进而推高毛利率。至少在新产能建成、供需恢复平衡之前会如此。相反，若2002年需求预计会下降而非上升，进而导致产能利用率降低，那么图表12.2所预测的毛利率可能会低于2010年，而非更高。（关于固定成本与变动成本相互作用的进一步讨论，请参阅第3章。）

<!--en-->
In a capital-intensive business such as basic chemicals, the projected capacity utilization percentage (for both the company and the industry) is a key variable. At full capacity, fixed costs are spread out over the largest possible volume, so unit costs are minimized. Furthermore, if demand exceeds capacity so that all producers are running flat out, none will have an incentive to increase volume by cutting prices. When such conditions prevail, cost increases will be fully (or more than fully) passed on, and gross margins will widen. That will be the result, at least, until new industry capacity is built, bringing supply and demand back into balance. Conversely, if demand were expected to fall rather than rise in 2002, leading to a decline in capacity utilization, Exhibit 12.2's projected gross margin would probably be lower than in 2010, rather than higher. (For further discussion of the interaction of fixed and variable costs, see Chapter 3.)

与销售数据类似，分析师可以逐部门地自下而上预测销货成本。由于图表12.3中的部门信息仅显示营业利润而非毛利率，因此分析师需将各部门的折旧费用加到营业利润中，再根据各部门销售额的比例来分配销售、一般及行政费用以及研发费用。例如，若按部门销售额比例分配销售、一般及行政费用和研发费用，则2010年各部门的营业利润如表12.5所示。

<!--en-->
As with sales, the analyst can project cost of goods sold from the bottom up, segment by segment. Since the segment information in Exhibit 12.3 shows only operating income, and not gross margin, the analyst must add segment depreciation to operating income, then make assumptions about the allocation of selling, general, and administrative (SG&A) expense and research and development (R&D) expense by segment. For example, operating income by segment for 2010 works out as shown in Exhibit 12.5, if SG&A and R&D expenses are allocated in proportion to segment sales.

财务报表预测：通过汇总数年的相关数据，分析师可以建立模型，按业务板块分别预测毛利率。

<!--en-->
Forecasting Financial Statements
By compiling the requisite data for a period of several years, the analyst can devise models for forecasting gross margin percentage on a segment-by-segment basis.

**销售、一般及行政费用**：图表12.2中的预测假设SG&A费用与销售额的比例将保持历史水平，即约为销售额的15%。如果最近的季度损益表或可靠的行业信息显示该比例有上升或下降趋势，分析师在预测时会相应调整这一百分比。

<!--en-->
**Selling, General, and Administrative Expense** The forecast in Exhibit 12.2 assumes continuation of a stable relationship in which SG&A expense has historically approximated 15 percent of sales. The analyst would vary this percentage for forecasting purposes if, for example, recent quarterly income statements or comments by reliable industry sources indicated a trend to a higher or lower level.

**折旧**：折旧费用主要取决于公司固定资产的规模以及其摊销年限。如果公司各类不动产、厂房及设备（PP&E）的平均摊销期为八年，那么按直线法计算，每年折旧额将占其价值的八分之一（12.5%）。随着新增PP&E超过折旧费用，可折旧资产基数会逐年增加。

<!--en-->
**Depreciation** Depreciation expense is essentially a function of the amount of a company's fixed assets and the average number of years over which it writes them off. If, on average, all classes of the company's property, plant, and equipment (PP&E) are depreciated over eight years, then on a straight-line basis, the company will write off one-eighth (12.5 percent) each year. From year to year, the base of depreciable assets will grow to the extent that additions to PP&E exceed depreciation charges.

图表12.2基于两项指标在长期内保持稳定的比例关系，预测折旧费用相当于上年末PP&E价值的13.5%。

<!--en-->
Exhibit 12.2 forecasts depreciation expenses equivalent to 13.5 percent of PP&E as of the preceding year-end, based on a stable ratio between the two items over an extended period.

当然，预测时应纳入任何可预见的历史模式偏差。例如，公司可能会因会计政策趋于保守或激进，或因设备淘汰速度变化而调整平均摊销期。此外，公司资产结构也可能发生变化。随着数据处理设备等使用寿命较短的资产在资本支出中所占比重上升，而房屋建筑等长期资产比重下降，平均摊销期应会逐渐缩短。

<!--en-->
Naturally, a projection should incorporate any foreseeable variances from historical patterns. For example, a company may lengthen or shorten its average write-off period, either because it becomes more liberal or more conservative in its accounting practices or because such adjustments are warranted by changes in the rate of obsolescence of equipment. Also, a company's mix of assets may change. The average write-off period should gradually decline as comparatively short-lived assets, such as data-processing equipment, increase as a percentage of capital expenditures and as long-lived assets, such as bricks and mortar, decline.

**研究与开发**：与广告费用类似，研发费用通常按销售额的百分比来预算。如果公司收购了所处行业研发密集度远高于或低于现有业务的企业，研发费用占比可能会发生变化。另外，专利保护期的延长或缩短等研发激励政策的变化，也可能影响公司为保持竞争力所需的研发支出比例。除非出现此类变动，否则分析师可以较为确信地认为，未来一年的研发费用占销售额的比例将与去年相近。

<!--en-->
**Research and Development** Along with advertising, R&D is an expense that is typically budgeted on a percentage-of-sales basis. The R&D percentage may change if, for example, the company makes a sizable acquisition in an industry that is either significantly more, or significantly less, research intensive than its existing operations. In addition, changing incentives for research, such as extended or reduced patent protection periods, may alter the percentage of sales a company believes it must spend on research to remain competitive. Barring developments of this sort, however, the analyst can feel fairly confident in expecting that the coming year's R&D expense will represent about the same percentage of sales as it did last year.

图表12.2采用了4%这一基于销售额的百分比作为假设。预测与证券分析

<!--en-->
Such an assumption (at 4 percent of sales) is built into Exhibit 12.2.
FORECASTS AND SECURITY ANALYSIS

**营业利润**：将四项预测的费用相加得出总成本与费用总额（19.15亿美元），再从预测销售额中扣除该数值，便可得出1.95亿美元的预计营业利润。

<!--en-->
**Operating Income** The four projected expense lines are summed to derive total costs and expenses. The total ($1,915 million) is subtracted from projected sales to calculate projected operating income of $195 million.

**利息费用**：图表12.6展示了财务报表附注中的相关信息，可用于估算下一年度的利息费用。（并非每份年报都提供如此详细的数据；信息越简略，对假设的依赖程度就越高。）

<!--en-->
**Interest Expense** Exhibit 12.6 displays information found in the notes to financial statements that can be used to estimate the coming year's interest expense. (Not every annual report provides the amount of detail shown here. Greater reliance on assumptions is required when the information is sketchier.)

此处采用的预测方法关键在于估算Colossal Chemical公司的债务隐含成本，即该公司现有长期债务的加权平均利率。将5.43%的隐含成本应用于Colossal公司2010年末的长期债务（包括视为具有相同平均利率的即将到期债务），可得出2232万美元的预计利息费用。如图表12.6所示，2011年的现金流预测表明当年未偿债务不会有大幅减少。因此，尽管这只是近似值，但所用方法应不会偏离实际太远。

<!--en-->
The key to the forecasting method employed here is to estimate Colossal Chemical's embedded cost of debt, that is, the weighted average interest rate on the company's existing long-term debt. Applying the embedded cost of 5.43 percent to Colossal's 2010 year-end long-term debt (includingcurrent maturities, which are assumed to carry the same average interest rate) produces projected interest charges of $22.32 million. As shown in Exhibit 12.6, the 2011 cash flow projection suggests no substantial reduction in debt outstanding during 2011. Accordingly, the method employed here should not prove far off the mark, even though it is merely an approximation.

*图表12.6 长期债务、短期债务及利息费用详情*

<!--en-->
