### 可持续增长率

<!--en-->
*Sustainable Growth Rate*

可持续性问题不仅体现在异常的收益激增上，也涉及判断一家公司历史上的每股收益增长率是否具备持续性。如果这种增长并非源于每股留存收益的增加，那么答案很可能是否定的。

<!--en-->
Sustainability is an issue not only in connection with unusual surges in earnings but also when it comes to determining whether a company's historical rate of growth in earnings per share is likely to continue. The answer is probably no if the growth has been fueled by anything other than additions to retained earnings per share.

请看以下每股收益的推导过程：

<!--en-->
Consider the following derivation of earnings per share:

$$
\text{Asset turnover} \times \text{Return on sales} \times \text{Leverage} \times \text{Book value per share} = \text{Earnings per share}
$$

或者：

<!--en-->
Or:

$$
\frac{\text{Sales}}{\text{Assets}} \times \frac{\text{Net income}}{\text{Sales}} \times \frac{\text{Assets}}{\text{Net worth}} \times \frac{\text{Net worth}}{\text{Shares outstanding}} = \frac{\text{Net income}}{\text{Shares outstanding}}
$$

股票分析 323

<!--en-->
Equity Analysis
323

每股收益并不会仅仅因为销售额的增加而增长。在上述公式中，这种增长会被抵消，因为销售额既出现在销售利润率公式的分母中，又出现在资产周转率公式的分子中。只有当等式左侧的四个参数中有一个增加，或者流通股数量减少时，乘积（即每股收益）才会上升。激进的管理层或许能提高资产周转率，但资产终将达到其生产能力的极限；销售利润率同样无法无限扩大，因为过高的利润率会招致竞争；杠杆作用也有其限度，因为随着财务风险的增加，贷款人不会继续提供资金。因此，只有每股账面价值——通过留存收益的增加而持续上升——才能成为每股收益可持续增长的源泉。只要每股投入的股本金额持续增加，就能在该股本上赚取更多收益，进而使每股收益提高（读者可通过推导上述公式来验证这一点）。

<!--en-->
Earnings per share will not grow merely because sales increase. Any such increase will be canceled out in the preceding formula, since sales appears in the denominator of return on sales as well as in the numerator of asset turnover. Only by an increase in one of the four terms on the left side of the equation, or by a reduction in the number of shares outstanding, will the product (earnings per share) rise. Aggressive management may boost asset turnover, but eventually the assets will reach the limits of their productive capacity. Return on sales, likewise, cannot expand indefinitely because too-fat margins will invite competition. Leverage also reaches a limit because lenders will not continue advancing funds beyond a certain point as financial risk increases. This leaves only book value per share, which can rise unceasingly through additions to retained earnings, as a source of sustainable growth in earnings per share. As long as the amount of equity capital invested per share continues to rise, more income can be earned on that equity, and (as the reader can demonstrate by working through the preceding formula) earnings per share can increase.

然而，如果一家公司将其全部收益以股息形式分配给股东，其每股账面价值将根本不会上升。（顺便说一句，这正是为什么股息支付率的立即提高通常不会直接导致股价成比例上涨的原因，尽管公式$P = D/K - g$似乎暗示了这一点。）假设该公司能对其内部再投资的利润产生常规的股本回报率，那么提高股息支付率反而会降低其每股收益的增长率（$g$）。这种做法实际上是适得其反的：由于分子（$D$）和分母（$K - g$）同时上升，而$P$保持不变，最终结果便是如此。

<!--en-->
A company's book value per share will not rise at all, however, if it distributes 100 percent of its earnings in dividends to shareholders. (This, by the way, is why an immediate increase in the dividend-payout ratio will not ordinarily cause a direct, proportionate rise in the stock price, as might appear to be the implication of the equation $P = D/K - g$.) Assuming the company can earn its customary return on equity on whatever profits it reinvests internally, raising its dividend-payout ratio reduces its growth in earnings per share ($g$). Such a move proves to be self-defeating, as both the numerator and the denominator ($D$ and $K - g$, respectively) rise and $P$ remains unchanged.

为了实现每股收益的可持续增长，企业必须留存一部分盈利。留存的比例越高，每股所积累的账面价值就越多，每股收益的增长率也就越高。基于这一逻辑，可推导出以下公式：

<!--en-->
To achieve sustainable growth in earnings per share, then, a company must retain a portion of its earnings. The higher the portion retained, the more book value is accumulated per share and the higher can be the EPS growth rate. By this reasoning, the following formula is derived:

$$
\text{Sustainable growth rate} = (\text{Return on equity}) \times (\text{Income reinvestment rate})
$$

其中，收益再投资率 = $1 - \text{Dividend payout ratio}$ 如前所述，在穷尽前述所有方法后，提高每股收益的剩余途径就是减少流通股数量。20世纪90年代，许多公司在收入增长机会受限的情况下，通过股票回购来维持每股收益的增长。1995年至1999年间，国际商业机器公司斥资341亿美元回购股票，这一数额甚至超过了同期313亿美元的累计净利润。通过股票购买来减少股东权益，IBM提高了其**杠杆比率**，进而增加了财务风险。此外，该公司还通过增加债务来加剧这种效应。财经评论员詹姆斯·格兰特戏称，如果IBM继续回购股票，它将经历一场缓慢进行的杠杆收购。² 这类提升每股收益的计划往往具有自我限制性，因为正如前文所述，贷款人最终会拒绝容忍债务的进一步增加。预测与证券分析

<!--en-->
where Income reinvestment rate = $1 - \text{Dividend payout ratio}$
As mentioned, the one remaining way to increase earnings per share, after exhausting the possibilities already discussed, is to reduce the number of shares outstanding. During the 1990s, a number of companies used stock buybacks to maintain EPS growth in the face of constrained opportunities for revenue growth. Between 1995 and 1999, International Business Machines spent $34.1 billion to repurchase shares, more than its cumulative net income for the period of $31.3 billion. By reducing its shareholders' equity throughstock purchases, IBM increased its **leverage** and, therefore, its financial risk. Moreover, the company intensified this effect by adding to its debt. Financial commentator James Grant quipped that if IBM continued to buy in shares, it would undergo a slow-motion leveraged buyout.² Such EPS-boosting plans tend to be self-limiting, for as already noted, lenders refuse at some point to countenance increased indebtedness.
FORECASTS AND SECURITY ANALYSIS

分析师在计算股票回购对每股收益的影响时需注意一个细微之处：如果企业用闲置现金来支付回购费用，那么每股收益的增加会被因放弃投资收益而导致的减少所抵消。如果一家公司的资产负债表上持有的现金远多于其在经营中能有效利用的数额，那么指责管理层通过回购股票来虚增每股收益便有失公允。

<!--en-->
Analysts should note one subtlety in calculating the impact of stock repurchases on earnings per share. To the extent that the company funds the buybacks with idle cash, the increase in EPS is offset by a reduction arising from forgone income on investments. If a company has far more cash on its balance sheet than it can employ profitably in its operations, it is unfair to accuse management of deceitfully inflating its per share income by buying in stock.

## 杜邦公式

<!--en-->
*THE DU PONT FORMULA*

前文关于可持续增长的讨论引入了一个公式，该公式通过将每股收益拆解为几个简单的财务比率，从而提供了对其更深入的理解。这种拆解方式在股权分析中还能以其他有益的方式加以应用，最著名的便是所谓的杜邦公式。（这一思路通常归功于唐纳德森·布朗，他在E.I.杜邦德尼莫尔公司任职期间开发了该公式，并于20世纪20年代在担任通用汽车公司财务副总裁时加以应用。）借助杜邦公式，分析师能够更轻松地识别企业资产回报率的来源：

<!--en-->
The preceding discussion of sustainable growth introduced a formula that provided insight into earnings per share by disaggregating it into several simple financial ratios. Disaggregation can be applied in other beneficial ways in equity analysis, most notably in a technique known as the Du Pont Formula. (The idea is generally credited to Donaldson Brown, who developed the formula while at E. I. du Pont de Nemours, then applied it during the 1920s as vice president of finance at General Motors.) With the aid of the Du Pont Formula, the analyst can more readily perceive the sources of a firm's return on assets:

$$
\text{Asset turnover} \times \text{Return on sales} = \text{Return on assets} \\ \frac{\text{Sales}}{\text{Assets}} \times \frac{\text{Income}}{\text{Sales}} = \frac{\text{Income}}{\text{Assets}}
$$

这种分析还可以进一步扩展，以确定财务杠杆对股本回报率的影响：

<!--en-->
This analysis can be expanded to ascertain the contribution of financial leverage to return on equity:

$$
\text{Asset turnover} \times \text{Return on sales} \times \text{Financial Leverage} = \text{Return on Equity} \\ \frac{\text{Sales}}{\text{Assets}} \times \frac{\text{Income}}{\text{Sales}} \times \frac{\text{Assets}}{\text{Equity}} = \frac{\text{Income}}{\text{Equity}}
$$

需要注意的是，“财务杠杆”在此处并非像大多数情况下那样直接定义为债务与资产或权益的比率，而是定义为资产与权益的比率。从定义上讲，资产超过权益的部分即为负债，且不限于债务。从概念上讲，这种形式的财务杠杆反映了企业权益所支撑的资产规模有多大。与大多数比率分析一样，杜邦公式的价值不仅在于它回答的问题，还在于它引发的新问题。如果一家公司通过寻找减少营运资本但不损害竞争力的方法来提高资产周转率，那么它很可能就能维持较高的业绩水平。另一方面，削减必要的资本支出在短期内也会对资产回报率产生积极影响：由于折旧作用，资产周转率公式中的分母会减小；同时，由于当年资本支出减少，未来的折旧费用也会降低，从而使销售利润率上升。然而，过度削减开支最终会损害企业的竞争力，进而影响其长期的资产回报率，因此分析师必须深入探究这些比率变化的真实原因。

<!--en-->
Note that “financial leverage” is not directly defined as a ratio of debt to assets or equity, as in most other contexts. Rather, it is the ratio of assets to equity. By definition, the excess of assets over equity consists of liabilities,not limited to debt. Conceptually, this version of financial leverage indicates how large an asset base is supported by the company's equity.
Equity Analysis
Like most ratio analysis, the Du Pont Formula is valuable not only for the questions it answers but also for the new ones it raises. If a company increases its return on assets by finding ways to reduce working capital without impairing competitiveness (thereby improving asset turnover), then it is likely to be able to perform at the higher level. On the other hand, cutting back on necessary capital expenditures will also have a positive effect—in the short run—on return on assets. Not only will the denominator decline in the asset turnover factor as a result of depreciation but also return on sales will rise as future depreciation charges are reduced by lower capital outlays in the current year. Underspending will eventually hurt competitiveness, and therefore the company's long-run return on assets, so analysts must probe to determine the true nature of shifts in these ratios.

对食品加工行业的杜邦分析（图表14.7）证实了剖析股本回报率各组成部分的重要性。例如，仅从股本回报率来看，迪恩食品公司（17.77%）和荷美尔食品公司（16.86%）似乎相近。但实际上它们实现这一数值的途径截然不同：迪恩食品公司的资产周转次数较少（1.42次对比1.76次），销售利润率也较低（2.15%对比5.67%），导致其资产回报率不到后者的三分之一（3.06%对比9.99%）。迪恩食品公司较高的股本回报率完全是因为其使用的杠杆比率高出三倍多（5.80倍对比1.69倍）。持有迪恩食品股票的投资者应预料到，由于该公司财务风险相对较高，股价可能会出现较大波动。在本次分析时点，迪恩食品公司的债券评级为较低的Double-B级，而荷美尔食品公司则为中等的Single-A级。

<!--en-->
A Du Pont analysis of the food processing industry (Exhibit 14.7) confirms the value of examining the components of return on equity. Based on ROE alone, for example, Dean Foods (17.77 percent) and Hormel Foods (16.86 percent) appear similar. They achieved those numbers by very different methods, however. Dean Foods turned over its assets less frequently (1.42 times versus 1.76 times) and earned a lower margin on sales (2.15 percent versus 5.67 percent), resulting in a return on assets less than one-third as high (3.06 percent versus 9.99 percent). The higher return on equity for Dean Foods is purely a consequence of using more than three times as much leverage (5.80 times versus 1.69 times). Investors in Dean Foods stock should expect to experience volatility as a function of the company's comparatively high financial risk. Its bond ratings at the point of this analysis are in the low Double-B category versus the medium Single-A category for Hormel Foods.

在图表14.7中同样值得注意的一点是美赞臣营养品公司的负财务杠杆现象。这家婴幼儿配方奶粉制造商的净资产为-6.749亿美元。但这并不意味着该公司已经破产。事实上，美赞臣的销售利润率在同类企业中最高，且其信用评级达到投资级（BBB级，中等偏上）。

<!--en-->
Also noteworthy in Exhibit 14.7 is the negative financial leverage of Mead Johnson Nutrition Company. The manufacturer of infant formulas has net worth of -$674.9 million. This does not indicate that the company is bankrupt. In fact, Mead Johnson boasts the group's highest return on sales and has investment grade ratings (medium to high Triple-B).

对于该公司而言，杜邦分析仅在资产回报率这一层面才有意义；由于美赞臣的正净利润除以其负股东权益后会得出一个负数，这意味着这家盈利的公司却呈现出负的股东权益回报率。

<!--en-->
For this company, the DuPont analysis is meaningful only up to the point of return on assets, as Mead Johnson's positive net income divided by its negative equity produces a negative figure, implying that the profitable company has a negative return on equity.

美赞臣营养品公司的案例只是图表14.7中所观察到的一种现象的极端表现。这些公司的股东权益虽不为负，但数额较低，从而导致其股东权益回报率极高，例如金宝汤公司（78.79%）和好时公司（60.51%）。部分原因在于这两家公司采用了较高的债务融资策略。*图表14.7 食品加工行业2009年的杜邦分析结果**

<!--en-->
The Mead Johnson Nutrition case is just an extreme case of a phenomenon observed with several companies in Exhibit 14.7. They have low, although not negative, equity balances, resulting in spectacularly higher returns on equity, for example, Campbell Soup (78.79 percent) and Hershey (60.51 percent). 从行业内的财务杠杆水平来看，这些公司的权益价值相对较高。不过，其极高的净资产收益率其实源于极低的账面价值。品牌食品生产商的价值主要来源于消费者对其知名品牌的认可，而非用于生产的实体厂房。根据美国通用会计准则（GAAP），这些公司在产品研发和广告宣传上的投入——它们同样能创造持久价值，就像工厂或油井一样——被计入费用而非资本项目。与会计体系不同，金融市场能够识别品牌名称的经济价值。图表14.8显示，Campbell Soup的账面价值仅为其市场价值的十二分之一。行业中值公司的市场价值是账面价值的3.44倍，这反映出投资者对基于会计数据的净资产的重视程度之低。

<!--en-->
Equity Analysis of the comparatively high financial leverage within the industry. In addition, though, the outlandishly high ROEs result from the companies' very low levels of book value. Producers of branded food products typically derive their equity value primarily from consumer acceptance of their well-known brands, rather than the physical plants in which they produce their goods. Under generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP), the costs of these companies' product development and advertising, which create enduring value just as a factory or an oil well does, is expensed rather than capitalized. Unlike the accounting system, the financial markets recognize the economic value of brand names. Exhibit 14.8 shows that Campbell Soup's book value is a mere one-twelfth of its market value. The median company's market value is 3.44 times book value, underscoring how little attention investors pay to accounting-based net worth.

FORECASTS AND SECURITY ANALYSIS

尽管企业会投入资金来提升品牌的经济价值，但根据美国通用会计准则（GAAP），科技和制药公司的研发支出在发生时即被费用化，因此不被视为资产。对于这类后工业经济的代表企业而言，若以市值而非历史成本来衡量股权价值，其股本回报率便不会显得那么惊人（参见第2章中的“基于市值的股权数据的利弊”一节）。

<!--en-->
expenditures aimed at building the economic value of their brands, the research and development outlays of technology and pharmaceutical companies are written off as incurred and consequently are assigned no asset value under GAAP. For these exemplars of the postindustrial economy, return on equity looks less stratospheric when equity is viewed in terms of market capitalization rather than historical cost (see “Pros and Cons of a Market-Based Equity Figure” in Chapter 2).

## 通过重组潜力进行估值

<!--en-->
*VALUATION THROUGH RESTRUCTURING POTENTIAL*

杜邦分析法更为微妙的好处在于，它能揭示企业通过公司重组来提升价值的潜力。无论重组是内部发起还是外部强加，运营与财务战略的重大调整都可能大幅提升公司普通股的价格。图表14.7中所展示的分析有助于确定在特定情况下能够释放隐藏价值的重组类型。有些公司有可能通过更高效地利用资产来提高股价，而另一些公司则可通过增加财务杠杆来提升价值。³ 背景资料显示，企业管理者常常在公司政策问题上与股市投资者及投机者产生分歧。总体而言，管理者倾向于在企业中保留一定的冗余能力，即应对危机和机遇的储备容量。如果公司产生的多余现金停留在资产负债表上，仅获得低风险、短期金融工具所能提供的微薄收益，管理者对此往往比投资者更为宽容。他们认为，一旦盈利和现金流意外下滑，或突然出现绝佳的收购机会，这些现金便能派上用场。

<!--en-->
A subtler benefit of the Du Pont analysis is the insight it can provide into companies' potential for enhancing value through corporate restructuring. Whether initiated internally or imposed from outside, major revisions in operating and financial strategies can dramatically increase the price of a corporation's common shares. The analysis illustrated in Exhibit 14.7 helps to identify the type of restructuring that can unlock hidden value in a particular instance. Some companies have the potential to raise their share prices by utilizing their assets more efficiently, whereas others can increase their value by increasing their financial leverage.³
By way of background, corporate managers frequently find themselves at odds with stock market investors and speculators over issues of corporate policy. In general, managers prefer to maintain a certain amount of slack in their organizations, that is, a reserve capacity to deal with crises and opportunities. They tend to be less troubled than investors if their companies generate excess cash that remains on the balance sheet earning the modest returns available on low-risk, short-dated financial instruments. That cash may come in handy, they argue, if earnings and cash flow unexpectedly turn down or if an outstanding acquisition opportunity suddenly presents itself.

相比之下，投资者和投机者更希望看到这些现金被用于回购股票或返还给股东。管理者也比股东更倾向于相信表现不佳的业务部门能够被挽救。他们的判断有时会受到不愿承认自己主导的收购项目成效不佳这一心理的影响。

<!--en-->
Investors and speculators, in contrast, prefer to see the cash used to repurchase stock or returned to shareholders. Managers also tend to be more inclined than shareholders to believe that underperforming units can be rehabilitated. Their judgment is sometimes influenced by reluctance to admit that acquisitions in which they had a hand have worked out poorly.

多年来，管理层与股东之间围绕此类运营及财务政策问题的争执采用了多种策略。早在1927年和1928年，先驱证券分析师本杰明·格雷厄姆就成功说服北方管道公司管理层出售那些对原油运输业务并非必需的资产，并将所得款项分配给股东。格雷厄姆在这项努力中得到了重要机构股东——洛克菲勒基金会的关键支持。这一结果颇为罕见，因为当时及此后多年里，机构投资者通常都站在管理层一边；最多只是在对公司经营方式彻底不满时才出售股票。即便在20世纪80年代，试图推动变革也并非机构的普遍做法。

<!--en-->
Over the years, management-shareholder disputes over such operating- and financial-policy issues have featured a variety of tactics. As far back as 1927 and 1928, pioneer securities analyst Benjamin Graham waged a successful campaign to persuade the management of Northern Pipeline to liquidate certain assets that were not essential to the company's crude oil transportation business and distribute the proceeds to shareholders. Graham enlisted pivotal support for his effort from a major institutional holder, theRockefeller Foundation. The outcome was unusual, as institutional investors generally sided with management, both at the time and for many years afterward. At most, institutions sold their shares if they became thoroughly dissatisfied with the way a company was being run. Trying to bring about change was not a widespread institutional practice, even in the 1980s.

因此，在公司治理之争中，管理层的主要对手是激进的金融操盘手。20世纪50年代，这些人物通过代理权争夺战推动战略转向，从而备受瞩目。他们的手法是在股东年会上通过选举董事来争取董事会的多数控制权。股票分析 329

<!--en-->
Therefore, management's main adversaries in battles over corporate governance were aggressive financial operators. During the 1950s, these swashbucklers attracted considerable attention by pushing for strategic redirection through proxy battles. Their modus operandi consisted of striving to obtain majority control of the board through the election of directors at the annual meeting of shareholders.
Equity Analysis
329

20世纪70年代，战术转向了敌意收购——这种交易此前被担任并购中介的投资银行视为不光彩之举。敌意收购在20世纪80年代尤为盛行，部分原因是高收益债务（俗称“垃圾债券”）的供应大幅增加。高收益债券还为大量杠杆收购（LBO）提供了资金；这些交易的发起人辩称，若将公司私有化并使其免受公开市场对短期利润增长的贪婪需求影响，公司就能改善长期业绩。

<!--en-->
The 1970s brought the tactical shift to hostile takeovers, a type of transaction previously regarded as unsavory by the investment banks that acted as intermediaries in mergers and acquisitions. Hostile takeovers became especially prominent in the 1980s, fueled in part by the greatly increased availability of high-yield debt (informally referred to as *junk bond*) financing. High-yield bonds also financed scores of leveraged buyouts (LBOs), whose sponsors defended these controversial transactions in part by arguing that corporations could improve their long-run performance if they were taken private and thereby shielded from the public market's insatiable demand for short-run profit increases.

20世纪90年代，机构投资者终于开始意识到，凭借其庞大的持股量，他们能在公司董事会中施加巨大影响力。

<!--en-->
In the 1990s, institutional investors finally began to understand the influence they could wield in corporate boardrooms by virtue of their vast share holdings.

大型机构投资者开始敦促企业采取精简业务、剥离亏损部门以及用多余现金回购股票等措施来推高股价。在某些情况下，仅仅发出集体呼声并无明显效果，这些机构便直接促使高层管理人员下台。

<!--en-->
Large institutional shareholders began to prod corporations to increase their share prices by such measures as streamlining operations, divesting unprofitable units, and using excess cash to repurchase shares. In some instances, where merely making their collective voice heard had no discernible effect, the institutions precipitated the ouster of senior management.

20世纪90年代的股东积极主义在市盈率相对较高的环境中蓬勃发展。此外，这一时期还出现了对上世纪80年代过度使用财务杠杆趋势的抵制。当时的环境不利于那种推动80年代企业重组的借贷收购交易。

<!--en-->
The shareholder activism of the 1990s flourished in an environment of comparatively high price-earnings ratios. Additionally, the period was characterized by a backlash against the previous decade's trend toward increased financial leverage. Conditions were not conducive to the sort of borrow-and-acquire transactions that drove much of the corporate restructurings of the 1980s.

不过，杠杆收购并未消失。20世纪90年代初的杠杆收购破产潮过后，收购公司重新开始了交易活动。在私募股权的旗号下，杠杆收购公司在21世纪获得了新的重要地位。显然，这类另类投资（即传统意义上的股票、债券和现金之外的投资）已成为金融市场中的常见现象。杠杆收购中反复出现的繁荣与萧条周期似乎也已根深蒂固地融入了投资格局之中。

<!--en-->
Leveraged buyouts did not disappear, however. After the early-1990s wave of LBO bankruptcies, the buyout firms resumed their deal making. Under the banner of private equity, the LBO shops gained new prominence in the 2000s. It seemed clear that this category of alternative investments (those outside the traditional categories of public equities, bonds, and cash) had become a standard feature of the financial markets. A recurring boom-and-bust cycle in LBOs also appeared to have gotten ingrained into the investment landscape.

预测与证券分析

<!--en-->
FORECASTS AND SECURITY ANALYSIS

典型的杠杆收购是指通过在股价低迷时购入股票来获得公司控制权，随后向资本结构中注入大量债务。在周期初期，此类机会大量存在，因为机构投资者正在从之前的萧条中复苏。由于不存在过多资金追逐少量交易的压力，只需提高债务与股本比率，就能在不产生过度破产风险的情况下创造价值。私募股权公司特别重视修正后的杜邦公式中的第二个因素——财务杠杆。

<!--en-->
The prototypical leveraged buyout consists of gaining control of a company by buying its stock at a depressed price, then adding a large amount of debt to the capital structure. In the initial stage of the cycle, opportunities of this sort are abundant, because institutional investors are recovering from the previous bust. Absent the pressure of too many dollars chasing too few deals, it is feasible to extract value without creating undue bankruptcy risk, simply by increasing the ratio of debt to equity. The private equity firms emphasize the second factor in the modified Du Pont Formula—financial leverage.

在评估一家公司是否适合作为杠杆收购对象时，私募股权公司并不依赖传统的股票估值技术。以虚构的Sitting Duck Corporation为例（图表14.9）。按照常规假设，考虑到同类公司当前的盈利倍率为15倍，Sitting Duck的股权价值将被估为9.75亿美元，约为其4.13亿美元账面价值的2.4倍。

<!--en-->
In assessing a company's potential as a leveraged buyout candidate, private equity firms do not focus on traditional equity valuation techniques. Consider the fictitious Sitting Duck Corporation (Exhibit 14.9). Under conventional assumptions, and given a prevailing earnings multiple of 15 on similar companies, Sitting Duck's equity will be valued at $975 million, about 2.4 times its book value of $413 million.

然而，杠杆收购的发起人对估值的处理方式截然不同。他们关注的不是盈利，而是现金流。*图表14.9 Sitting Duck Corporation*

<!--en-->
Leveraged buyout sponsors, however, would approach the valuation much differently. Their focus would not be on earnings, but on cash flow.

权益分析 331

<!--en-->
Equity Analysis
331

在支付了约三分之一的盈利作为股息，并通过新的厂房和设备投资抵消了折旧之后，Sitting Duck公司在2010年产生了3000万美元的现金。现任管理层利用这笔现金进一步降低了本已较低的债务资本比率（36%），并用于增加公司现有的有价证券组合。对于收购专家而言，更合适的用途应为用其来为对公司的溢价收购提供资金。

<!--en-->
After paying out approximately one-third of its earnings in dividends and more than offsetting depreciation through new expenditures for plant and equipment, Sitting Duck generated $30 million of cash in 2010. The incumbent management group used this cash to reduce an already conservative (36 percent) total-debt-to-total-capital ratio and to add to the company's existing portfolio of marketable securities. To a buyout specialist, a more appropriate use would be to finance a premium bid for the company.

具体计算如下：假设贷款方和债券购买者目前愿意为那些EBITDA能够覆盖债务利息2.5倍的项目提供融资。（债权提供者并不关心公司的账面利润，而更看重其偿还债务的能力；现金流正是这种能力的关键决定因素。）Sitting Duck公司的营业利润为1.86亿美元，加上3800万美元的折旧费用后，EBITDA达到2.24亿美元。2.24亿美元所能覆盖的2.5倍利息额为9000万美元，这比Sitting Duck公司目前的利息支出增加了7100万美元。假设杠杆收购融资的综合借贷成本为10%，那么收购方可以在现有的2.37亿美元债务基础上再增加7.1亿美元债务，总计9.47亿美元。

<!--en-->
The arithmetic goes as follows: Assume lenders and bond buyers are currently willing to finance sound leveraged buyout projects that can demonstrate EBITDA coverage of 2.5 times. (The debt providers do not care about the company's book profits, but rather about its ability to repay debt. Cash generation is a key determinant of that ability.) Sitting Duck's operating income of $186 million, with $38 million of depreciation added back, produces EBITDA of $224 million. The amount of interest that $224 million can cover by 2.5 times is $90 million, an increase of $71 million over Sitting Duck's present interest expense. Assuming a blended borrowing cost of 10 percent on the LBO financing, a raider can add $710 million of debt to the existing $237 million, for a total of $947 million.

如果现行的贷款标准要求交易中股权比例至少达到25%，那么收购方还需额外投入3.2亿美元，从而使总资本达到12.67亿美元。按照这一计算，收购方可以支付比Sitting Duck公司当前市值高出30%的溢价（12.67亿美元 ÷ 9.47亿美元 = 1.30）。收购价格相当于公司收益的19.5倍，而目前市场给予该公司的估值倍数仅为15倍。不过，杠杆收购发起方得出这一数字所依据的是现金流指标，而非会计收益。此次出价的EBITDA倍数仅为5.7倍，按杠杆收购专家的标准来看并不算过高。（正如第8章所述，EBITDA绝非衡量现金流的*最佳*指标，但它确实可被视为杠杆金融领域的主流标准。）

<!--en-->
If prevailing lending standards require equity of at least 25 percent in the transaction, the raider must put up an additional $320 million, for a total capitalization of $1.267 billion. By this arithmetic, the takeover artist can pay a premium of 30 percent ($1.267 billion ÷ $947 million = 1.30) over Sitting Duck's present market capitalization. The purchase price equates to a multiple of 19.5 times earnings, rather than the 15X figure currently assigned by the market. The LBO sponsor got to this number, however, through a measure of cash flow, rather than earnings. The EBITDA multiple of the bid is 5.7 times, not an astronomical level by the standards of LBO specialists. (As explained in Chapter 8, EBITDA is by no means the *best* measure of cash flow, but it can be fairly described as the standard in leveraged finance circles.)

抛开这些计算不谈，人们不禁会问：在比Sitting Duck公司股票市价高出30%的情况下，杠杆收购发起方是否真的能指望获得高额投资回报？事实上，许多此类交易确实能带来丰厚利润，新所有者最终会通过出售公司或**首次公开募股**的方式退出，即将公司重新推向公开市场。

<!--en-->
Stepping back from these calculations, one is bound to wonder whether the LBO sponsor can truly expect to earn a high return on investment after paying 30 percent above the prevailing price for Sitting Duck's shares. Many such transactions do prove highly profitable, with the new owners eventually exiting through sale of the company or an **initial public offering**, that is, returning the company to the public market.

在某些情况下，收购发起方会在退出前提取大量股息以增加自身利润。尽管私募股权公司往往淡化时机对其成功的作用，但的确遵循着在股市估值较低时买入、估值较高时卖出的制胜法则。唯一的问题是，杠杆收购活动及EBITDA倍数的高峰往往伴随着经济衰退和股市熊市。因此，周期末期的交易往往会面临盈利下滑的问题，导致公司难以负担大幅增加的利息支出，此时通过IPO退出的途径也变得不可行。预测与证券分析

<!--en-->
In some cases, the buyout sponsor takes out substantial dividends before exiting, adding to its profits. Although private equity firms downplay the role of timing in their success, buying companies when equity market valuations are low and selling when they are high is a winning formula. The only problem is that peaks in LBO activity—and EBITDA multiples—tend to be followed by recessions and bear markets in stocks. Late-cycle deals consequently become plagued by depressed earnings, making it difficult to cover the company'svastly increased interest charges at a time when exiting through an IPO is not feasible.
FORECASTS AND SECURITY ANALYSIS

私募股权公司并非完全依赖其把握股市涨跌的能力，它们还试图通过以下方式来提升成功概率：

<!--en-->
Rather than rely entirely on their ability to catch the highs and lows in the equity market, private equity firms try to enhance their probability of success by the following means:

1. *利润率的提升。*杠杆收购之所以能改善盈利能力，原因主要有两个。首先，所有权变更会带来对公司运营的全新审视。新投资者通常对那些历史悠久但已不再盈利的产品线缺乏情感上的眷恋；此外，他们更容易采取那些虽在情感上难以接受但却必要的措施来恢复竞争力，比如裁员和外包生产。其次，收购后管理层可能会获得公司更大比例的利益份额。与那些能确保他们退休后生活无忧的股票期权不同，高层甚至中层管理人员可能会获得股权，这些股权有可能在几年内让他们变得极为富有。激励机制的改变会减少管理者维持运营冗余的积极性，转而促使他们从公司资产中榨取每一分可能的利润。由于有了分享收益的机会，管理者可能会削减以往被容忍的不必要开支，并比过去更积极地开拓潜在新市场。无论通过何种途径实现，利润率的提升都意味着更高的EBITDA；进而推高公司估值，为杠杆收购的股权投资人创造利润。需要注意的是，分析师必须警惕那些仅仅源于投资支出减少而带来的利润率改善。杠杆收购后，公司可以通过削减广告及研发开支来立即提升盈利水平。尽管会计准则不允许将这些支出资本化处理，但它们能为未来带来收益。大幅削减此类开支或推迟资本性支出以节省现金，可能会损害公司的未来竞争力，从而使当期盈利的增长显得虚幻不实。今天的利润改善，可能正是公司因过度节约而导致失去竞争力、最终走向破产的前兆。遗憾的是，损益表提供的细节往往不足以判断特定类型的投资支出是否已被削减；因此分析师必须向行业人士求证该公司投资支出是否充足。如果公司在杠杆收购后客户反映服务质量下降，这可能意味着重要的销售支持职能已被削弱。短期内盈利或许会上升，但随着客户转向其他供应商，盈利很快便会受损。股票分析 333
2. *资产出售。* 由于股市主要关注盈利情况，一家公司的市值可能远低于其资产的总价值。例如，某子公司对净利润的贡献微乎其微，但能通过折旧产生大量现金流；在私人市场上，该子公司的价值可能相当可观。在此类市场中，该子公司的定价会基于EBITDA的倍数来确定。另外，某个子公司之所以不盈利，可能仅仅是因为其规模不足。竞争对手或许愿意收购该子公司并将其与自身业务整合，整合后的总盈利水平将高于两家公司独立运营时的水平。如果杠杆收购方在公司内部发现此类机会，可能会投入少量股权资金，并借贷大部分收购款项，随后出售那些低净利润的业务以偿还借款。若按计划实施，资产出售将使收购方免除债务，同时拥有公司的剩余部分——即此前贡献了绝大部分净利润的业务。在以市盈率倍数为导向的股市中，这部分业务的估值可能与整个公司此前的估值相当。随后，杠杆收购方可通过将该公司重新上市来套现。一切尘埃落定后，收购方所获得的收益应足以覆盖支付给出售股份的原始股东的溢价。未实现的盈利潜力和EBITDA倍数绝非公司治理争议中涉及的唯一估值因素。那些主张通过政策调整来提升股东价值的人，有时会重点关注财务报表中所列示的特定资产价值。例如，石油公司会在年度报告中披露其储量规模。由于能源公司频繁买卖储量，且大宗交易价格常被公开报道，因此当前的市场估值数据随手可得。如果近期地下储量的出售价格相当于每桶18美元，那么拥有5000万桶储量的公司理论上可借此获得9亿美元的收入。⁴ 9亿美元加上基于市盈率倍数计算的炼油、营销及运输资产的价值，很可能远超该公司当前的市值。倘若如此，所谓石油储量的“未被认可的价值”便可成为评估该公司股票的一种替代方法。

预测与证券分析：有意进行企业重组的人士也会在其他类型的矿产、房地产以及与公司核心业务无关的长期投资中寻找这种“未被认可的价值”。实现此类资产价值的方法包括：
* 将资产出售换取现金。
* 将其置入一家独立的子公司，然后让该子公司的一部分上市，从而为公司的剩余权益确立市场价值。
* 将资产置入一家有限合伙企业中，并将相关权益分配给股东。从通过重组潜力进行估值的概述中得出的关键结论是：以市盈率倍数为基础的估值方法虽是最知名的基本面分析方法，但并非投资者唯一可依赖的手段；实际上，基本面分析存在多种途径。尽管财务报表之外的因素也会对基本面估值产生影响，但对财务报表的深入理解仍是所有分析方法的基础。

<!--en-->
1. *Profit Margin Improvement.* A leveraged buyout can bring about improved profitability for either of two reasons. First, a change in ownership results in a fresh look at the company's operations. The newcomers typically have less sentimental attachment to product lines that are long on tradition but are no longer profitable. In addition, they can more easily take the emotionally difficult but necessary steps to restore competitiveness, such as reducing the work force and outsourcing production. Second, management may obtain a significantly enlarged stake in the firm's success as the result of a buyout. In lieu of stock options that could leave them comfortably provided for in their retirement, senior and even middle-level executives may receive equity interests that can potentially make them immensely wealthy within a few years. The change in incentives can reduce managers' zeal for maintaining slack in their operations and cause them instead to squeeze every possible dollar of profit out of their company's assets. With an enhanced opportunity to participate in the benefits, managers may crack down on unnecessary costs that they formerly tolerated and pursue potential new markets more aggressively than in the past. Regardless of how it comes about, however, improvement in profit margins means higher EBITDA. That, in turn, leads to a higher valuation and generates a profit for the LBO's equity investors.
As a caveat, analysts must watch out for improvements in reported profit margins that represent nothing more than reductions in investment spending. Following an LBO, a company can report an immediate improvement in earnings by cutting back expenditures on advertising and research and development. Even though the accounting rules do not permit these items to be capitalized, the outlays provide benefits in future periods. Sharply reducing such outlays, or delaying capital expenditures to conserve cash, can impair a company's future competitiveness, making the increase in current-period earnings illusory. Today's profit improvement can be a precursor of tomorrow's bankruptcy by a company that has economized its way to an uncompetitive state.
Regrettably, the income statement may provide too little detail to determine whether specific kinds of investment spending have been curtailed. Analysts must therefore query industry sources for evidence regarding the adequacy of the company's investment spending. If thecompany's customers report a drop in the quality of service following a leveraged buyout, it may indicate that important sales support functions have been eviscerated. Earnings may rise in the short run but suffer soon as customers switch to other providers.
Equity Analysis
333
2. *Asset Sales.* As a function of the stock market's primary focus on earnings, a company's market capitalization may be far less than the aggregate value of its assets. For example, a subsidiary that contributes little to net income but generates substantial cash flow from depreciation has a potentially large value in the private market. In that realm, the unit would be priced on a multiple of EBITDA. Alternatively, a subsidiary might be unprofitable only because its scale is insufficient. A competitor might be willing to buy the unit and consolidate it with its own operations. The result would be higher combined earnings than the two operations were able to generate independently. An LBO sponsor who Spies this sort of opportunity within a company may invest a small amount of equity and borrow the greater part of the purchase price, then liquidate the low-net-income operations to repay the borrowings. If carried out as planned, the asset sales will leave the acquirer debt-free and in possession of the remainder of the company, that is, the operations that previously contributed almost all of the net income. In the P/E-multiple-oriented stock market, that portion of the company will be worth as much as the entire company was previously. The LBO sponsor may then cash out by taking it public again. After all the dust has settled, the sponsor should have cleared more than enough to cover the premium paid to original shareholders who sold into the buyout.
Unrealized earnings potential and EBITDA multiples are by no means the only valuation factors that come into play in corporate governance controversies. Proponents of policy changes in pursuit of enhanced shareholder value sometimes focus on the values of specific assets identified in the financial statements. For example, oil companies disclose the size of their reserves in their annual reports. Because energy companies frequently buy and sell reserves, and because the prices of larger transactions are widely reported, current market valuations are always readily at hand. If recent sales of reserves in the ground have occurred at prices that equate to $18 a barrel, then a company with 50 million barrels of reserves could theoretically liquidate those assets for $900 million.⁴ It may be that the sum of $900 million and a P/E-multiple-based price for the company's refining, marketing, and transportation assets substantially exceeds the company's current market capitalization. If so, the so-called unrecognized value of the oil reserves can be the basis of an alternative method of evaluating the company's stock.
FORECASTS AND SECURITY ANALYSIS
Would-be corporate restructurers also seek unrecognized value in other types of minerals, real estate, and long-term investments unrelated to a company's core business. Methods of realizing the value of such an asset include:
* Selling the asset for cash.
* Placing it in a separate subsidiary, then taking a portion of the subsidiary public to establish a market value for the company's residual interest.
* Placing the asset in a master limited partnership, interests in which are distributed to shareholders.
The key message to take away from this overview of valuation via restructuring potential is that a focus on price-earnings multiples, the best-known form of fundamental analysis, is not the investor's sole alternative to relying on technicians' stock charts. There are in fact several approaches to fundamental analysis. A solid understanding of financial statements is essential to all of them, even though factors outside the financial statements also play a role in fundamental valuation.

## 结论

<!--en-->
*CONCLUSION*

正如本章开篇所述，基于财务报表得出的估值仅代表数百万股票买卖双方在每个交易时段所进行的分析的一部分。事实上，交易所内交易员瞬间的决策几乎称不上是任何形式的分析；那不过是对供需关系瞬时变化的高度直觉性反应罢了。

<!--en-->
As noted at the outset of this chapter, valuations derived from financial statements represent only a portion of the analyses being conducted by millions of stock buyers and sellers during each trading session. Indeed, the split-second decision making of traders on the exchange floors can scarcely be described as analysis of any kind. Rather, it amounts to a highly intuitive response to momentary shifts in the balance of supply and demand.

然而，对于采取长期视角的投资者而言，财务报表分析为估值提供了宝贵的参考依据。一只股票可能会因对某种影响有限的事件做出狂热反应而暂时上涨或暴跌。但最终，理性通常会重新占据上风。股价随后会回归到基于公司长期盈利和产生现金流能力所决定的合理水平。关注资产清算价值以及市盈率（P/E）和EBITDA倍数，与这一观点是一致的。归根结底，此前未被认定的资产价值同样取决于其产生现金流的潜力，而这必须在过往业绩的背景下加以衡量。通过分析公司的历史财务报表来预测其未来表现，分析师便能得出不受市场短期情绪影响的股票内在价值。附录

<!--en-->
For the investor who takes a longer view, however, financial statement analysis provides an invaluable reference point for valuation. A stock may temporarily soar or plummet in frenzied reaction to a development of little ultimate consequence. Eventually, however, rationality usually reasserts itself. The share price then returns to a level that is justifiable on the basis of the company's long-range capacity to generate earnings and cash. Focusing on breakup values, as well as P/E and EBITDA multiples, is consistent with this thesis. Ultimately, the value of previously unrecognized assets likewise rests on their potential to generate cash, which must be measured in the context of previous performance. By studying the company's historical financial statements to forecast its future results, the analyst can derive an intrinsic value for a stock that is unaffected by the market's transitory mood.

The unaudited pro forma condensed combined financial statements do not reflect Hertz's expected realization of annual cost savings of $180 million by 2013. These savings are expected indirect operating, depreciation of revenue earning equipment and selling, general and administrative functions. Although Hertz management expects that cost savings will result from the merger, there can be no assurance that these cost savings will be achieved. The unaudited pro forma condensed combined financial statements do not reflect estimated restructuring and integration charges associated with the expected cost savings, which are estimated to be approximately $70 million, of which approximately $23 million (associated with the purchase of information technology hardware and software) will be capitalized and the remainder will be expensed as incurred. Additionally, severance charges for DTG senior management of approximately $23 million are not reflected in these pro forma financial statements, and will be expensed as incurred.

2. Although this book focuses on for-profit companies, nonprofit companies and governmental entities also produce financial statements. Readers should not presume that those entities invariably eschew reporting trickery. Like their for-profit counterparts, nonprofit organizations seek to raise capital. They have incentives to portray their financial positions in as favorable a light as possible, when trying to borrow or to demonstrate their financial viability to providers of grants. On the other hand, nonprofits sometimes strive to make themselves appear less flush than they really are, to impress on donors the urgency of their appeal for funds. Governmental units sometimes resort to disingenuous reporting to avoid political fallout from the consequences of unsound fiscal policies. Anticapitalist ideologues cannot truthfully contend that the profit motive alone leads to devious financial reporting.

5. In this analysis, it is essential to carry out the full growth-rate calculations, rather than simply add the percentage increases for price and units, then subtract the reported revenue gain. To illustrate, suppose a manufacturer sells 100 units at $5.00 each for revenue of $500 in Year 1. In Year 2, unit sales grow by 12 percent, and the price increases by 8 percent. Revenue increases to 112 units @ $5.40 = $604.80. That represents a revenue increase of $604.80 ÷ $500 = 20.96 percent. In round terms, the revenue increase is 21 percent, rather than the sum of the percentage volume and price increases, that is, 12 percent + 8 percent = 20 percent.

## 第13章 信用分析

<!--en-->
*CHAPTER 13 Credit Analysis*

1. 实际上，如果企业陷入资不抵债境地，美国破产法鼓励其进行重组而非直接清算。通常，重组会通过向经过债务减免而重获新生的企业发行证券来清偿债权人的债权。不过，由于各类债权人所获证券的价值确定与资产保护密切相关，因此下述分析方法同样适用于重组和清算情形。
2. 本段中关于优先股的论述也普遍适用于优先股，后者在形式上与优先股相似，但在资本结构中地位次于优先股。
3. 在此及后续关于总资本的定义中均包含少数股东权益。在杠杆计算中应将此项视为权益，因为它不涉及合同性支付且排序次于债务。
4. 尼克·菲尔丁、理查德·汤姆森与拉里·布莱克合著，《O&Y面临未公开的债务隐患》，《独立报》，1992年5月10日，周日商业版，第1页。
5. 从技术层面讲，尽管法定税率难以控制，但有效税率仍相对可控。不过，将营业利润率与税前利润率分开计算仍有意义，这样便能分别衡量管理层的运营能力和财务决策水平。
6. 参见爱德华·I·奥尔特曼、罗伯特·G·哈尔德曼与保罗·纳拉亚南合著的《Zeta分析：识别企业破产风险的新模型》，《银行与金融杂志》，1977年6月，第29–54页。

Typically, a reorganization results in settlement of creditors' claims via distribution of securities of a firm that has been rehabilitated through forgiveness of a portion of its debt. Determination of the value of securities awarded to each class of creditor is related to asset protection, however, so the analysis that follows applies equally to reorganization and liquidation.

## 第14章 股票分析

<!--en-->
*CHAPTER 14 Equity Analysis*

1. 与债务利息不同，股息是由董事会酌情决定的，而非履行契约义务。因此，股息更容易出现变动——包括减少、增加或暂停——其波动性大于债券票息或预定的本金偿还。
2. Bethany McLean，“IBM如何实现每年27%的增长”，《财富》杂志，2000年6月26日，第165页。
3. 认为公司可以通过提高财务杠杆来增加其市值的观点，似乎与现代金融学的基本原则相悖。诺贝尔经济学奖得主Franco Modigliani和Merton Miller证明，在某些关键假设下，公司的股票市场价值对其资本结构中债务与股权的比例并不敏感。不过，Modigliani和Miller随后进一步研究了在放宽假设以反映现实情况时会怎样。他们及后续研究者发现，通过提高财务杠杆来充分利用债务带来的税收抵免效应，确实能够提升公司的股票市场价值。因为借款利息属于可抵税费用，而股票股息则不可抵税。
4. 不过请注意，第2章“价值问题”一节中讨论的储备估值不确定性。![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/f58f5bce11754246d7c288ce5e905fb6.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261012%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261012T065612Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=dc4829aef111b90268ef1872ff1c94642181f049b484ce9504346cb417320603)

<!--en-->
1. Dividends, unlike interest payments on debt, are payable at the discretion of the board of directors, rather than in fulfillment of a contractual obligation. They are consequently subject to greater variability—through reduction, increase, or suspension—than bond coupons or scheduled principal repayments.
2. Bethany McLean, “Hocus-Pocus: How IBM Grew 27% a Year,” *Fortune*, June 26, 2000, 165.
3. The notion that a company can increase its market capitalization by boosting its financial leverage appears to fly in the face of a fundamental tenet of modern finance. Nobel economics laureates Franco Modigliani and Merton Miller demonstrated that under certain critical assumptions, a company's stock market value was insensitive to the proportions of debt and equity in its capital structure. Modigliani and Miller followed up on this pioneering work, however, by exploring what happened when the assumptions were relaxed to reflect real-world conditions. In particular, they and subsequent researchers found that the company's stock market value could in fact rise as a result of boosting financial leverage to take fuller advantage of the tax shield provided by debt. Interest on borrowings is a tax-deductible expense, whereas dividends on stock are not.
4. Note, however, the uncertainties associated with reserve valuations, discussed in Chapter 2 under the heading “The Value Problem.”

# 术语表

<!--en-->
*Glossary*

**加速**：要求立即偿还违约债务，从而行使贷款合同中规定的权利。

<!--en-->
**accelerate** To demand immediate repayment of debt in default, exercising thereby a right specified in the loan contract.

**会计原则委员会（APB）**：曾是美国注册会计师协会下属的制定规则的机构，是财务会计准则委员会的前身。

<!--en-->
**Accounting Principles Board (APB)** Formerly, a rule-making body of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants. Predecessor of the Financial Accounting Standards Board (see).

**权责发生制会计**：一种会计制度，其中收入在赚取期间确认，费用在发生时确认，无论是否收到或支付现金。

<!--en-->
**accrual accounting** An accounting system in which revenue is recognized during the period in which it is earned and expenses are recognized during the period in which they are incurred, whether or not cash is received or disbursed.

**APB**：会计原则委员会（参见上文）。

<!--en-->
**APB** Accounting Principles Board (see).

**真实利润**：指代表真正财富增加的报告利润，而非利用会计系统漏洞而产生的、不反映实际经济收益的利润。

<!--en-->
**bona fide profit** A reported profit that represents a genuine increase in wealth as opposed to one that exploits a flaw in the accounting system and reflects no economic gain.

**账面价值**：资产在资产负债表上记载的金额。账面价值由资产的建造或购置成本减去折旧（参见）以及后续的价值减值构成。资产的市场价值上涨或通货膨胀并不会导致其账面价值上升。（另见“历史成本会计”。）

<!--en-->
**book value** The amount at which an asset is carried on the balance sheet. Book value consists of the asset's construction or acquisition cost, less depreciation (see) and subsequent impairment of value, if applicable. An asset's book value does not rise as a function of an increase in its market value or inflation. (See also *historical cost accounting*.)

**盈亏平衡率**：指贡献毛益（参见）等于固定成本（参见）时的生产量，此时税前利润为零。

<!--en-->
**breakeven rate** The production volume at which contribution (see) is equivalent to fixed costs (see), resulting in a pretax profit of zero.

示例：

<!--en-->
Example:

$$
\begin{align*}
\text{Price per unit} &= \$2.50 \\
\text{Variable cost per unit} &= \$1.00 \\
\text{Fixed costs} &= \$600 \\
\text{To calculate breakeven: } [\$(2.50 - \$1.00) \times B] - \$600 &= 0 \\
(\$1.50 \times B) &= \$600 \\
B &= 400 \text{ units}
\end{align*}
$$

**经营性现金流**：广播电视台运营商使用的财务绩效指标，定义为营业利润 + 折旧与摊销 + 企业管理费 – 购买新节目的现金支出 + 已购节目成本的摊销。**经济周期**：经济增长、就业和价格水平的周期性波动。经典周期的顺序为：顶峰、衰退、谷底和复苏。术语表

<!--en-->
**broadcast cash flow** A measure of financial performance used by operators of radio and television stations, defined as Operating Income + Depreciation and Amortization + Corporate Overhead - Cash Outlays for Acquisition of New Programming + Amortization of Cost of Previously Acquired Programming.
**business cycle** Periodic fluctuations in economic growth, employment, and price levels. Phases of the classic cycle, in sequence, are peak, recession, trough, and recovery.
GLOSSARY

**资本密集型**：指资产基础中厂房和设备所占比例较大的特征。资本密集带来的高额折旧费用会导致固定成本高企且盈利波动较大。**支出资本化**：将某项支出记为资产，以便在未来期间逐步摊销，理由是该项支出产生的效益会延续到当前会计周期之外。**持有成本**：与商品仓储相关的费用，如融资、保险、储存、安保及损耗费用。**现金对现金利润率**：在房地产领域，指物业产生的现金流除以投入的现金股本。与根据权责发生制会计（参见）计算的传统收益率指标不同，现金对现金利润率不会因折旧等非现金费用而减少。这反映了这样一种假设：土地和建筑物的价值往往会随时间增值，而不会像厂房和设备那样因磨损而贬值。

<!--en-->
**capital-intensive** Characterized by a comparatively large proportion of plant and equipment in asset base. The heavy depreciation charges that arise from capital intensity create a high level of fixed costs and volatile earnings.
**capitalization (of an expenditure)** The recording of an expenditure as an asset, to be written off over future periods, on the grounds that the outlay produces benefits beyond the current accounting cycle.
**carrying cost** Charges associated with warehousing of goods, such as financing, insurance, storage, security, and spoilage.
**cash-on-cash profit** In real estate, the cash flow from a property divided by the cash equity invested. Unlike conventional rate-of-return measures calculated in accordance with accrual accounting (see), cash-on-cash profit is not reduced by noncash charges such as depreciation (see). This reflects a presumption that land and buildings tend to increase in value over time, rather than lose value through wear and tear, as in the case of plant and equipment.

**第11章** 根据《破产法》，这是一种解决破产问题的方法，它允许将陷入困境的企业进行重组，而非直接清算。 **集体诉讼** 根据《联邦民事诉讼规则》第23条提起的一种诉讼类型，只要满足特定条件，允许具有类似诉求的大型原告群体中的一名成员代表整个群体提起诉讼。某些集体诉讼中判定的赔偿金额巨大，足以危及被告企业的偿付能力。 **可比性** 在会计领域，其目标是便于对一组公司进行财务比较，具体做法要求这些公司采用相似的报告准则。示例：

<!--en-->
**Chapter 11** Under the Bankruptcy Code, a method of resolving bankruptcy that provides for reorganization of the failed firm as an alternative to liquidating it.
**class-action suit** A type of lawsuit filed under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23, which allows one member of a large group of plaintiffs with similar claims to sue on behalf of the entire class, provided certain conditions are met. Damages awarded in certain class-action suits have been large enough to compromise the solvency of corporate defendants.
**comparability** In accounting, the objective of facilitating financial comparisons of a group of companies, achieved by requiring them to use similar reporting practices.
Example:

<table><thead><tr><td>年份</td><td>资产价值（美元）</td></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>0</td><td>377</td></tr><tr><td>1</td><td>421</td></tr><tr><td>2</td><td>414</td></tr><tr><td>3</td><td>487</td></tr><tr><td>4</td><td>541</td></tr><tr><td>5</td><td>596</td></tr></tbody></table>

<!--en-->
<table><thead><tr><td>Year</td><td>Value of Asset ($)</td></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>0</td><td>377</td></tr><tr><td>1</td><td>421</td></tr><tr><td>2</td><td>414</td></tr><tr><td>3</td><td>487</td></tr><tr><td>4</td><td>541</td></tr><tr><td>5</td><td>596</td></tr></tbody></table>

该资产价值的年度增幅并不均匀，从第2年的-1.7%到第4年的17.6%不等。不过，如果每年增幅均为9.6%，那么其价值将从最初的377美元增长到最终的596美元。复合年增长率的计算是高端手持计算器上的标准功能；也可通过复利表来得出CAGR值。

<!--en-->
The year-to-year increase in the asset's value has been uneven, ranging from -1.7 percent in Year 2 to 17.6 percent in Year 4. If the increase had been 9.6 percent in each year, however, the value would have grown from the beginning figure of $377 to the terminal figure of $596. Computation of the compound annual growth rate is a standard function on sophisticated hand-held calculators. CAGRs can also be derived from compound interest tables.
**consolidation (of an industry)** A reduction in the number of competitors in an industry through business combinations.
**contribution** Revenue per unit minus variable costs (see) per unit.
Glossary
**convertible** With reference to bonds or preferred stock, redeemable at the holder's option for common stock of the issuer, based on a specified ratio of bonds or preferred shares to common shares. (See also *exchangeable*.)
**cost of capital** The rate of return that investors require for providing capital to a company. A company's cost of capital consists of the cost of capital for a risk-free borrower, a premium for business risk (the risk of becoming unable to continue to cover operating costs), and a premium for financial risk (the risk of becoming unable to continue covering financial costs, such as interest).

无风险资本成本通常等同于美国国债的现行利率。 **累积性** 这是大多数优先股股息的特征：在向普通股股东支付股息之前，必须先补发所有拖欠的股息。 **违约** 指债务义务人未能按时支付约定的利息或本金。发生违约的发行人将面临对其资产的追索，债权人可能会要求其立即全额偿还本金。 **折旧** 一种非现金费用，用于反映一定时期内因磨损而消耗的资本设备价值。 **衍生品**（参见“金融衍生品”）。 **稀释** 指现有股东对盈利的按比例享有的权益被削减。如果在收购中发行新股，且被收购资产产生的盈利不足以维持收购前公司的每股收益水平，就会发生稀释现象。同样，若公司以低于账面价值的价格发行新股，现有股东的利益也会被稀释。在这种情况下，新股东投入的一美元所能购买的公司股份比例，要大于老股东所持有的每股净资产所对应的比例。 **折现率** 用于将未来价值折算为现值的利率。

<!--en-->
The risk-free cost of capital is commonly equated with the prevailing interest rate on U.S. Treasury obligations.
**cumulative** A characteristic of the dividends of most preferred stocks whereby any dividends in arrears must be paid before dividends may be paid to common shareholders.
**default** The failure of a debt obligor to make a scheduled interest or principal payment on time. A defaulting issuer becomes subject to claims against its assets, possibly including a demand by creditors for full and immediate repayment of principal.
**depreciation** A noncash expense meant to represent the amount of capital equipment consumed through wear and tear during the period.
**derivative** (see *financial derivative*).
**dilution** A reduction in present shareholders' proportional claim on earnings. Dilution can occur through the issuance of new shares in an acquisition if the earnings generated by the acquired assets are insufficient to maintain the level of earnings per share previously recorded by the acquiring company. Existing shareholders' interest is likewise diluted if the company issues new stock at a price below book value. In this circumstance, a dollar invested by a new shareholder purchases a larger percentage of the company than is represented by a dollar of net worth held by an old shareholder.
**discount rate** The interest rate used to equate future value (see) with present value (see).

它也被称为资本成本（参见相关条目）。 **现金流折现** 一种基于假定利率，将未来现金流折算为当前金额的技术。例如，100美元以8%的年利率复利计算三年后，其总额将达到125.97美元（忽略税收影响）。该数值可通过以下公式算出：

<!--en-->
Also referred to as cost of capital (see).
**discounted cash flow** A technique for equating future cash flows to a present sum of money, based on an assumed interest rate. For example, $100 compounded annually at 8 percent over three years will cumulate to a sum of $125.97, ignoring the effect of taxes. This figure can be calculated via the equation

$$
P \times (1+r)^n = F
$$

其中 $P$ = 期初本金价值（现值）$r$ = 利率$n$ = 期数$F$ = 期末本金价值（未来值）。在本例中，$100 \times (1.08)^3 = 125.97$。（注意：该公式隐含假设在整个期间收到的现金利息会按原利率进行再投资。）术语表

<!--en-->
where
$P$ = Principal value at beginning of period (Present value)
$r$ = Interest rate
$n$ = Number of periods
$F$ = Principal value at end of period (Future value)
In this case, $100 \times (1.08)^3 = 125.97$. (Note that this formula implicitly assumes reinvestment of cash interest received at the original rate of interest throughout the period.)
GLOSSARY

如果三年后的125.97美元相当于今天的100美元——基于假设的8%年折现率——那么100.00美元与125.97美元之比，即0.794，便可用来确定以相同日期和相同利率折现的任何其他金额的现值。

<!--en-->
If $125.97 three years hence is equivalent to $100 today—given the assumed discount rate (see) of 8 percent per annum—then the ratio $100.00/$125.97, or 0.794, can be used to determine the present value (see) of any other amount discounted back from the same date and at the same rate.

利用同一通用公式，可以根据某项资产预期产生的一系列现金流来为其定价。举例来说，假设分销某种产品的权利预计能在四年内每年产生5,000美元的现金流，之后便不再产生价值。在15%的折现率下，该分销权的价值将为14,820美元，计算如下：

<!--en-->
By using the same general formula, it is possible to assign a value to an asset, based on a series of cash flows it is expected to generate. By way of illustration, suppose the right to distribute a particular product is expected to generate cash flow of $5,000 a year for four years, then expire, leaving no terminal value. At a discount rate of 15 percent, the distribution rights would be valued at $14,820, derived as follows:

**可自由支配的现金流**：指企业在满足基本运营需求后仍然可用的现金流。对于可自由支配的现金流，目前尚无普遍认可的精确定义，但概念上它等于经营活动产生的资金减去所需的营运资本新增投资以及非可自由支配的资本支出。后者难以精确量化，但通常高于维持现有厂房和设备正常运转所需的维护水平。通常，为了保持企业在产能、成本和技术方面的竞争力，还需要一些可称为“半可自由支配”的额外支出。只有资本预算中的一部分——包括那些在需求增长低于预期时可推迟的扩张性支出——才能真正被视为可自由支配的现金流。同样，债务的强制性本金偿还按定义也不能算作可自由支配的现金流。不过，如果一家企业现金流充裕，且实际上有把握为到期债务再融资，那么即便看似专门用于偿还债务的资金，企业也拥有相当大的支配自由度。**多元化**：在投资组合管理中，指通过将资产分散投资于多种不同的证券或投资类型来降低风险的技术。

<!--en-->
**discretionary cash flow** Cash flow that remains available to a company after it has funded its basic operating requirements. There is no universally accepted, precise definition of discretionary cash flow, but conceptually it includes funds from operations less required new investment in working capital and nondiscretionary capital expenditures. The latter figure is difficult to quantify with precision, but it exceeds the required maintenance level required to keep existing plant and equipment in good working order. Ordinarily, some additional expenditures, which may be designated semidiscretionary, are necessary to keep a company competitive with respect to capacity, costs, and technology. Only a portion of the total capital budget, including expansion-oriented outlays that can be deferred in the event of slower-than-expected growth in demand, can truly be considered discretionary. In a similar vein, mandatory principal repayments of debt, by definition, cannot be regarded as discretionary. Still, a company with strong cash flow and the assurance, as a practical matter, of being able to refinance its maturing debt, has considerable freedom in the disposition even of amounts that would appear to be earmarked for debt retirement.
**diversification** In portfolio management, the technique of reducing risk by dividing one's assets among a number of different securities or types of investments.

应用于企业战略时，该术语指涉足多个互不相关的业务领域。其背后的逻辑往往是逆周期性，即通过某些业务板块盈利上升而另一些板块盈利下降的现象，来实现收益的长期稳定。**复式记账法**：一种记账系统，其中每一笔分录都需有一笔对应的抵消分录。例如，向供应商付款会导致现金和应付账款同时减少。术语表：**道琼斯工业平均指数**：一个广受关注的美国股市指数，由30家主要工业公司的普通股组成。

<!--en-->
Applied to corporate strategy, the term refers to participation in several unrelated businesses. The underlying premise is often countercyclicality, or the stabilization of earnings over time through the tendency of profits in certain business segments to be rising at times when they are falling in others.
**double-entry bookkeeping** A system of keeping accounts in which each entry requires an offsetting entry. For example, a payment to a trade creditor causes both cash and accounts payable to decline.
Glossary
**Dow Jones Industrial Average** A widely followed index of the U.S. stock market composed of the common stocks of 30 major industrial corporations.

**息税前利润（EBIT）**：扣除利息费用和所得税前的利润。

<!--en-->
**EBIT** Earnings before deduction of interest expense and income taxes.

**息税折旧摊销前利润（EBITDA）**：扣除利息费用、所得税、折旧和摊销前的利润。**规模经济**：由于大批量生产而导致的单位成本降低现象。这种降低成本的效果很大程度上源于固定成本（即不随生产量直接变化的成本）被分摊到更多的产品单位上，而小规模生产商无法做到这一点。**范围经济**：将相关知识或技术应用于相关产品而导致的单位成本降低现象。**外部增长**：企业通过收购其他公司来实现的营收增长。**保理商**：一种金融机构，通过折价购买企业的应收账款来为企业提供融资。

<!--en-->
**EBITDA** Earnings before deduction of interest expense, income taxes, depreciation, and amortization.
**economies of scale** Reductions in per unit cost that arise from large-volume production. The reductions result in large measure from the spreading of fixed costs (i.e., those that do not vary directly with production volume) over a larger number of units than is possible for a smaller producer.
**economies of scope** Reductions in per unit cost that arise from applying knowledge or technology to related products.
**external growth** Revenue growth achieved by a company through acquisition of other companies.
**factor** A financial institution that provides financing to companies by buying accounts receivable at a discount.

**公允价值会计**：一种会计系统，其中某些资产和负债按其市场价值记录。

<!--en-->
**Fair Value Accounting** An accounting system in which certain assets and liabilities are recorded at their market values.

也称为*市价计价会计*。**财务会计准则委员会（FASB）**：参见相关条目。

<!--en-->
Also known as *mark-to-market accounting*.
**FASB** Financial Accounting Standards Board (see).

**财务会计准则委员会（FASB）**：会计行业的规则制定机构。其成员由一个基金会任命，而该基金会的成员则由美国注册会计师协会的董事选定。**金融衍生品**：一种金融工具，其收益与债券或货币等标的资产的表现挂钩。**财务灵活性**：通过稳健的资本结构和较高的流动性等手段所具备的能力，能够在经济衰退或其他财务压力之下继续投资以维持增长和竞争力。**财务杠杆**：参见*杠杆（金融）*。**固定成本**：不随生产量变化的成本。例如租金、利息费用、高层管理人员薪酬，以及除非采用产量比例法计算的折旧（参见相关条目）。**固定利率债务**：一种债务工具，其利率在贷款清偿前保持在约定水平。（参见*浮动利率债务*。）**浮动利率债务**：一种债务工具，其利率会根据指定的公式随市场利率的变化而波动。

<!--en-->
**Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB)** A rule-making body for the accounting profession. Its members are appointed by a foundation, the members of which are selected by the directors of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants.
**financial derivative** A financial instrument with a return linked to the performance of an underlying asset, such as a bond or a currency.
**financial flexibility** The ability, achieved through such means as a strong capital structure and a high degree of liquidity, to continue to invest in maintaining growth and competitiveness despite business downturns and other financial strains.
**financial leverage** (See *leverage (financial)*.)
**fixed costs** Costs that do not vary with the volume of production. Examples include rent, interest expense, senior management salaries, and, unless calculated by the units-of-production method, depreciation (see).
**fixed-rate debt** A debt obligation on which the interest rate remains at a stated level until the loan has been liquidated. (Compare *floating-rate debt*.)
**floating-rate debt** A debt obligation on which the interest rate fluctuates with changes in market rates of interest, according to a specified formula.

（参见*固定利率债务*。）**自由现金流**：经营性现金流减去资本支出和股息。**重新开始会计**：指从破产中复苏的公司的会计处理方式，即按公允价值记录资产和负债；因此，新报告实体的财务报表通常与破产前的历史报表不具备可比性。**基本面分析**：一种证券分析方法，旨在根据发行人的预期盈利和财务风险等因素来确定股票或债券的内在价值。相比之下，技术分析则试图根据证券的历史价格变动来预测其未来价值。术语表

<!--en-->
(Compare *fixed-rate debt*.)
**free cash flow** Operating cash flow minus capital expenditures and dividends.
**fresh start accounting** Accounting for a company that emerges from bankruptcy, in which assets and liabilities are recorded at fair value, with the result that the new reporting entity's financial statements generally are not comparable to the prebankruptcy historical statements.
**fundamental analysis** A form of security analysis aimed at determining a stock or bond's intrinsic value, based on such factors as the issuer's expected earningsand financial risk. In contrast, technical analysis aims to predict a security's future value based on its past price changes.
GLOSSARY

**未来价值**：在给定利率下，一笔已知金额的资金到指定未来日期时所累积的金额。例如，100美元以8%的年利率复利计算，三年后将累积至125.97美元（不考虑税收影响）。该数值可通过以下公式算出：

<!--en-->
**future value** The amount to which a known sum of money will accumulate by a specified future date, given a stated rate of interest. For example, $100 compounded annually at 8 percent over three years will cumulate to a sum of $125.97, ignoring the effect of taxes. This figure can be calculated via the formula

$$
P \times (1 + r)^n
$$

其中，$P$ = 期初本金，$r$ = 利率，$n$ = 期数。在本例中，$100 \times (1.08)^3 = 125.97$。（该公式隐含假设收到的现金利息会在整个期间按原利率进行再投资。）（另见*现金流折现*、*净现值*和*现值*。）

<!--en-->
where
$P$ = Principal at beginning of period
$r$ = Interest rate
$n$ = Number of periods
In this case, $100 \times (1.08)^3 = 125.97$. (This formula implicitly assumes that cash interest received will be reinvested at the original rate of interest throughout the period.) (See also *discounted cash flow*, *net present value*, and *present value*.)

**GAAP**：公认会计原则（参见相关条目）。**GDP**：国内生产总值（参见相关条目）。**公认会计原则**：规范财务报表编制的规则，依据包括财务会计准则委员会等权威会计机构的公告、行业惯例以及会计文献（包括书籍和文章）。**商誉**：因企业合并而产生的资产负债表项目，代表收购价格超过被收购公司有形资产价值的差额。

<!--en-->
**GAAP** Generally accepted accounting principles (see).
**GDP** Gross domestic product (see).
**generally accepted accounting principles** Rules that govern the preparation of financial statements, based on pronouncements of authoritative accounting organizations such as the Financial Accounting Standards Board, industry practice, and the accounting literature (including books and articles).
**goodwill** A balance sheet item arising from accounting for a business combination, representing the excess of the purchase price over the acquired company's tangible asset value.

**国内生产总值**：一个国家内居民和非居民所生产的所有商品和服务的价值。**业绩指引**：管理层向投资者提供的每股收益预测，用以传达其预期。**历史成本会计**：一种会计体系，其中资产按其原始价值记录（扣除任何适用的折旧或其他价值减损），即便由于通货膨胀或稀缺性增加等原因导致资产的名义美元价值上升。

<!--en-->
**Gross domestic product** The value of all goods and services that residents and nonresidents produce in a country.
**guidance** An earnings per share projection provided to investors to convey management's expectations.
**historical cost accounting** An accounting system in which assets are recorded at their original value (less any applicable depreciation or other impairment of value), notwithstanding that the nominal dollar value of the assets may rise through some cause such as inflation or increased scarcity.

（另见*账面价值*。）**恶意收购**：一家公司在被收购公司董事会最初反对的情况下，通过公开要约收购其他公司的流通股而实现的收购行为。**首次公开募股（IPO）**：此前为私有制的公司首次向公众出售股票。IPO过程被称为“上市”。**内部增长**：企业通过对其现有业务的资本投资所实现的收入增长。**内部产生的资金**：通过经营活动获得的现金，包括净利润、折旧、递延税款以及营运资本的减少。**投资者关系专员**：由公司指定负责与证券分析师沟通的人员。术语表 **非自愿性存货积压**：由于销售放缓而未被生产率下降所抵消，导致的公司存货水平意外增加。**LBO**：杠杆收购（参见相关条目）。**财务杠杆**：利用债务融资以期提高股本回报率。在以下例子中，无杠杆公司因其资本结构中不含债务，可产生3000万美元的经营利润，缴纳1020万美元税款后，获得1980万美元净利润，股本回报率为13.2%（净利润除以股东权益）。

<!--en-->
(See also *book value*.)
**hostile takeover** An acquisition of a corporation by another corporation or by a group of investors, typically through a tender for outstanding shares, in the face of initial opposition by the acquired corporation's board of directors.
**initial public offering (IPO)** A first-time sale of stock to the public by a previously privately owned company. The IPO process is called going public.
**internal growth** Revenue growth achieved by a company through capital investment in its existing business.
**internally generated funds** Cash obtained through operations, including net income, depreciation, deferred taxes, and reductions in working capital.
**investor-relations officer** An individual designated by a corporation to handle communications with securities analysts.
Glossary
**involuntary inventory accumulation** An unintended increase in a company's inventory levels, resulting from a slowdown in sales that is not offset by a reduced rate of production.
**LBO** Leveraged buyout (see).
**leverage (financial)** The use of debt financing in hopes of increasing the rate of return on equity. In the following example, the unleveraged company, with no debt in its capital structure, generates operating income of $30.0 million, pays taxes of $10.2 million, and nets $19.8 million for a return on equity (net income divided by shareholders' equity) of 13.2 percent.

而采用杠杆的公司，尽管经营利润相同，但三分之一的资本来源于长期债务（利率为12%）。利息支出导致其税前净利润（2400万美元）低于无杠杆公司（3000万美元）。缴税后，杠杆公司的净利润（1580万美元）虽少于无杠杆公司（1980万美元），但由于其股本基数较小（1亿美元对比1.5亿美元），反而为股东提供了更高的回报率（15.8%对比13.2%）。

<!--en-->
The leveraged company, with an equivalent amount of operating income, relies on long-term debt (at an interest rate of 12 percent) for one-third of its capital. Interest expense causes its net income before taxes to be lower ($24 million) than the unleveraged company's ($30 million). After taxes, the leveraged company earns less ($15.8 million) than the unleveraged company ($19.8 million), but on a smaller equity base ($100 million versus $150 million) provides shareholders a higher rate of return (15.8 percent versus 13.2 percent).

不过请注意，杠杆作用同样具有反向效应。在以下情景中，两家公司的营业利润均减少了三分之二（降至1000万美元）。由于无需支付利息费用，未使用杠杆的公司可获得660万美元的净利润，其股本回报率达到4.4%。而使用杠杆的公司需将60%的营业利润用于支付利息费用，导致其股本回报率进一步下滑至2.6%。采用财务杠杆会增加股权持有者的风险，使其收益更容易出现波动。资本结构中债务所占比例越大，这种波动的可能性就越高。

<!--en-->
Note, however, that leverage works in reverse as well. In the following scenario, operating income declines by two-thirds (to $10 million) at both companies. With no interest expense, the unleveraged company manages to net $6.6 million for a 4.4 percent return on equity. The leveraged company, obliged to pay out 60 percent of its operating income in interest expense, suffers a sharper decline in return on equity (to 2.6 percent). Incurring financial leverage increases the risk to equity holders, whose returns become more subject to fluctuations. The greater the percentage of the capital structure that consists of debt, the greater the potential for such fluctuations.

**经营杠杆**：用固定成本（参见相关词条）替代可变成本（参见相关词条），以期提高股本回报率。在下例中，A公司的成本结构以可变费用为主，其中劳动力成本占很大比重。当销售量增加5%（从50万单位增至52.5万单位）时，其股东权益回报率便从11.0%升至13.7%。相比之下，B公司安装了节省劳动力的设备，大幅减少了单位产品的工时；其可变成本低于A公司（每单位分别为30美元和50美元），但由于折旧费用较高（参见相关词条），其固定成本也更高（每年分别为2500万美元和3000万美元）。B公司较高的经营杠杆带来的好处是：当其销量增加5%时，股东权益回报率可从11.0%升至14.7%，这一增幅要大于A公司在类似销量增长下的增幅。同理，如果两家公司的销量随后从52.5万单位回落至50万单位，B公司的股东权益回报率降幅也会比A公司更为显著。术语表 360

<!--en-->
**leverage (operating)** The substitution of fixed costs (see) for variable costs (see) in hopes of increasing return on equity. In the following example, Company A's cost structure is dominated by variable expenses, of which labor represents a substantial portion. A 5 percent increase in sales volume (from 500,000 to 525,000 units) raises the rate of return on shareholders' equity from11.0 percent to 13.7 percent. Company B, on the other hand, has installed labor-saving equipment that sharply reduces man-hours per unit of production. Its variable costs are lower than Company A's ($50.00 versus $30.00 per unit), but as a function of its greater depreciation (see) charges, its fixed costs are higher ($30 million versus $25 million per annum). The benefit of Company B's higher operating leverage is that a 5 percent increase in its unit sales raises its return on shareholders' equity from 11.0 percent to 14.7 percent, a larger boost than Company A receives from a comparable rise in volume. By the same token, Company B's return on shareholders' equity will fall more sharply than Company A's if unit volume at both companies subsequently recedes from 525,000 to 500,000 units.

Glossary
361

**杠杆收购（LBO）**：主要指通过借贷资金来收购一家公司或其业务部门。股权投资者通常期望通过经营活动产生的现金流（以及可能的资产出售所得）来偿还债务，从而提高其所持股份的净值。**杠杆性资本重组**：一种企业战略，即支付一笔由债务融资的大规模现金股息。该策略常被用作抵御恶意收购的手段，原因有二：首先，通过增加企业的财务杠杆（参见相关词条），可以降低收购方利用借贷资金的能力，以免收购后的公司背负过重的债务；其次，资本重组会提高试图保持控制权的股东们的所有权集中度。**流动性**：指企业在到期时履行短期义务的能力。**宏观经济**：涉及整个经济或其主要细分领域，如制造业、农业、政府部门等。（另见*微观经济*。）**市值**：一家企业所有已发行股票及债务证券的市场价值总和。

<!--en-->
**leveraged buyout (LBO)** An acquisition of a company or a division, financed primarily with borrowed funds. Equity investors typically hope to profit by repaying debt through cash generated by operations (and possibly from proceeds of asset sales), thereby increasing the net value of their stake.
**leveraged recapitalization** A corporate strategy involving the payment of a large, debt-financed cash dividend. The strategy is often employed as a defense against an attempted hostile takeover, for two reasons. First, by increasing the company's financial leverage (see), the transaction reduces the potential for a raider to use borrowed funds, lest the posttakeover company become excessively debt-laden. Second, the recapitalization increases the concentration of ownership in the hands of those attempting to retain control.
**liquidity** The ability of a company to meet its near-term obligations when due.
**macroeconomic** Pertaining to the economy as a whole or its major subdivisions, such as the manufacturing sector, the agricultural sector, the government. (See also *microeconomic*.)
**market capitalization** The aggregate market value of all of a company's outstanding equity and debt securities.

它也被宽泛地用来表示公司股价与流通股数的乘积。（另见*企业总价值*。）**市价计价会计**：根据财务报表日期该金融工具的公允市场价格来对其持仓进行估值的方法。如果该金融工具并非定期交易，则可参照同类交易工具的价格来推断其当前市场价值。**成熟**：就产品、企业或行业而言，指处于这样一种发展阶段：销售增长率仍为正值，但已不再超过经济的总体增长率。**微观经济**：涉及经济的某个小领域，如某个行业或特定企业。（另见*宏观经济*。）**倍数**：就普通股而言，指股价与每股收益之比。同样，收购中支付的价格也可视为被收购公司盈利、现金流或EBITDA的倍数（参见相关词条）。**多变量**：在定量建模领域，指采用多个解释性因素的特性。**净现值**：未来现金流入流的现值（参见相关词条）减去相关现金流出流的现值。

<!--en-->
Also used loosely to represent the product of a company's share price and number of shares outstanding. (See also *total enterprise value*.)
**mark-to-market accounting** The practice of valuing a holding of a financial instrument according to its fair market price on the date of the financial statement. If the instrument does not trade on a regular basis, a current market value may be inferred from the prices of comparable instruments that do.
**mature** With respect to a product, firm, or industry, at a stage of development at which the rate of sales growth remains positive but no longer exceeds the general growth rate of the economy.
**microeconomic** Pertaining to a small segment of the economy, such as an individual industry or a particular firm. (See also *macroeconomic*.)
**multiple** With respect to a common stock, the ratio of the share price to earnings per share. Similarly, the price paid in an acquisition can be viewed as a multiple of the acquired company's earnings, cash flow, or EBITDA (see).
**multivariate** In the field of quantitative modeling, having the characteristic of employing more than one explanatory factor.
**net present value** The present value (see) of a stream of future cash inflows, less the present value of an associated stream of current or future cash outflows.

这种计算方法有助于比较不同投资项目的吸引力，如下一页的示例所示。两个拟议的资本项目在第一年均需支出6000万美元。项目A产生的现金流更高，且不会像项目B那样在后期逐渐衰减。项目A在第10年的残值也更为优越。即便如此，基于更高的净现值（1770万美元对比项目A的1430万美元），项目B仍是更盈利的投资。**名义美元**：以货币面值表示的金额，未根据指定基准期的购买力变化进行调整。（另见*实际美元*。）

<!--en-->
This calculation is useful for comparing the attractiveness of alternative investments, as shown in the example on the following page. Both proposed capital projects require an expenditure of $60 million during the first year. Project A generates a higher cash flow, without trailing off in the latter years as Project B is projected to do. Residual value in year 10 is likewise superior in Project A. Even so, Project B is the more profitable investment, based on a higher net present value ($17.7 million versus $14.3 million for Project A).
**nominal dollar** A monetary sum expressed in terms of its currency face amount, unadjusted for changes in purchasing power from a designated base period. (See also *real dollar*.)
